The historical framing and the emphasis on the growing centrality of biophysics are potentially useful contributions. However, the review's evidentiary basis is not transparently presented. The search strategy is described only at a high level, and the quantitative claims (e.g., 792 articles, 57% addressing stability) are not traceable to reproducible methods. The manuscript would benefit from a more rigorous systematic methodology, including explicit search strings, screening criteria, and a transparent data extraction framework. The narrative is readable but at times asserts trends without direct citation support in the visible text. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers in protein engineering, structural biology, and biophysics, particularly those interested in the scientific landscape of Latin America. The review may also be of interest to science policy analysts and funding agencies seeking an overview of capacity and trends in Brazilian protein science. The historical narrative and the emphasis on hybrid experimental-computational workflows could serve as a useful entry point for newcomers to the field. Major strengths The manuscript addresses a genuinely under-documented topic: the historical and thematic development of protein engineering in Brazil. The organization around five biophysical properties (folding, stability, dynamics, molecular recognition, catalytic efficiency) provides a coherent conceptual scaffold. The authors correctly emphasize the interdependence of protein properties and the need for orthogonal validation, which is a scientifically sound perspective. The inclusion of recent AI-based methods (AlphaFold, ProteinMPNN, language models) reflects an up-to-date understanding of the field. 01 基本信息 标题 : Beyond AlphaFold 3: a standardised benchmark of open-source co-folding models for antibody-antigen complexes, from docking accuracy to interaction specificity 作者与单位 : Ramon, Aubin; Cheruku, Arnav; Sormanni, Pietro（伦敦帝国理工学院，Sormanni 实验室）；Haowen Shen（未提供具体单位） 期刊/预印本平台 : mAbs（同行评审期刊） 年份 : 2026（在线发表日期 2026-11-12） 论文类型 : 基准测试/方法评估研究 领域 : 蛋白质结构预测 × 抗体-抗原复合物共折叠建模 关键词 : 抗体-抗原复合物、共折叠模型、DockQ、AlphaFold 3、Protenix-v2、ESMFold2、OpenDDE、相互作用特异性 DOI/arXiv 号 : 10.1080/19420862.2026.2760737 代码 : https://gitlab.doc.ic.ac.uk/sormanni-lab/cofolding-benchmarking 数据 : https://zenodo.org/records/22874923 阅读日期 : 未提供 在该方向中的位置 : 本文是抗体-抗原复合物共折叠模型的标准化基准测试研究，系统比较了 AlphaFold 3 与三个开源模型（Protenix-v2、ESMFold2、OpenDDE）在对接精度、置信度校准和相互作用特异性方面的表现，为该领域提供了可复现的评估框架和数据集（SAbDab2-Bench）。 02 一句话总结 本文构建了包含 200 个抗体-抗原复合物的标准化基准数据集（SAbDab2-Bench + Ab-FoldBench），在统一输入、采样和评估协议下比较了 AlphaFold 3、Protenix-v2、ESMFold2 和 OpenDDE 五个共折叠模型，发现 OpenDDE 对接精度最高但耗时最长，Protenix-v2 在精度-效率平衡上最优，且所有模型对界面突变和抗原置换的置信度响应存在差异。 03 研究问题 具体问题 : 最新一代共折叠模型（AF3、Protenix-v2、ESMFold2、OpenDDE）在抗体-抗原复合物结构预测中的对接精度、置信度可靠性及相互作用特异性识别能力如何？在标准化条件下，哪个模型最适合抗体发现和工程设计？ 为什么重要 : 抗体-抗原复合物结构预测是抗体药物发现、表位定位、亲和力成熟和从头设计的关键步骤。不同模型在架构、训练数据和推理策略上差异显著，但缺乏在统一条件下的系统比较，导致实际应用中的模型选择缺乏依据。 现有方法不足 : 已有基准测试（如 FoldBench）覆盖时间窗口有限（截至 2024），且各模型在各自原始研究中使用的数据集、评估指标和采样策略不一致，难以直接横向比较。此外，现有评估多聚焦于对接精度，忽略了置信度校准和相互作用特异性（即能否区分结合对与非结合对）。 精确的 Can 问题 : Can open-source co-folding models match or exceed AlphaFold 3's antibody-antigen docking accuracy under standardized conditions, and can their confidence scores reliably distinguish specific from non-specific interactions? 04 背景与发展脉络 阶段一：单链预测时代 — AlphaFold2 实现了近实验精度的单链蛋白质结构预测，但无法直接处理复合物。 阶段二：复合物共折叠模型 — AlphaFold-Multimer 扩展了 AlphaFold2 以处理多聚体，但抗体-抗原复合物因缺乏共进化信号而精度有限。 阶段三：扩散模型与大规模预训练 — AlphaFold 3 引入扩散架构和统一输入表示，显著提升复合物预测能力，但权重受限（非商业）。Protenix-v2、ESMFold2、OpenDDE 等开源模型相继发布，声称在抗体-抗原预测上达到或超越 AF3。 阶段四：标准化基准测试需求 — 各模型在独立研究中报告的性能差异可能源于数据集、评估协议和采样策略的不同，亟需统一框架下的公平比较。本文在此阶段提出 SAbDab2-Bench 和标准化评估流程。 本文主张的位置 : 在开源共折叠模型快速迭代的背景下，提供首个包含最新模型（截至 2026 年）的标准化基准，并首次将相互作用特异性（通过突变和抗原置换扰动）纳入评估维度。 05 核心痛点 痛点 表现 成因或作者解释 文中证据 跨研究不可比性 各模型在原始论文中报告的性能差异大，但无法确定是模型差异还是评估协议差异 数据集、采样策略、评估指标和置信度定义不统一 Introduction 第 3-4 段；Results 第 2 节 "standardized input preparation, sampling, candidate ranking and evaluation procedures" 置信度校准不足 模型置信度分数（如 ipTM）与真实精度相关性因模型而异 各模型使用不同的置信度训练目标和输出头 Results 图 3a，ipTM-DockQ 相关性 0.77-0.82 不等 相互作用特异性未评估 现有基准仅测试已知结合对，不测试模型能否拒绝非结合对 缺乏标准化的负样本生成和评估协议 Introduction 最后一段；Results 第 4 节 数据集时效性不足 FoldBench 覆盖窗口截至 2024 年，无法评估模型对更新结构的泛化能力 结构数据库持续增长，模型训练截止日期各异 Results 第 1 节 "SAbDab2-Bench...all deposited after the 2024 FoldBench deposition window" 计算成本差异大 OpenDDE 精度最高但耗时 40 小时/200 复合物，ESMFold2-fast 仅需数小时 模型架构（扩散步数、MSA 需求）和推理策略不同 Results 图 2f，折叠时间分布 运行不确定性 固定种子下 Protenix-v2 输出仍存在运行间差异 PyTorch 默认非确定性算法 Methods 第 3.9 节，表 S6 06 核心思想 表面方法 : 构建包含 200 个抗体-抗原复合物的基准数据集（88 个新收集的 SAbDab2-Bench + 112 个重建的 Ab-FoldBench），在统一输入（相同 MSA、模板搜索）、统一采样（10 种子 × 5 扩散样本 = 50 预测/复合物）和统一评估（角色感知的 DockQ 和 ipTM 定义）条件下，比较五个共折叠模型。 核心洞察 : - 模型性能排序对评估指标敏感：DockQ 中位数排序 ≠ 通过率排序 ≠ 高精度预测数量排序。 - 置信度分数（ipTM）的校准因模型而异，最优阈值跨度大（0.73-0.91），不能跨模型通用。 - 模型对界面突变和抗原置换的置信度响应不同，反映其对相互作用特异性的编码能力差异。 - 计算成本与精度之间存在明确权衡，模型选择应基于应用场景。 可能的普适教训 [Analysis]: 共折叠模型的评估必须区分"结构恢复精度"和"相互作用特异性判别"两个维度，前者衡量几何准确性，后者衡量物理化学合理性。一个模型可能在 DockQ 上表现优异，但对非结合对的置信度区分能力不足，这在筛选场景中可能导致大量假阳性。 07 方法总览 输入 : 抗体和抗原的氨基酸序列；对于模板支持模型，自动搜索 PDB 模板（截止 2021-09-30）；MSA 通过 ColabFold MMseqs2 流程生成（UniRef30 2023-02 + 环境数据库 2021-08）。 输出 : 每个复合物的 50 个预测结构（10 种子 × 5 扩散样本），附带置信度分数（ipTM、pTM）。 模块 : 1. 数据集构建：SAbDab2 解析、泄漏过滤、结构质量筛选、抗原长度限制 2. introduction, results and discussion, methods, and figure legends. Assessment boundary Scientific validity, methodological rigor, reproducibility, and interpretation of results as presented. No assessment of editorial fit or scope for the specific journal. Shared manuscript claim summary The authors present a standardized benchmark of five co-folding models (AlphaFold 3, Protenix-v2, ESMFold2, ESMFold2-fast, OpenDDE) for antibody-antigen complex prediction, using a newly curated dataset (SAbDab2-Bench) combined with a reconstructed subset of FoldBench (Ab-FoldBench). They evaluate docking accuracy, confidence-based selection, inference-time scaling, and sensitivity to interface mutations and non-cognate antigen shuffling. They report that OpenDDE achieves the highest median DockQ and pass rate, followed by Protenix-v2, with both outperforming AlphaFold 3. They also find that confidence metrics are generally informative but require model-specific calibration, and that all models show stronger rejection of non-cognate antigens than of interface mutations. Visible evidence base Full text with results, figures (Figure 1-4), tables (Table 1-4), and methods sections. Supplementary figures and tables are referenced but not fully provided. Missing materials affecting confidence Supplementary figures (S1-S13), supplementary tables (S1-S6), and the full dataset details are referenced but not included in the provided material. This limits full verification of some analyses, particularly the stratified analyses and extended configurations. Reviewer Overall assessment This manuscript addresses a timely and practically important question: how do recently released open-source co-folding models compare to AlphaFold 3 for antibody-antigen complex prediction under standardized conditions? The authors have made a commendable effort to control for confounding variables by standardizing input preparation, sampling, and evaluation. The inclusion of decoy-based specificity testing is a valuable addition beyond simple docking accuracy benchmarks. However, several methodological choices and interpretations require clarification or additional analysis before the conclusions can be fully supported. The statistical approach, while appropriate in parts, has some limitations that should be addressed. The practical guidance provided is useful but would benefit from more explicit consideration of the trade-offs involved. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers in antibody engineering, structural biology, and computational protein design would find this benchmark highly relevant. The practical comparison of model performance, including runtime and licensing considerations, is directly useful for practitioners selecting tools for epitope mapping, candidate triage, and structure-guided design. The analysis of confidence calibration and specificity testing is also relevant to the broader protein-protein interaction prediction community. Major strengths 1. The standardization of input preparation, sampling, and evaluation across models is a significant strength, addressing a common limitation in prior benchmarks. 2. The construction of a new, curated dataset (SAbDab2-Bench) with post-training structures and sequence-diversity filtering is valuable and extends the evaluation beyond existing benchmarks. 3. The inclusion of decoy-based specificity testing (mutations and antigen shuffling) goes beyond simple accuracy metrics and addresses a critical practical need. 4. The analysis of confidence-based selection and the reporting of model-specific calibration is practically useful. 5. The release of code, data, and generated structures is commendable and supports reproducibility. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Statistical rigor Claim pointer The manuscript claims that OpenDDE achieved the highest median DockQ and pass rate, followed by Protexin-v2, and that both outperformed AlphaFold 3 on these measures. Evidence pointer Figure 2b-c, Table 2 Concern The statistical comparison between models relies on paired tests (McNemar for pass rates, permutation for medians) that are appropriate for paired data. However, the manuscript does not adequately address the issue of multiple testing across the 10 pairwise model comparisons. While the Benjamini-Hochberg correction is applied, the power of these tests to detect meaningful differences, particularly between adjacent models in the ranking, is not discussed. The statement that "some of these differences, and notably all differences between ranking-adjacent models, did not reach the threshold for statistical significance" is important, but the manuscript does not provide effect sizes or confidence intervals for the differences in median DockQ. This makes it difficult to assess whether the lack of significance reflects a true lack of difference or insufficient power. The authors should report effect sizes and confidence intervals for the key comparisons, and discuss the practical significance of the observed differences. Why it matters The central claim of the paper is the relative performance ranking of the models. Without a clear assessment of the magnitude and uncertainty of the differences, the ranking may be over-interpreted. The practical guidance provided in the conclusions depends on this ranking being reliable. Resolution test Provide effect sizes (e.g., median difference with 95% confidence intervals) for the key pairwise comparisons. Discuss the statistical power of the tests given the sample size of 200 complexes. Consider whether a non-inferiority or equivalence framework might be more appropriate for comparing adjacent models. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Methodological validity Claim pointer The manuscript states that "Providing the antigen in the conformation observed in its cognate antibody-bound structure increased docking pass rates for AF3, Protenix-v2 and OpenDDE" and that "non-cognate templates produced more modest gains in high-quality predictions." Evidence pointer Figure S2, Figure S3 Concern The analysis of template contribution is confounded by the fact that the cognate-bound antigen structure is, by definition, the target structure being predicted. Supplying this structure provides the model with information about the bound conformation that would not be available in a real prospective scenario. The comparison between cognate-bound and non-cognate templates is useful, but the manuscript does not clearly distinguish between the value of having any template versus the value of having the exact bound conformation. The authors should clarify that the cognate-bound template condition represents an upper bound on template utility, and the non-cognate template condition is more representative of real-world use. The practical recommendation to supply antigen structures should be framed in this context. Why it matters The practical guidance for users depends on understanding the realistic benefit of template usage. Overstating the benefit of cognate-bound templates could mislead users into expecting similar gains in prospective applications where such structures are unavailable. Resolution test Clearly label the cognate-bound template condition as an oracle or upper-bound scenario. Discuss the implications of the non-cognate template results for practical use. Consider analyzing the subset of cases where the non-cognate template is structurally similar to the cognate-bound antigen to better understand the source of the benefit. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Reproducibility Claim pointer The manuscript reports that "Under default settings, ipTM and pTM varied across runs in a complex-dependent manner, showing that fixed seeds alone do not guarantee reproducibility." Evidence pointer Table S6, Methods Section 3.9 Concern The finding of non-determinism in Protenix-v2 is important, but the manuscript does not fully explore its implications. The primary analysis uses ten seeds and reports results averaged across all subsets of five seeds. If the model is non-deterministic even with fixed seeds, then the results from a single run with a given seed may not be reproducible. The manuscript should clarify whether the non-determinism is due to non-deterministic PyTorch operations that can be controlled by setting a deterministic flag, or whether it is inherent to the model architecture. The practical guidance should include a recommendation for users to enable deterministic execution when reproducibility is critical. Why it matters Reproducibility is a core principle of scientific benchmarking. If the results cannot be reproduced by other researchers, the benchmark's value is significantly diminished. The manuscript should provide clear guidance on how to obtain reproducible results. Resolution test Provide a detailed analysis of the sources of non-determinism. Recommend a specific configuration (e.g., setting the deterministic flag) that users should adopt for reproducible results. Report the impact of this configuration on runtime and performance. Concern ID R1-M4 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Interpretation Claim pointer The manuscript concludes that "current models appear better at rejecting clearly non-cognate partners than at recognizing sequence changes that disrupt or diminish binding." Evidence pointer Figure 4, Tables 4, S2, S3 Concern The decoy analysis is a valuable addition, but the interpretation is limited by the nature of the decoys. The interface mutations are designed to be disruptive, but their actual effect on binding is not experimentally verified. The manuscript acknowledges this ("these decoys are expected, rather than experimentally shown, to bind weakly or not at all"), but the discussion could be more nuanced. The finding that OpenDDE retains high confidence for many mutated interfaces could be interpreted as a limitation, but it could also reflect that some mutations do not significantly disrupt the overall binding mode. The authors should discuss alternative interpretations and the need for experimental validation. Why it matters The conclusion about specificity is a key finding of the paper. If the decoys are not representative of real non-binding pairs, the conclusion may not generalize. The practical implications for screening and design depend on this conclusion. Resolution test Discuss the limitations of the decoy design more thoroughly. Consider analyzing the relationship between the magnitude of the predicted binding affinity change and the confidence score. Suggest future work with experimentally validated non-binding pairs. Minor Comments Concern ID R1-m1 Severity Minor Axis Clarity Affected element Abstract Evidence pointer Abstract Issue The abstract states "OpenDDE achieved the highest median DockQ and docking pass rate, followed by Protenix-v2, although their difference was not statistically significant." This is slightly confusing as it implies a ranking that is not statistically supported. It would be clearer to state that OpenDDE and Protenix-v2 performed similarly and both outperformed the other models. Required correction Rephrase to avoid implying a definitive ranking where statistical significance is lacking. For example: "OpenDDE and Protenix-v2 achieved the highest median DockQ and docking pass rates, with no statistically significant difference between them, and both outperformed AlphaFold 3." Concern ID R1-m2 Severity Minor Axis Clarity Affected element Results, Section "Standardised inference and evaluation" Evidence pointer Table 1 Issue The table lists "Seeds ∣ Samples" as "10 ∣ 5" for all models. It is unclear whether this means 10 seeds with 5 samples per seed, or 5 seeds with 10 samples per seed. The text later clarifies "five samples for each of ten seeds," but the table notation is ambiguous. Required correction Clarify the notation in the table legend or use a more explicit format, such as "10 seeds × 5 samples." Concern ID R1-m3 Severity Minor Axis Completeness Affected element Methods, Section "Model implementation and compute specifications" Evidence pointer Methods Section 3.4 Issue The manuscript mentions that ESMFold2 was "slower than its competitor in this study" and attributes this to "the absence of optional acceleration libraries." However, it is not clear whether this is a limitation of the model or the specific installation. The authors should clarify whether the reported runtimes are representative of typical usage. Required correction Add a sentence clarifying that the ESMFold2 runtimes may be improved by installing the optional acceleration libraries, and that the reported times are specific to the authors' installation. Concern ID R1-m4 Severity Minor Axis Interpretation Affected element Results, Section "Performance in antibody-antigen complex prediction" Evidence pointer Figure 2g Issue The correlation between H-CDR3 sequence novelty and DockQ is weak, but the manuscript does not discuss potential reasons for this. For example, the diversity of the benchmark set or the specific metric used for sequence novelty could influence the result. Required correction Add a brief discussion of why the relationship might be weak, and consider whether alternative measures of novelty (e.g., structural novelty) might be more relevant. Concern ID R1-m5 Severity Minor Axis Clarity Affected element Conclusions Evidence pointer Conclusions Issue The conclusion that "Protenix-v2 offers a useful balance for antibody-design campaigns" is based on the benchmark results, but the manuscript does not explicitly discuss the trade-offs between accuracy, speed, and licensing for different use cases. A more explicit decision framework would be helpful. Required correction Add a brief paragraph in the conclusions that summarizes the key trade-offs (accuracy vs. speed vs. licensing) and provides guidance on model selection for different scenarios (e.g., high-throughput screening vs. high-accuracy design). Technical failings that need to be addressed before the case is established R1-M1: Lack of effect sizes and confidence intervals for key performance comparisons. R1-M2: Confounded interpretation of template benefit without clear distinction between oracle and realistic scenarios. R1-M3: Insufficient guidance on achieving reproducible results given the observed non-determinism. Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality : The work is original in its comprehensive, standardized comparison of recently released open-source models, including a novel decoy-based specificity analysis. However, the individual components (benchmarking, confidence analysis) are not entirely new. Scientific importance : The findings are practically important for the antibody engineering community, providing guidance on model selection and highlighting limitations in specificity testing. The release of a new benchmark dataset is a valuable contribution. Interdisciplinary readership : The topic is of interest to structural biologists, computational biologists, and antibody engineers. The manuscript is written in a way that is largely accessible to these groups, though some methodological details may be challenging for non-specialists. Technical soundness : The overall methodology is sound, with careful standardization. However, the statistical analysis could be strengthened (R1-M1), and the interpretation of the template analysis needs clarification (R1-M2). The reproducibility issue (R1-M3) is a concern. Readability for nonspecialists : The manuscript is generally well-written and clear. The figures are informative. However, the methods section is dense and may be difficult for non-experts to follow. The abstract and conclusions are accessible. Recommendation posture Supportive if technical concerns are resolved. The manuscript addresses an important question with a well-designed benchmark. The major concerns regarding statistical rigor, interpretation of template benefits, and reproducibility guidance need to be addressed before the conclusions can be fully supported. The minor comments are mostly clarifications that would improve readability.

no access to full manuscript, figures, tables, or supplementary materials Shared manuscript claim summary The authors report a whole-proteome structural analysis of Treponema pallidum subsp. pallidum (Nichols strain, TPANIC) using AlphaFold and FoldSeek, achieving high-confidence models for approximately 92% of the proteome, assigning putative functions to 24 previously uncharacterized proteins, and proposing a revised composition of the outer membrane biogenesis machinery (a spirochete-specific BAM-TAM complex containing BamA, TamB, BamD, and BamB) based on comparative structural analyses and AlphaFold-Multimer modeling. Visible evidence base Abstract text only; no figures, tables, methods, or supplementary data provided Missing materials affecting confidence Full manuscript, all figures and tables, methods details, model confidence metrics, validation statistics, list of the 24 assigned proteins, details of the BAM-TAM complex modeling, and any experimental corroboration Reviewer Overall assessment The abstract presents a potentially valuable application of AlphaFold-based structural prediction to a pathogen with a minimal genome and many uncharacterized proteins. The stated goals are clear and the approach is timely. However, the abstract alone provides insufficient evidence to evaluate the robustness of the structural models, the confidence of the functional assignments, or the validity of the proposed BAM-TAM complex revision. The claim of a "clearer prediction" of biological and pathogenic attributes is not substantiated by the evidence visible in the abstract. The work may be of interest to the spirochete and structural biology communities, but the case is not established from the supplied material. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers studying Treponema pallidum biology and syphilis pathogenesis, spirochete outer membrane biology, and those applying AlphaFold-based structural genomics to minimal or fastidious organisms. The proposed BAM-TAM complex would be of particular interest to investigators of bacterial outer membrane protein biogenesis and spirochete-specific secretion systems. Major strengths The abstract addresses a clear and important gap, namely the large fraction of uncharacterized proteins in a clinically significant pathogen. The use of both precomputed and newly generated AlphaFold models, combined with FoldSeek for structural homology matching, is a sensible and current methodological approach. The reported coverage of approximately 92% of the proteome is a strong quantitative claim if supported by appropriate confidence metrics. The proposed revision of the BAM-TAM complex composition is a specific and testable hypothesis that could have broader implications for spirochete biology. They report that the HD is the main source of conformational disorder, that the CAT-Cter assembly preserves the canonical sulfatase catalytic architecture, that the HD modestly alters average structure but destabilizes catalytic framework dynamics, that catalytic residue maturation modulates the conformational landscape without changing overall architecture, and that N-glycan chitobiose cores have limited structural effects. They propose a modular organization with implications for dual-site inhibitor design. Visible evidence base Abstract text only; no figures, tables, methods, or simulation details provided Missing materials affecting confidence Full manuscript, simulation parameters, force field details, system setup, equilibration protocols, trajectory lengths, convergence analyses, replica or repeat information, structural validation of the AlphaFold2 model, quantitative metrics for disorder and dynamics, and any comparison with experimental data Reviewer Overall assessment The abstract presents a plausible and potentially useful computational study of HSulf-2, a protein of biomedical relevance for which experimental structures are lacking. The modular organization hypothesis is coherent and the proposed inhibitor design concept is interesting. However, the abstract alone provides no quantitative evidence, no methodological detail, and no validation of the AlphaFold2 model or the simulation outcomes. The central claims, while internally consistent, cannot be evaluated for technical soundness or robustness from the supplied material. The work may be of interest to the computational glycosaminoglycan and sulfatase communities, but the case is not established at this stage. Who would be interested in the results, and why Computational biophysicists studying intrinsically disordered proteins and multidomain enzymes; researchers in glycosaminoglycan biology and heparan sulfate signaling; cancer biologists interested in HSulf-2 as a therapeutic target; and medicinal chemists pursuing selective enzyme inhibitors, particularly those exploring dual-site or allosteric strategies. Major strengths The study addresses a biologically and clinically relevant target with no experimental structure, using a modern predictive approach. The focus on the functional roles of disordered regions and post-translational modifications is timely. The proposed modular architecture and the dual-site inhibitor concept provide a clear translational rationale. The abstract is well written and accessible to a broad readership. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Technical soundness Claim pointer The simulations identified several intrinsically disordered regions, confirming that the HD constitutes the principal source of conformational disorder within the enzyme. Evidence pointer Abstract; location not provided Concern The abstract provides no quantitative measure of disorder, no definition of the criteria used to classify regions as intrinsically disordered, and no comparison with predictors or experimental data. The claim that the HD is the principal source of disorder is presented without supporting metrics such as root mean square fluctuations, secondary structure propensity over time, or order parameter distributions. Why it matters Without defined disorder criteria and quantitative comparisons across domains, the central conclusion about the HD being the principal disorder source cannot be verified. This claim underpins the proposed modular organization and the inhibitor design rationale. Resolution test Provide disorder metrics (for example, per-residue fluctuations, secondary structure persistence, or radius of gyration distributions) for each domain, with clear thresholds for disorder classification, and show that the HD values are statistically distinct from those of the CAT and Cter regions. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Technical soundness Claim pointer The CAT-Cter assembly reproduces the canonical catalytic architecture conserved throughout the sulfatase family, whereas the HD induces only minor changes in the average structure while significantly destabilizing the conformational dynamics of the catalytic framework. Evidence pointer Abstract; location not provided Concern The abstract reports a comparison of average structure and dynamics between systems with and without the HD, but no details are given on how the systems were constructed, how the HD was removed or included, how the simulations were equilibrated, or how statistical significance was assessed. The phrase "significantly destabilizing" implies a statistical test, but no test or effect size is reported. Why it matters The distinction between minor average structural changes and significant dynamic destabilization is a key mechanistic claim. Without evidence of statistical significance and adequate sampling, the claim could reflect insufficient convergence or system preparation artifacts rather than a genuine physical effect. Resolution test Report the number of independent simulations, total simulation time per system, convergence checks, and the statistical comparison (for example, bootstrapped confidence intervals or block averaging) for the dynamic metrics of the catalytic framework with and without the HD. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Technical soundness Claim pointer Maturation of the catalytic residue modulates the conformational landscape of HSulf-2 without altering its overall architecture, whereas the conserved chitobiose cores of N-glycans exert only limited structural effects. Evidence pointer Abstract; location not provided Concern The abstract states that catalytic residue maturation and N-glycosylation have specific effects, but no details are provided on how these states were modeled. For the catalytic residue, it is unclear which residue was modified and how the maturation state was represented. For N-glycans, only the chitobiose cores were included, and the rationale for this truncation is not given. No quantitative comparison of conformational landscapes or structural effects is presented. Why it matters These claims are central to the conclusion that the catalytic domain is structurally robust to modifications. Without modeling details and quantitative comparisons, the reader cannot assess whether the chosen representations are physically appropriate or whether the conclusions are sensitive to the modeling choices. Resolution test Specify the catalytic residue and its maturation state, describe the glycan construction and truncation rationale, and provide quantitative comparisons (for example, root mean square deviation distributions, free energy landscapes, or principal component projections) for the systems with and without each modification. Concern ID R1-M4 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Model validity Claim pointer Molecular dynamics simulations based on the AlphaFold2 model of HSulf-2 were used to investigate the structural and dynamic contributions of its domains and selected post-translational modifications. Evidence pointer Abstract; location not provided Concern The abstract does not report any validation of the AlphaFold2 model used as the simulation starting point. No comparison with experimental data, such as small angle X-ray scattering, cross-linking mass spectrometry, or homology to related sulfatases with known structures, is mentioned. The reliability of the simulation conclusions depends directly on the quality of the starting model, particularly for the disordered HD. Why it matters AlphaFold2 predictions are generally reliable for folded domains but are less trustworthy for disordered regions and for the relative orientation of multiple domains. If the model is not validated, the conclusions about domain dynamics and the HD contribution could be artifacts of the predicted model rather than properties of the actual protein. Resolution test Provide a validation section comparing the AlphaFold2 model with any available experimental information, discuss the confidence scores for the HD and interdomain regions, and justify the use of the model for dynamic simulations. Minor Comments Concern ID R1-m1 Severity Minor Axis Reproducibility Affected element Simulation protocol Evidence pointer Abstract; location not provided Issue The abstract does not mention the force field, water model, salt concentration, temperature, or pressure coupling used in the simulations. Required correction Include these details in the methods section of the full manuscript. Concern ID R1-m2 Severity Minor Axis Clarity Affected element Terminology Evidence pointer Abstract; location not provided Issue The term "maturation of the catalytic residue" is used without specifying the chemical nature of the modification, such as conversion of cysteine to formylglycine. Required correction Define the maturation state explicitly in the abstract or the main text. Concern ID R1-m3 Severity Minor Axis Scope Affected element Inhibitor design claim Evidence pointer Abstract; location not provided Issue The proposal for dual-site inhibitors targeting the catalytic pocket and the HD is presented as a perspective, but no binding site analysis or druggability assessment is mentioned. Required correction Clarify that this is a speculative proposal, or add a brief analysis of the HD surface properties to support the suggestion. Concern ID R1-m4 Severity Minor Axis Completeness Affected element Comparison with HSulf-1 Evidence pointer Abstract; location not provided Issue The abstract mentions HSulf-1 in the introduction but does not compare the structural findings for HSulf-2 with any known or predicted features of HSulf-1. Required correction Add a brief comparison or state explicitly that HSulf-1 was not included in this study. Risk / unsupported claims The claim that the HD is the principal source of conformational disorder is unsupported without quantitative disorder metrics. The claim that the HD significantly destabilizes the catalytic framework dynamics is unsupported without statistical testing and convergence evidence. The claim that catalytic residue maturation modulates the conformational landscape without altering overall architecture is unsupported without modeling details and quantitative comparisons. The claim that N-glycan chitobiose cores exert only limited structural effects is unsupported without details on glycan construction and comparative metrics. The claim that the CAT-Cter assembly reproduces the canonical catalytic architecture is unverifiable without structural comparison data. The dual-site inhibitor proposal is speculative and not supported by any binding or druggability analysis in the abstract. The overall reliability of the simulation results cannot be assessed without validation of the AlphaFold2 model and full methodological details.

boundary Claims and evidence presented in the supplied abstract; no full text, figures, tables, or supplementary materials were provided Shared manuscript claim summary The authors apply a previously developed dynamic coarse graining technique based on Markov state modeling to a model peptidic system that unfolds in a non-two-state manner. Using donor-acceptor distances of helical hydrogen bonds as collective variables with dimension reduction, they construct a Markov model that reproduces the microscopic unfolding behavior at moderate pulling velocities. They claim the method is suitable for systems where end-to-end distance is an insufficient order parameter and where unfolding is not cooperative. Visible evidence base Abstract text only; no quantitative results, model validation metrics, simulation parameters, or comparisons with reference methods are provided Missing materials affecting confidence Full manuscript, all figures and tables, simulation protocols, model construction details, validation statistics, and any comparison with experimental or alternative computational results Reviewer Overall assessment The abstract presents a methodologically plausible extension of Markov state modeling to forced unfolding of a peptide with non-two-state behavior. The choice of hydrogen bond donor-acceptor distances as collective variables is physically motivated and addresses a known limitation of end-to-end distance based order parameters. However, the abstract provides no quantitative evidence to support the central claims of correctness, accuracy, or applicability. The claim that the model "correctly represents the microscopic behavior" is unsubstantiated without validation data. The scope of the claim regarding "not too fast pulling velocities" is vague and lacks a defined regime. The work may be of interest to computational biophysicists, but the current evidence base is insufficient to assess technical soundness or significance. Who would be interested in the results, and why Computational biophysicists and physical chemists working on protein folding and mechanical unfolding simulations would be interested. Researchers developing coarse graining and dimensionality reduction methods for biomolecular dynamics would also find relevance. The work addresses a practical gap in applying Markov state models to non-equilibrium forced unfolding, which is a growing area in single molecule force spectroscopy and simulation. Major strengths The methodological framing is clear and addresses a recognized limitation in the field, namely the inadequacy of end-to-end distance as an order parameter for certain unfolding pathways. The choice of hydrogen bond distances as collective variables is physically sensible and likely to capture local structural transitions that global coordinates miss. The explicit acknowledgment of the pulling velocity regime as a limiting factor shows awareness of the method's boundaries. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Evidence sufficiency Claim pointer The abstract claims the Markov model "correctly represents the microscopic behavior of the system for not too fast pulling velocities." Evidence pointer Abstract only; no validation data provided Concern No quantitative evidence is presented to support the claim of correct representation. There are no metrics such as Chapman-Kolmogorov tests, implied timescale plots, or comparisons between model predictions and direct simulation observables. The phrase "correctly represents" is a strong assertion that requires demonstration. Why it matters The central contribution of the paper is the claim that the Markov model faithfully reproduces the unfolding dynamics. Without validation, the method's utility cannot be assessed, and the claim is not established. Resolution test Provide quantitative validation in the full manuscript, including but not limited to Chapman-Kolmogorov consistency checks, comparison of state populations or transition probabilities against direct MD simulations, and error estimates. Specify the range of pulling velocities for which the model is valid and show where it breaks down. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Scope and generalizability Claim pointer The abstract claims the method "can be used to mimic the mechanical unfolding process of systems for which the end-to-end distance does not provide a sufficient order parameter and that do not unfold in a simple cooperative manner." Evidence pointer Abstract only; single model peptide system Concern The claim of general applicability is based on a single example. No evidence is provided that the method transfers to other systems with different secondary structure elements, sizes, or unfolding mechanisms. The choice of hydrogen bond distances as collective variables may be system specific. Why it matters The stated significance of the work depends on its generalizability beyond the specific peptide studied. A single demonstration is insufficient to support a broad methodological claim. Resolution test Either temper the claim to be system specific or provide additional examples or a systematic discussion of the conditions under which the collective variable choice is expected to work. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Reproducibility Claim pointer The abstract describes the use of "an earlier developed dynamic coarse graining technique" and "dimension reduction" without specifying the methods. Evidence pointer Abstract only; no methodological details Concern The abstract does not identify the specific Markov state modeling approach, the dimension reduction technique, or the parameters used. This prevents assessment of reproducibility and comparability with existing methods. Why it matters Reproducibility is a core requirement for computational studies. Without specification of the methods, readers cannot evaluate or replicate the work. Resolution test In the full manuscript, clearly identify the Markov state modeling framework, the dimension reduction algorithm, and all relevant parameters including lag time, number of states, and discretization choices. Required correction Specify the range of pulling velocities tested and the criterion used to determine the validity limit. Required correction Add a brief statement in the abstract or introduction on how the method compares with existing approaches in terms of accuracy or computational cost. Concern ID R1-m3 Severity Minor Axis Terminology Affected element Use of "dynamic coarse graining" Evidence pointer Abstract Issue The term "dynamic coarse graining" is not standard and may confuse readers. Required correction Define the term explicitly on first use or use a more standard terminology such as "kinetic coarse graining" or "Markov state model based coarse graining." Technical failings that need to be addressed before the case is established R1-M1 and R1-M2 are blocking. The absence of validation data for the central claim of correct representation and the overgeneralization from a single system must be resolved before the case is established. Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality The approach of using hydrogen bond distances as collective variables for Markov state modeling of forced unfolding is a reasonable incremental contribution, but the abstract does not demonstrate conceptual novelty beyond existing Markov state model applications. Scientific importance The work addresses a practical limitation in simulating non-two-state unfolding, which is relevant to the field, but the significance is not established without broader demonstration. Interdisciplinary readership The topic is of interest to computational biophysicists and physical chemists, but the abstract is unlikely to attract a broad interdisciplinary audience without clearer implications for experimental single molecule studies. Technical soundness Cannot be assessed from the abstract alone. The lack of validation data and methodological detail prevents evaluation. Readability for nonspecialists The abstract is reasonably clear for a specialist audience but uses jargon such as "dynamic coarse graining" and "Markov state modeling" without sufficient context for nonspecialists. Recommendation posture Currently not established from the provided evidence. The abstract presents a plausible methodological idea, but the central claims of correctness and generalizability are unsupported. I would be supportive if the full manuscript provides quantitative validation, defines the velocity regime, and tempers or substantiates the generalizability claim. Risk / unsupported claims The claim that the Markov model "correctly represents the microscopic behavior" is unsupported without validation data. The claim of general applicability to systems with insufficient end-to-end distance order parameters is unsupported by a single example. The existence of a well-defined "not too fast pulling velocities" regime is asserted but not quantified. The suitability of hydrogen bond donor-acceptor distances as collective variables is plausible but not demonstrated to be optimal or sufficient.

02 一句话总结 本文通过 X 射线晶体学和 1500 ns 分子动力学模拟，证明 HIV 蛋白酶 PRp51 中 11 个远端氨基酸替换与 3 个近端替换协同作用，通过扩大活性位点体积和增加构象动态性直接导致 darunavir 耐药（Ki 上升 1,438 倍），而 GRL142 因更强的活性位点适配仅损失 43 倍活性。 03 研究问题 具体问题 ：HIV 蛋白酶中远离活性位点的氨基酸替换（distal substitutions，传统上称为 minor substitutions）是否以及如何直接导致蛋白酶抑制剂耐药？ 为什么重要 ：临床上 HIV 耐药突变常以「主要突变 + 次要突变」分类，次要突变通常被认为通过补偿性机制（如恢复复制适应性）间接起作用。如果远端替换直接改变活性位点结构，则现有耐药监测和抑制剂设计的策略需要重新审视。 现有方法不足 ：多数研究聚焦于活性位点内直接与抑制剂接触的残基（proximal），对远端替换的结构效应缺乏定量描述；短时程 MD 模拟（纳秒级）难以捕捉构象重排；晶体结构静态快照无法反映动态体积变化。 精确研究问题 ：Can distal amino-acid substitutions in HIV protease directly contribute to inhibitor resistance by expanding the active site volume and altering conformational dynamics, to a degree comparable to proximal substitutions? 04 背景与发展脉络 注：以下脉络主要基于本文引言和讨论的框架，部分经外部核验（标注）。 阶段 代表性方法/事件 优点 局限 本文位置 manuscript text, including Introduction, Results, Discussion, Materials and Methods, and figure legends. Supplementary Information referenced but not provided. Assessment boundary Scientific claims, methodological adequacy, structural interpretation, and consistency of the evidence presented in the manuscript text. No assessment of editorial fit or journal policy. Shared manuscript claim summary The authors report that a highly darunavir-resistant HIV protease variant (PRp51) carrying fourteen amino-acid substitutions, of which eleven are distal to the active site, exhibits resistance to darunavir through concerted structural changes that expand the active site cavity. They further report that the same variant is substantially less resistant to the experimental inhibitor GRL142, and that molecular dynamics simulations and crystallographic analyses support a mechanism in which distal substitutions contribute to resistance as directly as proximal ones. Visible evidence base Enzyme inhibition data (Ki values), antiviral activity data (EC50 values), X-ray crystal structures (PDB IDs 9CTX, 6MKL, 4HLA, 5TYS), molecular dynamics simulations (1500 ns), active site volume calculations, and structural interaction analyses. Missing materials affecting confidence Supplementary Information (including Supplementary Table 1 with crystallographic statistics and Supplementary Figures 1-5) was not provided. Raw MD trajectory data, convergence metrics, and force field validation details are not described in sufficient detail. No statistical analysis of MD population differences is presented. Reviewer Overall assessment The manuscript addresses an important question in HIV drug resistance, namely whether distal amino-acid substitutions contribute mechanistically to protease inhibitor resistance. The authors combine experimental and computational approaches to argue that distal substitutions act concertedly with proximal ones to expand the active site cavity, thereby reducing inhibitor binding. The crystallographic and enzymatic data are valuable, and the comparison between darunavir and GRL142 is informative. However, the central mechanistic claim rests heavily on MD simulation analyses that are presented without adequate statistical treatment, convergence assessment, or validation. The manuscript would be strengthened by a more rigorous quantitative framework and by direct experimental testing of the proposed mechanism. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers in HIV drug resistance, antiviral drug development, and structural virology would be interested. The work also speaks to the broader field of protein engineering and drug design, where understanding how distal mutations affect ligand binding is of general relevance. Clinicians and public health researchers focused on antiretroviral therapy optimization may also find the implications for predicting resistance to darunavir-containing regimens relevant. Major strengths 1. The study addresses a clinically relevant and mechanistically underexplored question. 2. The combination of enzymatic, antiviral, crystallographic, and computational methods is appropriate and potentially powerful. 3. The comparison between two inhibitors with different resistance profiles provides a useful internal control. 4. The crystallographic structures of PRp51 in complex with both inhibitors are valuable resources. 5. The observation that distal substitutions form clusters of van der Waals interactions is interesting and potentially novel. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Statistical rigor of MD analysis Claim pointer The authors claim that MD simulations "unequivocally demonstrate" that the active site of DRV-PRp51 undergoes a larger expansion compared to GRL142-PRp51, and that population differences in inter-residue distances support the proposed mechanism. Evidence pointer Results section, subsection on MD simulation; Figures 4 and 5; Table 3 Concern The population differences reported in Figures 4 and 5 are presented as percentages without any statistical treatment. No error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests are provided. The claim of "unequivocal" demonstration is not supported by the evidence as presented. MD simulations of this length (1500 ns) for a system of this size typically require multiple independent replicates to assess convergence and sampling adequacy. The manuscript does not report whether replicate simulations were performed, nor does it provide any convergence metrics (e.g., RMSD stabilization, block averaging, or autocorrelation analysis). Why it matters The central mechanistic claim of the paper rests on the MD-derived population differences. Without statistical validation, the reader cannot assess whether the observed differences are robust or could arise from insufficient sampling or stochastic variation. This is particularly important given that the differences between DRV-PRp51 and GRL142-PRp51, while directionally consistent, may be within the noise of the simulation method. Resolution test Provide replicate MD simulations (at least three independent runs per system), report convergence metrics, and perform statistical comparison of population distributions (e.g., bootstrap or permutation tests) with appropriate multiple-testing correction. Alternatively, provide a clear justification for why a single long trajectory is sufficient and demonstrate convergence through block analysis. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Causal attribution of resistance to distal substitutions Claim pointer The title and Discussion claim that distal amino-acid substitutions contribute to HIV protease inhibitor resistance "as directly as" proximal substitutions. Evidence pointer Title; Discussion section; Results section, molecular surface analysis Concern The manuscript demonstrates correlation between the presence of distal substitutions and structural changes, but does not establish causation. The PRp51 variant carries fourteen substitutions simultaneously, and the authors do not dissect the individual or combinatorial contributions of distal versus proximal substitutions. The claim of "as directly as" implies a comparable mechanistic role, but no experiment isolates the effect of distal substitutions alone. The molecular surface analysis shows that distal substitutions form clusters, but this is descriptive rather than causal. Why it matters The title makes a strong claim that goes beyond the evidence presented. Without mutagenesis experiments that separate distal from proximal substitutions, or at minimum a computational alanine-scanning or decomposition analysis, the claim of direct equivalence is not established. This overstatement could mislead readers about the mechanistic understanding of resistance. Resolution test Perform site-directed mutagenesis to generate variants with only distal substitutions, only proximal substitutions, and combinations thereof, then measure inhibitor binding and enzymatic activity. Alternatively, perform computational free energy decomposition or perturbation analysis to quantify the individual contributions of each substitution to the resistance phenotype. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Quantitative link between structural changes and resistance Claim pointer The authors state that the larger active site expansion in DRV-PRp51 "must be contributing to the loss of binding affinity" and that this explains the resistance phenotype. Evidence pointer Discussion section; Results section, active site volume calculations Concern The manuscript does not provide a quantitative relationship between the measured active site volume changes and the observed Ki or EC50 changes. The volume increase of 36.7 Å3 (8.2%) for DRV-PRp51 is presented as mechanistically significant, but no calculation or simulation links this volume change to a predicted binding free energy change. The claim that this "must be contributing" is an inference without quantitative support. Why it matters Without a quantitative link, the mechanistic narrative remains qualitative. The field would benefit from a testable prediction, such as a calculated binding free energy change that can be compared to the experimentally measured Ki values. This would strengthen the causal argument and provide a framework for predicting resistance to other inhibitors. Resolution test Perform binding free energy calculations (e.g., MM-PBSA, FEP, or TI) for DRV and GRL142 against PRwt and PRp51, and compare the calculated differences to the experimentally measured Ki fold-changes. Alternatively, correlate the active site volume changes with binding affinity changes across a panel of inhibitors. Concern ID R1-M4 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Generalizability of the conclusion Claim pointer The Discussion suggests that the findings warrant reexamination of distal substitutions in other HIV drug targets and other therapeutic areas. Evidence pointer Discussion section, final paragraph Concern The study examines a single protease variant (PRp51) and two inhibitors. The claim that distal substitutions generally contribute "as directly as" proximal substitutions across other targets and therapeutic areas is an extrapolation beyond the data. While the authors appropriately frame this as a suggestion for future work, the title and abstract may be read as making a broader claim than the evidence supports. Why it matters Overgeneralization could lead to inappropriate assumptions in drug development programs. The field needs more examples across different targets and inhibitor classes before such a general principle can be established. Resolution test Soften the title and abstract claims to reflect the specific system studied, or provide additional data from other protease variants or inhibitor classes to support the general claim. Minor Comments Concern ID R1-m1 Severity Minor Axis Clarity of crystallographic analysis Affected element Results section, structural analysis Evidence pointer Figure 2; Supplementary Figure 1 Issue The description of structural differences between PRwt and PRp51 complexes focuses on side-chain conformations but does not provide quantitative measures such as RMSD values for the full structures or for the substituted residues specifically. The statement that "secondary structures aligned well" is qualitative. Required correction Provide RMSD values for backbone and side-chain atoms, and consider reporting per-residue RMSD or displacement values for the fourteen substituted positions. Concern ID R1-m2 Severity Minor Axis Completeness of methods for MD simulations Affected element Materials and Methods, MD simulation section Evidence pointer Materials and Methods section Issue The description of the MD simulation protocol is brief. Key parameters such as temperature coupling method, pressure coupling, barostat, long-range electrostatics treatment, and the specific version of the OPLS3 force field are not fully specified. The equilibration protocol is described only as "minimized and equilibrated" without details. Required correction Provide a complete description of the simulation protocol including thermostat/barostat parameters, equilibration steps, and any restraints applied during equilibration. This is essential for reproducibility. Concern ID R1-m3 Severity Minor Axis Presentation of active site volume calculations Affected element Results section, active site volumes Evidence pointer Figure 5 Issue The active site volume calculations are presented as single values from the crystal structures and as distributions from MD. The method for defining the active site boundary for volume calculation is not described, and the sensitivity of the results to this definition is not assessed. Required correction Describe the active site definition used by the Schrödinger script, and ideally report volumes with different probe radii or active site definitions to demonstrate robustness. Concern ID R1-m4 Severity Minor Axis Consistency of terminology Affected element Throughout Evidence pointer Title; Introduction; Discussion Issue The terms "major" and "minor" substitutions are used in the Introduction to describe the traditional classification, but the manuscript does not clearly define which of the fourteen substitutions in PRp51 are considered major versus minor beyond the statement that three are proximal and eleven are distal. The relationship between the proximal/distal classification and the major/minor classification is not explicitly stated. Required correction Clarify the classification of each of the fourteen substitutions as major or minor, and explicitly state whether the proximal/distal distinction used in the title corresponds to the major/minor classification. Concern ID R1-m5 Severity Minor Axis Figure quality and accessibility Affected element Figures 1-5 Evidence pointer Figure legends Issue The figure legends are descriptive but do not always state the number of replicates or the statistical treatment (where applicable). Figure 4 panels g-h are referenced in the text but the description of what is shown is brief. Required correction Ensure all figure legends state sample sizes, replicate numbers, and any statistical tests performed. Expand the legend for Figure 4 to clearly describe all panels. Technical failings that need to be addressed before the case is established 1. Lack of statistical treatment of MD population differences (R1-M1). 2. Absence of experimental or computational dissection of distal versus proximal substitution contributions (R1-M2). 3. No quantitative link between structural changes and binding affinity changes (R1-M3). 4. Incomplete reporting of MD simulation parameters for reproducibility (R1-m2). 5. Unclear definition of active site boundary for volume calculations (R1-m3). Risk / unsupported claims The claim that distal substitutions contribute "as directly as" proximal substitutions is not supported by the experimental design, which does not isolate the effects of each class of substitution. The statement that MD simulations "unequivocally demonstrate" active site expansion is unsupported without statistical analysis and convergence assessment. The inference that active site expansion "must be contributing" to loss of binding affinity is presented without quantitative support. The suggestion that findings warrant reexamination of distal substitutions in other targets and therapeutic areas is an extrapolation beyond the data presented. The claim that the study "presents a simple and intuitive explanation" for the role of distal substitutions is not fully justified given the complexity of the system and the lack of causal experiments.

blot、共聚焦显微镜）验证计算预测，同时探索药理学伴侣（pharmacochaperone）对突变蛋白折叠和运输的挽救机制。该文展示了AI预测与实验验证相结合的工作流程，对蛋白质结构-功能关系研究和基于结构的治疗策略开发具有参考价值。 02 一句话总结 本文通过AI结构预测工具和细胞实验相结合的方法，鉴定了一个新的SLC6A1错义突变（A357T）导致GABA转运蛋白1（GAT-1）稳定性下降、内质网滞留增加和GABA摄取功能降低，并证明4-苯基丁酸（4-phenylbutyrate, PBA）通过药理学伴侣机制恢复突变蛋白的折叠、成熟和功能。 03 研究问题 具体问题 : 新发现的SLC6A1基因A357T突变（c.1069G>A）是否致病？其分子机制是什么？是否可被药理学伴侣挽救？ 重要性 : SLC6A1编码GABA转运蛋白GAT-1，是维持中枢神经系统兴奋-抑制平衡的关键分子。SLC6A1突变与多种癫痫综合征和神经发育障碍相关。该突变在两个兄弟姐妹中表现为发育性癫痫性脑病（DEE），但为意义未明变异（VUS），需要功能验证以确定致病性并指导治疗。 现有方法不足 : 单纯依赖AI预测工具无法确定突变的功能后果；而实验验证每个突变成本高、周期长。需要建立AI预测与实验验证相结合的高效工作流程。 精确研究问题 : 能否通过AI结构预测与细胞功能实验相结合的方式，确定SLC6A1(A357T)突变的致病性、阐明其分子机制，并评估药理学伴侣PBA的治疗潜力？ 04 背景与发展脉络 （标注：此脉络基于本文引言及讨论，经外部核验部分已注明） 阶段 代表性方法/发现 利用多种AI结构预测工具（DynaMut2、mCSM、SDM、DUET、I-Mutant、MUpro、INPS、MAESTROweb）评估A357T和A357V突变对GAT-1蛋白稳定性的影响，然后在HEK293T细胞、人iPSC来源的星形胶质细胞和皮层神经元中过表达野生型或突变型GAT-1，通过³H-GABA摄取实验、Western blot和共聚焦显微镜表征突变蛋白的功能、表达和亚细胞定位，最后用PBA、TUDCA、丁酸盐和SAHA处理，评估对突变蛋白功能的挽救效果。 2) 核心洞察 AI预测与实验结果的强相关性 ：所有AI工具一致预测A357T比A357V更显著地降低蛋白稳定性（平均ΔΔG：-1.4 vs -0.5 kcal/mol），实验证实A357T的GABA摄取功能丧失更严重（17.25% vs 37%），表明AI预测可作为突变严重程度分层的有效工具。 药理学伴侣是PBA挽救的主要机制 ：通过比较PBA（化学伴侣+HDAC抑制剂）与丁酸盐/SAHA（纯HDAC抑制剂）的效果，发现PBA和TUDCA（纯化学伴侣）均能显著恢复GABA摄取，而HDAC抑制剂效果不稳定，证明PBA主要通过药理学伴侣机制发挥作用。 WT/mutant共表达揭示显性负效应 ：在模拟患者杂合状态的共表达条件下，突变蛋白增加了野生型GAT-1的未成熟形式，提示突变蛋白可能通过干扰野生型蛋白的折叠/运输产生显性负效应，这为理解常染色体显性遗传机制提供了新视角。 3) 可能的普适教训 [Analysis] AI预测工具的多模型共识比单一模型更可靠 ：本文使用8种工具，所有工具均预测稳定性降低，但幅度差异大（DUET预测-3.4 kcal/mol，其他工具预测范围更小），多工具共识可增强结论的鲁棒性。 计算预测与功能实验的"双向验证"模式 ：AI预测指导实验设计（选择哪些突变做功能验证），实验结果反过来校准AI预测的可靠性，这种闭环可推广到其他膜蛋白突变研究。 区分药理学伴侣与HDAC抑制的贡献 ：对于具有多重活性的候选药物，通过比较结构类似但机制不同的化合物，可以解析其主要作用机制，这一策略适用于其他"老药新用"研究。 非端到端。AI预测仅用于评估稳定性变化，功能验证完全依赖实验。AI预测与实验之间无自动闭环。 算力成本 : 未提供。AI工具均为轻量级预测工具，计算成本低。 历史数据依赖 : 中。AI工具的预测基于已知蛋白结构数据库和突变效应数据库，对GAT-1这类膜转运蛋白的预测精度可能受限于训练数据中膜蛋白的代表性。 模型依赖 : 高。不同AI工具预测的ΔΔG绝对值差异大（如DUET预测-3.4 Assessment boundary Scientific content, experimental design, data interpretation, and claims as presented in the provided text. Statistical reporting and figure quality assessed only insofar as described in the text. Shared manuscript claim summary The authors report a novel SLC6A1 variant (c.1069G>A, p.A357T) identified in two siblings with developmental epileptic encephalopathies (DEEs). They characterize clinical phenotypes, use AI-based structural prediction tools to assess protein stability, and perform functional assays (3H-GABA uptake, Western blot, confocal microscopy) in HEK293T cells and human iPSC-derived astrocytes and neurons. They report that the A357T variant reduces GABA uptake, increases ER retention, and that pharmacochaperones (PBA, TUDCA) or genetic upregulation of ER chaperones (BiP, calnexin) rescue function. Visible evidence base Results sections describing clinical data (Fig. 1), AI predictions (Fig. 2), GABA uptake assays (Fig. 3), Western blot analyses (Fig. 4), confocal microscopy (Fig. 5), and pharmacological/genetic rescue experiments (Fig. 6). Figure legends are present but actual figure images are not available for inspection. Missing materials affecting confidence Actual figure images and full figure legends with statistical annotations; supplementary tables (including clinical data in Supplementary Table 1); detailed experimental protocols; raw data and statistical outputs; information on biological replicates beyond "n = 5-8 transfections"; details on iPSC line validation and differentiation quality control; information on whether experiments were blinded or randomized. Reviewer Overall assessment This manuscript addresses a clinically relevant question: functional characterization of a novel SLC6A1 variant and evaluation of pharmacochaperone-based rescue. The clinical description of two siblings with the same variant is valuable, and the combination of AI-based prediction with experimental validation is a reasonable approach. However, several technical concerns limit the strength of the conclusions. The mechanistic claims regarding pharmacochaperone versus HDAC inhibition are not fully supported by the data presented, and the quantification methods for confocal microscopy and Western blots are described with insufficient detail. The study is potentially of interest to the epilepsy and neurogenetics community, but the current evidence does not fully establish the central claims. Who would be interested in the results, and why Clinicians and researchers in epilepsy genetics, neurodevelopmental disorders, and GABAergic neurotransmission. The study adds a new variant to the SLC6A1 mutation spectrum and provides preliminary evidence for a potential therapeutic strategy (pharmacochaperones) that could be relevant for personalized medicine approaches in SLC6A1-related disorders. Major strengths 1) Clinical characterization of two siblings with the same variant, including EEG data and neuropsychiatric comorbidities, is a useful addition to the literature. 2) The combination of AI-based structural prediction with experimental validation is a modern and potentially efficient approach. 3) The study addresses a clinically actionable question: whether pharmacochaperones can rescue mutant GAT-1 function. 4) The use of multiple cell types (HEK293T, iPSC-derived astrocytes and neurons) strengthens the translational relevance. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Experimental design and controls Claim pointer The authors claim that PBA and TUDCA restore GABA uptake via pharmacochaperoning, while HDAC inhibitors (butyrate, SAHA) show inconsistent effects, supporting a pharmacochaperone mechanism. Evidence pointer Figure 6A-B; Results section "The impaired GABA uptake in the mutant protein was restored by pharmacological or genetic upregulation of chaperones in the ER" Concern The comparison between PBA/TUDCA (pharmacochaperones) and butyrate/SAHA (HDAC inhibitors) is presented as evidence for a pharmacochaperone mechanism. However, the text states that butyrate and SAHA "exhibited inconsistent increase of GABA uptake." This is ambiguous. Were these effects statistically significant or not? The lack of clear statistical reporting for these comparisons makes it impossible to evaluate whether the distinction between pharmacochaperone and HDAC inhibitor effects is robust. Furthermore, PBA is known to have both pharmacochaperone and HDAC inhibitory activities, so the claim that the effect is "likely contributed by its pharmacochaperoning effect" is not directly tested. A more rigorous approach would include a specific HDAC inhibitor that does not have chaperone activity at the concentrations used, or genetic knockdown of HDACs. Why it matters The central mechanistic claim of the paper is that pharmacochaperoning, not HDAC inhibition, underlies the rescue. If this distinction is not clearly demonstrated, the mechanistic conclusion is not supported, and the therapeutic rationale for using PBA specifically as a pharmacochaperone is weakened. Resolution test Provide complete statistical analysis for all drug treatment conditions, including effect sizes, confidence intervals, and p-values for pairwise comparisons. Include a dose-response experiment with a selective HDAC inhibitor (e.g., vorinostat) to determine whether HDAC inhibition alone can rescue GABA uptake. Alternatively, use a pharmacochaperone that lacks HDAC inhibitory activity to directly test the pharmacochaperone hypothesis. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Data quantification and reproducibility Claim pointer The authors claim that the A357T mutant has increased ER retention compared to wild-type, and that PBA reduces this retention (Figure 5). Evidence pointer Figure 5A-C; Results section "GAT-1(A357T) mutant protein had increased endoplasmic reticulum retention while PBA can reduce the ER retained GAT-1 protein" Concern The quantification of ER retention is based on colocalization of GAT-1-YFP with an ER marker (ERCFP). The methods state that "the percent fluorescence signal of GAT-1 overlapping with ER marker ERCFP was higher in the mutant" but the details of the colocalization analysis are not provided. What threshold was used for colocalization? Was Manders' or Pearson's coefficient used? How many cells were analyzed per condition? The statement that "cells expressing mutant GAT-1 exhibited a more rounded morphology" is subjective and not quantified. Additionally, the authors acknowledge that "direct surface labeling was not performed," which is a significant limitation given that the claim is about impaired trafficking to the plasma membrane. Why it matters ER retention is a key mechanistic claim linking the mutation to reduced function. Without rigorous, quantitative colocalization analysis and ideally surface biotinylation or surface staining, the evidence for ER retention is circumstantial. The functional data (reduced GABA uptake) are consistent with reduced surface expression, but the direct evidence is lacking. Resolution test Provide detailed colocalization analysis parameters, including the coefficient used, thresholds, and number of cells/fields analyzed. Perform surface biotinylation or immunofluorescence without permeabilization to directly quantify surface versus intracellular GAT-1. Quantify cell morphology using a defined metric (e.g., circularity index). Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Statistical analysis and data presentation Claim pointer The authors report that GABA uptake in A357T is reduced to 17.25% of wild-type in HEK293T cells, 39.86% in astrocytes, and 31% in neurons (Figure 3). Evidence pointer Figure 3A-C; Results section "GAT-1(A357T) and GAT-1(A357V) had impaired GABA reuptake in HEK293T, human iPSC-derived astrocytes, and neurons overexpressing the mutant GAT-1" Concern The statistical analysis for the GABA uptake data is not described in sufficient detail. The figure legend mentions "n = 7-8 different transfections" and use of ANOVA with Newman-Keuls test, but it is unclear whether each transfection represents an independent biological replicate or a technical replicate. The variability between experiments is not shown (no error bars described in the text). Additionally, the normalization to wild-type (100%) without showing the raw uptake values makes it difficult to assess the biological significance of the differences. The comparison to the GAT-1 inhibitor Cl-966 is mentioned but not shown in the text description. Why it matters The functional assay is the primary outcome measure. Without clear reporting of variability and statistical rigor, the reliability of the quantitative claims cannot be assessed. Resolution test Provide raw data (or at least mean ± SEM with individual data points) for all uptake experiments. Clarify the definition of n (biological vs. technical replicates). Report the results of the Cl-966 control experiments. Consider showing data as scatter plots with overlaid means. Concern ID R1-M4 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Clinical-genetic correlation Claim pointer The authors state that the variant was "not identified in the shared parents, suggesting gonadal mosaicism." Evidence pointer Figure 1B; Results section "Mutation analysis identified SLC6A1(A357V) variation in two siblings" Concern The claim of gonadal mosaicism is inferred from the absence of the variant in parental saliva samples. However, the possibility of germline mosaicism in one parent cannot be distinguished from other mechanisms (e.g., somatic mosaicism in the parents not detected in saliva, or de novo occurrence in both siblings which is extremely unlikely but not impossible). The text does not mention whether parental samples were tested with sufficient sensitivity (e.g., deep sequencing) to exclude low-level mosaicism. Additionally, the variant is described as "novel" but no information is provided on its frequency in population databases (e.g., gnomAD) or on in silico pathogenicity predictions beyond the stability tools used. Why it matters Accurate genetic counseling depends on understanding the inheritance pattern. The distinction between gonadal mosaicism and other mechanisms has implications for recurrence risk. Resolution test Provide details on the sequencing depth and methodology used for parental testing. If possible, test parental samples with a more sensitive method (e.g., amplicon-based deep sequencing) to exclude low-level mosaicism. Report the variant frequency in gnomAD and any ACMG/AMP classification. 如何在超大规模化学空间（数千万至数百亿分子）中高效发现 SARS-CoV-2 NSP3 Mac1 的新型中性（非带电）抑制剂骨架？ 为什么重要 : Mac1 是 SARS-CoV-2 免疫逃逸的关键毒力因子，其活性位点失活可使病毒在小鼠模型中减毒。中性抑制剂有望克服此前阴离子抑制剂细胞通透性差的瓶颈，为抗病毒药物开发提供新起点。 现有方法为何不足 : 传统 docking 对超大规模库的计算成本过高；基于片段的筛选需要大量晶体学工作；生成式方法在 Mac1 这类极性、浅口袋上的成功率有限。CACHE3 挑战赛各参与者的总体命中率仅 1.8%，说明该靶点的计算可处理性（computational tractability）较低。 精确研究问题 : Can a machine learning-augmented virtual screening workflow (Deep Docking) applied to a diverse subset of an ultra-large chemical library identify novel, neutral, crystallographically-validated inhibitors of SARS-CoV-2 NSP3 Mac1? 04 背景与发展脉络 docking 引擎，对 Enamine REAL Diversity Subset（2300 万分子）进行迭代筛选。每轮 docking 少量分子（5 万），训练一个二分类器（基于 Morgan 指纹）预测剩余库中分子的 docking score 是否优于阈值，逐步修剪低分分子。最终保留约 650 万分子，再以 Glide SP 全量 docking，经 ICM 重打分、RMSD 共识过滤、视觉检查，选出 83 个化合物进行实验测试。 核心洞察 : - 多样性子集 + 主动学习 ：与其直接处理全库，不如先在一个代表性、结构多样的子集上训练，利用主动学习迭代修剪，以极小计算量保留绝大多数高分分子。 - 共识策略优于单一打分 ：Glide 与 ICM 两种 docking 程序 + RMSD 一致性过滤 + 人工视觉检查，可有效降低假阳性。 - 结构验证闭环 ：X 射线晶体学不仅确认结合，还揭示了 Phe132 的构象变化（closed → everted），为后续优化提供结构基础。 可能的普适教训 [Analysis]: - 对「难」靶点（极性、浅、柔性口袋），单一计算方法的命中率天然有限， 多方法共识 + 人工专家干预 仍是必要的质量控制环节。 - 主动学习在 分子多样性高 的库上修剪效率会下降（本文中 reduction power 仅 3.5 倍，远低于全库场景），说明该方法更适合结构冗余的全库而非多样性子集。 - 结构生物学反馈（晶体结构）不仅用于验证，更能揭示 docking 模型未预测到的构象变化，是改进打分模型的重要数据来源。 07 方法总览 输入 : 靶标结构：PDB 5SRY（LRH-0003-Mac1 复合物，1.05 Å） 配体库：Enamine REAL Diversity Subset（约 8000 万分子，过滤后
