They report one confirmed hit (CACHE3-HI_1706_56) with a KD of 20 µM by SPR, a crystal structure confirming the binding mode, and a subsequent analogue expansion in the REAL Space (44 billion compounds) yielding a series with improved affinities (best KD 12 µM). The work was part of the CACHE3 challenge, which the authors state they won. Visible evidence base Main text figures (Fig. 1-4), methods sections (protein preparation, docking, HTRF, SPR, crystallography), results narrative, Table 1 (referenced, not shown in text), Supplementary Figures 1-4 and Supplementary Tables 1 (referenced, not shown in text) Missing materials affecting confidence Supplementary figures and tables (including dose-response curves, SPR sensorgrams, crystallographic statistics, full analogue table), crystallographic data deposition identifiers, PDB accession codes for the new structure, raw HTRF data, compound synthesis details, and the full CACHE3 challenge results for comparison Reviewer Overall assessment The manuscript describes a technically competent application of an established machine learning-accelerated virtual screening approach to a relevant antiviral target. The work is clearly presented and the experimental validation is appropriate in scope. However, the scientific advance over existing literature is modest, as the target has been extensively studied and multiple inhibitor series already exist. The single confirmed hit with micromolar affinity, while validated crystallographically, represents a limited demonstration of the workflow's utility. The analogue expansion is a strength, but the lack of cellular data limits the translational significance. The manuscript would benefit from clearer contextualization of the novelty relative to prior Mac1 inhibitor discovery efforts and a more critical discussion of the limitations of the screening approach. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers in computational drug discovery, particularly those working on machine learning-accelerated virtual screening methods, will find the workflow description and its prospective validation of interest. The structural biology community studying SARS-CoV-2 proteins may also find the new Mac1-ligand crystal structure useful. Medicinal chemists working on antiviral development may be interested in the new chemical series as a starting point, though the micromolar potency and lack of cellular data limit immediate therapeutic relevance. Major strengths 1) Prospective validation of a machine learning-accelerated screening workflow in a blinded challenge setting (CACHE3), which provides an unbiased assessment of method performance. 2) High-quality crystallographic confirmation of the binding mode, including the observation of a Phe132 conformational change, which provides structural insight into Mac1 plasticity. 3) The analogue expansion strategy using the REAL Space database is a practical demonstration of how to efficiently explore ultra-large chemical spaces. 4) Clear and concise writing with appropriate methodological detail for reproducibility. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Scientific significance / novelty Claim pointer The authors claim that their workflow "enabled to discover novel Mac1 inhibitor chemotypes" and that the identified series represents "a structurally distinct example within the pyrrolidinone-based Mac1 inhibitor series." Evidence pointer Results section "Discovery and characterization of a novel Mac1 inhibitor scaffold"; Conclusions Concern The novelty of the identified scaffold is not sufficiently established. The authors acknowledge that the pyrrolopyrimidine group has been "frequently observed among previously reported Mac1 inhibitors" and that prior neutral inhibitors exist (e.g., LRH-0003). The distinction claimed is based on the bromine substitution and carboxamide group, but the manuscript does not provide a comprehensive comparison with previously reported Mac1 inhibitors to demonstrate that this specific combination is genuinely novel. Furthermore, the micromolar affinity (KD 20 µM) is modest compared to existing inhibitors, and the authors do not discuss whether this scaffold offers any advantage over previously reported series in terms of potency, selectivity, or drug-likeness. Why it matters The central claim of the manuscript is the discovery of a novel inhibitor chemotype. If the scaffold is not sufficiently distinct from known inhibitors, or if it does not offer a clear advantage, the scientific significance of the work is substantially diminished. The CACHE3 challenge context implies that the workflow should identify novel, useful starting points, and this needs to be demonstrated more rigorously. Resolution test The authors should provide a systematic comparison of CACHE3-HI_1706_56 and its analogues with all previously reported Mac1 inhibitors, including structural overlays, potency comparisons, and physicochemical property assessments. If the scaffold is genuinely novel, this analysis should clearly demonstrate distinct structural features and a favorable profile. If not, the claims of novelty should be tempered. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Technical soundness / data completeness Claim pointer The authors state that "12 were confirmed as NSP3 Mac1 binders via SPR" and report KD values for several analogues in Table 1 and Figure 4. Evidence pointer Results section "Chemical series expansion in the REAL space"; Table 1 (referenced); Supplementary Figures 3 and 4 (referenced) Concern The SPR data supporting the KD values are not shown in the main text. The authors reference Supplementary Figures 3 and 4, but these are not available for review. Given that SPR is the primary quantitative binding assay, the quality of the sensorgrams, the fitting models used, and the reproducibility of the measurements are critical for assessing the reliability of the reported affinities. Additionally, the manuscript does not specify how many independent replicates were performed, what the error bars represent, or whether the binding was reversible. The steady-state affinity model mentioned in the methods may not be appropriate for all binding kinetics, particularly if association or dissociation rates are slow. Why it matters The reported KD values are the key quantitative output of the study and form the basis for the structure-activity relationships discussed. If the SPR data are not robust, the conclusions about which analogues are most potent and the rationale for the chemical series expansion are undermined. Resolution test The authors should provide representative SPR sensorgrams and fitting curves for all reported compounds, including the negative control (PARP14), in the main text or a clearly accessible supplementary file. They should also specify the number of replicates, the error calculation method, and the criteria for data inclusion/exclusion. If steady-state fitting was used, justification for this choice over kinetic fitting should be provided. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Technical soundness / methodological rigor Claim pointer The authors state that "the crystal structure of CACHE3_HI_1706_56 bound to Mac1 was solved to a resolution of 1.02 Å" and that the ligand occupancy was 26%. Evidence pointer Results section "Discovery and characterization of a novel Mac1 inhibitor scaffold"; Figure 3d; Supplementary Figure 2 (referenced) Concern The low ligand occupancy (26%) raises concerns about the reliability of the structural interpretation. While the authors acknowledge this and provide a plausible explanation (conformational change of the Phe132 loop), the manuscript does not provide details on how the occupancy was refined, what the estimated standard uncertainty is, or whether alternative interpretations (e.g., partial occupancy at multiple sites, ligand disorder) were considered. The electron density maps are only shown in the supplementary material, which is not available for review. The claim that the binding mode is "confirmed" by crystallography may be overstated given the low occupancy. Why it matters The crystal structure is a key piece of evidence supporting the docking predictions and the proposed binding mode. If the structural interpretation is not robust, the basis for the analogue design and the understanding of the structure-activity relationships is weakened. Resolution test The authors should provide the electron density maps (2Fo-Fc and Fo-Fc) for the ligand and surrounding residues in the main text or a clearly accessible supplementary file, along with details of the occupancy refinement and validation metrics (e.g., real-space correlation coefficient). They should also discuss the limitations of interpreting a structure with 26% occupancy and consider whether the docking predictions are still valid given the observed conformational change. Concern ID R1-M4 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Scientific significance / contextualization Claim pointer The authors state that their workflow "demonstrated competitive performance in the prospective CACHE3 challenge against a range of alternative screening methods, including fragment-based, generative, and deep learning workflows." Evidence pointer Conclusions; Introduction (CACHE3 description) Concern The manuscript does not provide any quantitative comparison with other CACHE3 participants' results. The authors mention that they won the challenge, but no details are given about the evaluation criteria, the performance metrics, or how their results compared to other methods. Without this context, the claim of "competitive performance" is not substantiated. Additionally, the authors do not discuss what aspects of their workflow contributed to its success or what limitations were revealed by the challenge. Why it matters The CACHE3 challenge is a key part of the manuscript's significance, as it provides a prospective, blinded evaluation of the workflow. A detailed comparison with other methods would help readers understand the strengths and weaknesses of the approach and its generalizability to other targets. Resolution test The authors should provide a summary of the CACHE3 challenge results, including the evaluation criteria, the performance of their workflow relative to other participants, and a discussion of the factors that contributed to their success. If this information is confidential, they should state this explicitly and temper their claims accordingly. Minor Comments Concern ID R1-m1 Severity Minor Axis Clarity / reproducibility Affected element Methods section "Small molecule library preparation" Evidence pointer Materials and methods Issue The description of the library preparation is incomplete. The authors state that the SMILES of 43,759,934 compounds were downloaded, but then refer to a "resulting dataset of 80 million molecules" after applying filters. The relationship between these two numbers is unclear. Additionally, the CACHE3 'hit-like' filter is referenced but not described in detail. Required correction Clarify the relationship between the initial download and the filtered dataset. Provide a detailed description of the CACHE3 'hit-like' filter criteria, either in the main text or by referencing a public source. Concern ID R1-m2 Severity Minor Axis Clarity / data presentation Affected element Figure 3 and Figure 4 Evidence pointer Figure legends Issue The figure legends are incomplete. Figure 3 does not describe the SPR data shown in panel (b), and Figure 4 does not describe the SPR data shown in panels (b) and (c). The legends also do not specify the error bars or the number of replicates. Required correction Expand the figure legends to fully describe all panels, including the assay conditions, the data representation (e.g., mean ± SD), and the number of independent experiments. Concern ID R1-m3 Severity Minor Axis Technical soundness / assay details Affected element Methods section "Homogeneous time-resolved fluorescence (HTRF)" Evidence pointer Materials and methods Issue The HTRF assay description is brief. The authors do not specify the concentration of the ADP-ribose peptide used, the peptide sequence beyond the abbreviated notation, or the positive/negative controls used. The statement that "Compounds were dispensed into ProxiPlate-384 Plus assay plates using an Echo 650 acoustic liquid handler" does not specify the compound concentration range tested. Required correction Provide full details of the HTRF assay, including the peptide sequence, concentrations of all reagents, the compound concentration range, and the controls used. This is essential for reproducibility. Concern ID R1-m4 Severity Minor Axis Clarity / terminology Affected element Results section "Discovery and characterization of a novel Mac1 inhibitor scaffold" Evidence pointer Figure 3d and accompanying text Issue The text refers to "Phe132 (P132_d)" and "P132_c" without defining these terms. The distinction between the "closed" and "everted" conformations is described, but the notation is confusing. Required correction Define the notation (e.g., "d" for "down" and "c" for "closed" or similar) and use consistent terminology throughout the text and figures. Concern ID R1-m5 Severity Minor Axis Clarity / data presentation Affected element Table 1 Evidence pointer Table 1 (referenced, not shown in text) Issue Table 1 is referenced but not included in the manuscript text. The reader cannot assess the structure-activity relationships without seeing the full table. Required correction Include Table 1 in the main text or provide a summary of the key data points in the text. If the table is too large, consider moving it to the main text as a condensed version. Technical failings that need to be addressed before the case is established R1-M1 (novelty claim not substantiated), R1-M2 (SPR data not shown), R1-M3 (crystallographic occupancy concerns) Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality The application of Deep Learning-accelerated virtual screening to Mac1 is not entirely novel, as similar approaches have been applied to other targets. The specific combination of Deep Docking with consensus scoring and analogue expansion in the REAL Space is a reasonable workflow, but the individual components are established. The crystallographic observation of the Phe132 conformational change is a useful contribution, though its significance is limited by the low ligand occupancy. Scientific importance The target (SARS-CoV-2 Mac1) is of high relevance, and the need for novel antiviral agents remains. However, the identified inhibitors have only micromolar affinity and no cellular activity data, limiting their immediate therapeutic significance. The work is more relevant as a methodological demonstration than as a direct contribution to antiviral drug development. Interdisciplinary readership The manuscript will appeal to computational chemists, structural biologists, and virologists. The methods are described in sufficient detail for computational specialists, and the biological context is clearly explained. However, the lack of cellular data may limit interest from a broader biomedical audience. Technical soundness The computational workflow is technically sound, and the experimental validation is appropriate. However, the incomplete presentation of SPR data and the low crystallographic occupancy are concerns that need to be addressed. The manuscript would benefit from more rigorous statistical analysis of the screening results and a clearer discussion of the limitations of the approach. Readability for nonspecialists The manuscript is generally well-written and accessible. The introduction provides adequate context, and the figures are clear. However, some methodological details (e.g., Deep Docking parameters, consensus scoring) may be challenging for nonspecialists. The authors should consider adding a brief explanation of the machine learning approach for a general audience. Recommendation posture Supportive if technical concerns are resolved. The manuscript describes a competent application of a useful computational workflow with experimental validation. However, the novelty claim needs to be substantiated with a more thorough comparison to existing Mac1 inhibitors, and the SPR and crystallographic data need to be presented more completely. If these issues are addressed, the manuscript would be suitable for publication in a specialized journal.

：本文不直接涉及蛋白质结构计算，但提出了一种通用的「结构化重解码」方法，可扩展预训练模型的决策空间。该思想可迁移至蛋白质结构预测/生成任务中，用于在已有模型（如 AlphaFold、ESMFold）基础上通过结构化约束重新解码，扩展构象采样空间或改进序列-结构映射。 02 一句话总结 本文提出一种名为「结构化重解码」的通用推理框架，通过对预训练模型的解码过程施加结构化约束并重新解码，在不重新训练模型的前提下扩展其决策空间，从而提升模型在多种任务上的表现。 03 研究问题 具体问题 ：预训练模型在推理时受限于其固定的解码策略和决策空间，难以在已有知识基础上探索更优或更多样的输出。如何在不重新训练的情况下扩展预训练模型的决策空间？ 为什么重要 ：预训练模型（如 Assessment boundary Claims and evidence presented in the abstract, with reference to the linked repository as a supporting resource Shared manuscript claim summary The authors introduce sparse autoencoders (SAEs) into ProteinMPNN to expand its latent space, uncover correlations between sparse activations and protein features (secondary structure, residue volume, residue shape, disulfide bridges, ligand coordination), and demonstrate that manipulating sparse activations yields a Brolucizumab variant with improved thermostability relative to variants from traditional machine learning methods, as assessed by high temperature molecular dynamics simulations. Visible evidence base Abstract text; repository URL (https://github.com/neelmukkavilli/SAEProteinMPNN) mentioned but not inspected Missing materials affecting confidence Full manuscript text, all figures and tables, methods descriptions, quantitative results, statistical analyses, and simulation details are not provided. The repository is referenced but its contents were not available for review. Reviewer Overall assessment The abstract presents an ambitious and potentially valuable application of sparse autoencoders to a widely used protein design model. The core idea, that SAEs can render polysemantic activations in ProteinMPNN more interpretable and manipulable, is timely and of broad interest. However, the abstract alone provides insufficient evidence to evaluate the validity of the central claims. Key quantitative outcomes, methodological details, and validation procedures are absent. The claim of improved thermostability over traditional methods is particularly consequential and cannot be assessed without detailed simulation protocols and comparative baselines. The work is promising in concept but the case is not established from the supplied material. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers in protein design, machine learning interpretability, and computational biology would be interested. The work addresses a recognized limitation of black-box protein sequence models and proposes a concrete interpretability tool. Those developing or using ProteinMPNN and related models would value mechanistic insights and a pathway to targeted sequence modification. The thermostability application is relevant to therapeutic protein engineering, particularly for antibody fragments. Major strengths The choice of ProteinMPNN as a target is well motivated given its widespread adoption. The use of SAEs is a current and technically appropriate approach for addressing polysemanticity. The abstract identifies a specific set of protein features for correlation analysis, which provides a concrete framework for interpretability. The demonstration of a practical application, thermostability improvement, elevates the work beyond descriptive analysis. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Evidence sufficiency Claim pointer The authors claim that sparse activations can be manipulated to produce a Brolucizumab variant that is more thermostable than variants produced by traditional machine learning methods. Evidence pointer Abstract, thermostability statement; location not provided Concern The abstract states that the SAE-derived variant is more thermostable than variants from traditional machine learning methods, but no quantitative data, simulation parameters, or comparative statistics are provided. The basis for this comparison is unclear, including which traditional methods were used, how thermostability was measured, and whether the comparison was controlled for sequence context or computational cost. Why it matters This is the most consequential claim in the abstract. If the thermostability improvement is not rigorously demonstrated with appropriate controls and error estimates, the practical utility of the SAE approach is not established. Overstated claims of improvement over existing methods could mislead downstream users. Resolution test Provide quantitative thermostability metrics (for example, melting temperature estimates or free energy differences) for the SAE-derived variant, for variants from the traditional methods, and for the wild type, with uncertainty estimates. Specify the molecular dynamics protocol, force field, simulation length, and analysis methods. Demonstrate that the comparison is fair, for example by using identical simulation conditions and comparable sequence diversity. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Evidence sufficiency Claim pointer The authors claim that SAEs uncover correlations between sparse activations and protein features such as secondary structure, residue volume, residue shape, disulfide bridges, and coordination to ligands. Evidence pointer Abstract, feature correlation statement; location not provided Concern The abstract lists several protein features but provides no information on the strength, significance, or specificity of the reported correlations. It is unclear whether these correlations are robust across protein families, whether they are causal or merely associative, and whether the SAE dimensions are consistently interpretable or only in a subset of cases. Why it matters The interpretability claim is the foundation of the paper. Without quantitative measures of correlation quality, such as correlation coefficients, significance thresholds, or validation on held-out proteins, the reader cannot judge whether the SAE features are genuinely meaningful or an artifact of the expansion procedure. Resolution test Report correlation coefficients and significance values for each protein feature against the relevant sparse dimensions. Show that the correlations generalize across a diverse test set of proteins not used in training the SAE. Provide examples of dimensions that are interpretable and quantify the fraction of dimensions that are not. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Technical soundness Claim pointer The authors state that SAEs expand the latent space of ProteinMPNN and that this expansion uncovers correlations between activations and protein features. Evidence pointer Abstract, SAE introduction statement; location not provided Concern The abstract does not describe the SAE architecture, training procedure, or how the SAE was integrated with ProteinMPNN. Key details such as the size of the expanded latent space, the sparsity penalty, the training data, and the reconstruction fidelity of the SAE are absent. Without these, the technical validity of the approach cannot be assessed. Why it matters Sparse autoencoders are sensitive to hyperparameter choices and training protocols. If the SAE is poorly trained or the expansion is not faithful to the original activations, the subsequent interpretability and manipulation claims are compromised. The technical setup determines whether the results are reproducible and meaningful. Resolution test Provide a full description of the SAE architecture, including layer sizes, activation functions, sparsity regularization, and training data. Report reconstruction error or fidelity metrics for the SAE on held-out activations. Describe how the SAE was inserted into the ProteinMPNN pipeline and whether the original model outputs are preserved. Minor Comments Concern ID R1-m1 Severity Minor Axis Clarity Affected element Abstract, feature list Evidence pointer Abstract, feature correlation statement; location not provided Issue The list of protein features is presented without any indication of how each feature was defined or computed. For example, residue volume and residue shape are related but distinct concepts, and their operational definitions matter for interpretation. Required correction Define each feature and specify the computational method used to assign it to residues or positions in the protein structure. Concern ID R1-m2 Severity Minor Axis Reproducibility Affected element Abstract, repository reference Evidence pointer Abstract, repository URL; location not provided Issue The repository is mentioned but no version, license, or usage instructions are given. The abstract does not state whether the code and data are sufficient to reproduce the reported results. Required correction Provide a clear statement on code availability, including versioning, dependencies, and instructions for reproducing the key figures and results. Concern ID R1-m3 Severity Minor Axis Scope Affected element Abstract, thermostability claim Evidence pointer Abstract, thermostability statement; location not provided Issue The abstract claims improvement over traditional machine learning methods but does not specify which methods were compared. This makes the claim difficult to contextualize. Required correction Name the traditional methods used for comparison and briefly describe why they were chosen as baselines. Technical failings that need to be addressed before the case is established R1-M1, R1-M2, R1-M3. The absence of quantitative results, methodological detail, and validation protocols means that none of the three central claims (interpretability, manipulability, thermostability improvement) can be verified from the supplied material. Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality is high. Applying SAEs to a protein sequence model for interpretability and targeted manipulation is a novel contribution that extends prior interpretability work in language models to a new domain. Scientific importance is potentially high, given the broad use of ProteinMPNN and the general need for interpretable protein design tools. Interdisciplinary readership is plausible, as the work bridges machine learning, structural biology, and protein engineering. Technical soundness cannot be assessed from the abstract alone. Readability for nonspecialists is adequate in the abstract, though the feature list and the thermostability claim would benefit from more explicit explanation. Overall, the work has strong potential but the current evidence base is insufficient to support the claims. Recommendation posture Currently not established from the provided evidence. The concept is promising and the direction is worthwhile, but the abstract does not provide the quantitative and methodological support needed to validate the central claims. A full manuscript with detailed methods, results, and validation would be required to assess whether the case can be made. Risk / unsupported claims The claim that SAE-derived Brolucizumab variants are more thermostable than variants from traditional machine learning methods is unsupported. No quantitative data, simulation details, or comparative baselines are provided. The claim that SAEs uncover correlations between sparse activations and protein features is unsupported. No correlation coefficients, significance values, or validation on held-out data are provided. The claim that sparse activations can be manipulated to produce a desired variant is unsupported. The mechanism of manipulation and the success rate or specificity of the manipulation are not described. The general claim that SAEs provide mechanistic understanding of protein design models is not established. The abstract demonstrates correlation, not causation, and the depth of mechanistic insight is unclear. The reproducibility of the work cannot be assessed. The repository is referenced but its contents, version, and completeness were not available for review.

min(N+, N−) 个不相交配对；(3) 对每个配对计算表示差异并做单位归一化；(4) 用配对层相似度的 softmax 权重（τ = 0.10）聚合这些单位归一化差异，得到引导向量。该向量在每一层重新计算，但配对和权重共享。 核心洞察 ：性质改进方向在表示空间中 不是全局一致的 ，而是随序列背景（protein background）系统变化。通过 相似度匹配 正负性质蛋白，可以保留"可比背景下的方向信息"，避免全局平均带来的方向模糊。单位归一化则消除了配对间位移幅度差异的干扰，使方向信息不被大位移配对主导。 可能的普适教训 [Analysis]： - 配对而非群体对比 ：在生物序列表示空间中，群体级别的对比（如质心差）会丢失个体级别的方向异质性。任何涉及"方向"的表示学习任务（如突变方向预测、构象变化方向）都可能受益于配对级别的对比设计。 - 轨迹级评估优于静态评估 ：引导向量的质量不应仅由静态属性（稳定性、局部对齐）判断，而应通过实际优化轨迹中每步的方向支持来评估。这一思路可迁移至 MD 模拟中的偏置方向评估、构象采样中的推进方向选择。 - 无需预测器的排序信号 ：LDS 提供了一种不依赖性质预测器的候选排序方法，在标签稀缺场景下具有实用价值。 07 方法总览 输入 ：目标蛋白序列 ：预测突变方向时，配对级对比（同背景下的突变前后）可能优于全局平均效应。 单位归一化 + 相似度加权聚合 ：对配对差异做单位归一化可以避免幅度干扰，而相似度加权可以突出与目标背景更相关的方向。这一聚合策略可迁移至任何需要从示例对中提取方向信息的任务。 轨迹级评估指标（LDS） ：静态引导向量诊断（如 bootstrap 稳定性）不足以评估实际优化可靠性。LDS 通过检查每一步实际位移与局部参考方向的对齐程度，提供了更贴近实际效果的评估。这一思路可迁移至： - MD 模拟中的偏置方向评估 ：评估每一步模拟是否沿预期方向推进。 - 强化学习中的策略评估 ：评估每一步动作是否朝向局部最优方向。 无需预测器的候选排序 ：LDS 提供了一种不依赖性质预测器的排序信号，在标签稀缺场景下具有实用价值。这提示在蛋白质设计中， 过程指标 （如轨迹方向支持度）可以替代 结果指标 （如预测分数）进行早期筛选。 实验设计启示 ：将数据严格分为构建集、测试集、参考池三部分，并去除重叠，是评估引导方法的关键设计，避免信息泄漏。 15 与已有知识连接 激活引导（Activation Steering） ：本文直接建立在 [21, 17] 的激活引导框架上，并针对蛋白质领域提出改进。与 NLP 中的激活引导（如表示工程、方向探针）相比，本文强调了 生物序列的背景依赖性 methodological soundness, evidence quality, and reproducibility as presented in the supplied text Shared manuscript claim summary The authors propose PULSE, a context-aware activation steering method for protein sequence optimization that constructs steering vectors from similarity-matched positive-negative protein pairs rather than global population contrasts. They report improved optimization outcomes across solubility, immunogenicity, and toxicity, and introduce Local Directional Support (LDS) as a trajectory-level reliability metric enabling predictor-free candidate prioritization. Visible evidence base Main text figures (Figs. 2–7), Table 1, Table 2, Supplementary Tables 3–5, Appendix A–C Missing materials affecting confidence Figure images not provided; exact numerical values for many reported results not given in text; full algorithm pseudocode not provided; dataset composition details partially described; code repository not inspected Reviewer Overall assessment The manuscript addresses a relevant problem in controllable protein sequence generation and proposes a conceptually interesting alternative to global steering vector construction. The motivation for context-aware steering is well articulated and supported by the background-dependence analysis. However, the evidence as presented has several gaps that prevent full assessment of the method's validity and generalizability. The reliance on predictor-based outcomes without experimental validation, the limited model scope, and the absence of key methodological details (e.g., exact hyperparameter values, computational costs, sensitivity analyses) temper enthusiasm. The LDS metric is a useful conceptual contribution, but its practical utility requires stronger validation. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers in protein engineering, computational protein design, and machine learning for biology would be interested. The work speaks to those developing controllable generation methods for protein language models and those seeking reliability metrics for iterative sequence optimization. The predictor-free prioritization aspect may appeal to experimental groups with limited screening capacity. Major strengths The core idea of moving from global to local, context-dependent steering is well motivated and timely. The pairing strategy using representation similarity is methodologically clean. The introduction of LDS as a trajectory-level diagnostic addresses a genuine gap in evaluating iterative optimization. The evaluation across three distinct protein properties provides breadth. The authors are transparent about limitations, including the lack of experimental validation. Major Concerns See detailed items below. Minor Comments See detailed items below. Technical failings that need to be addressed before the case is established R1-M1 (predictor dependence), R1-M2 (limited model scope), R1-M3 (missing methodological details), R1-M4 (LDS validation gap) Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality: The paired-unit steering concept is a meaningful departure from existing global contrast methods, and LDS is a novel diagnostic. Scientific importance: The problem of context-aware steering is significant for the field, but the current evidence does not yet establish broad impact. Interdisciplinary readership: The work bridges machine learning and protein engineering, but the presentation assumes familiarity with both fields without sufficient scaffolding. Technical soundness: The core methodology is reasonable, but several implementation details and validation choices weaken the current case. Readability for nonspecialists: The abstract and introduction are accessible, but the methods section is dense and would benefit from clearer exposition of the mathematical notation. Recommendation posture Supportive if technical concerns are resolved. The core idea has merit, but the current evidence base is insufficient to fully establish the claims. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Evidence quality Claim pointer "PULSE consistently outperforms global population-centroid steering in both final predicted property scores and optimization success rates" (Abstract; Section 3.2) Evidence pointer Section 3.2, Fig. 2, Table 2 Concern All performance claims rest on predictor-based outcomes. The predictors used for solubility, immunogenicity, and toxicity are themselves models with unknown accuracy for the specific target proteins tested. Without experimental validation or at least a demonstration that predictor scores correlate with known experimental measurements for a held-out set, the reported improvements may reflect artifacts of the predictors rather than genuine property improvements. Why it matters The central claim of the paper is that PULSE produces better protein optimizations. If the evaluation oracle is unreliable, the claim is not established. The authors acknowledge this limitation in Section 4.2, but the acknowledgment does not mitigate the evidentiary gap. Resolution test Provide experimental validation on a small set of designed proteins, or demonstrate that the predictors used have been benchmarked against experimental data for the relevant property and sequence space, with quantified accuracy. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Generalizability Claim pointer "PULSE consistently outperforms global population-centroid steering" (Abstract; Section 3.2) Evidence pointer Section 3.1, Section 4.2 Concern All experiments use a single model backbone (ESMC-600M). The authors acknowledge this in Section 4.2, but the claim of consistent outperformance is only demonstrated for one architecture. It is unknown whether the paired-unit steering advantage persists with other protein language models of different sizes or architectures. Why it matters The method's utility depends on its generalizability across the diverse landscape of protein language models. A single-backbone evaluation is insufficient to support the strength of the stated claim. Resolution test Repeat key experiments with at least one additional model backbone (e.g., ESM-2 of comparable size, or a smaller model) and report whether the performance advantage holds. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Reproducibility Claim pointer "PULSE adpots the same site selection and decoding as ASPO; only the construction of v(l) differs" (Section 2.1) Evidence pointer Section 2.1, Section 2.2, Appendix C Concern Several methodological details required for reproduction are missing or incompletely specified. The exact values of α (steering intensity) are said to be in Table 5, but the table is not provided in the supplied text. The site selection procedure references a ranking and masking step, but the precise criterion (e.g., lowest-scoring by what measure) is not fully defined. The decoding procedure is described in words but not with sufficient mathematical precision to implement without guessing. Why it matters Reproducibility is a core requirement for scientific claims. Without complete methodological specification, independent verification is impossible. Resolution test Provide complete pseudocode for the optimization loop, exact hyperparameter values in the main text or a fully specified appendix, and clarify the site selection and decoding equations. Concern ID R1-M4 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Conceptual validation Claim pointer "LDS captures differences in trajectory reliability and enables predictor-free candidate prioritization" (Abstract; Section 3.6) Evidence pointer Section 3.5, Section 3.6, Fig. 5, Fig. 6 Concern The claim that LDS enables predictor-free prioritization is supported by AUROC comparisons, but the analysis does not establish that LDS provides information beyond what could be obtained from simpler metrics (e.g., final property score change, or trajectory length). No comparison against alternative prioritization strategies is provided. Why it matters The practical value of LDS depends on its incremental utility over existing or simpler approaches. Without such comparison, the contribution of LDS as a prioritization tool is unclear. Resolution test Compare LDS-based ranking against ranking by final predicted score, by total trajectory displacement, or by random selection, and report AUROC and enrichment for each. Minor Comments Concern ID R1-m1 Severity Minor Axis Clarity Affected element Section 2.2, pairing procedure Evidence pointer Section 2.2 Issue The description of the Hungarian algorithm application states that K = min(N+, N−) disjoint pairs are obtained, but it is unclear how ties in similarity are broken and whether the matching is performed once on the full dataset or per target. Required correction Clarify the matching procedure, including tie-breaking and whether matching is global or target-specific. Concern ID R1-m2 Severity Minor Axis Statistical reporting Affected element Section 3.2, Table 2 Evidence pointer Section 3.2, Table 2 Issue The text states that paired comparisons were statistically significant after multiple-testing correction, but effect sizes and confidence intervals are not reported in the main text. Required correction Report effect sizes and confidence intervals for the paired differences alongside p-values. Concern ID R1-m3 Severity Minor Axis Notation consistency Affected element Section 2.1, Section 2.2 Evidence pointer Section 2.1, Section 2.2 Issue The notation for representations is introduced as h(l)x for the representation of residue r at layer l, but the subscript r is not defined in the text. The mean over residues is denoted h̄(l)x, but the averaging operation is not explicitly stated. Required correction Define all notation explicitly, including the residue index and the averaging operation. Concern ID R1-m4 Severity Minor Axis Computational cost Affected element Section 2.2, Hungarian algorithm Evidence pointer Section 2.2 Issue The computational cost of the Hungarian algorithm for large datasets is not discussed. For protein datasets with tens of thousands of sequences, this could be a practical bottleneck. Required correction Report the computational time for the pairing step and discuss scalability. Concern ID R1-m5 Severity Minor Axis Robustness Affected element Section 3.5, Fig. 5 Evidence pointer Section 3.5 Issue The sensitivity analysis uses 10 independently sampled reference pools, but the variance across these pools is not reported beyond the claim that the advantage was robust. Required correction Report the distribution of LDS differences across reference pools (e.g., mean and standard deviation). Concern ID R1-m6 Severity Minor Axis Presentation Affected element Section 3.3, Table 1 Evidence pointer Section 3.3, Table 1 Issue The Spearman correlations are reported, but the corresponding scatter plots or binned summaries are only referenced in supplementary material. Required correction Include representative scatter plots in the main text or supplementary for visual inspection. Risk / unsupported claims The claim that PULSE "consistently outperforms" global steering is not fully supported given the single model backbone and predictor-based evaluation. The claim that LDS "enables predictor-free candidate prioritization" is not supported by comparison against alternative prioritization methods. The claim that "property-improving directions vary across different protein sequence backgrounds" is supported by correlational evidence, but the causal interpretation is not established. The statement that PULSE's advantage is due to "retaining pair-specific information prior to aggregation" is a plausible interpretation but not directly tested (e.g., via ablation of the weighting scheme). The generalizability of findings to other protein properties beyond the three tested is not established. The practical utility of the method for experimental workflows is asserted but not demonstrated with wet-lab data.

supplementary materials were provided Shared manuscript claim summary The authors audit three components of a protein generate-and-screen pipeline: repetition steering, ESMFold confidence, and an activation readout. They report that steering preserves confidence at its operating point but exhibits a cliff at a specific alpha value, that direction matters at moderate push but not at saturation, that unsteered generator activations predict the confidence gate with moderate accuracy, that length sensitivity can manufacture false nulls, and that no balanced-accuracy interval excludes chance for experimental stability on matched design-scramble pairs. They conclude that predicting the gate does not establish foldability and that readouts should be tested for what they measure before use in selection. Visible evidence base Abstract text only; no figures, tables, methods, or supplementary materials Missing materials affecting confidence Full manuscript, all figures and tables, methods descriptions, statistical details, dataset descriptions, code repository contents, and any supplementary information Reviewer Overall assessment The abstract presents a potentially useful cautionary audit of common practices in protein language model pipelines. The core message, that predicted confidence and activation readouts should not be conflated with experimental foldability, is sensible and worth stating. However, the abstract as provided is too compressed to evaluate the technical soundness of the claims. Key quantities are presented without context, the relationship between the different analyses is not fully clear, and the statistical and methodological details necessary to assess the validity of the conclusions are absent. The work may be of interest to practitioners in protein design and machine learning, but the evidence base provided is insufficient to establish the case. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers developing protein generate-and-screen pipelines, particularly those using protein language models for steering or design, would be the primary audience. The cautionary findings about confidence metrics and activation readouts are relevant to anyone using ESMFold or similar tools for candidate selection. The replication of length sensitivity effects and the demonstration of false nulls are also relevant to experimentalists interpreting stability assays. The work may also interest methodologists working on interpretability and evaluation of language models in scientific domains. Major strengths The abstract addresses a practical and under-examined question, namely whether common readouts in protein design pipelines measure what they are assumed to measure. The inclusion of a negative result, that experimental stability cannot be predicted from the confidence gate, is valuable. The authors also appear to have conducted matched controls, such as composition- and length-matched design-scramble pairs, which is a strength if the underlying methods are sound. The provision of code and data is commendable. Major Concerns The abstract is too brief to support the claims made. Several quantitative results are presented without sufficient context or statistical detail. The relationship between the different analyses is not fully clear. The central negative result, that no balanced-accuracy interval excludes chance, is stated without the necessary details to assess its strength. The claim that predicting the gate does not establish foldability is a reasonable inference but requires more evidence than the abstract provides. Minor Comments The abstract would benefit from clearer definitions of key terms, such as the activation readout and the confidence gate. The use of the term "confessions" in the title is informal for a scientific manuscript. The abstract does not state the number of proteins, designs, or replicates used, which limits interpretability. The GitHub repository is mentioned but its contents are not described. Technical failings that need to be addressed before the case is established The abstract does not provide enough methodological detail to assess the validity of the statistical claims. The cliff at alpha_50 = 1.240x is presented without confidence intervals or a description of the fitting procedure. The ROC-AUC of 0.786 +/- 0.004 is reported but the underlying model and cross-validation scheme are not described. The balanced-accuracy intervals are mentioned but their construction is not explained. The length sensitivity replication is stated but not quantified. Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality: the question of whether readouts track their intended targets is not new, but the specific combination of steering, confidence, and activation readouts in a single audit may offer a useful synthesis. Scientific importance: the findings are potentially important for practitioners, but the abstract does not establish the robustness of the results. Interdisciplinary readership: the work sits at the intersection of machine learning and protein biophysics, and the abstract is written in a way that is largely accessible to both communities, though some terms are undefined. Technical soundness: cannot be assessed from the abstract alone; the statistical details are insufficient. Readability for nonspecialists: the abstract is concise but assumes familiarity with protein language models, steering, and ESMFold, which limits accessibility. A full manuscript with methods, figures, and statistical analyses would be required to evaluate the work properly. 传统 MD 模拟受限于力场精度和采样成本 - 纯深度学习系综生成器（如 IDPFold、BioEmu、ESMFold）依赖训练数据分布，对条件依赖性折叠蛋白（ligand/ion 诱导折叠）系统性失效 - 已有 bAIes 仅验证了 AF2，未系统评估其他预测器的适用性 精确研究问题 ：Can bAIes generate IDP conformational ensembles with comparable experimental accuracy regardless of which AI structure predictor (AF2, AF3, Boltz-1, Boltz-2, ESMFold, ESMFold2) provides the distogram information? 04 背景与发展脉络 注：此脉络基于本文引用与作者叙述整理，标注为「经外部核验」部分基于文中明确引用的文献。 阶段 代表性方法 优点 局限 传统 MD 模拟 全原子力场（如 amber99SB-ILDN, a99SB-disp） 物理原理驱动，可解释性强 计算成本高，力场对 IDP 精度不足 粗粒化 MD CALVADOS 等 CG 模型 可模拟全 IDP 组（IDRome），效率高 分辨率低，需回映射 片段组装 IDP-o（基于 AF 数据库片段） 计算高效 依赖片段库质量，局部精度有限 深度学习系综生成 IDPFold（SE(3) 扩散）、BioEmu（扩散 + AF2 embedding）、ESMFold（flow matching）、PepTron（ESMFold + IDP-o 微调） 生成速度快 训练数据偏差，无法处理条件依赖性折叠，可能生成非物理构象 混合方法（本文位置） bAIes（贝叶斯推断 + MD 采样 + AI distogram 作为数据） 物理先验保证构象合理性，AI 信息提供构象偏好，对预测器选择鲁棒 仍需 MD 采样成本，长程相互作用描述有限 本文主张的位置 ：bAIes 处于「AI 预测器输出 + 物理力场」的交叉点，通过贝叶斯框架将两者融合，既保留 MD 的物理合理性和可扩展性（可加自定义约束、配体等），又利用 AI 预测器中编码的序列-结构关系信息。本文的核心贡献是证明该框架对预测器选择具有鲁棒性，从而确立其作为通用 IDP 系综生成工具的地位。 05 核心痛点 痛点 表现 成因或作者解释 文中证据 IDP 系综实验表征成本高 NMR、SAXS 等实验耗时且需要大量样品 IDP 本质是动态系综，单一技术只能提供部分信息 Introduction 第 3-5 段 传统 MD 力场对 IDP 精度不足 模拟系综与实验数据偏差大 力场参数化主要基于折叠蛋白，对 IDP 的构象偏好描述不准确 Introduction 第 4 段引用 14-16 纯深度学习系综生成器对条件依赖性折叠蛋白失效 Spm-FrpC、drkN、d131d、FLN5A3A3 被系统性预测为折叠态 训练数据（PDB 静态结构）不包含配体/离子/环境条件信息 Results 图 5A、Discussion 第 2 段 不同 AI 预测器 distogram 存在差异 IDP 长程接触预测一致性低（50-85% 共享） 架构差异（Transformer vs. 扩散 vs. 语言模型）和训练数据差异 Results 图 S3C,D 预测器对条件依赖性折叠蛋白的 distogram 不可靠 折叠预测导致 distogram 中出现大量非真实长程接触 训练数据以折叠蛋白为主，对 intrinsically disordered regions 的构象多样性编码不足 Discussion 第 2 段、Results 图 5A 长程接触和整体压缩度描述不准确 bAIes 在 SAXS 和 PRE 上表现弱于局部探针 AI 预测器训练数据中缺乏 IDP 动态长程接触信息 Results 图 4E,F、Discussion 第 1 段 06 核心思想 1) 表面方法 ： bAIes 是一个贝叶斯推断框架，将 AI 结构预测器输出的 distogram（每对残基的 Cβ-Cβ 距离分布）转化为高斯似然项，与基于 amber99SB-ILDN 简化得到的随机线圈力场（仅保留排斥项 + 骨架二面角校正）结合，通过 MD 采样（OpenMM 实现，CustomBondForce 实现约束）生成 IDP 构象系综。本文的扩展在于：将六种预测器（AF2、AF3、Boltz-1、Boltz-2、ESMFold、ESMFold2）的 distogram 分别接入 bAIes，系统比较输出系综对实验数据的还原能力。 2) 核心洞察 ： - Distogram 是 AI 预测器中可迁移的中间表示 ：尽管不同预测器架构差异巨大（AF2 的 Evoformer + structure module、AF3/Boltz 的扩散模块、ESMFold 的语言模型），但它们都产生 distogram 这一共同输出格式，bAIes 只需 distogram 即可工作，因此天然兼容所有预测器。 - 贝叶斯框架的噪声模型是关键鲁棒性来源 ：bAIes 对每个 distogram 拟合高斯分布并估计不确定性 σi，低置信度的预测（宽分布）自动被降权。这使得个别预测器的错误长程接触不会显著影响系综质量。 - 物理先验 + AI 信息的互补性 ：随机线圈力场提供局部构象的物理合理性（Ramachandran 偏好），AI distogram 提供序列特异的构象偏好（如螺旋倾向区域），两者结合优于任一单独使用。 - 预测器对 IDP 的 distogram 差异主要在长程接触 ：短程接触（局部结构）各预测器高度一致，长程接触（全局折叠）差异大且可靠性低，这解释了 bAIes 在局部探针（化学位移、3J 耦合）上表现好、在长程探针（PRE、SAXS）上表现弱。 3) 可能的普适教训 [Analysis] ： - AI 预测器的中间输出（而非最终结构）可能更适合作为 IDP 系综生成的输入 ：最终预测结构是单一构象，丢失了不确定性信息；distogram 保留了分布信息，更适合系综建模。 - 对 IDP 而言，AI 预测器的价值主要在局部构象偏好，而非全局折叠 ：这提示 IDP 计算研究应聚焦于提取局部结构倾向（螺旋、β 倾向），而非期望预测器给出全局构象。 - 贝叶斯不确定性加权是融合多源信息（AI + 物理 + 实验）的有效机制 ：这一思路可推广到其他「AI 预测 + 物理模拟」混合方法。 07 方法总览 输入 ： - 蛋白质氨基酸序列 - 六种 AI 结构预测器（AF2、AF3、Boltz-1、Boltz-2、ESMFold、ESMFold2）各自输出的 distogram（Nres × Nres × 64 的 logits 数组） 输出 ： - 原子分辨率的 IDP 构象系综（MD 轨迹） 模块 ： 1. Distogram 处理模块 ：从各预测器提取 distogram → 选择残基对（序列间隔 ≥ 4）→ 对每个 distogram 拟合高斯分布 → 提取峰值位置 di 和不确定性 σi 2. 随机线圈力场模块 ：基于 amber99SB-ILDN 简化，去除所有非键相互作用（仅保留排斥项），添加骨架二面角 Φ/Ψ 的残基类型特异性校正项（MAP 校正） 3. 贝叶斯推断模块 ：将 distogram 导出的高斯似然项与力场先验结合，形成后验能量函数 4. MD 采样模块 ：OpenMM 实现，使用 CustomBondForce 实现 distogram 约束，Langevin 恒温器（298.1 K），2 fs 时间步长，SHAKE 约束氢原子键 5. 实验数据反算模块 ：SPARTA+/UCBShift 计算化学位移，Karplus 关系计算 3J 耦合，PALES 计算 RDC，Pepsi-SAXS 计算 SAXS 谱 流程 ： 1. 对目标蛋白运行六种预测器，获取 distogram 2. 处理 distogram，选择接触对并拟合高斯参数 3. 以预测结构为起始构象，加氢后转换为 MD 格式 4. 能量最小化（LBFGS） 5. 运行 NVT MD 模拟，采样构象 6. 按间隔保存构象（间隔 = N/δt ps，N 为残基数） 7. 反算实验可观测量并与实验数据比较 训练 ：无监督训练（bAIes 本身不训练，仅使用预训练预测器的输出） 工具 ：OpenMM 7.6.0、GROMACS 2022.5（pdb2gmx）、LAMMPS（对比）、SPARTA+、UCBShift、PALES、Pepsi-SAXS 关键假设 ： - distogram 中的距离分布可近似为高斯分布 - 各残基对的约束相互独立 - 随机线圈力场足以描述 IDP 的局部构象偏好 08 核心模块拆解 模块 功能 为何需要 输入输出 支撑证据 移除后的已知或预期影响 Distogram 提取与处理 从各预测器提取 distogram，选择接触对，拟合高斯参数 将 AI 预测器的原始输出转化为 MD 可用的约束形式 输入：预测器输出 logits；输出：接触对列表 + (di, σi) 参数 Methods "Structure prediction and distogram extraction" 节 无法将 AI 信息接入 MD 采样 随机线圈力场（bAIes prior） 提供 IDP 的物理先验，仅保留排斥项 + 骨架二面角校正 保证构象的物理合理性，避免非物理构象 输入：原子坐标；输出：能量/力 Methods "The structural prior" 节；引用 31 的验证 退化为纯约束满足问题，可能产生非物理构象 贝叶斯似然项 将 distogram 约束转化为高斯似然，σi 控制约束强度 实现 AI 信息与物理先验的融合，不确定性加权 输入：当前构象中接触对距离 + (di, σi)；输出：似然能量 Methods "The data likelihood" 节 失去 AI 信息对构象的引导 不确定性估计（σi） 从 distogram 拟合高斯宽度，低置信度预测自动降权 使方法对预测器错误鲁棒 输入：distogram；输出：σi Methods "The uncertainty prior" 节；Results 中跨预测器一致性 所有约束等权，错误预测将显著扭曲系综 MD 采样引擎（OpenMM） 执行 NVT 模拟，采样后验分布 生成构象系综 输入：能量函数 + 起始构象；输出：轨迹 Methods "Computational performance" 节；图 2 无法生成系综 实验数据反算 从系综计算 NMR/SAXS 可观测量 评估系综质量 输入：构象系综；输出：化学位移、3J、RDC、SAXS 预测值 Methods "Back-calculation" 节 无法定量评估系综准确性 消融效应说明 ：文中未提供系统性消融实验（如移除 σi 不确定性、仅用力场无 AI 约束等），但通过跨预测器比较间接表明：σi 噪声模型使方法对预测器选择不敏感（Discussion 第 1 段）。[Analysis] 预期移除 σi 不确定性将导致低置信度长程约束过度约束系综，使 SAXS/PRE 表现进一步恶化。 09 关键公式符号 1) 贝叶斯后验 ： p(X|D) ∝ p(D|X) · p(X) X：构象坐标 D：AI 预测器提供的距离数据（distogram 集合） p(X|D)：后验概率 p(D|X)：似然函数 p(X)：先验概率 2) 先验定义 ： p(X) ∝ exp[-E_FF(X)/k_BT] E_FF：随机线圈力场能量（amber99SB-ILDN 简化版，仅保留排斥项 + 骨架二面角 MAP 校正） k_B：玻尔兹曼常数 T：温度 3) 高斯似然 ： p(D|X) = ∏ᵢ (1/√(2πσᵢ²)) · exp[-(dᵢ(X) - dᵢ)² / (2σᵢ²)] dᵢ(X)：构象 X 中第 i 对残基的 Cβ-Cβ 距离（Gly 为 Cα） dᵢ：第 i 对残基 distogram 高斯拟合的峰值位置 σᵢ：第 i 对残基的不确定性参数（从 distogram 拟合得到） i 遍历所有被选中的残基对（序列间隔 ≥ 4） 4) 边缘化后的似然 （文中给出形式）： p(D|X) = ∏ᵢ [σ_minᵢ / (σᵢ · √(2π))] · exp[-(dᵢ(X) - dᵢ)² / (2σᵢ²)] σ_minᵢ：第 i 对残基的最小不确定性（从高斯拟合中提取） 5) bAIes 能量函数 ： E_bAIes(X) = E_FF(X) + k_BT · Σᵢ [(dᵢ(X) - dᵢ)² / (2σᵢ²) - ln(σ_minᵢ/σᵢ)] 6) 归一化 RMSE ： RMSE_N(m) = (1/T) · Σₜ [RMSE_t(m) / RMSE_t(m_ref)] m：待评估的系综生成模型 m_ref：参考模型（随机线圈先验） T：实验数据类型数（5 种：化学位移、RDC、PRE、3J、SAXS） RMSE_t(m)：第 t 类实验的平均 RMSE 7) 接触对选择标准 （引用 31, 41）： - Shared manuscript claim summary The authors extend their bAIes framework, previously developed for AlphaFold2 distograms, to six AI structure predictors (AF2, AF3, Boltz-1, Boltz-2, ESMFold, ESMFold2) and demonstrate that bAIes generates atomistic ensembles of intrinsically disordered proteins with accuracy comparable to experimental NMR and SAXS data and competitive with state-of-the-art all-atom simulations and alternative ensemble generation methods. Reviewer Overall assessment The manuscript presents a timely and potentially valuable extension of the bAIes framework to multiple AI structure predictors, addressing an important question in the disordered protein community: whether distograms from different predictors carry useful conformational information for ensemble generation. The conceptual framing is clear and the methodological approach is well motivated. However, the provided text alone does not contain the quantitative evidence needed to assess whether the claims are fully supported. The results sections are descriptive rather than data-bearing, and the absence of all figures and tables makes it impossible to evaluate the magnitude of reported effects, the statistical significance of comparisons, or the validity of the stated conclusions. The manuscript is likely to be of interest to a specialized audience, but the case for broad impact and definitive conclusions is not established from the supplied material. Who would be interested in the results, and why Computational biophysicists and structural biologists working on intrinsically disordered proteins and regions, particularly those interested in integrating AI-based structure prediction with physics-based sampling. Developers of ensemble generation methods and users of tools like AlphaFold, ESMFold, and Boltz for disordered systems would find the comparison across predictors and the benchmarking against experimental data relevant. The work may also interest method developers in the broader protein structure prediction community who are concerned with the information content of distogram outputs. Major Strengths The question addressed is well defined and practically important: whether the choice of AI structure predictor materially affects the quality of downstream ensemble generation for IDPs. The extension of bAIes to six predictors, including recent models with different architectures and training strategies, is a logical and useful contribution. The benchmarking strategy is thoughtful, using both a curated dataset with multiple experimental observables and a comparison against several alternative ensemble generation methods. The authors acknowledge limitations honestly, including the issue of conditionally folded proteins and the difficulty of reproducing long-range observables. The new OpenMM implementation with GPU support is a practical improvement that will likely increase the usability of the method. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Evidence sufficiency Claim pointer The manuscript claims that "bAIes generates ensembles with comparable accuracy against experimental NMR and SAXS data, and competitive performance relative to state-of-the-art all-atom simulations and alternative IDP ensemble generation methods." Evidence pointer Results sections "Experimental validation of bAIes across AI structure predictors" and "Benchmarking of bAIes against other IDP ensemble generation methods"; Figures 3-5; Tables S1-S3 Concern The central quantitative claim of the manuscript cannot be evaluated from the provided text. All numerical results, including RMSE values, error bars, statistical comparisons, and benchmark rankings, are contained in figures and tables that were not supplied. The results sections describe trends qualitatively but provide no data points, no effect sizes, and no uncertainty estimates. Without access to the actual numbers, it is impossible to verify whether the stated conclusions follow from the evidence. Why it matters The claim of "comparable accuracy" and "competitive performance" is the core contribution of the work. If the underlying data do not support these statements, or if the comparisons are underpowered or confounded, the manuscript's value is substantially diminished. The reader cannot assess the magnitude of differences between predictors or between methods, nor whether the reported performance is practically meaningful. Resolution test Provide the full set of figures and tables with numerical values, including error bars and statistical tests, so that the claims can be quantitatively verified. If the data are available in a repository, state this explicitly and provide access details. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Methodological transparency Claim pointer The manuscript states that "bAIes is robust to the choice of structure predictor" and that "the distance distributions generated by different deep learning architectures contain valuable information about the conformational preferences of disordered proteins." Evidence pointer Methods section "Comparison of distograms across predictors using PeptoneDB-CS"; Figures 1, S1-S5 Concern The comparison of distograms across predictors is described qualitatively, but the criteria for "agreement" and "disagreement" between predictors are not fully specified. The Wasserstein distance and Pearson correlation are mentioned, but the thresholds for meaningful agreement or disagreement are not defined. Furthermore, the claim that distograms contain "valuable information" is not operationalized: what specific features of the distograms are informative, and how is this information quantified? The analysis appears to be descriptive rather than hypothesis-driven. Why it matters The manuscript's motivation rests on the premise that distograms from different predictors differ in ways that matter for ensemble generation. If the comparison is purely descriptive, the reader cannot determine whether the observed differences are systematic, biologically meaningful, or simply noise. The claim of robustness to predictor choice is central and requires a more rigorous definition of what constitutes a meaningful difference. Resolution test Define quantitative criteria for agreement and disagreement between predictors. Provide statistical tests for differences in distogram properties between ordered and disordered proteins. Clarify what specific distogram features are claimed to be informative and how they relate to downstream ensemble quality. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Benchmark validity Claim pointer The manuscript claims that bAIes is "competitive" with "state-of-the-art all-atom simulations and alternative IDP ensemble generation methods" on the PeptoneDB-Integrative benchmark. Evidence pointer Methods section "Benchmarking against other IDP ensemble generation methods"; Figure 5; Table S2 Concern The comparison against other methods is described, but the details of how these methods were run are not provided. Were the alternative methods (IDP-o, IDPFold, idpGAN, BioEmu, ESMFlow, PepTron) run by the authors or were results taken from the literature? What hyperparameters or settings were used? The exclusion of four proteins with conditionally folded predictions is described, but the rationale for exclusion is based on the behavior of other methods, which could introduce bias. The criteria for "competitive" performance are not defined in terms of a specific metric or threshold. Why it matters Benchmarking studies are only meaningful if the comparison is fair and transparent. If the alternative methods were not run under equivalent conditions, or if the exclusion criteria favor bAIes, the conclusions about competitiveness may not be reliable. The reader needs to know the exact protocol to judge the validity of the comparison. Resolution test Provide full details of how each alternative method was run, including software versions, hyperparameters, and any preprocessing steps. Justify the exclusion criteria for the four conditionally folded proteins. Define the metric and threshold used to determine "competitive" performance. Concern ID R1-M4 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Generalizability of conclusions Claim pointer The manuscript concludes that "bAIes is robust to the choice of structure predictor" and that the framework is "a flexible tool" for IDP ensemble generation. Evidence pointer Results sections "Experimental validation of bAIes across AI structure predictors" and "Benchmarking of bAIes against other IDP ensemble generation methods"; Figures 3-5 Concern The benchmark datasets are limited in size (17 and 16 proteins, respectively) and may not be representative of the diversity of IDP sequences and behaviors. The authors note that the total number of proteins is limited (29), but the implications of this limitation for the generalizability of the conclusions are not discussed in depth. The claim of robustness across predictors is based on a small sample, and the variability between proteins within each category is not quantified. Why it matters If the conclusions are based on a small and potentially biased sample, they may not hold for the broader population of IDPs. The claim of robustness is strong and requires evidence that the findings are not specific to the particular proteins studied. Resolution test Discuss the limitations of the dataset size and composition explicitly. If possible, provide evidence that the conclusions hold across a more diverse set of IDPs, or temper the claims accordingly. Minor Comments Concern ID R1-m1 Severity Minor Axis Clarity Affected element Methods section "Overview of the bAIes approach" Evidence pointer Methods, first subsection Issue The Bayesian formalism is presented in equations, but the notation is not fully defined in the text. For example, the meaning of the likelihood function p(D|X) and the prior p(X) is stated, but the specific forms of the Gaussian likelihood and the marginal likelihood are not explained in words. Required correction Add a brief verbal description of each equation, explaining the role of each term and how the marginalization over sigma is performed. Concern ID R1-m2 Severity Minor Axis Reproducibility Affected element Methods section "Structure prediction and distogram extraction" Evidence pointer Methods, subsection on structure prediction Issue The manuscript states that model code was modified to extract distograms for AF3, Boltz-1, Boltz-2, and ESMFold, but does not specify the nature of these modifications or provide a link to the modified code. Required correction Provide a detailed description of the code modifications or a link to a repository containing the modified code, to ensure reproducibility. Concern ID R1-m3 Severity Minor Axis Statistical rigor Affected element Methods section "Computational performance across simulation platforms" Evidence pointer Methods, subsection on computational performance Issue The performance comparison between LAMMPS and OpenMM is reported as a single speed value for each system size. It is unclear whether these are single runs or averages over multiple replicates, and no error estimates are provided. Required correction Report the number of replicates and the variability (e.g., standard deviation) for each performance measurement. Concern ID R1-m4 Severity Minor Axis Interpretation Affected element Discussion section Evidence pointer Discussion, paragraph on limitations Issue The discussion of the limitations of the approach is brief and does not address the potential impact of the choice of force field (amber99SB-ILDN with corrections) on the results. The authors note that the prior is a simplified random coil model, but do not discuss how this might affect the transferability of the method to systems with different physicochemical properties. Required correction Expand the discussion of the limitations of the prior model and its potential impact on the accuracy of the generated ensembles. Concern ID R1-m5 Severity Minor Axis Completeness Affected element Results section "Consistency of IDP distograms across structure predictors" Evidence pointer Results, first subsection Issue The analysis of distogram consistency is described for the PaaA2 example, but it is unclear how representative this example is of the broader dataset. The manuscript states that "all methods systematically predict the two helices" but does not provide a systematic quantification of this agreement across the full benchmark. Required correction Provide a quantitative summary of the agreement across all proteins in the benchmark, not just a single example. Technical failings that need to be addressed before the case is established R1-M1: Absence of all quantitative data (figures, tables) prevents verification of the central claims. R1-M2: Lack of defined criteria for distogram agreement and information content weakens the motivational premise. R1-M3: Insufficient detail on the benchmarking protocol for alternative methods undermines the validity of the comparison. Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality: The work is an incremental but useful extension of a previously published method. The idea of comparing multiple AI predictors for IDP ensemble generation is not entirely novel, as the authors themselves note that other groups have explored similar directions. The originality lies primarily in the systematic comparison and the open-source implementation, which is a moderate contribution. Scientific importance: The question of whether AI structure predictors can inform IDP ensemble generation is of genuine importance to the field. However, the importance of the specific findings, as presented, is difficult to gauge without the quantitative results. If the conclusions hold, the work would provide practical guidance for users of such tools, but the impact is likely to be incremental rather than transformative. Interdisciplinary readership: The manuscript is written for a specialized audience of computational structural biologists. The methods and terminology assume familiarity with Bayesian inference, molecular dynamics, and structure prediction. The broader significance for cell biology or biochemistry is not articulated in a way that would attract readers outside the immediate field. Technical soundness: The methodological framework is sound in principle, and the authors have prior work demonstrating the validity of the bAIes approach. However, the technical soundness of the specific claims in this manuscript cannot be assessed without the data. The lack of detail on the benchmarking protocol and the statistical treatment of results is a concern. Readability for nonspecialists: The abstract is clear and accessible, but the methods and results sections are dense and assume substantial background knowledge. The manuscript would benefit from a more explicit statement of the practical implications for nonspecialist readers. Recommendation posture Currently not established from the provided evidence. The manuscript addresses a relevant question and the methodological approach is reasonable, but the absence of all quantitative data and the lack of detail on key methodological aspects prevent verification of the central claims. The authors should be invited to resubmit with the full set of figures, tables, and statistical analyses, along with a more detailed description of the benchmarking protocol. If the data support the stated conclusions, the manuscript could be suitable for publication in a specialized journal, though the impact may not reach the level expected for Nature. Risk / unsupported claims The claim that "bAIes generates ensembles with comparable accuracy against experimental NMR and SAXS data" is unsupported in the provided text, as no numerical results are visible. The claim that bAIes is "competitive" with "state-of-the-art all-atom simulations and alternative IDP ensemble generation methods" is unsupported without the benchmark data and details of the comparison protocol. The claim that "the distance distributions generated by different deep learning architectures contain valuable information about the conformational preferences of disordered proteins" is not operationalized and cannot be evaluated. The claim that "bAIes is robust to the choice of structure predictor" is stated as a conclusion but is not supported by quantitative evidence in the provided text. The performance comparison between LAMMPS and OpenMM implementations is reported without error estimates or replicate information, making the claim of improved efficiency unverifiable.

01 基本信息 标题 ：REVEAL: RNA Ensemble Validation and Exploration with AI-guided Landscapes 作者与单位 ：Bhakat S; Vats S（单位未提供） 期刊/预印本平台 ：bioRxiv 年份 ：2026 论文类型 ：方法学/工作流预印本 领域 ：RNA 构象系综生成与验证 × AI 引导的分子模拟 关键词 ：RNA 构象系综、二级结构采样、trRosettaRNA2、无偏分子动力学、马尔可夫状态模型、群体加权共识评分 DOI/arXiv 号 ：10.64898/2026.11.10.765771 代码 ：https://github.com/sbhakat/REVEAL 数据 ：未提供（使用 HIV-1 TAR 突变体 TAR Mut 作为基准系统） 阅读日期 ：未提供 在该方向中的位置 ：本文属于「蛋白质/RNA 结构相关计算研究 × AI 方法 × 物理模拟」交叉方向，具体位于「AI 生成结构系综作为 MD 种子 → 无偏采样 → MSM 集成」这一新兴范式在 RNA 上的延伸。与 AlphaFold2-RAVE、AlphaFold-MSM、BioEmu-MSM 等蛋白体系方法形成直接类比，但以 RNA 二级结构系综作为结构多样性的来源，而非 MSA 子采样或扩散模型。同时引入不依赖集体变量的评分函数（PWCS），用于从模拟数据中直接识别平衡态主导构象。 02 一句话总结 针对 RNA 稀有激发态（如 HIV-1 TAR 突变体的 ES2↔GS 寄存器移位）无法被传统无偏 MD 采样的难题，REVEAL 通过「二级结构系综 → trRosettaRNA2 条件化三级结构预测 → 多种子无偏 MD → MSM 集成」的流程，在 6.8 µs 聚合采样内恢复了可逆的 ES2↔GS 转变，并引入群体加权共识评分（PWCS）直接从模拟数据中识别主导态，无需实验约束或增强采样偏置。 03 研究问题 具体问题 ：RNA 的功能相关激发态（excited states）通常稀疏布居且寿命短，传统无偏 MD 从单一实验结构出发无法在可达时间尺度内跨越 ES2↔GS 这类寄存器移位（register shift）的能垒。能否仅用序列信息，通过 AI 生成的结构系综作为种子，让无偏 MD 自发采样到这些稀有转变？ 为什么重要 ：RNA 的分子识别、配体结合和调控功能往往依赖这些瞬态构象。若能不依赖 NMR 等实验约束（如 RDC）即可获得平衡系综，将极大扩展 RNA 构象研究的适用范围，尤其是对缺乏实验数据的治疗相关 RNA。 现有方法为何不足 ： 传统无偏 MD 从单一结构出发，受限于起始构象的吸引域，无法跨越寄存器移位能垒； 增强采样（如 metadynamics、REMD）需要预选集体变量或偏置势，而 RNA 寄存器移位的相关自由度往往未知； 序列到结构预测模型（AlphaFold3、Boltz-2 等）输出的是单一或少数近天然态构象，无法反映平衡系综的布居分布； 已有的 RNA 系综方法（如 FARFAR2 + RDC 重加权）依赖实验数据，不适用于无数据体系。 精确的 Can 问题 ：Can a workflow that seeds unbiased MD from a secondary-structure-conditioned AI-generated tertiary structure ensemble capture a rare ES2↔GS register shift in RNA, without any external bias potential or experimental restraints? 04 背景与发展脉络 注：以下脉络主要基于本文 Introduction 的叙述框架，标注「仅本文框架」；部分节点经外部核验。 阶段 代表性方法 优点 局限 本文位置 单结构范式 实验结构（NMR/X-ray）作为 MD 起点 高精度起始结构 无法反映系综；稀有态不可达 本文明确反对的基线 二级结构系综 → 三级结构 ViennaRNA/LinearSampling/Sfold 采样二级结构 → FARFAR2 或 trRosettaRNA2 预测三级结构 将序列多样性转化为结构多样性 FARFAR2 计算昂贵；trRosettaRNA2 单结构预测不保证系综正确 本文核心组件 蛋白系综种子 MD AlphaFold2-RAVE、AlphaFold-MSM、BioEmu-MSM、AlphaFold-SFA（MSA 子采样/扩散/流匹配生成种子） 显著加速构象采样 依赖 MSA 或扩散模型；尚未推广到 RNA 本文的蛋白类比对象 RNA 系综实验重加权 FARFAR2 库 + RDC 重加权 与实验一致 依赖 NMR 数据；无法预测新体系 本文用 PWCS 替代实验约束 数据驱动 CV 时间滞后自编码器、DeepTICA、SRV 自动发现慢变量 对 RNA 寄存器移位不可靠（本文发现） 本文的对照方法 本文主张的位置 ：将「二级结构系综 → 条件化三级结构预测 → 多种子无偏 MD → MSM」这一流程首次系统应用于 RNA 寄存器移位，并引入不依赖 CV 的 PWCS 评分作为系综验证工具。 05 核心痛点 痛点 表现 成因或作者解释 文中证据 无偏 MD 无法跨越寄存器移位能垒 从 NMR ES2 结构出发的 MD 在 10 µs 内仍困于 ES2 吸引域 寄存器移位涉及多个碱基对的协同重排，能垒高且相关自由度未知；单一起始结构无法提供跨越能垒的初始动量 Results 图 2B：NMR-seeded MD 始终停留在 ES2 盆地 序列到结构预测模型无法反映系综布居 AlphaFold3、Boltz-2、ESMFold2、OpenFold3、Protenix-v2 输出的所有结构均落在 GS 侧或离路径区域，无一接近 ES2 这些模型训练数据以单一近天然态为主，RNA 在训练集中稀疏且缺乏激发态标注；模型默认输出最可几折叠 Results 图 2C：所有 Seq2Ens 预测结构位于负 CV2 区域 种子结构多样性不足导致 MD 采样偏差 Seq2Ens-MD（60 种子 × 200 ns = 12 µs）将 GS 错误预测为主导态，且形成离路径盆地 种子结构虽多但集中在单一构象区域，携带预测模型的系统偏差进入动力学 Results 图 2D：Seq2Ens-MD 的 FES 显示 GS 主导、ES2 缺失 数据驱动 CV 无法解析 RNA 寄存器移位 SFA、TAE、DeepTICA 在低维潜空间中无法分离 GS、ES2 和中间态 时间滞后方法对离散的碱基配对重排不敏感；RNA 寄存器移位是离散事件而非连续慢扩散 Results 图 9B-D：SFA/TAE/DeepTICA 潜空间对比度低 缺乏不依赖实验数据的系综验证指标 传统方法需 RDC 等 NMR 数据来重加权或验证系综 多数治疗相关 RNA 缺乏此类数据 Conclusions：PWCS 提供无实验约束的替代路径 06 核心思想 1) 表面方法 REVEAL 是一个四步流水线： 1. 二级结构系综生成 ：用 ViennaRNA、LinearSampling 和 Sfold 从序列预测多个热力学可行的二级结构； 2. 条件化三级结构预测 ：将每个二级结构作为约束输入 trRosettaRNA2，生成对应的三级结构（34 个种子）； 3. 多种子无偏 MD ：每个种子独立运行 200 ns 无偏 MD（共 6.8 µs）； 4. MSM 集成与 PWCS 评分 ：用 MSM 估计平衡布居和转变时间尺度，用 PWCS 对每个构象打分排序。 2) 核心洞察 二级结构空间是 RNA 寄存器移位的自然离散化 ：寄存器移位本质上是碱基配对模式的重新排列，而二级结构系综恰好枚举了这些离散的配对模式。将三级结构预测条件化在二级结构上，等价于在正确的离散自由度上播种，而非在连续的三维坐标空间中盲目采样。 AI 生成器的角色是「种子提供者」而非「系综预测器」 ：trRosettaRNA2 不需要预测正确的平衡布居，只需要在正确的盆地中放置起始结构；布居和动力学由 MD + MSM 提供。这避免了生成模型在布居预测上的系统性偏差。 PWCS 将「系综验证」从实验依赖中解放出来 ：通过 MSM 平衡权重重加权多个特征空间的混合高斯密度，PWCS 直接量化每个构象在平衡系综中的代表性，无需 RDC 等实验数据。 3) 可能的普适教训 [Analysis] 「生成器 + 物理模拟」的分工原则 ：生成模型负责覆盖构象空间（recall），物理模拟负责分配权重（precision）。这一分工在蛋白体系（AlphaFold2-RAVE 等）已被验证，本文将其推广到 RNA，并明确指出「生成器的偏差会通过种子进入动力学」这一风险。 离散自由度优先于连续 CV ：对于涉及碱基配对重排的构象转变，在离散的二级结构空间播种比在连续的三维坐标空间采样更高效。这一原则可能适用于其他具有明确离散中间态的核酸体系（如核糖开关、假结）。 评分函数应独立于 CV 选择 ：PWCS 的多特征、多分量共识设计使其对 CV 选择不敏感，这为系综验证提供了更稳健的工具。 07 方法总览 输入 ：RNA 序列（HIV-1 TAR 突变体 TAR Mut，31 nt：5′-GGCAGAUCUGAGCCUUCGGGAGCUCUCUGCC-3′） 输出 ： MSM 估计的平衡态布居（π）和态间平均首次通过时间（MFPT） 每个构象的 PWCS 分数 状态解析的、按平衡权重排序的代表性结构 模块 ： 1. 二级结构系综生成（ViennaRNA 非冗余 Boltzmann 采样 → 20 个代表结构；LinearSampling → 10 个；Sfold → 4 个） 2. 三级结构预测（trRosettaRNA2，条件化于每个二级结构；另加 1 个序列直接预测，共 35 个候选，筛除 1 个配对不匹配者，得 34 个种子） 3. 生成器负责「覆盖」（recall），物理模拟负责「加权」（precision）。生成器的输出不应被直接视为系综，而应作为 MD 种子；布居和动力学必须来自物理模拟 + 统计集成。这一原则对蛋白结构预测 + MD 的流程同样适用。 种子多样性是采样成功的第一决定因素 ：REVEAL 用 6.8 µs 完成了 NMR-seeded MD 用 10 µs 未完成的转变，差异仅在种子分布。这提示：在 MD 采样中，起始构象的多样性可能比总模拟时间更重要。 评分函数应独立于 CV 选择 ：PWCS 通过多特征、多分量 GMM 的共识打分，避免了对单一 CV 的依赖。在蛋白体系中，可类似地设计不依赖特定反应坐标的构象代表性评分。 「无 oracle 验证」的系综评估路径 ：PWCS 提供了一种不依赖实验数据的系综验证方法，通过 MSM 平衡权重重加权密度估计，直接识别主导态。这对缺乏实验数据的蛋白/RNA 体系具有直接借鉴价值。 生成模型的偏差会通过种子进入动力学 ：Seq2Ens-MD 的失败表明，生成模型的系统性偏差（偏向 GS）不会被 MD 纠正，反而会被放大。这提示：在使用 AI 生成结构作为 MD 种子时，必须验证种子的构象空间覆盖度，而非仅看结构质量。 15 与已有知识连接 AlphaFold2-RAVE
