Transformer）可先尝试零参数集成，再考虑学习融合权重。 「精度 vs 一致性」可以解耦 ：本文通过控制实验（E_orig vs E_anti vs E_Φ）清晰分离了「平均带来的精度提升」与「势函数化带来的一致性保证」。这种实验设计值得借鉴——在引入任何物理约束时，应同时报告「约束带来的精度变化」和「约束带来的一致性改善」，而非混为一谈。 多突变预测的端点构造是简单有效的扩展 ：将单突变预测器扩展到多突变时，从野生型和全突变背景分别计算贡献之和再取差，可保持反反对称性。可迁移到：组合突变设计、深度突变扫描（DMS）的外推。 「隐藏偏置是破坏一致性的根源」这一诊断思路可推广 ：本文通过数学推导定位了不一致性的具体来源（偏置项），而非笼统归因于「非线性」。这种「归因到具体参数」的诊断方法适用于任何物理约束失效的调试场景。 评估协议中应区分「回归精度」与「物理一致性」 ：本文在 S669 上同时报告 Pearson/MAE/RMSE 和反反对称缺陷/闭合误差，二者独立变化。这提示在蛋白质结构相关任务中，应建立「物理一致性指标」作为与精度并列的评估维度。 Review setup Input scope Full manuscript text (abstract, introduction, results, methods, discussion, data availability statement) Assessment boundary Scientific validity, methodological soundness, clarity of claims, and consistency of evidence presented in the provided text. No external data or code was accessed. Shared manuscript claim summary The authors present EvoPhi-DDG, a training-free adaptation of the MSAesm_ddG predictor that enforces exact thermodynamic antisymmetry and same-site transitivity by reformulating predictions as differences of a learned potential. They further combine EvoPhi-DDG with the published JanusDDG model via fixed equal-weight averaging, reporting improved predictive accuracy on S669, S96, and PTmul-NR benchmarks, and reduced multisite pathway-closure error. Visible evidence base Main text figures (Figures 1–6 referenced), Supplementary Figures S1–S3, Supplementary Tables S1–S10, and the Methods section describing datasets, model architectures, and evaluation protocols. Reviewer Overall assessment The manuscript addresses a relevant and timely problem in protein stability prediction: enforcing thermodynamic consistency in learned predictors. The proposed EvoPhi-DDG reformulation is elegant and the theoretical analysis of the ReLU head is a clear strength. The empirical evaluation is reasonably thorough, but several concerns about the strength of the claims, the interpretation of the benchmark results, and the generalizability of the theoretical guarantees need to be addressed. The distinction between predictive gains from averaging and consistency gains from the potential-based reformulation is well articulated, but the practical significance of the consistency improvements is not fully demonstrated. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers in computational protein engineering, biophysics, and machine learning applied to biology. The work is particularly relevant to those developing or using stability predictors, as it offers a principled way to enforce physical constraints without retraining, and to those interested in model ensembling and complementarity analysis. Major strengths 1. The theoretical analysis of the MSAesm_ddG head is a significant contribution. The derivation of the exact potential-difference form when hidden biases are zero, and the explicit residual for nonzero biases, provides a clear and testable architectural explanation for the observed near-transitivity. 2. The separation of predictive accuracy from physical consistency as distinct evaluation criteria is methodologically sound and clearly presented. 3. The use of fixed, equal-weight averaging without additional training is a parsimonious and well-justified integration strategy, avoiding overfitting concerns. 4. The residual analysis (Section 2.6) provides a useful statistical framework for understanding when and why ensembling helps, beyond simple model diversity arguments. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Claim strength vs. evidence Claim pointer The abstract and Section 2.3 state that the ensemble "outperforms both components on S669 and S96, achieving Pearson correlations of 0.59 and 0.55, respectively, compared with 0.55 and 0.52 for JanusDDG and 0.53 and 0.48 for EvoPhi-DDG." Evidence pointer Section 2.3, Figure 5, Supplementary Table S9 Concern The reported improvements in Pearson correlation (e.g., 0.55 to 0.59 on S669) are modest. The manuscript does not provide confidence intervals for these point estimates in the main text, nor does it report whether these differences are statistically significant. The bootstrap analysis is mentioned for the multisite RMSE comparison (Section 2.3), but not for the primary single-site accuracy metrics. Without uncertainty quantification, the claim of "outperforming" is not fully supported. Why it matters The central claim of the paper is that the ensemble improves predictive accuracy. If the observed gains are within the noise of the evaluation, the practical value of the ensemble for accuracy is questionable, and the paper's contribution would rest solely on the consistency guarantees. Resolution test Provide 95% confidence intervals (e.g., via the described protein-bootstrap procedure) for the Pearson correlations on S669, S96, and PTmul-NR for all models compared. Report whether the differences are statistically significant. If the gains are not significant, temper the language in the abstract and results accordingly. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Generalizability of theoretical guarantee Claim pointer Section 2.1 and Methods 3.2.4 state that EvoPhi-DDG "guarantees exact same-site transitivity under fixed alignment contexts." Evidence pointer Section 2.1, Methods 3.2.4 Concern The theoretical guarantee of exact transitivity is derived for a fixed alignment context and a fixed mutation site. The manuscript correctly notes that this does not establish general multisite transitivity. However, the practical utility of the guarantee is unclear. The evaluation of multisite consistency (Section 2.3, Figure 4) shows that the ensemble still has nonzero closure error (RMSE 0.10 kcal/mol at ten intermediates). While this is lower than JanusDDG, it is not zero. The manuscript should more clearly state that the exact guarantee applies only to a narrow set of conditions (same site, same alignment) and that the empirical improvement on multisite paths is a separate, weaker result. Why it matters Overstating the scope of the theoretical guarantee could mislead readers into thinking the model is exactly thermodynamically consistent in all practical scenarios. The distinction between the exact guarantee and the empirical improvement is crucial for correct interpretation. Resolution test In the abstract and discussion, explicitly state that the exact transitivity guarantee is limited to single-site mutations under a fixed alignment context, and that for multisite mutations, the model only shows empirically reduced, but not eliminated, closure error. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Benchmark interpretation Claim pointer Section 2.3 states that on PTmul-NR, the ensemble "achieves a Pearson correlation of 0.66, improving on JanusDDG’s 0.61 and matching the EvoPhi-DDG extension at the reported precision." Evidence pointer Section 2.3, Figure 5, Supplementary Table S9 Concern The PTmul-NR benchmark contains only 82 variants across 13 distinct WT sequences. The manuscript acknowledges this limitation in Section 2.3, but the claim of "matching" the EvoPhi-DDG extension is based on a very small sample. The lack of a clear advantage over the stronger component on this benchmark is not framed as a potential limitation of the ensembling approach for multiple mutations. Why it matters The manuscript aims to show that the ensemble is beneficial. If on the multiple-mutation benchmark the ensemble does not improve over the best component, this is an important boundary condition for the method's applicability. The discussion should address this more directly. Resolution test Discuss the implications of the PTmul-NR result more thoroughly. Is the lack of improvement due to the small sample size, the nature of the task, or a fundamental limitation of the ensembling approach for multiple mutations? Suggest potential avenues for future work to address this. Minor Comments Concern ID R1-m1 Severity Minor Axis Clarity Affected element Section 2.1, Figure 1 Evidence pointer Section 2.1, Figure 1 Issue The description of the EvoPhi-DDG architecture in Section 2.1 is dense and relies heavily on equations that are not fully introduced in the main text. Figure 1 is referenced but not described in detail. Required correction Provide a more accessible, high-level description of the EvoPhi-DDG architecture in the main text, and ensure Figure 1 clearly illustrates the key components (e.g., the shared encoder, the potential-difference head, the background-aware extension). Concern ID R1-m2 Severity Minor Axis Reproducibility Affected element Methods 3.1.2 Evidence pointer Methods 3.1.2 Issue The description of the alignment construction and filtering is brief. The specific parameters for MMseqs2 and HHfilter are mentioned, but the exact commands or a link to a configuration file are not provided. Required correction Provide the exact commands or a configuration file for the alignment generation and filtering steps to ensure reproducibility. Concern ID R1-m3 Severity Minor Axis Statistical rigor Affected element Section 2.4, Supplementary Table S10 Evidence pointer Section 2.4, Supplementary Table S10 Issue The classification analysis in Section 2.4 reports ROC-AUC and other metrics, but the manuscript does not state whether the differences between models are statistically significant. Given the small number of positive examples in some benchmarks (e.g., 23 stabilizing variants in S461), this is a concern. Required correction Report confidence intervals for the classification metrics, or at least acknowledge the limitations of the small sample sizes in the discussion. Concern ID R1-m4 Severity Minor Axis Presentation Affected element Section 2.6 Evidence pointer Section 2.6 Issue The residual analysis in Section 2.6 is interesting but the presentation is somewhat abrupt. The connection between the residual correlation and the ensemble's performance could be explained more intuitively. Required correction Add a sentence or two explaining why a high residual correlation with opposite signs for a fraction of variants leads to error cancellation, and what the practical implications are for model ensembling. Technical failings that need to be addressed before the case is established R1-M1: Lack of confidence intervals for primary accuracy metrics. R1-M2: Potential overstatement of the scope of the theoretical transitivity guarantee. Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality The idea of reformulating an existing predictor as a potential difference to enforce thermodynamic consistency is novel and elegant. The theoretical analysis of the ReLU head is a distinct contribution. This is not a simple application of existing methods. Scientific importance The problem of physical consistency in learned predictors is important for the field of protein stability prediction. The work provides a clear framework for addressing this, and the separation of consistency from accuracy is a valuable conceptual contribution. The practical impact is currently limited by the modest accuracy gains and the narrow scope of the exact guarantee. Interdisciplinary readership The work is relevant to computational biologists, biophysicists, and machine learning researchers. The main text is generally accessible, but the Methods section is highly technical. The potential for broader interest is moderate. Technical soundness The theoretical derivations appear sound. The empirical evaluation is reasonable but has limitations in statistical rigor (see R1-M1). The use of fixed, equal-weight averaging is well-justified. Readability for nonspecialists The abstract and introduction are clear. The Results section is dense but understandable. The Methods section is for specialists. The distinction between the two benefits (accuracy vs. consistency) is well-communicated. Recommendation posture Supportive if technical concerns are resolved. The core idea is promising and the theoretical analysis is a strength. However, the strength of the empirical claims needs to be backed by proper uncertainty quantification, and the scope of the theoretical guarantee needs to be stated more carefully. Once these are addressed, the manuscript would be a solid contribution. Risk / unsupported claims The claim that the ensemble "outperforms" both components on S669 and S96 is not fully supported without confidence intervals or significance testing. The claim of "exact same-site transitivity" is technically correct but could be misinterpreted as applying more broadly; the manuscript should be more explicit about its limited scope. The statement that the ensemble "matching the EvoPhi-DDG extension at the reported precision" on PTmul-NR is based on a very small benchmark and should be interpreted with caution. The manuscript states that the ensemble "reduces multisite pathway-closure RMSE relative to JanusDDG across all evaluated path lengths." While this is reported, the practical significance of a reduction from, e.g., 0.16 to 0.10 kcal/mol is not discussed. Is this level of error acceptable for practical applications?

构象熵变化高度异质 ：蛋白质构象熵并非均匀下降，而是由局部二级结构、序列背景和结构域类型共同调控。无序结构域（如结构域 11、16）损失构象熵，而含稳定 α-螺旋的结构域（如结构域 17）反而可能获得构象熵。 焓-熵补偿 ：伸展破坏蛋白质内部有利相互作用（不利焓变），但增强蛋白质-水相互作用（有利焓变），两者部分补偿，净自由能变化较小。 疏水水合机制 ：伸展暴露疏水表面，水分子在疏水表面附近形成更有序（低熵）的水合层，同时水-水氢键网络增强，这与疏水水合模型一致。 3) 可能的普适教训 [Analysis] 对 IDP 和弹性蛋白样序列，水的热力学贡献不可忽略，甚至可能主导力学响应。 蛋白质构象熵的「均一下降」假设过于简化；序列和结构背景决定局部熵响应方向。 焓-熵补偿是蛋白质-水系统的普遍特征，单独分析熵或焓都可能误导结论。 setup Input scope Full manuscript text (abstract, introduction, results, discussion, methods, figure legends) provided as plain text. No figures, tables, or supplementary files were available for direct inspection. Assessment boundary Assessment is limited to the scientific content, methodological soundness, and internal consistency of the claims as presented in the text. Statistical analyses, simulation details, and experimental validations are evaluated based on the descriptions provided. Shared manuscript claim summary The authors use multi-microsecond all-atom molecular dynamics simulations of a 225-residue "mini-tropoelastin" construct (domains 10-19 of human tropoelastin) to quantify protein conformational entropy, hydration-water entropy, and interaction enthalpies in free and fully extended states. They report that hydration-water entropy loss dominates the unfavorable entropic contribution to elastin stretching, exceeding the protein conformational entropy loss, and that opposing enthalpic contributions from disrupted intra-protein interactions and strengthened protein-water interactions largely compensate, yielding a small net free-energy change. Visible evidence base Text descriptions of Figures 1-7, Supplementary Figures S1-S10, Supplementary Tables, and Methods section. Numerical values for key thermodynamic quantities are reported in the text. Missing materials affecting confidence Actual figures, figure panels, supplementary figures, source data files, simulation parameter files, and convergence analyses were not available for direct examination. This limits verification of the quantitative results and the robustness of the statistical analyses. Reviewer Overall assessment This manuscript addresses a long-standing and important question in elastin biophysics: the molecular origin of entropic elasticity. The authors present a sophisticated computational approach that separately quantifies protein conformational and hydration-water entropy changes during stretching, which is a significant methodological advance over previous studies that treated the system as a whole. The central claim that hydration water provides the dominant unfavorable entropic contribution is clearly stated and supported by the reported numbers. However, several technical concerns regarding the interpretation of the fully extended state, the sensitivity of the entropy calculations to simulation parameters, and the generalizability of the mini-tropoelastin model to full-length elastin need to be addressed before the case is fully established. The manuscript is well-written and the thermodynamic decomposition framework is a valuable contribution to the field. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers in the fields of elastin biophysics, protein thermodynamics, intrinsically disordered proteins, and biomaterial design would be interested. The work provides a molecular-level resolution of the long-standing debate between rubber-elasticity and hydrophobic-hydration models of elastin, which has implications for understanding age-related elastin degradation and for designing elastin-mimetic biomaterials. The methodological framework for decomposing entropy into conformational and hydration contributions is also broadly applicable to other disordered proteins and hydrogels. Major strengths 1. The study directly addresses a 50-year-old controversy in elastin biophysics with a state-of-the-art computational approach. 2. The separation of protein conformational entropy and hydration-water entropy using established methods (dihedral-angle distributions and 2PT) is methodologically rigorous. 3. The use of multi-microsecond simulations represents a substantial improvement in sampling over previous computational studies of elastin. 4. The thermodynamic decomposition, including both entropic and enthalpic contributions, provides a more complete picture than entropy-only analyses. 5. The identification of sequence- and structure-dependent heterogeneity in the entropic response is a novel and informative finding. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Technical soundness Claim pointer The authors claim that the fully extended state serves as an appropriate reference state for isolating the thermodynamic consequences of chain extension, and that the free and fully extended states represent the endpoints needed to compute entropy and enthalpy changes. Evidence pointer Results and discussion, "Conformational entropy" section; Methods, "Molecular dynamics simulations of mini-tropoelastin" section; Figure 2b. Concern The fully extended state is generated by restraining only the terminal C-alpha atoms and stretching the chain to its contour length. This is an artificial construct that may not represent a physically relevant state. The authors acknowledge this is an "upper-bound molecular reference state," but the thermodynamic quantities derived from this state are used to draw conclusions about the mechanism of elastin elasticity. The choice of the fully extended state as an endpoint is critical because the entropy and enthalpy changes are computed as differences between the two states. If the fully extended state is not representative of the actual stretched state of elastin in tissue (where chains are cross-linked and not fully extended), the quantitative conclusions may not be directly applicable to the physiological mechanism. The authors should justify this choice more thoroughly and discuss how the results would change if a partially extended state were used instead. Why it matters The central conclusion that hydration water dominates the entropic penalty depends on the difference between the free and fully extended states. If the reference state is not physically meaningful, the quantitative decomposition of entropy and enthalpy changes is called into question, and the conclusions about the mechanism of elastin elasticity may not hold under physiological conditions. Resolution test The authors should provide a sensitivity analysis using partially extended states (e.g., 50%, 75% of full extension) to demonstrate that the qualitative conclusion (hydration water dominance) is robust to the choice of reference state. Alternatively, they should provide evidence that the fully extended state is representative of the stretched state of elastin in tissue, such as comparison with experimental force-extension curves or small-angle X-ray scattering data. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Technical soundness Claim pointer The authors report a protein-wide hydration entropy penalty of approximately 2024 kJ/mol (1583 kJ/mol translational + 441 kJ/mol rotational) and a conformational entropy penalty of 0.36 kJ/mol-res, concluding that hydration water is the dominant entropic contributor. Evidence pointer Results and discussion, "Hydration entropy" section; Figure 5a; Figure 7a. Concern The hydration entropy calculation relies on the 2PT method applied to 20-ps simulations with protein atoms position-restrained. The authors state that 2PT entropies converge within ~20 ps, but this is a very short timescale for capturing the full thermodynamic response of water to protein stretching. The position restraints on all protein atoms freeze the protein conformation, which may not allow the water structure to fully equilibrate to the stretched state. Additionally, the choice of the first hydration layer (FHL) cutoff at 0.41 nm is a critical parameter, and while the authors state the results are robust to variations (0.37-0.49 nm), the actual data for this sensitivity analysis is not shown. The 2PT method itself has known limitations for highly confined water, and the authors do not discuss potential artifacts. Why it matters The quantitative claim that hydration water dominates the entropic penalty is the central finding of the paper. If the 2PT calculations are not converged or are sensitive to the FHL definition, the quantitative conclusion could be significantly altered. The use of position restraints may also bias the water entropy calculation by preventing protein-water coupled fluctuations that could contribute to the entropy. Resolution test The authors should provide convergence tests for the 2PT calculations (e.g., 50 ps, 100 ps simulations) and show the sensitivity of the results to the FHL cutoff in a supplementary figure. They should also discuss the potential artifacts of position restraints on the water entropy calculation and, if possible, perform a test with harmonically restrained (rather than fixed) protein atoms to allow some protein flexibility. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Scientific importance Claim pointer The authors state that "hydration water provides the dominant unfavorable entropic contribution" to elastin stretching, and that this supports a "hydration-coupled thermodynamic mechanism" for elastin elasticity. Evidence pointer Abstract; Results and discussion, "Thermodynamic summary" section; Figure 7. Concern The authors compare their results to experimental studies that report system-level entropy changes, but the connection between the simulated mini-tropoelastin and the macroscopic elastin fiber is not fully established. The mini-tropoelastin is a monomeric fragment, whereas elastin in tissue is a highly cross-linked polymer network. The authors acknowledge this limitation but do not discuss how cross-linking might alter the relative contributions of conformational and hydration entropy. Cross-linking could restrict conformational entropy more than hydration entropy, potentially changing the balance. Additionally, the fully extended state of a single chain may not be representative of the deformation of a cross-linked network, where chains are stretched to varying degrees. Why it matters The claim that hydration water is the dominant entropic contributor is presented as a general mechanism for elastin elasticity. If this conclusion is specific to the monomeric, non-cross-linked system studied here, its relevance to the physiological function of elastin is limited. The authors should more carefully qualify their conclusions and discuss how cross-linking might affect the thermodynamic balance. Resolution test The authors should add a discussion section on the implications of cross-linking for their conclusions. They could also perform simulations of a cross-linked mini-tropoelastin dimer or trimer to test whether the relative contributions of conformational and hydration entropy change upon cross-linking. Concern ID R1-M4 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Technical soundness Claim pointer The authors report that the fully extended state has a more homogeneous water environment, with narrower distributions of molar entropies, and that this is due to the loss of secondary structure and the uniform exposure of the protein surface. Evidence pointer Results and discussion, "Hydration entropy" section; Figure 5a insets; Figure 6. Concern The interpretation of the water dynamics data (C2(t) and MSD) is somewhat superficial. The authors report reorientation times and diffusion coefficients but do not provide a detailed analysis of the spatial heterogeneity of these dynamical properties. The claim that the extended state has a "more homogeneous" water environment is based on the width of the entropy distributions, but this could be an artifact of the FHL definition or the limited sampling in the extended state. A more detailed spatial analysis (e.g., water dynamics near specific residue types or secondary structure elements) would strengthen the interpretation. Why it matters The structural and dynamical analysis of water is presented as supporting evidence for the hydration entropy calculations. If the interpretation of the water dynamics is not rigorous, the supporting evidence is weakened, and the reader may question the robustness of the main conclusions. Resolution test The authors should provide a more detailed spatial analysis of water dynamics, such as residue-specific or domain-specific water entropy maps, to support the claim of increased homogeneity in the extended state. They should also discuss the potential limitations of the static indexing approach for the C2(t) and MSD calculations. Minor Comments Concern ID R1-m1 Severity Minor Axis Readability for nonspecialists Affected element Introduction, Figure 1 Evidence pointer Figure 1 and accompanying text Issue The description of the competing models (rubber-elasticity vs. hydrophobic-hydration) in the introduction is clear, but the schematic in Figure 1 is not available for inspection. The text refers to "competing entropic models" and "major entropic transitions" but does not provide a clear verbal summary of the key differences between the models for a reader who cannot see the figure. Required correction Add a brief verbal summary in the text that describes the key predictions of each model (e.g., rubber-elasticity predicts dominant conformational entropy loss; hydrophobic-hydration predicts dominant hydration entropy loss) so that the reader can follow the argument without needing to interpret the figure. Concern ID R1-m2 Severity Minor Axis Technical soundness Affected element Methods, "Conformational entropy of protein" section Evidence pointer Methods section, equation 4 Issue The description of the conformational entropy calculation is brief. The authors state they use the method of ref. 28 but do not provide sufficient detail for a reader to reproduce the calculation without consulting the original reference. In particular, the treatment of side-chain rotamers and the handling of residues with multiple chi angles could be clarified. Required correction Expand the Methods section to include more detail on the entropy calculation, such as the exact binning scheme for side-chain chi angles, the treatment of terminal residues, and the number of frames used for convergence. Concern ID R1-m3 Severity Minor Axis Interdisciplinary readership Affected element Results and discussion, "Implications, limitations, and outlook" section Evidence pointer Final section of Results and discussion Issue The discussion of biomaterial design implications is brief and somewhat generic. The authors mention "tuning amino acid sequence, domain organization, and hydration" but do not provide specific examples of how their findings could guide the design of elastin-mimetic materials. Required correction Add a few concrete examples of how the identified hydration-driven mechanism could be exploited in material design (e.g., modifying hydration by incorporating hydrophilic residues, or designing sequences that modulate the balance between conformational and hydration entropy). Concern ID R1-m4 Severity Minor Axis Technical soundness Affected element Methods, "Error analysis and statistical testing" section Evidence pointer Methods section Issue The statistical analysis is limited to t-tests for selected comparisons. Given the complexity of the simulation data and the multiple comparisons made across domains and residue types, a more comprehensive statistical framework (e.g., correction for multiple comparisons) would be appropriate. Required correction The authors should either apply a multiple-comparison correction to their t-tests or justify why this is not necessary. They should also report effect sizes or confidence intervals for the key comparisons. Risk / unsupported claims The claim that hydration water is the "dominant" entropic contributor is supported by the reported numbers, but the sensitivity of this conclusion to the choice of reference state (fully extended) and to the 2PT parameters is not fully established. This is a risk if the fully extended state is not representative of physiological stretching. The claim that the findings support a "hydration-coupled thermodynamic mechanism" for elastin elasticity is an interpretation that goes beyond the direct simulation results. The simulations show correlations between hydration entropy and surface exposure, but do not establish causality. The generalizability of the findings from mini-tropoelastin to full-length, cross-linked elastin is not demonstrated and is acknowledged as a limitation. The claim that the mechanism is relevant to elastin's physiological function is therefore not fully supported. The comparison to experimental NMR data (ref. 13) is qualitative and relies on the assumption that the simulated system captures the same physics as the experimental system. The authors should be more careful in drawing direct comparisons between simulation and experiment. The statement that "no study has provided an atomistic, direct, and quantitative comparison" of the relevant thermodynamic quantities is a strong claim that is difficult to verify without a comprehensive literature search. The authors should soften this claim or provide more evidence that such a comparison has not been made.

本文通过基准测试多种结构/序列及机器学习/深度学习致病性预测器，发现折叠稳定性计算（Foldetta）和深度学习方法（ESM1b、AlphaMissense）在默认设置下对 SYNGAP1 错义变异致病性预测准确率最高，并通过阈值优化进一步提升性能，同时揭示了致病变异在 GAP/PH 结构域富集、相分离影响位点与磷酸化位点共定位的结构规律，最终开发了整合多源预测的 SGM 在线服务器。 03 研究问题 具体问题 : 如何准确评估 SYNGAP1 错义变异的致病性？哪些计算预测器对 SYNGAP1 最有效？致病变异在 SynGAP 蛋白结构上呈现怎样的分布规律？ 为什么重要 : SYNGAP1 相关疾病（SRD）是严重的神经发育障碍，约 65% 的 ClinVar 错义变异被归类为意义不明确变异（VUS），实验验证困难且昂贵，亟需可靠的计算预测工具辅助临床诊断。 现有方法不足 : ① 预测器性能具有蛋白特异性，缺乏针对 SYNGAP1 的系统评估；② 默认阈值可能不适用于特定基因；③ 现有工具分散在不同平台，缺乏整合资源；④ 对无序区域（IDR）变异和相分离相关变异的评估不足。 精确研究问题 : 能否通过系统基准测试和基因特异性阈值优化，建立一套对 SYNGAP1 错义变异致病性具有高准确率和覆盖率的最佳计算预测方案，并揭示其结构基础？ 04 背景与发展脉络 本文核心公式为评估指标和阈值优化方法，具体如下： Youden's J 统计量 （用于阈值优化）: J = Sensitivity + Specificity − 1 = TPR − FPR - 其中 TPR = TP/(TP+FN)，FPR = FP/(FP+TN) - 用途: 选择使 J 最大化的分类阈值，平衡敏感性和特异性 - 直觉: J 值越大，分类器在区分正负类上的综合能力越强 Matthews 相关系数 (MCC) : MCC = (TP×TN − FP×FN) / √[(TP+FP)(TP+FN)(TN+FP)(TN+FN)] - 用途: 评估二分类性能，对类别不平衡不敏感 - 直觉: 取值范围 [−1, 1]，1 为完美预测，0 为随机预测 Phi 系数 (φ) （用于预测器间一致性分析）: φ = (n₁₁×n₀₀ − n₁₀×n₀₁) / √(n₁₊×n₀₊×n₊₁×n₊₀) - 用途: 衡量两个二分类预测器之间的一致性 - 直觉: 与 MCC 数学等价，用于评估预测器间的共识程度 ROC-AUC （用于评估判别能力）: AUC = ∫₀¹ TPR(FPR⁻¹(x)) dx - 用途: 衡量分类器在所有可能阈值下的综合判别能力 - 直觉: 0.5 为随机猜测，1.0 为完美判别 10 实验设计与证据链 数据集 : ClinVar 中 本身存在标注偏差（致病变异多来自已发表病例，良性变异多来自人群测序），且部分标注可能基于计算预测而非实验验证。 端到端状态 : 本文是 评估研究 而非端到端预测系统开发；SGM 服务器是信息整合平台，不提供新的预测算法。 算力成本 : 未提供具体算力需求；MD 模拟（211 个变异 × 3 重复 × 150 ns）成本较高，但已预先完成。 历史数据依赖 : 预测器性能高度依赖 ClinVar 标注质量；随着新变异不断提交，性能需重新评估。 模型依赖 : AlphaMissense 和 ESM1b 为预训练模型，其训练数据包含大量蛋白序列/结构，对 SYNGAP1 的适用性受预训练分布影响。 最难情形 : IDR 区域的错义变异预测可靠性最低；位于结构域边界或影响蛋白-蛋白相互作用界面的变异难以通过折叠稳定性方法捕捉。 群体/领域边界 : 结论仅适用于 SYNGAP1；对其他基因的推广需重新基准测试。SGM 服务器面向 SRD 诊断和研究群体。 有边界的复述 : 在 ClinVar 标注的 SYNGAP1 错义变异上，折叠稳定性计算和深度学习方法（特别是阈值优化后的 AlphaMissense）能提供高准确率的致病性预测；致病变异主要富集于 GAP/PH 结构域；IDR 区域的相分离影响位点与磷酸化位点共定位，提示非折叠相关致病机制；SGM 服务器整合了这些资源供临床和研究使用。 12 作者自认局限 局限 具体表现 作者提出的未来方向 来源 基准测试集规模有限 仅 191 个明确标注的变异（128 良性 + 63 致病） 随着更多 ClinVar 标注积累，需重新评估和校准 Discussion 节 ClinVar 标注偏差 标注可能受计算预测影响，存在循环验证风险 使用实验验证的变异集进行独立评估 Discussion 节 Review setup Input scope Full manuscript text Assessment boundary Scientific content, methodology, claims, and conclusions as presented in the provided text Shared manuscript claim summary The authors benchmark multiple in silico pathogenicity predictors against clinically curated SYNGAP1 missense variants, identify top performers (folding stability calculations, ESM1b, AlphaMissense), optimize thresholds for improved accuracy, describe structural enrichment patterns of pathogenic variants, propose a link between missense variation and phase separation/phosphoregulation, and present a new web server (SGM) for variant assessment. Visible evidence base Abstract, Introduction, Results (Sections 2.1–2.7), Discussion, Conclusions, Methods (Sections 5.1–5.8), Data Availability Statement Missing materials affecting confidence Figures 1–6, Tables 1 and S1–S12, Supporting Information text and equations, Supplementary Figures S1–S8, benchmark dataset details, server implementation details Reviewer Overall assessment This manuscript addresses a clinically relevant problem, the interpretation of SYNGAP1 missense variants, using a broad panel of computational predictors. The benchmarking approach is systematic, and the development of a publicly accessible server is a valuable community resource. However, the study's core conclusions are limited by the small and potentially biased benchmark set, the lack of experimental validation, and the absence of key methodological details in the provided text. The claims regarding phase separation and phosphoregulation are largely speculative and require further support. The manuscript is technically sound in its computational execution but the clinical utility of the proposed framework remains to be established. Who would be interested in the results, and why Clinical geneticists and molecular diagnosticians interpreting SYNGAP1 variants, researchers studying SYNGAP1-related disorders, computational biologists developing and benchmarking variant effect predictors, and the broader neurodevelopmental disease community. The SGM server provides a practical tool for variant assessment. Major strengths 1. Systematic benchmarking of a wide range of predictors, from traditional sequence-based to state-of-the-art deep learning methods. 2. Gene-specific threshold optimization with cross-validation, demonstrating a clear improvement for AlphaMissense. 3. Identification of structural domain enrichment patterns that align with biological expectations. 4. The SGM server is a practical, accessible resource that integrates multiple data types and provides AI-generated summaries. 5. The study highlights important limitations of current predictors for disordered regions. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Benchmark dataset adequacy Claim pointer The benchmark set is described as "limited but carefully curated" and is used to draw strong conclusions about predictor performance and to calibrate thresholds for clinical use. Evidence pointer Section 5.2, Figure 1d, Tables 1 and S1–S3 Concern The benchmark set contains only 191 clinically labeled variants (75 benign, 53 likely benign, 21 pathogenic, 42 likely pathogenic). This is a very small sample for evaluating and calibrating predictors, especially for a gene with a high burden of pathogenic missense variation. The set is likely imbalanced and may not represent the full spectrum of SYNGAP1 variants. The inclusion of "conflicting" variants reclassified based on submission counts is a subjective criterion that could introduce bias. The small sample size raises concerns about overfitting during threshold optimization, despite the cross-validation approach. Why it matters The clinical utility of the SGM server and the recommended thresholds depend entirely on the quality and representativeness of this benchmark set. If the set is biased or too small, the reported performance metrics and optimized thresholds may not generalize to real-world clinical cases, potentially leading to misclassification. Resolution test Provide a detailed breakdown of the benchmark set, including the distribution of variants across protein domains and disorder regions. Justify the reclassification of conflicting variants with explicit criteria. Perform a power analysis to demonstrate that the sample size is sufficient to detect meaningful performance differences. Ideally, validate the optimized thresholds on an independent, larger cohort of SYNGAP1 variants with functional or clinical data. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Validation of predictions Claim pointer The manuscript claims that top-performing predictors, especially optimized AlphaMissense, provide accurate predictions for SYNGAP1 variant pathogenicity. Evidence pointer Sections 2.1–2.2, Figure 2, Tables 1 and S3 Concern The benchmarking is entirely computational, relying on ClinVar labels as ground truth. There is no experimental validation of any predictions, such as functional assays or protein stability measurements. The authors acknowledge that "rigorous testing with any such sets cannot guarantee prediction accuracy" but still present the optimized thresholds as suitable for clinical use. The only experimental dataset mentioned is from a prior study (Meili et al., N = 57), which is not used for validation here. Why it matters ClinVar labels themselves can be incorrect or biased, especially for variants in genes with limited functional data. Without experimental validation, the true accuracy of the predictors, and particularly the optimized AlphaMissense thresholds, remains unknown. This limits the confidence with which the SGM server can be used for clinical decision-making. Resolution test Validate the predictions against an independent experimental dataset, such as the Meili et al. stability measurements or functional assays for a subset of variants. If experimental data are not available, clearly state this as a major limitation and temper the clinical recommendations accordingly. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Phase separation and phosphoregulation claims Claim pointer The manuscript proposes that missense variants in disordered regions, particularly those affecting phosphosites, could alter phase separation behavior and contribute to SYNGAP1-related disorder pathogenesis. Evidence pointer Section 2.6, Figure 5, Tables S9–S12 Concern This section is largely speculative. The identification of 70 PS-impacting variants by PSMutPred is a computational prediction with no experimental validation. The colocalization analysis between phosphosites and PS-impacting variants, while statistically significant, is a correlative observation. The claim that these regions "could act as phase separation-promoting segments" is presented as a plausible mechanism but is not directly tested. The functional significance of the specific variants identified is unknown. Why it matters This is a potentially important biological insight, but as presented, it is a hypothesis-generating observation rather than a demonstrated mechanism. Overstating these findings could mislead readers about the established role of these variants in disease. Resolution test Soften the language to clearly frame this as a hypothesis. Provide additional computational or experimental support, such as predictions from multiple PS prediction tools, analysis of known phase-separation-promoting sequence features, or preliminary experimental data on variant effects on phase separation. Concern ID R1-M4 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Reproducibility and transparency Claim pointer The SGM server is presented as a comprehensive resource, and the methods are described as reproducible. Evidence pointer Sections 5.3–5.7, Data Availability Statement Concern The provided text lacks critical details for reproducibility. The exact versions and parameters for all predictors are not specified. The criteria for MD-based classification of variants as "potentially pathogenic, benign, or uncertain" are described as "visually observed structural impacts," which is subjective and not quantifiable. The AI-generated summaries are produced by a model (gpt-oss-20b) whose specific prompt and output validation process are not described in detail. Why it matters For a resource intended for clinical use, transparency and reproducibility are essential. Subjective classification criteria and undocumented parameters undermine confidence in the results and prevent others from replicating or independently verifying the findings. Resolution test Provide a detailed supplementary methods section with exact software versions, parameters, and analysis pipelines. For MD-based classifications, provide quantitative criteria or a rubric for the visual assessment. Describe the AI prompt and any quality control measures for the generated summaries. Minor Comments Concern ID R1-m1 Severity Minor Axis Clarity of writing Affected element Section 2.1, Figure 2 Evidence pointer "Figure 2 and Tables 1 and S1" Issue The text states that "substantial overlap in the bootstrap confidence intervals" indicates similar performance, but this is not a rigorous statistical comparison. The figure and tables are not available for review. Required correction Provide a formal statistical test for comparing predictor performance, such as a DeLong test for AUC differences, and report the results clearly. Concern ID R1-m2 Severity Minor Axis Terminology Affected element Section 2.2, "AlphaMissense: Optimized" Evidence pointer "the optimized AlphaMissense classification scheme was incorporated into the SGM server as 'AlphaMissense: Optimized'" Issue The term "optimized" is used without specifying the exact optimization criterion beyond Youden's J. It is unclear if this refers to a single or dual threshold. Required correction Clarify the optimization procedure, including the specific objective function and whether single or dual thresholds were used. Concern ID R1-m3 Severity Minor Axis Data presentation Affected element Section 2.5, Figure 4 Evidence pointer "Figure 4a,b and S5" Issue The text mentions "relative enrichment" and "pathogenic density" but the exact calculation methods are not described in the main text. Required correction Define these metrics explicitly in the Methods section or refer to the Supporting Information for the formulas. Concern ID R1-m4 Severity Minor Axis Literature context Affected element Section 3, Discussion Evidence pointer "To our knowledge, ACMG evidence-strength thresholds have not been calibrated for SYNGAP1 yet" Issue This claim is not supported by a citation or a literature search description. Required correction Provide a reference or state that a systematic literature search was conducted to support this claim. Concern ID R1-m5 Severity Minor Axis Accessibility Affected element Section 5.7, SGM server Evidence pointer "optimized for laptops or desktop computers" Issue The server is not optimized for mobile devices, which may limit its accessibility for some users. Required correction Acknowledge this limitation and consider providing a mobile-friendly version or a clear statement about the recommended browsing environment. Technical failings that need to be addressed before the case is established 1. The benchmark set is too small and potentially biased to support the strong claims about predictor performance and threshold optimization. 2. The lack of experimental validation for any predictions, particularly the optimized AlphaMissense thresholds, is a critical gap. 3. The subjective nature of MD-based variant classification needs to be replaced with quantitative criteria. 4. The phase separation and phosphoregulation claims are speculative and need to be framed as such or supported by additional evidence. Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality Moderate. The application of a broad panel of predictors to SYNGAP1 is somewhat novel, but the general approach of benchmarking in silico predictors is well-established. The SGM server is a useful contribution but not conceptually novel. Scientific importance High for the SYNGAP1 community. The study addresses a real clinical need for better variant interpretation tools. However, the impact is limited by the lack of experimental validation and the small benchmark set. Interdisciplinary readership Moderate. The topic is relevant to clinical genetics, computational biology, and neuroscience. The writing is generally accessible, but the heavy reliance on computational details may limit appeal to a broader audience. Technical soundness The computational methods are generally sound, but the small benchmark set and subjective classification criteria are significant weaknesses. The cross-validation approach is appropriate but does not fully mitigate the risk of overfitting. Readability for nonspecialists The abstract and introduction are clear, but the results and methods sections are dense and assume familiarity with variant effect prediction. The manuscript would benefit from a more accessible summary of the key findings and their implications. Recommendation posture Supportive if technical concerns are resolved. The manuscript addresses an important problem and presents a potentially valuable resource. However, the current evidence does not fully support the strength of the claims made. The authors must address the concerns regarding benchmark set size and bias, provide experimental validation or clearly state its absence as a major limitation, and improve the transparency and reproducibility of their methods. If these issues are adequately resolved, the manuscript could make a meaningful contribution to the field.

01 基本信息 标题 ：Quantum-accurate enhanced sampling and mini-protein folding through replica exchange for multiscale neural network potentials 作者 ：Solazzo, Riccardo; Gordiy, Igor; Riniker, Sereina 单位 ：未提供（推测为 ETH Zürich，Riniker 课题组） 期刊/平台 ：Chemical Science 年份 ：2026 论文类型 ：方法学 + 应用验证 领域 ：计算化学 / 生物物理 / 机器学习势函数 / 增强采样 关键词 ：Neural network potentials (NNPs), ML/MM, REST2, enhanced sampling, mini-protein folding, chignolin, CLN025 DOI/arXiv ：10.1039/d6sc04555c 代码 ：https://github.com/rinikerlab/rest2_ampmm 数据 ：起始坐标、配置文件、运行代码在 GitHub；原始 MD 数据可向通讯作者索取 阅读日期 ：2026-11-10 在本课题方向中的位置 ：该文将经典增强采样方法 REST2 与 ML/MM 多尺度神经网络势（AMPv3-EE-BMS25）结合，实现了无需预定义反应坐标的 mini-protein 折叠模拟，处于「AI 势函数 × 增强采样 × 构象采样」交叉点，为蛋白质结构预测/构象生成提供了新工具。 02 一句话总结 该文提出一种与 ML/MM 框架兼容的 REST2 类副本交换增强采样算法（REST2-AMP/MM），通过直接缩放 NNP 能量项实现选择性溶质升温，在保持近 DFT 精度的同时，成功从伸展构象自主折叠 chignolin 和 CLN025 两个 mini-protein。 03 研究问题 具体问题 ：如何将 REST2 类增强采样算法推广到 ML/MM 多尺度神经网络势框架中，以实现无需预定义反应坐标的高精度构象采样和 mini-protein 折叠？ 为什么重要 ：ML/MM 模拟虽具近 QM 精度，但计算成本仍高于经典力场，且生物相关构象转变（如蛋白质折叠）涉及高能垒，需要增强采样才能在实际时间尺度内完成。现有增强采样方法（如 metadynamics、umbrella sampling）需要预定义反应坐标，对未知折叠路径的系统不适用。 现有方法不足 ： 反应坐标类方法（metadynamics 等）需先验知识，不适用于未知构象空间。 温度副本交换（TRE）需要大量副本，计算成本高。 标准 QM/MM 哈密顿量不可分离，无法直接应用 REST2 的参数缩放策略。 尚无 REST2 类方法被实现于 ML/MM 框架。 精确研究问题 ：Can a REST2-like replica exchange scheme be implemented for ML/MM simulations by directly scaling the NNP energy terms, and can it enable reaction-coordinate-free folding of mini-proteins with near-DFT accuracy? 04 背景与发展脉络 注：此脉络基于本文引言及作者引用，经外部核验部分已标注。 QM/MM 多尺度模拟（1976–至今） ：Levitt, Warshel, Karplus 提出 QM/MM 方案，在关键区域保持 QM 精度，环境用 MM 描述。局限：计算成本高，时间尺度受限。 神经网络势（NNP）兴起（2011–至今） ：从 Behler-Parrinello 到等变架构（如 NequIP、MACE），NNP 以接近 QM 精度、远低于 QM 成本的优势成为 QM 替代方案。AMP 系列模型（Anisotropic Message Passing）支持静电嵌入，适合 ML/MM。 增强采样方法发展 ： - 反应坐标类：umbrella sampling、metadynamics、WE 等，需先验知识。 - 广义系综类：TRE、REST/REST2 等，无需反应坐标，但 TRE 副本数多、成本高。 - REST2 通过仅升温溶质、保持溶剂温度，大幅减少副本数，已在经典力场中广泛应用。 ML/MM 增强采样现状 ：已有工作将 metadynamics 等与 ML/MM 结合，但均需反应坐标；广义系综类方法在 ML/MM 中尚属空白。 本文位置 ：首次将 REST2 类算法实现于 ML/MM 框架，利用 AMP 模型哈密顿量的可分解性，直接缩放能量项而非力场参数，填补了「ML/MM × 广义系综增强采样」的空白。 05 核心痛点 痛点 表现 成因或作者解释 文中证据 ML/MM 模拟时间尺度受限 生物相关构象转变（如折叠）涉及高能垒，常规 MD 无法在可及时间内跨越 NNP 虽比 QM 快，但仍比经典力场慢数个数量级；高能垒需要增强采样 Introduction: "ML/MM MD simulations remain slower than those with classical force fields... will require the use of enhanced-sampling techniques" 现有增强采样需反应坐标 metadynamics、umbrella sampling 等需预定义集体变量，对未知折叠路径不适用 反应坐标类方法本质依赖先验知识 Introduction: "a key limitation of these methods is the requirement for a priori knowledge of the process" 标准 QM/MM 哈密顿量不可分离 无法将溶质/溶剂能量项独立缩放 QM 区域的能量来自单一 SCF 计算，不可分解 Introduction: "no such decomposition is available for a standard electrostatic-embedding QM/MM Hamiltonian" REST2 参数缩放策略不适用于 NNP NNP 无显式力场参数（电荷、LJ ε、扭转常数）可缩放 NNP 的能量由网络内部表征，参数不可直接映射到物理量 Results: "This parameter-level route is not available to AMP: all multipoles... are predicted internally by the NNP rather than assigned as fixed parameters" 高缩放因子下结构不稳定 强升温可能导致键长/键角非物理畸变 溶质内能大幅降低后，缺乏维持几何完整性的机制 Results: "U_r represents optional scaled harmonic bond and angle restraints, which are applied to prevent unphysical distortions" 06 核心思想 1) 表面方法 ： - 将 REST2 算法适配到 AMP/MM 框架，通过直接缩放 NNP 输出的能量项（EML 和 EML–MM）实现选择性溶质升温。 - 引入可选的缩放谐波键/角约束（Ur），在高缩放因子下维持结构完整性。 - 使用标准 Metropolis 判据进行副本交换，保持详细平衡。 2) 核心洞察 ： - AMP 模型的哈密顿量天然可分解为 EML（ML 区内部）、EML–MM（ML-MM 相互作用）和 EMM（MM 区内部）三项，这为 REST2 所需的能量项独立缩放提供了物理基础。 - 与经典力场不同，NNP 没有可缩放的显式参数，但能量项本身是可微函数，可以直接缩放——这绕过了参数级缩放的限制。 - 缩放 EML 和 EML–MM 等价于降低溶质内能和溶质-溶剂相互作用，从而有效升温溶质，而溶剂保持物理温度。 3) 可能的普适教训 [Analysis] ： - 对于任意可分解哈密顿量的 ML 势（不仅是 AMP），只要能量项可分离，REST2 类方法即可推广。这为其他等变 NNP（如 MACE、NequIP）与增强采样的结合提供了通用路径。 - Assessment boundary Technical and scientific evaluation of the REST2-AMP/MM method, its implementation, validation, and reported results. No assessment of editorial fit or journal policy. Shared manuscript claim summary The authors present a REST2-like enhanced sampling scheme for multiscale ML/MM simulations using the AMPv3-EE-BMS25 neural network potential. They claim that the approximate separability of the AMP Hamiltonian into solute-solute, solute-solvent, and solvent-solvent terms enables effective solute tempering, and demonstrate enhanced conformational sampling, partial refolding of misfolded peptides, and reaction-coordinate-free folding of chignolin and CLN025 mini-proteins with near-DFT accuracy. Visible evidence base Full text with equations, figure references, table references, and supplementary material descriptions. Figures and tables themselves are not directly viewable; only their captions and in-text descriptions are available. Missing materials affecting confidence Actual figures, tables, and supplementary information files are not provided. Raw simulation data, convergence analyses, and detailed validation results referenced in the text and SI are not accessible. This limits quantitative verification of several claims. Reviewer Overall assessment The manuscript presents a conceptually interesting and technically relevant extension of REST2 enhanced sampling to ML/MM frameworks. The core idea of exploiting the approximate separability of the AMP Hamiltonian is well motivated and clearly explained. The validation across multiple peptide systems of increasing complexity is commendable. However, several technical aspects require clarification and additional evidence to fully establish the method's robustness and the strength of the folding claims. The lack of direct access to figures and SI data limits the depth of verification possible. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers in computational chemistry and biophysics working on enhanced sampling methods, machine learning potentials, and protein folding simulations. The work is also relevant to those developing multiscale simulation methods and seeking to apply ML-based potentials to biologically relevant timescales. Major strengths The manuscript addresses a clear gap in the field by extending REST2 to ML/MM frameworks. The theoretical justification for the Hamiltonian decomposition is well articulated. The validation strategy is systematic, progressing from simple dipeptides to mini-protein folding. The use of a global, transferable model without fine-tuning strengthens the practical relevance. The discussion of limitations, particularly regarding equilibrium folding populations, is honest and appropriate. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Technical soundness Claim pointer The claim that the approximate separability of the AMP Hamiltonian into EML, EML-MM, and EMM terms is "in practice, an accurate approximation" for REST2 scaling. Evidence pointer Introduction, paragraph 4; Results and discussion, "Implementation of REST2 in the AMP/MM framework" section. Concern The manuscript acknowledges that polarization energy is absorbed into the EML term through environment-dependent node embeddings, yet the magnitude of this effect is only referenced to a previous publication (ref. 35) and a single parameter value (λpol = 0.35). The accuracy of the separability approximation is central to the validity of the entire REST2-AMP/MM approach. Without direct evidence in this manuscript quantifying the error introduced by this approximation across the tested systems, the core methodological premise is not fully established. Why it matters If the polarization contribution is not negligible for certain solute-solvent configurations, the scaling of EML and EML-MM would not correctly reproduce the intended effective temperature of the solute, potentially biasing the sampled ensemble and compromising the accuracy of the results. Resolution test Provide a quantitative analysis of the magnitude of the polarization energy relative to EML and EML-MM for representative configurations of each tested system. Show that the error in the scaled Hamiltonian due to the approximate separability is small compared to thermal energy (kBT) across the replica ladder. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Technical soundness Claim pointer The claim that REST2-AMP/MM achieves "folding of the mini-proteins chignolin and CLN025 from extended conformations" and that the simulations "demonstrate recovery of the experimentally characterized folded conformations." Evidence pointer Results and discussion, "Reaction-coordinate-free folding simulations" section; Figures 6 and 7. Concern The manuscript states that the simulations reach a plateau at approximately 0.2 nm Cα-RMSD, but the figures and detailed trajectory analyses are not available for inspection. The distinction between reaching a folded-like state and demonstrating true folding is subtle. The authors correctly note that equilibrium folding populations are not established, but the claim of "folding" from extended conformations requires more robust evidence, such as analysis of multiple independent trajectories, assessment of the fraction of trajectories that fold, and comparison of the folded ensemble with the experimental structure beyond a single RMSD metric. Why it matters The central demonstration of the method's capability rests on these folding simulations. If the evidence is limited to a single trajectory or a few trajectories that happen to reach a folded-like state, the claim of robust folding capability is overstated. The field has established standards for demonstrating folding, including multiple independent runs and statistical analysis of folding probabilities. Resolution test Provide data from multiple independent folding simulations for both chignolin and CLN025. Report the fraction of trajectories that reach the folded basin, the distribution of folding times, and a comparison of the folded ensemble with the experimental structure using multiple structural metrics (e.g., contact maps, secondary structure content). Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Technical soundness Claim pointer The claim that the REST2-AMP/MM approach "enables access to biologically relevant timescales while maintaining near-DFT accuracy." Evidence pointer Abstract; Results and discussion, "Enhanced conformational sampling of small peptides" section; Table S2. Concern The computational cost of the simulations is only briefly mentioned, with wall-clock performance reported in Table S2 (not accessible). The claim of accessing biologically relevant timescales is not quantified in the main text. The total simulation lengths (20-60 ns) are relatively short for folding studies, and the effective speedup compared to conventional MD or other enhanced sampling methods is not clearly stated. Why it matters The practical utility of the method depends on its computational efficiency. Without a clear quantification of the speedup and the computational resources required, it is difficult to assess whether the method offers a significant advantage over existing approaches. Resolution test Provide a detailed analysis of computational cost, including total GPU hours, speedup relative to conventional AMP/MM simulations, and a comparison with other enhanced sampling methods applied to similar systems. Quantify the effective sampling acceleration achieved by the REST2 scheme. Minor Comments Concern ID R1-m1 Severity Minor Axis Clarity and reproducibility Affected element Methods, "REST2-AMP/MM simulations" section Evidence pointer Table 1 Issue The manuscript states that REST2 parameters are "system dependent and therefore must be established empirically" but does not provide guidance on how to choose these parameters for new systems. The scaling factor ranges and distributions are given in Table 1, but the rationale for these choices is not fully explained. Required correction Add a brief discussion of the criteria used to select the scaling factor ranges and distributions, and provide practical guidance for parameter selection in future applications. Concern ID R1-m2 Severity Minor Axis Technical soundness Affected element Results and discussion, "Enhanced conformational sampling of small peptides" section Evidence pointer Figure 2D Issue The comparison between REST2-AMP/MM and conventional AMP/MM for alanine dipeptide uses different total simulation times (20 ns for REST2 vs. 160 ns for conventional). While this is appropriate for demonstrating efficiency, the manuscript does not clearly state whether the conventional simulations were long enough to converge the free-energy landscape. Required correction Clarify whether the conventional simulations were converged and, if so, provide evidence of convergence (e.g., block analysis or comparison of independent runs). Concern ID R1-m3 Severity Minor Axis Clarity and reproducibility Affected element Methods, "Analysis" section Evidence pointer Equation 5 Issue The definition of RMSDdist is clear, but the choice of atoms used for the calculation is only described as "selected atoms (default: non-hydrogen atoms)". It is unclear whether the same atom selection was used for all systems and whether the results are sensitive to this choice. Required correction Specify the exact atom selection used for each system and discuss the sensitivity of the results to this choice. Concern ID R1-m4 Severity Minor Axis Technical soundness Affected element Results and discussion, "Partial folding of peptide systems" section Evidence pointer Figure 5 Issue The Trp- cage refolding experiment uses a modified structure where the α-helix is replaced by a coil. The manuscript does not describe how this modified structure was generated or whether it represents a realistic misfolded state. Required correction Provide details on the construction of the misfolded Trp-cage structure and justify its relevance as a test case. Technical failings that need to be addressed before the case is established R1-M1 and R1-M2 are blocking concerns. The separability approximation must be quantitatively validated, and the folding claims must be supported by more robust statistical evidence from multiple trajectories. Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality: High. The extension of REST2 to ML/MM frameworks is a novel contribution that addresses a real need in the field. Scientific importance: Moderate to high. The method has potential to enable enhanced sampling with quantum accuracy, which is relevant to many biophysical applications. Interdisciplinary readership: Moderate. The work will primarily interest computational chemists and biophysicists, with potential appeal to a broader structural biology audience. Technical soundness: Currently not fully established. The core methodological premise requires additional validation, and the folding claims need stronger statistical support. Readability for nonspecialists: Good. The manuscript is clearly written and the concepts are explained accessibly, though some familiarity with enhanced sampling and ML potentials is assumed. Recommendation posture Supportive if technical concerns are resolved. The core idea is promising and the validation strategy is thoughtful, but the blocking concerns regarding the separability approximation and the robustness of the folding claims must be addressed before the case is fully established. Risk / unsupported claims The claim that the separability of the AMP Hamiltonian is "in practice, an accurate approximation" is not directly supported by data in this manuscript; it relies on a reference to a previous publication. The claim of "folding" of chignolin and CLN025 from extended conformations is not fully supported without evidence of multiple independent folding events and statistical analysis. The claim of "near-DFT accuracy" is not directly demonstrated in this manuscript; it is inferred from the underlying model's training and previous validation. The claim of accessing "biologically relevant timescales" is not quantified and cannot be assessed from the provided information. The generalizability of the method to non-peptidic systems and enzymatic reactions is speculative and not demonstrated.

01 基本信息 标题 ：ThermoMutDB 2.0: semiautomated literature curation and structural enrichment of thermostability data for protein mutations 作者与单位 ：Rodrigues, Gratchela Dutra; Clementino-Silva, Alisson; Brant-Ribeiro, Taffarel; de Mendonca, Maria Luiza Maciel; Zuccolotto-Guimaraes, Barbara; Dos Santos, Fernanda Elen Silva; Guimaraes, Ronison Alves; Ferreira, Valentina Gessinger; Ehlert, Maria Eduarda; Quintanilha-Peixoto, Gabriel; Rodrigues-Silva, Damares; de Menek, Gabriel Liston; Goulart, Lucas Mocellin; Silva, Danilo de Castro; Zadra, Vivian Ferreira; Goes-Neto, Aristoteles; Pires, Douglas Eduardo Valente; Kremer, Frederico Schmitt; Xavier, Joicymara Santos（单位未提供） 期刊/预印本平台 ：Nucleic Acids Research 年份 ：2026 论文类型 ：数据库/资源型论文（Database/Resource Article） 领域 ：蛋白质热稳定性数据、文献挖掘、结构生物学、生物信息学数据库 关键词 ：thermostability, protein mutations, literature curation, large language model, structural enrichment, database DOI/arXiv 号 ：10.1093/nar/gkag1116 代码 ：未提供 数据 ：ThermoMutDB 2.0 数据库，网址 http://thermomutdb.pathotrack.health/ 阅读日期 ：2026-11-10（基于发布日期） 在课题方向中的位置 ：本文属于「蛋白质结构相关计算研究 × AI 方法」中的 数据基础设施层 ——为蛋白质稳定性预测、突变效应分析、结构-功能关系研究提供高质量标注数据。其核心贡献在于将 LLM 引入文献筛选流程，实现半自动化的数据提取与结构富集，为下游的稳定性预测模型（如基于序列或结构的深度学习模型）提供训练数据与基准。该文不直接提出新的预测方法，而是为这类方法提供数据支撑与工作流范式。 02 一句话总结 本文构建了 ThermoMutDB 2.0，通过将大语言模型与规则实体识别结合、辅以专家验证的半自动化文献筛选流程，从 5,934 篇候选文献中筛选出 254 篇供专家评审，最终纳入 102 篇文献和 1,763 条新的蛋白质突变热稳定性数据，并为每条突变生成突变体结构模型以实现三维结构上下文可视化。 03 研究问题 具体问题 ：如何从海量生物医学文献中高效、准确地提取蛋白质突变的热稳定性实验数据，并将其与结构信息关联，以支持蛋白质稳定性研究与预测模型开发？ 为什么重要 ：蛋白质热稳定性数据是理解蛋白质结构-功能关系、突变分子后果及疾病机制的基础。然而，这类数据分散在数十年的大量文献中，人工提取耗时费力，且数据质量直接影响下游预测模型的训练与评估。 现有方法不足 ：传统文献挖掘依赖纯人工筛选，效率低、可扩展性差；已有的自动化方法（如基于规则或简单文本匹配）在识别相关文献时精度有限，难以处理复杂的生物医学文本表述。此外，现有数据库（如 ThermoMutDB 1.0）缺乏系统性的结构信息整合，无法提供突变的三维结构上下文。 精确研究问题 ：Can a human-in-the-loop pipeline combining large language models with rule-based entity recognition achieve scalable and accurate literature triage for protein thermostability data, while systematically enriching curated mutations with structural models? LLM 初筛模块 ：使用大语言模型对文献标题/摘要进行分类，判断是否涉及蛋白质突变热稳定性实验测量。 3. 规则 NER 模块 ：基于规则识别文献中的蛋白质名称、突变位点、热力学参数等实体，辅助 LLM 判断。 4. 优先级排序模块 ：综合 LLM 与 NER 结果，对文献进行优先级打分。 5. 专家审阅模块 ：高优先级文献由专家人工审阅，提取数据并验证。 6. 结构富集模块 推测存在此机制）。 假设 ：LLM 能有效识别相关文献；规则 NER 能提供可靠的实体锚点；结构预测模型能生成合理的突变体结构。 08 核心模块拆解 模块 功能 为何需要 输入输出 支撑证据 移除后的已知或预期影响 LLM 初筛 判断文献是否涉及蛋白质突变热稳定性 大幅压缩候选文献量，减少人工审阅负担 输入：文献标题/摘要；输出：相关性评分/分类 5,934 篇压缩至 254 篇（压缩率 supplementary materials Shared manuscript claim summary The authors present ThermoMutDB 2.0, a redesigned database and curation framework that integrates a large language model with rule-based entity recognition to semiautomate literature triage for protein thermostability mutation data, retains expert validation as the final step, and systematically enriches curated entries with mutant structural models for interactive three-dimensional visualization. Applied to literature from January 1976 to the most recent 2026 update, the pipeline screened 5,934 candidate publications, prioritized 254 for expert review, and incorporated 102 articles and 1,763 new entries. 核心思想 1) 表面方法 ： 构建了一个「AI 结构预测 → DALI 结构比对 → 功能注释 → OMP 鉴定 → B 细胞表位预测」的流水线。先用 RoseTTAFold 对 990 个 T. pallidum 蛋白进行全蛋白质组结构建模，对 RF 失败或低置信度的蛋白用 AlphaFold 数据库或 I-TASSER 补充；然后将所有高置信度模型提交 DALI 服务器进行 PDB 结构比对，基于结构同源推断功能；对已知和预测的 OMP 进行多工具信号肽、亚细胞定位、β-桶结构预测，并整合 4 种 B 细胞表位预测工具，结合结构表面暴露分析筛选疫苗候选表位。 2) 核心洞察 ： - 结构相似性比序列相似性更保守，可以揭示序列层面无法发现的远缘功能同源——这是「结构到功能」范式的核心前提。 - 将多个 AI 预测工具（RF、AlphaFold2/3、I-TASSER）组合使用，可以弥补单一工具的覆盖率不足，实现接近全蛋白质组的建模覆盖。 - OMP 的鉴定不应仅依赖序列特征，结构模型中的 β-桶折叠是更可靠的判别依据。 - 表位预测需要结合结构信息（表面暴露、loop 区域）而非仅序列，才能筛选出真正可被抗体接触的靶点。 3) 可能的普适教训 [Analysis]： - 对「难以实验研究的病原体」，计算结构生物学是可行的替代路径，但必须建立严格的置信度过滤标准（如 RF GDT ≥ 0.5、DALI Z ≥ 8.0、覆盖率 ≥ 10%）。 - 全蛋白质组结构预测的价值不仅在于单个蛋白的结构，更在于通过结构比对网络发现功能关联——这是一种「结构互作组」思维。 - 多工具交叉验证（多个表位预测器、多个亚细胞定位预测器）可以显著提高计算筛选的可信度，但最终仍需实验验证。 11 结论正确解读 任务范围 : 本文是纯计算研究，覆盖 T. pallidum Nichols 株全蛋白质组的结构建模、功能注释、OMP 鉴定和 B 细胞表位预测。结论限于计算预测层面，不涉及任何湿实验验证。 oracle/真值输入 : 功能注释的「真值」来自 NCBI 基因组序列注释（PGAP 流程），结构比对的参考库为 PDB。方法验证以序列注释为基准，但序列注释本身可能不完整或有误。 端到端状态 : 流程从序列到表位预测是端到端的，但每个环节都有独立的置信度阈值，最终输出的 90 个表位是经过 9 项标准筛选的结果，不代表所有真实表位。 算力成本 : 未提供具体算力数据；RF 服务器为公共资源，AlphaFold 数据库为预计算模型，I-TASSER 为补充使用。 历史数据依赖 : 依赖 PDB 中已有结构；随着 PDB 扩充，DALI 匹配结果可能变化。 模型依赖 : 结果依赖 RF/AlphaFold 的预测精度；对低置信度区域（如 loop、结构域边界）的推断需谨慎。 最难情形 : 14 个蛋白完全无法建模；83 个未知功能蛋白无法注释；部分 OMP 的 β-桶结构预测在两种 AI 工具间存在差异。 群体/领域边界 : 结论仅适用于 T. pallidum Nichols 株；SS14 株的序列差异可能影响表位保守性，但作者已通过跨菌株比对部分解决。 不确定性 : 所有功能注释和表位预测均为计算推断，作者明确强调需要实验验证。特别是金属结合特异性（如 TPANIC_0110 的铁特异性）被标注为需谨慎解读。 有边界的复述 : 本文通过 AI 结构预测与结构比对，为 T. pallidum 全蛋白质组中 88.6% 的蛋白提供了高置信度功能注释，并鉴定出 7 个新 OMP 候选和 90 个保守 B 细胞表位，但这些均为计算预测，其生物学功能、膜定位和免疫原性均需实验验证。 12 作者自认局限 局限 具体表现 作者提出的未来方向 来源 缺乏实验验证 所有功能注释、OMP 鉴定和表位预测均为计算推断 需湿实验验证蛋白定位、功能和免疫原性 Discussion 节 结构建模未考虑构象动态 模型为静态结构，未涉及蛋白构象变化、蛋白-蛋白互作 未来可纳入分子动力学模拟、多聚体建模 Discussion 为补充的策略，有效提高了建模覆盖率。迁移到本课题：在蛋白质结构预测任务中，不应依赖单一工具，而应建立「主工具 + 补充工具」的组合策略，并明确各工具的适用边界。 置信度阈值体系 ：RF GDT ≥ 0.5、DALI Z ≥ 8.0、覆盖率 ≥ 10%、PDB 分辨率 < 4.0 Å 的四重过滤标准，为结构-功能推断提供了可复制的质量控制框架。迁移到本课题：任何基于结构比对的推断都应建立类似的量化阈值，而非仅凭视觉判断。 OMP 鉴定的结构导向方法 ：用结构模型中的 β-桶折叠作为 OMP 判据，比仅依赖序列特征更可靠。迁移到本课题：对于膜蛋白、β-桶蛋白等特殊折叠类型的识别，结构信息应作为重要补充。 表位预测的「结构 + 序列」整合策略 ：将 4 种表位预测工具与结构表面暴露分析（DeepTMHMM "outside" 区域）结合，筛选出真正可被抗体接触的表位。迁移到本课题：在抗原设计、抗体表位预测中，应整合结构信息而非仅用序列工具。 「结构到功能」的验证方法论 ：通过与 NCBI 序列注释对比来验证结构注释的可靠性（82.9% 一致率），并区分「更具体注释」和「不同注释」的增量价值。迁移到本课题：任何新的计算注释方法都应建立类似的验证协议，明确与现有注释的一致性和增量贡献。 数据共享与资源建设 ：作者将数据存入 Harvard Dataverse 并计划开发 TPPD 数据库，这种「计算资源公开化」的做法值得借鉴。迁移到本课题：结构预测结果应系统化存储和共享，便于社区复用。 15 与已有知识连接 AlphaFold2
