It is unclear whether this refers to the proportion of heritability explained per annotation, the improvement in model fit, or some other metric. Rosetta 建模模块 : 将 alt-distogram 转化为距离约束能量项，通过 centroid 初始化、能量最小化、全原子精修三个阶段生成构象模型 4. 模型评估模块 : 使用 Rosetta 能量分数和 TM-score 选择最佳模型 工具 : ColabFold v1.5.2, PyRosetta (2019.42+release.3666509), TM-align 反馈回路 : 无显式反馈回路，但通过 15 组参数 × 10 次独立采样（共 150 个模型）进行充分采样 假设 : - AF2 distogram 中的多峰分布反映构象异质性 - 替代构象的距离信息可以从多峰中提取 - Rosetta 能量优化可以有效地将距离约束转化为结构变化 文字流程 : 1. 对目标蛋白序列运行 AF2 预测，获得 5 个模型及对应 distogram 2. 选择 rank005 模型的 distogram 进行分析（因其包含最多替代构象信号） 3. 对每个残基对的距离分布进行高斯拟合，识别多峰信号 4. 将多峰信号与已知初始构象的距离比较，去除对应初始构象的峰，保留替代构象的峰 5. 将提取的替代构象距离约束转化为 Rosetta 能量项（Eij_alt），同时保留共同信号约束（Eij_com） 6. 从初始构象出发，使用 Rosetta 进行能量最小化和全原子精修 7. 评估生成的模型，选择最佳预测 08 核心模块拆解 模块 功能 为何需要 输入输出 支撑证据 移除后的已知或预期影响 AF2 预测模块 生成结构预测和 distogram 提供多构象信息的来源 输入: 序列; 输出: 5个模型+distogram Results 节，图 1 显示 rank005 包含最多替代信号 无法获取多峰距离分布信息 信号提取模块 识别和分类多峰信号 从 distogram 中提取替代构象信息 输入: distogram+初始结构; 输出: alt-distogram Results 节，Table 2 显示信号提取精度 无法区分替代构象与噪声信号 高斯拟合分类 拟合多峰分布，分类信号类型 系统化识别多峰信号 输入: 距离概率分布; 输出: 信号分类 (Class I-VI) Methods 节，图 3 展示六种信号类型 无法有效提取替代构象距离信息 Rosetta 建模模块 将距离约束转化为结构模型 物理模拟驱动构象转变 输入: 初始结构+alt-distogram; 输出: 构象模型 Results 节，Table 3 显示预测成功率 无法将距离信息转化为结构变化 能量约束设计 构建 Eij_alt 和 Eij_com 能量项 平衡替代信号与共同信号 输入: alt-distogram 信号; 输出: 能量函数 Methods 节，公式 4-10 无法有效引导构象转变 模型评估模块 选择最佳预测模型 从 150 个模型中筛选最优 输入: 150个模型; 输出: 最佳模型 Methods 节，模型选择标准 无法从采样结果中选出最优预测 09 关键公式符号 1. Softmax 转换 distogram 概率 （Methods 节，公式 1）: softmax(DM_logits_i) = exp(DM_logits_i) / Σ_j exp(DM_logits_j) DM_logits_i: AF2 输出的第 i 个距离 bin 的 logit 值 用途: 将 AF2 的原始 logits 转换为概率分布 2. 双变量高斯拟合 （Methods 节，公式 2）: p(x) = a1·exp(-(x-μ1)²/(2σ1²))/(σ1√(2π)) + a2·exp(-(x-μ2)²/(2σ2²))/(σ2√(2π)) μ1, μ2: 两个峰的均值（对应距离） σ1, σ2: 两个峰的标准差 a1, a2: 两个峰的振幅 用途: 拟合多峰距离分布，识别替代构象信号 3. 替代构象能量项 （Methods 节，公式 4-5）: Eij_temp = tanh(Eij) 若 Eij > 0; Eij 若 Eij < 0 Eij_alt = Eij_temp(n) - (n-n0)/(n1-n0), 当 n ~ [n0, n1] n: 距离 bin 索引（1-64，覆盖 2-22 Å） n0: 初始构象距离对应的 bin n1: 能量首次过零的 bin 用途: 平坦化初始构象的能量势垒，引导向替代构象转变 4. 共同信号能量项 （Methods 节，公式 8-9）: Mo = mode(Eij) # 正能量的统计众数 Eij_com = tanh(Eij - Mo) 若 Eij > Mo; Eij 若 Eij < Mo 5. 缩放参数 （Methods 节，公式 10-14）: mag = max(min(Eij_alt)/min(min(Eij_com)) × 1/(1+e^(-plast-bin)) × pnl × Hnorm, 若 plast-bin ≥ 0.5 mean(min(Eij_alt)/mean(min(Eij_com)) × 1/(1+e^(-plast-bin)) × pnl × Hnorm, 若 plast-bin < 0.5 pnl = Nalt/L: 替代信号数与序列长度比 plast-bin = Nlast-bin/Nalt: 长距离信号比例 Hnorm = (Hmax-H)/(Hmax-Hmin): 归一化熵 用途: 自适应调整共同信号约束强度 10 实验设计与证据链 数据集 : - (2022)。 AFsample/AFsample2 : 本文在 OC23 和 TP16 数据集上与 AFsample 方法进行了基准比较，AFsample 通过修改 MSA 和随机种子来采样构象。本文方法可作为 AFsample 的补充策略。 trRosettaX 能量转化 : 本文的能量转化方法借鉴了 trRosettaX 的概率-能量转化思路，但针对多峰分布进行了扩展。 Rosetta 约束建模 : 本文使用 PyRosetta 进行约束建模，与蛋白质设计中的约束满足方法相关。 构象采样方法谱系 : 本文属于「AI 预测 + 物理优化」的混合方法，与 MD 模拟增强采样（如 metadynamics）、正态模式分析等方法互补。 双状态蛋白数据库 : 使用的 20 个双状态蛋白来自 Flores et al. 和 Saldaño et al. 的数据库，这些数据库可用于其他构象预测方法的基准测试。 Distance-AF : 讨论中提及 Distance-AF 可能增强 distogram 信息的利用，提示未来可探索将本文方法与 Distance-AF 结合。 16 研究想法 Agent 生成的研究候选 : 候选名称 : 多状态 AF2 distogram 分析扩展到三态蛋白系统 - They propose a protocol to extract alternative-conformation distance signals from AF2 distograms, convert them into Rosetta energy restraints, and successfully model alternative conformations for two-state proteins, achieving performance comparable to existing approaches on benchmark datasets. Visible evidence base Main text tables (Tables 1–3), main text figures (Figures 1–8 as referenced), equations (1)–(15), and descriptions of methods and results Missing materials affecting confidence Supplementary figures and tables (S1–S12) referenced but not provided; benchmark dataset details for OC23 and TP16 not fully described; code repository not inspected; no structural alignments or PDB identifiers for predicted models in main text Reviewer Overall assessment The manuscript addresses a timely and relevant question: whether AF2 distograms contain usable multi-state information beyond the single preferred conformation. The observation that lower-ranked AF2 models (rank005) contain alternative conformational signals is interesting and potentially useful. However, the manuscript has several significant weaknesses. The methodological description is dense and at times unclear, particularly regarding the signal classification criteria and the energy restraint construction. The evaluation metrics and success criteria are not fully justified, and the comparison to existing methods is limited. The claim of "comparable performance" to AFsample2 is not quantitatively substantiated in the visible text. The generalization to single-state proteins is presented as a preliminary extension but lacks rigorous validation. Overall, the core idea has merit, but the evidence as presented does not fully establish the case. Who would be interested in the results, and why Computational structural biologists, protein biophysicists, and researchers developing methods for conformational sampling and ensemble prediction. The work is relevant to those interested in extracting more information from deep learning structure prediction models and combining them with physics-based refinement. The potential application to studying conformational dynamics and alternative functional states would interest a broad structural biology audience. Major strengths The manuscript identifies a previously underutilized feature of AF2 predictions (distogram multi-peak signals in low-ranked models) and proposes a practical protocol to exploit it. The approach is orthogonal to MSA-subsampling strategies, which is a useful conceptual contribution. The testing across 20 two-state proteins with diverse conformational change types adds breadth. The inclusion of control experiments (CTRL1 and CTRL2) is commendable. The authors also test on out-of-training-set targets, which strengthens the generalization claim. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Evidence quality Claim pointer The authors claim that their method "effectively samples alternative conformations" and achieves "performance comparable to existing approaches" on OC23 and TP16 datasets. Evidence pointer Table 3, Figures 7 and 8, "Distogram-guided modeling of alternative conformation further refines the AF2 predictions" section Concern The quantitative comparison to existing methods is not presented in the visible text. The claim of "comparable performance" to AFsample2 is stated but no numerical comparison (e.g., TM-score distributions, success rates, or statistical tests) is shown. The AUC analysis in Figure 7C is mentioned but the actual values and comparison baselines are not described. Without these data, the performance claim cannot be evaluated. Why it matters The central claim of the manuscript is that the proposed method is useful for predicting alternative conformations. If the performance relative to existing state-of-the-art methods is not quantitatively demonstrated, the practical value of the approach is unclear. Resolution test Provide a table or figure with quantitative comparison of TM-scores, success rates, or other relevant metrics between the proposed method and AFsample2 (and ideally AFsample) on the same datasets, including statistical significance testing where appropriate. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Methodological clarity Claim pointer The signal classification criteria (Classes I–VI) and the energy restraint construction (Equations 4–10) are described as central to the method. Evidence pointer "Extracting information on alternative conformations from distogram analysis" and "Converting distogram into energy restraints for Rosetta modeling" sections, Figure 3 Concern The classification criteria are described in a highly condensed manner. The distinction between Classes I–VI is not clearly explained in terms of how each class is treated differently in the restraint construction. The parameters for the bivariate Gaussian fitting (initial values, convergence criteria) are not specified. The energy function construction, particularly the role of the hyperbolic tangent preprocessing and the piecewise form of the scaling parameter mag, is difficult to follow from the equations alone. The choice of the threshold values (e.g., pmax2>0.1pmax1, pmax1−pmax2<0.05pmax1) is not justified. Why it matters Reproducibility is a core requirement for a methods paper. If the classification and restraint construction are not described with sufficient detail, other researchers cannot implement or build upon the method. Resolution test Provide a step-by-step algorithmic description of the classification and restraint construction, including all parameters, thresholds, and their rationales. Consider a pseudocode or flowchart. Clarify how each class of signal is treated differently in the energy function. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Evidence quality Claim pointer The authors state that "AF2 predictions with deep MSA yielded hundreds of multi-peak signals" for 12 of 20 proteins, and that the average precision of alternative conformation signals was 0.73. Evidence pointer Table 2, "Extracting structural information of the alternative conformation based on a known structure and AF2 distogram" section Concern The precision calculation (Equation 3) defines true positives and false positives, but the ground truth for determining true versus false positives is not clearly described. How is it determined whether a predicted alternative signal corresponds to the actual alternative conformation? Is this based on comparison to the experimentally known alternative state? The definition of "precision" in this context needs clarification. Additionally, the relationship between the number of signals and the modeling success is not analyzed. Why it matters The precision metric is used to support the claim that the extracted signals are meaningful. If the ground truth definition is ambiguous, the precision values are difficult to interpret. Resolution test Clearly define the ground truth for true and false positive signals. Describe how the known alternative conformation is used to validate the extracted signals. Provide a more detailed breakdown of precision by protein and by signal class. Concern ID R1-M4 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Scope of claims Claim pointer The authors extend their analysis to 20 single-state proteins and claim that "most modeled protein systems exhibit some degree of conformational flexibility" and that "in several cases, our approach uncovered putative alternative conformations." Evidence pointer "Discussion" section, Supporting Information S4, S8, S9 Concern This extension is presented as a potential application, but the validation is limited. For single-state proteins, there is no experimentally known alternative conformation to validate against. The claim of "putative alternative conformations" is speculative. The criteria for judging whether a sampled conformation is a meaningful alternative state versus a distorted or degenerate model are not defined. Why it matters Overclaiming on preliminary results can mislead readers about the method's capabilities. The single-state extension is interesting but needs to be framed as exploratory with appropriate caveats. Resolution test Either remove or substantially soften the claims about single-state proteins, or provide additional validation (e.g., comparison to known functional states from literature, consistency with experimental data such as hydrogen-deuterium exchange or cross-linking). Minor Comments Concern ID R1-m1 Severity Minor Axis Clarity Affected element Abstract Evidence pointer Abstract Issue The abstract states that the method "effectively samples alternative conformations" but does not mention the success rate (85% for best-scored, 90% for best-sampled in one direction). Including a quantitative result would strengthen the abstract. Required correction Consider adding a brief quantitative summary of performance in the abstract. Concern ID R1-m2 Severity Minor Axis Reproducibility Affected element Methods, "Source of distogram" section Evidence pointer "Source of distogram" section Issue The version of ColabFold (v1.5.2) and the specific parameters are stated, but the exact command or script used for prediction is not provided. The "save_all" option is mentioned but the specific output files used are not fully described. Required correction Provide a link to the code repository and a minimal example command or script for generating the distograms. Concern ID R1-m3 Severity Minor Axis Statistical rigor Affected element Results, "Assessment of predicted structures" section Evidence pointer Table 3 Issue The success criteria are defined as TM-score improvement over the initial state, but no statistical significance testing is reported. Given that 150 models are sampled, it would be useful to know if the improvements are consistent across independent runs. Required correction Report the variance or confidence intervals for the TM-score improvements across the 150 models, or perform a statistical test comparing the best-scored models to the initial state. Concern ID R1-m4 Severity Minor Axis Presentation Affected element Figures 5 and 6 Evidence pointer Figures 5 and 6 Issue The figure captions are not provided in the text. It is difficult to interpret the structural alignments and radar plots without captions. Required correction Ensure figure captions are included and describe the color schemes, alignment methods, and metrics displayed. Concern ID R1-m5 Severity Minor Axis Completeness Affected element Discussion Evidence pointer Discussion section Issue The discussion mentions that the method is "orthogonal to MSA-subsampling strategies" but does not discuss potential limitations of this orthogonality or scenarios where the method might fail (e.g., proteins with very subtle conformational changes or intrinsically disordered regions). Required correction Add a paragraph discussing limitations and potential failure modes of the method. Technical failings that need to be addressed before the case is established R1-M1 (quantitative comparison to existing methods missing), R1-M2 (methodological details insufficient for reproducibility), R1-M3 (ground truth for precision calculation unclear) Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality The idea of mining AF2 distograms for multi-state information without MSA manipulation is relatively novel. Most prior work has focused on MSA subsampling or dropout-based sampling. The specific approach of classifying multi-peak signals and converting them into Rosetta restraints appears to be a new contribution. However, the conceptual foundation builds directly on prior work by the same group (reference 30), and the incremental advance needs to be more clearly articulated. Scientific importance The problem of predicting alternative conformations is important for understanding protein function and dynamics. If the method is robust and generalizable, it could be a useful tool. However, the importance is somewhat limited by the focus on two-state proteins and the reliance on known starting structures. The broader applicability to de novo prediction of conformational ensembles is not demonstrated. Interdisciplinary readership The work sits at the interface of computational structural biology, machine learning, and biophysics. The methods are specific to these fields, and the manuscript is likely to appeal primarily to specialists. The broader significance for cell biology or biochemistry is not strongly argued. Technical soundness The technical approach is plausible, but the manuscript has significant gaps in methodological detail and quantitative validation. The control experiments are a positive feature, but the lack of comparison to state-of-the-art methods weakens the technical case. The statistical treatment of results is minimal. Readability for nonspecialists The manuscript is written in a technical style that assumes familiarity with AF2, distograms, Rosetta, and TM-scores. The introduction provides some context, but the methods section is dense and would be challenging for nonspecialists. The figures are referenced but not described in the text, making it difficult to follow the results. Recommendation posture Supportive if technical concerns are resolved. The core idea is interesting and potentially useful, but the manuscript in its current form does not provide sufficient evidence to fully establish the claims. The missing quantitative comparison, methodological ambiguities, and unclear validation criteria need to be addressed. If the authors can provide a clear, reproducible protocol and a rigorous quantitative evaluation against existing methods, the work could be a valuable contribution to the field. Risk / unsupported claims The claim of "performance comparable to existing approaches" (AFsample2) is not supported by quantitative data in the visible text. The claim that the method "effectively samples alternative conformations" for 19 of 20 proteins is based on TM-score improvements, but the statistical significance and consistency of these improvements are not reported. The extension to single-state proteins and the claim of "putative alternative conformations" is exploratory and lacks validation against experimental data. The precision values reported in Table 2 depend on a ground truth definition that is not clearly described. The statement that "AF2 predictions inherently contain latent information about the alternative structural states" is supported by the results but is presented as a general conclusion from a limited set of 20 proteins; the generalizability to all two-state proteins is not established. The claim that the method is "orthogonal to MSA-subsampling strategies" is conceptually valid but not empirically demonstrated through direct comparison.

no methods, figures, tables, or supplementary materials were provided Shared manuscript claim summary The authors present three edge-aware graph attention network (GAT) variants (Edge-Conditioned, Edge-Injected, Edge-Gated) that incorporate edge information during message passing. Relative to a standard GAT, these models improve coordinate prediction and recover complementary aspects of residue communication. Applied to Chignolin and HIV-1 protease, the models characterize communication networks underlying protein folding, allostery, and mutation-induced functional remodeling. The three models are claimed to preferentially emphasize distinct network features: communication hubs (Edge-Conditioned), high-intensity communication in functionally important regions (Edge-Injected), and long-range communication relay (Edge-Gated). AlphaFold Multimer 的链间排列预测？ 为什么重要 ：蛋白质通常以复合物形式发挥功能，准确预测复合物结构对理解生物机制、药物设计、肽段结合研究等至关重要。然而，许多复合物缺乏高分辨率实验结构，但研究者可能拥有部分距离约束信息（如来自交联实验、突变分析等），这些信息目前难以有效整合到 AlphaFold 流程中。 现有方法为何不足 ：标准 AlphaFold Multimer 仅使用序列信息和 MSA（多序列比对）进行预测，无法直接利用用户提供的距离约束。已有的约束整合方法（如 AF2 的 restraint 功能）通常只支持单一距离约束或需要修改模型内部结构，缺乏系统性的多步骤框架来逐步优化链间排列。 精确研究问题 ：Can a multi-step approach that iteratively applies user-defined distance 01 基本信息 标题 ：pLM-bVAE: protein language model-enhanced binary representation improves quantum annealing-based protein sequence design 作者 ：Hiromi H Ueda; Andrejs Tučs; Koji Tsuda; Mitsuo Umetsu; Yutaka Saito 单位 ：未提供（bioRxiv 预印本未在摘要中列出作者单位） 期刊/平台 ：bioRxiv（预印本） 年份 ：2026（预印本日期 2026-11-06） 论文类型 ：预印本（方法学 + 计算实验） 领域 ：蛋白质序列设计 × 量子退火（QA）× 蛋白质语言模型（pLM）× 变分自编码器（VAE） 关键词 ：quantum annealing, protein sequence design, binary variational autoencoder, protein language model, binary representation DOI/ID ：10.64898/2026.11.05.764447 代码 ：https://github.com/hueda8/pLM-bVAE 数据 ：三个公开蛋白质变异数据集（具体名称未在摘要中提供） 阅读日期 ：2026-05-14（按当前日期） 在该方向中的位置 ：本文处于「蛋白质序列设计 × 量子计算」交叉点，具体解决 QA 优化中蛋白质序列的二进制编码质量问题。它将预训练 pLM 的表示能力引入 bVAE，替代原先面向自然语言的编码器，从而提升二进制编码的序列重建精度与 QA 优化效率。该工作属于「AI 方法（pLM + VAE）增强物理/组合优化（QA）管线」的典型范式，与 AlphaFold 类结构预测方法互补——它不预测结构，而是直接优化序列以适应给定适应度函数。 02 一句话总结 本文提出 pLM-bVAE，将预训练蛋白质语言模型的表示注入 bVAE 的编码器，在三个公开蛋白质变异数据集上相比原版 bVAE 获得更高的序列重建精度和更好的二进制编码质量，并显著提升了量子退火（QA）框架下高适应度序列的生成数量与序列多样性。 03 研究问题 具体问题 ：在 QA 驱动的蛋白质序列设计中，如何获得高质量的二进制编码（binary encoding）与高精度的序列重建（sequence reconstruction），以提升 QA 优化效果？ 为什么重要 ：QA 在组合序列空间中搜索时，序列必须先编码为二进制向量，优化后的向量再解码回氨基酸序列。编码质量直接决定搜索空间的可达性与解码保真度。若编码丢失序列信息，QA 再强也无法找到真正高适应度的序列。 现有方法为何不足 ：原版 bVAE 是为自然语言建模开发的，其编码器未利用蛋白质特有的序列-结构-功能先验。蛋白质序列的氨基酸分布、保守位点、进化约束等与自然语言差异显著，直接迁移 bVAE 可能导致二进制表示中关键功能信息丢失。 精确研究问题 ：Can incorporating pretrained protein language model representations into bVAE improve binary encoding quality and sequence reconstruction accuracy, thereby enhancing QA-based protein sequence design? 成功的关键，本文通过消融实验证明移除 PDE 项导致 r 从 0.822 降至 0.699 - 预训练语言模型嵌入可作为连接序列空间与物理模型的通用桥梁 - 一维反应坐标模型虽简化，但对双态折叠蛋白（如 GFP）足够有效，提示「适度简化」在复杂生物系统中的价值 07 方法总览 输入 : 空间坐标 x ∈ [0,1]，时间 t ∈ [0,1]，ProtT5 序列嵌入 e ∈ R^1024，环境参数 Θ={T, pH, P} 输出 : 折叠分数 u(x,t) ∈ [0,1] 的时空分布 网络架构 : 全连接前馈网络，输入层 1026 神经元（x, t, e），两个隐藏层各 64 神经元，tanh 激活，输出层 sigmoid 激活，Xavier 初始化 物理模型 : 反应扩散方程 ∂u/∂t = D∂²u/∂x² + f(u;Θ)，其中 f(u;Θ) = α(Θ)u(1-u) - β(Θ)u 环境调制 : α(Θ) = α₀·exp(-κ_T(T-T_opt)²)·exp(-κ_pH(pH-pH_opt)²)，β(Θ) = β₀(1+γ_P(P-P₀)) 损失函数 : L = λ_PDE·L_PDE + λ_data·L_data + λ_IC·L_IC + λ_BC·L_BC，其中 λ_data=190, λ_PDE=10, λ_IC=100, λ_BC=50 训练 : Adam 优化器，初始学习率 5×10⁻³，ReduceLROnPlateau 调度器（patience=5000），早停（patience=5000） 验证 : ① 与 FDM 数值解对比（数学一致性）；② 与 GFP 实验荧光数据对比（生物学验证） 数据 : GFP 荧光数据集（Sarkisyan 2016），21,446 条序列，80/20 随机划分（seed=1234），训练 17,157 条，测试 任务范围 : 本文聚焦于双态折叠蛋白（以 GFP 为代表）的 mesoscopic 尺度折叠动力学建模，不涉及多结构域蛋白、 intrinsically disordered proteins（IDPs）或共翻译折叠等复杂场景。 输入/真值依赖 : - 生物学验证依赖 GFP 荧光数据作为折叠状态的代理指标，荧光强度与折叠分数并非严格等价 - 序列嵌入来自预训练 ProtT5 模型，其表示质量影响下游预测 - 环境参数（温度、pH、压力）通过反应系数间接影响，非直接物理模拟 端到端状态 : 模型并非端到端的「序列→折叠动态」预测器。它需要先通过 ProtT5 获取嵌入，再通过 PINN 求解 PDE，且 PDE 参数（D, α₀, β₀, κ_T, κ_pH, γ_P）为全局固定值，不随序列变化。 算力成本 : 相比 MD 模拟显著降低，但训练 PINN 需要大量 PDE 残差计算；推理时需对每个 (x,t) 点进行网络前向传播。 历史数据依赖 : 模型训练依赖 GFP 荧光数据集，该数据集仅包含 GFP 变体，跨蛋白家族的泛化能力未验证。 最难情形 : 碱性应激（pH ≥ 8.0）条件下预测精度显著下降（R² = -0.264），表明模型对极端环境条件的建模能力有限。 群体/领域边界 : 结论仅适用于与 GFP 类似的 cooperatively folding 的双态蛋白；对多态折叠、knotted proteins、膜蛋白等未验证。 有边界的复述 : PhyFold 在 GFP 变体数据集上，通过将反应扩散方程嵌入 PINN 并结合 ProtT5 序列嵌入，实现了与实验荧光高度相关的折叠动力学预测（r=0.822），并在温度、pH、压力变化时表现出物理一致的响应；但该方法的可靠性边界为近生理条件，对极端碱性环境预测能力有限，且跨蛋白家族的泛化性尚未验证。 12 作者自认局限 局限 具体表现 作者提出的未来方向 来源 一维反应坐标的简化 无法解析三维结构复杂性和非局部接触 开发更高维的 collective variable 空间 ：作者明确承认一维反应坐标的局限，并指出需要更高维表示。这种「明确模型边界」的做法值得借鉴——任何简化模型都应清楚标注其适用边界。 消融实验设计 ：通过系统移除 PDE 损失和改变权重配置来验证各组件贡献，为混合模型的组件贡献分析提供了范例。 GFP 荧光数据集的复用 ：将实验荧光数据作为折叠状态的代理指标，为计算模型提供了可扩展的验证资源。类似策略可用于其他具有实验可测指标的蛋白质性质预测。 AlphaFold 类似，同为静态结构预测方法，本文将其归入「equilibrium conformations」预测类别。 ProtT5 (Elnaggar et al., 2021) : 本文直接使用 ProtT5 作为序列嵌入提取器，属于蛋白质语言模型在下游任务中的应用。ProtT5 的表示能力是 PhyFold 序列特异性的基础。 PINN (Raissi et al., 2019) : 本文的 PINN 方法直接继承自该框架，将 PDE 残差作为损失项。本文的创新在于将 PINN 应用于蛋白质折叠这一生物物理问题，并引入序列嵌入条件。 反应扩散方程 (Turing, 1952) : 本文的 PDE 模型基于经典反应扩散理论，但将其应用于蛋白质折叠这一新场景，并引入环境调制系数。 能量景观理论 (Bryngelson & Wolynes, 1987; Onuchic et al., 1997) : 本文的一维反应坐标建模基于能量景观理论，将折叠视为沿主导反应坐标的扩散过程。 Kramers 扩散理论 (Kramers, 1940) : 本文在结论中提及 Kramers 扩散形式主义作为一维反应坐标的理论基础。 DeepBenchmark (Xia et al., 2023) : 本文通过该基准获取 GFP 荧光数据集，属于蛋白质功能预测基准的复用。 Sarkisyan et al. Assessment boundary Scientific validity, methodological soundness, novelty, and clarity of the proposed PhyFold framework, based solely on the supplied text. No external data, code, or supplementary materials were accessed. Shared manuscript claim summary The authors propose PhyFold, a physics-informed neural network (PINN) framework that integrates a reaction-diffusion equation (RDE) with ProtT5 protein sequence embeddings to model protein folding dynamics under varying environmental conditions (temperature, pH, pressure). The model is validated against finite difference method (FDM) solutions and experimental GFP fluorescence data, reporting a Pearson correlation of 0.822 on a held-out test set. Visible evidence base Abstract, introduction, related work, model formulation (equations 1-6), PINN architecture description, FDM benchmark description, experimental setup (GFP dataset, train/test split), results (Figures 3-21, Tables 1-4), ablation study, parameter sensitivity analysis, and conclusion. Missing materials affecting confidence Figures 1-21 are referenced but not visible in the provided text. Table 2 is partially visible (values for some conditions are cut off). No code, hyperparameters (beyond learning rate), training epochs, loss curves, or statistical significance tests are provided. The exact definition of the "effective folding fraction" and its relationship to fluorescence intensity is not fully formalized. Reviewer Overall assessment The manuscript presents a conceptually interesting hybrid approach that combines a mesoscopic reaction-diffusion model with deep sequence embeddings via a PINN. The idea of using PINNs for protein folding dynamics with environmental modulation is timely and could be of interest to the computational biology community. However, the current manuscript has significant methodological gaps and validation weaknesses that prevent the claims from being fully established. The mathematical well-posedness analysis is superficial, the biological validation is indirect and lacks rigor, and the comparison with existing methods is insufficient. The work is at an early stage and requires substantial revisions and additional experiments before it can be considered for publication. Who would be interested in the results, and why Computational biologists and bioinformaticians working on protein folding prediction, particularly those interested in moving beyond static structure prediction toward dynamic modeling. Researchers in the PINN community interested in new applications of physics-informed machine learning to biological systems. Scientists studying protein folding under stress conditions (e.g., pH, temperature) may find the environmental modulation aspect relevant. Major strengths 1. The conceptual integration of a reaction-diffusion PDE with sequence embeddings via a PINN is a novel combination not commonly seen in the literature. 2. The explicit inclusion of environmental parameters (T, pH, P) into the governing equation is a thoughtful step toward physiologically relevant modeling. 3. The dual validation approach (numerical vs. biological) is commendable in principle, even if execution is lacking. 4. The authors acknowledge limitations (e.g., 1D reaction coordinate, alkaline stress) and suggest future directions, showing scientific honesty. Major Concerns R1-M1 (Blocking: Yes) Axis Scientific importance / Technical soundness Claim pointer The authors claim that PhyFold "effectively captures environment dependent folding dynamics and shows strong agreement with both numerical reference solutions and experimental fluorescence measurements." Evidence pointer Results section, Figures 3-21, Tables 2-4 Concern The biological validation is fundamentally flawed. The model predicts a "folding fraction" u(x,t) from a 1D reaction-diffusion equation, but this is compared to fluorescence intensity, which is a bulk, ensemble-averaged property. The mapping between the two is not rigorously defined. The authors state that "the spatially and temporally averaged folding fraction was computed as a scalar summary per protein sequence and compared against normalized experimental fluorescence labels," but the exact averaging procedure, the time point at which the average is taken, and the normalization of the fluorescence data are not specified. Moreover, the GFP dataset from Sarkisyan et al. measures fluorescence as a proxy for folding stability, but the relationship between the model's u and fluorescence is not a direct one. The reported Pearson correlation of 0.822 could be an artifact of the averaging procedure or the specific normalization chosen. Without a clear, mechanistic link between the model output and the experimental observable, the biological validation is not convincing. Why it matters The central claim of the paper is that PhyFold produces biologically meaningful predictions. If the validation metric is not properly aligned with the model output, the entire premise of the work is undermined. The reader cannot assess whether the model is genuinely capturing folding dynamics or merely fitting a curve to fluorescence data through an arbitrary post-processing step. Resolution test The authors must provide a clear, mathematical definition of how u(x,t) is converted to a predicted fluorescence value. This should include: (1) the exact spatial and temporal averaging scheme, (2) the time point(s) at which predictions are compared to experimental data, (3) the normalization procedure for both predicted and experimental values, and (4) a justification for why this mapping is physically meaningful. Additionally, the authors should show a scatter plot of predicted vs. experimental values with error bars and discuss the distribution of residuals, not just the correlation coefficient. R1-M2 (Blocking: Yes) Axis Technical soundness Claim pointer The authors state that "the proposed reaction diffusion model is mathematically well posed and admits a unique, bounded, and physically meaningful solution." Evidence pointer "Existence and uniqueness of solution" subsection Concern The well-posedness analysis is superficial and incomplete. The authors show that the reaction term is Lipschitz continuous, but they do not address several critical aspects: (1) the regularity of the solution given the Gaussian initial condition and Neumann boundary conditions, (2) the long-time behavior of the solution (does it converge to a steady state?), (3) the dependence of the solution on the environmental parameters Θ, and (4) whether the solution remains in the physically meaningful range [0,1] for all times. The claim that the "parabolic maximum principle" ensures boundedness is not sufficient, as the reaction term f(u;Θ) can drive u outside [0,1] if α(Θ) > β(Θ) and u is near 1. The authors need to provide a more rigorous analysis or at least numerical evidence that the solution stays within the admissible range. Why it matters The mathematical foundation of the model is a key selling point of the paper. If the well-posedness is not properly established, the reliability of all subsequent numerical results is questionable. Moreover, if the solution can leave the physically meaningful range, the biological interpretation of the results is compromised. Resolution test The authors should provide a complete well-posedness proof, including: (1) existence and uniqueness in the appropriate Sobolev or Hölder spaces, (2) a proof or numerical demonstration that u(x,t) ∈ [0,1] for all t > 0 given the initial and boundary conditions, and (3) a sensitivity analysis of the solution with respect to the environmental parameters. Alternatively, they could add a projection or clipping step in the PINN architecture to enforce the physical bounds and discuss the implications of this choice. R1-M3 (Blocking: Yes) Axis Scientific importance / Technical soundness Claim pointer The authors claim that "PhyFold introduces a hybrid Bio-Physics Informed Neural Network framework... an approach not previously demonstrated in the literature." Evidence pointer Introduction, Related works Concern The novelty claim is overstated. While the specific combination of a reaction-diffusion PDE with ProtT5 embeddings in a PINN may be new, the general idea of using PINNs for protein folding or biophysical processes is not. The authors do not adequately compare their approach with existing PINN-based methods for protein modeling or with other hybrid physics-ML approaches. For example, there are works on using PINNs for molecular dynamics, for solving Fokker-Planck equations related to folding, and for integrating sequence information into physical models. The authors should provide a more thorough literature review and clearly delineate what is genuinely novel about their approach. Why it matters The scientific contribution of the paper depends on its novelty. If the approach is largely an incremental combination of existing ideas, the impact is significantly reduced. The authors need to convince the reader that their framework offers a distinct advantage over existing methods. Resolution test The authors should add a dedicated section comparing their method with at least 3-5 existing approaches (e.g., other PINN-based protein models, traditional kinetic models, deep learning-based folding predictors). The comparison should include both methodological differences and, ideally, quantitative performance comparisons on the same dataset. R1-M4 (Blocking: No) Axis Technical soundness Claim pointer The authors state that "the shared reaction diffusion parameters D, α₀, and β₀ represent universal physical mechanisms governing folding kinetics, while protein specific variability is captured through the high dimensional embedding conditioning." Evidence pointer "Formulation of PINN" subsection Concern The mechanism by which the ProtT5 embedding conditions the PINN is not described in sufficient detail. The authors mention that the input layer receives [x, t, e] where e ∈ R^1024, but it is unclear how the embedding interacts with the PDE parameters. Does the embedding modify the reaction term f(u;Θ) directly? Does it affect the diffusion coefficient D? Is the embedding used as a global conditioning vector that modulates the entire solution, or is it concatenated at every spatial point? The architecture description is too vague to be reproducible. Why it matters Reproducibility is a core requirement for scientific publication. Without a clear description of how the sequence embedding influences the PDE solution, other researchers cannot implement or build upon the method. Resolution test The authors should provide a detailed architectural diagram and a precise mathematical description of how the embedding is incorporated into the PINN. This should include the exact dimensions of all layers, the activation functions, and the forward pass equations. R1-M5 (Blocking: No) Axis Interdisciplinary readership / Readability Claim pointer The authors claim that the model is "computationally efficient surrogate for environment aware protein folding dynamics." Evidence pointer Abstract, Conclusion Concern No computational cost analysis is provided. The authors do not report training time, inference time, or hardware requirements. The claim of computational efficiency is unsubstantiated. Moreover, the comparison with FDM is only for a 1D problem; the computational advantage of PINNs over traditional numerical methods is well-known for high-dimensional problems, but for a 1D problem, FDM is typically very fast. The authors need to demonstrate a concrete computational advantage. Why it matters The practical utility of the method depends on its computational efficiency. If the PINN is slower than a simple FDM solver, the advantage of the approach is unclear. Resolution test The authors should report wall-clock training and inference times, and compare them with the FDM solver for the same problem. They should also discuss the scaling of the method to larger systems (e.g., multi-domain proteins). Minor Comments R1-m1 Axis Readability for nonspecialists Affected element Introduction Evidence pointer Introduction, first paragraph Issue The introduction contains several grammatical errors and awkward phrasings (e.g., "Simulations A wealth of information on folding pathways and energy landscapes [9, 10] has been obtained"). The flow is disrupted, and the text reads as if it was not carefully proofread. Required correction The authors should thoroughly revise the introduction for language and clarity. Consider having a native English speaker review the manuscript. R1-m2 Axis Technical soundness Affected element Table 2 Evidence pointer Table 2 Issue The table is incomplete in the provided text. The values for some conditions (e.g., "Sub-optimal (cool, acidic)") are partially cut off, and the column headers are not fully visible. This makes it impossible to fully assess the results. Required correction The authors should ensure that all tables are complete and properly formatted in the final submission. R1-m3 Axis Technical soundness Affected element Ablation study Evidence pointer Table 3 Issue The ablation study only varies the loss weights. It does not test the contribution of the ProtT5 embedding itself. A more informative ablation would include a version of the model without the embedding (i.e., a pure PINN) to demonstrate the added value of the sequence information. Required correction The authors should add an ablation experiment where the ProtT5 embedding is removed or replaced with a random vector, to isolate the contribution of the sequence information. R1-m4 Axis Scientific importance Affected element Discussion Evidence pointer "Biological interpretation and implications" subsection Issue The biological interpretation is largely qualitative and does not provide specific, testable predictions. For example, the authors state that "atypical alkaline stress specifically disrupts electrostatic interactions and hydrogen bonding network" but do not connect this to specific residues or structural features of GFP. Required correction The authors should provide more specific biological insights, such as identifying which residues or structural regions are most affected by environmental stress, and how these predictions could be experimentally tested. R1-m5 Axis Technical soundness Affected element Experimental setup Evidence pointer "Experimental setup" subsection Issue The authors do not describe how the environmental parameters (T, pH, P) are varied in the dataset. The GFP dataset from Sarkisyan et al. contains mutations, but it is unclear how temperature, pH, and pressure are assigned to each sequence. Are these parameters derived from experimental conditions, or are they simulated? Required correction The authors should clarify the source of the environmental parameter values and how they are incorporated into the model for each sequence. Technical failings that need to be addressed before the case is established R1-M1: Lack of a rigorous mapping between model output (folding fraction) and experimental observable (fluorescence). R1-M2: Incomplete well-posedness analysis, particularly regarding solution bounds. R1-M3: Overstated novelty without adequate comparison to existing methods. R1-M4: Insufficient architectural detail for reproducibility. Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality Moderate. The combination of RDE + PINN + sequence embeddings is somewhat novel, but the individual components are well-established. The approach does not represent a fundamental conceptual breakthrough. Scientific importance Moderate. The problem of dynamic protein folding under environmental conditions is important, but the current validation is too weak to demonstrate significant practical impact. The method does not yet offer clear advantages over existing approaches. Interdisciplinary readership Limited. The work sits at the intersection of ML and biophysics, but the presentation is likely too technical for a general biology audience and not rigorous enough for a specialized ML or biophysics audience. Technical soundness Weak. The validation methodology has significant flaws (R1-M1), the mathematical analysis is incomplete (R1-M2), and the implementation details are insufficient (R1-M4). Readability for nonspecialists Poor. The manuscript contains numerous grammatical errors and the logical flow is often disrupted. The technical sections are dense and not well-explained for a broader audience. Recommendation posture Currently not established from the provided evidence. The manuscript has a promising concept but requires major revisions to address the validation flaws, strengthen the mathematical analysis, and improve the presentation. I would be willing to reconsider after substantial revision. Risk / unsupported claims The claim that PhyFold "effectively captures environment dependent folding dynamics" is not supported by the current validation, as the link between the model output and the experimental data is not rigorously established. The claim that the model "shows strong agreement with experimental fluorescence measurements" is based solely on a Pearson correlation coefficient, which is insufficient without a proper error analysis and a mechanistic justification for the comparison. The claim of "computational efficiency" is unsubstantiated, as no performance benchmarks are provided. The claim that the model is "biologically grounded" is weakened by the lack of a clear connection between the 1D reaction coordinate and actual protein structural features. The statement that "the mathematical validity established under optimal conditions therefore directly extends to all stress condition simulations" is an assertion without proof, as the authors do not demonstrate that the solution properties (e.g., boundedness, uniqueness) hold for all parameter ranges.

manuscript, figures, tables, or supplementary materials Shared manuscript claim summary The authors evaluate nine sequence-based predictors of disordered flexible linkers (DFLs) using CAID3 data, expanding the assessment to residue, region, and protein levels, including a low-sequence-similarity subset. They report that several predictors accurately identify DFL residues, that performance varies by scenario, that recent progress is driven by deep learning and protein language models, and that current tools fail to reproduce correct sizes and numbers of DFL regions. They propose development strategies to address this weakness. Visible evidence base Abstract text only; no quantitative results, performance metrics, dataset details, or methodological descriptions are provided Missing materials affecting confidence Full manuscript, all figures and tables, detailed methods, dataset construction and filtering criteria, predictor descriptions, statistical analyses, and any supplementary information Reviewer Overall assessment The abstract presents a timely and potentially valuable benchmarking study of DFL predictors, addressing an important gap in the evaluation of intrinsically disordered region prediction. The scope is appropriate and the inclusion of a low-sequence-similarity subset is a commendable methodological choice. However, the abstract provides no quantitative evidence to support the stated conclusions, and several claims are too broad or underspecified to be assessed. The identified weakness regarding region size and number prediction is interesting but lacks supporting data. The study is likely of interest to the computational biology and protein science communities, but the case is not established from the abstract alone. Who would be interested in the results, and why Computational biologists and bioinformaticians developing or using predictors for intrinsically disordered regions and linkers; experimental biologists studying protein architecture and function who rely on such predictions; researchers interested in benchmarking methodology and the application of deep learning and protein language models to structural biology problems. Major strengths The study addresses a relevant and under-evaluated class of predictors. The use of CAID3 data provides a standardized and community-recognized benchmark. The expansion to multiple assessment levels and the inclusion of a low-sequence-similarity subset are methodologically sound and likely to yield more robust estimates. The identification of a specific weakness in region size and number prediction is a useful contribution. Assessment boundary Claims and evidence presented in the abstract Shared manuscript claim summary The authors report that the C-terminal intrinsically disordered region (IDR) of the transcription factor RUNX2 is required for chromatin binding and gene regulation during osteogenesis. They claim that linear IDR motifs are dispensable for function, and that conformational dynamics of the IDR predict function. They further report development of an algorithm for rational IDR design based on biophysical principles, and use of this algorithm to generate functional IDRs de novo. The authors position this work as extending generative protein design beyond the folded proteome. Visible evidence base Abstract text only. No figures, tables, methods, or supplementary materials were provided. Missing materials affecting confidence Full manuscript text, all figures and tables, methods descriptions, statistical analyses, sequence data, algorithm details, experimental validation protocols, and any supplementary information. Without these, the core claims cannot be independently evaluated. Reviewer Overall assessment The abstract presents a potentially significant advance in the design of intrinsically disordered regions, a field that has lagged behind folded protein design. The claim that conformational dynamics, rather than linear motifs, encode function in the RUNX2 IDR is conceptually interesting and would be of broad interest if rigorously supported. However, the abstract alone provides insufficient evidence to assess the validity of the central claims. The key assertions regarding dispensability of motifs, the predictive power of conformational dynamics, and the success of de novo designed functional IDRs are stated without quantitative support, experimental detail, or statistical context. The work may be important, but the case is not established from the supplied material. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers in protein biophysics, intrinsically disordered protein biology, transcription factor regulation, developmental biology, and computational protein design would be interested. The work addresses a fundamental gap in understanding how IDR sequence encodes function, and the proposed design algorithm could have practical applications in synthetic biology and therapeutic protein engineering. The connection to osteogenesis and RUNX2 may also attract interest from the bone biology community. Major strengths The conceptual framing is clear and addresses a recognized gap in the field. The choice of a developmental transcription factor with a well-defined functional readout (stem cell differentiation) provides a biologically meaningful test system. The claim that conformational dynamics, rather than linear motifs, drive function is a testable and potentially transformative hypothesis. The stated goal of extending generative design to IDRs is timely and relevant. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Evidence sufficiency Claim pointer The authors claim that linear IDR motifs are dispensable for RUNX2 function during osteogenesis. Evidence pointer Abstract, location not provided Concern The abstract states that linear motifs are dispensable, but provides no experimental detail on how this was tested. It is unclear whether all putative motifs were systematically mutated, whether motif prediction was comprehensive, or whether residual function was quantitatively assessed. The claim of dispensability is strong and requires evidence that motif disruption does not impair chromatin binding or gene expression. Why it matters If linear motifs are not required, this challenges a dominant paradigm in IDR biology. The claim must be supported by rigorous mutagenesis and functional assays to rule out redundant or compensatory motif activity. Resolution test Provide data showing that systematic mutation or deletion of all predicted linear motifs in the RUNX2 IDR has no significant effect on chromatin binding, gene expression, or osteogenic differentiation, with appropriate statistical power and controls. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Evidence sufficiency Claim pointer The authors claim that conformational dynamics of the IDR predict function. Evidence pointer Abstract, location not provided Concern The abstract does not specify which conformational features were measured, how they were quantified, or how predictive power was established. No correlation coefficients, effect sizes, or validation on independent sequences are reported. The claim that dynamics predict function requires a defined metric and a demonstrated relationship across multiple variants. Why it matters This is the central mechanistic claim of the work. Without a clear definition of the dynamic property and evidence of its predictive value, the claim is not falsifiable from the provided material. Resolution test Define the specific conformational parameter (e.g., radius of gyration, end-to-end distance, transient secondary structure propensity) and show that it correlates with functional output across a panel of IDR variants, with statistical significance and predictive validation on held-out sequences. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Evidence sufficiency Claim pointer The authors claim to have developed an algorithm for rational IDR design and used it to generate functional IDRs de novo. Evidence pointer Abstract, location not provided Concern No details of the algorithm are provided, including its inputs, biophysical principles, optimization criteria, or validation strategy. The claim that de novo designed IDRs are functional requires evidence that these sequences are unrelated to the native RUNX2 IDR and that they rescue function in a relevant assay. Why it matters The generative design claim is the headline advance. Without algorithmic details and functional validation data, the claim cannot be assessed for novelty, robustness, or generalizability. Resolution test Provide a full description of the algorithm, including its design principles and training or optimization data, and show that multiple de novo sequences with no significant homology to native IDRs rescue RUNX2 function in cellular or biochemical assays. Minor Comments Concern ID R1-m1 Severity Minor Axis Clarity Affected element Abstract wording Evidence pointer Abstract, location not provided Issue The phrase "conformational dynamics of the IDR predict function" is vague. It is unclear whether the authors refer to a specific biophysical measurement or a computational prediction. Required correction Specify the exact conformational property measured or computed, and clarify whether the prediction is correlative or causal. Concern ID R1-m2 Severity Minor Axis Context Affected element Abstract framing Evidence pointer Abstract, location not provided Issue The abstract does not state how the findings relate to existing IDR design efforts or prior work on RUNX2. This limits the reader's ability to gauge novelty. Required correction Add one or two sentences situating the work relative to prior IDR design studies and known RUNX2 biology. Concern ID R1-m3 Severity Minor Axis Reproducibility Affected element Abstract claims Evidence pointer Abstract, location not provided Issue No mention of replication, sample sizes, or statistical methods is made in the abstract. Required correction Include brief statements on the number of independent experiments and the statistical tests used for key comparisons. Technical failings that need to be addressed before the case is established R1-M1, R1-M2, R1-M3. The abstract does not provide sufficient experimental or computational detail to support the central claims of motif dispensability, dynamics-based prediction, and successful de novo design. All three are blocking concerns. Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality: The concept of designing functional IDRs based on conformational dynamics rather than linear motifs is original and would represent a conceptual advance if supported. However, originality cannot be fully assessed without comparison to prior IDR design literature. Scientific importance: The work addresses a fundamental question in IDR biology and has potential implications for protein design and developmental biology. The importance is high if the claims hold. Interdisciplinary readership: The topic bridges biophysics, computational biology, and developmental biology, and would appeal to a broad readership. The abstract is written in accessible language. Technical soundness: Not assessable from the abstract. No methods, data, or statistical analyses are presented. Readability for nonspecialists: The abstract is clear and concise, with minimal jargon. The key concepts are understandable to a general scientific audience. Recommendation posture Currently not established from the provided evidence. The conceptual framing is promising and the work could be significant, but the abstract alone does not provide sufficient evidence to support the central claims. A full manuscript with detailed methods, quantitative results, and validation data would be required to assess whether the case is made. Risk / unsupported claims The claim that linear IDR motifs are dispensable for RUNX2 function is unsupported without mutagenesis data. The claim that conformational dynamics predict function is unsupported without a defined metric and correlative evidence. The claim that the algorithm generates functional IDRs de novo is unsupported without algorithmic details and functional validation. The general claim that this work extends generative protein design beyond the folded proteome is not evaluable from the abstract alone.

01 基本信息 标题 ：PHENOMS: Open-Source Software for Rust-Accelerated Hydrogen-Bond Analysis in Molecular Dynamics Simulations 作者与单位 ：Novy, Brandon; Lin, Shu-Hang; Dey, Rishabh; Temple, Brenda; Hajicek, Nicole; Petrotchenko, Evgeniy V; Borchers, Christoph H; Sondek, John; Popov, Konstantin I（单位未提供，推测为 UNC 相关实验室，Popov Lab-UNC） 期刊/预印本平台 ：bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology 年份 ：2026-11-06（预印本日期） 论文类型 ：方法学/软件工具论文（开源软件 + 回顾性案例验证） 领域 ：结构生物学计算；MD 轨迹分析；氢键网络分析；HDX-MS 数据整合 关键词 ：氢键分析、分子动力学模拟、HDX-MS、Rust 加速、开源软件、氢键网络 DOI/arXiv 号 ：10.64898/2026.10.26.761768 代码 ：https://github.com/Popov-Lab-UNC/PHENOMS；PyPI: pip install phenoms 数据 ：Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22879722 阅读日期 ：未提供 该文在课题方向中的位置 ：本文属于「MD 模拟 × 氢键网络分析」工具类方法论文，聚焦于从 MD 轨迹中高效提取骨架氢键占用率与持久性，并与 HDX-MS 保护模式对接。其核心贡献在于：(1) Rust 加速引擎解决 MD 轨迹氢键分析的计算瓶颈；(2) 将氢键网络分析标准化为可复现、可比较的流程；(3) 提供与 HDX-MS 实验数据直接比对的残基级打分。与 AlphaFold 等 AI 结构预测方法形成互补——AI 预测难以捕捉配体诱导或突变引起的动态变化，而本文的物理模拟 + 氢键网络分析路径可提供近原子分辨率的动态机制解释。 02 一句话总结 本文开发了开源 Python 包 PHENOMS，通过 Rust 多线程加速引擎对 MD 轨迹逐帧执行 Baker–Hubbard 几何判据的氢键识别，计算残基对占用率与键持久性分数，并整合 HDX-MS 数据实现残基级保护模式对比，在基准测试中比 MDAnalysis 快 7–22 倍、比 MDTraj 快约 115 倍，且能复现 EGFR Δ747–749 突变体的已知 HDX-MS 动态变化。 03 研究问题 具体问题 ：如何从 MD 模拟轨迹中高效、可复现地提取骨架氢键网络信息，并将其与 HDX-MS 实验保护模式进行残基级定量对比？ 为什么重要 ：HDX-MS 提供肽段级保护信息，但缺乏原子分辨率；MD 模拟可提供原子级动态细节，但氢键分析的计算成本高、工具碎片化、结果可比性差。整合两者可揭示配体结合、突变等引起的局部构象变化机制，对药物发现和蛋白质工程有直接价值。 现有方法不足 ：(1) 主流工具（MDAnalysis、MDTraj）氢键识别速度慢，长轨迹大体系分析不现实；(2) 缺乏标准化流程（残基编号统一、复制间一致性检查、参数核验）；(3) 缺乏与 HDX-MS 数据直接对接的残基级打分体系；(4) 现有工具默认过滤低占用率氢键，可能丢失瞬态但功能重要的相互作用。 精确研究问题 ：Can a Rust-accelerated, standardized hydrogen-bond analysis pipeline enable residue-level interpretation of HDX-MS protection patterns from MD trajectories at computational costs feasible for routine use? Rust 氢键引擎 （ phenoms_hbond_rs ）：多线程并行，对每个帧独立执行 Baker–Hubbard 几何判据（H–A 距离 < 2.5 Å，D–H–A 角 > 120°），输出扁平化数组 3. Polars 数据处理层 ：将逐帧氢键列表组织为占用率矩阵与持久性统计 4. SimulationSet ：管理多个复制轨迹，执行残基编号标准化（基于序列比对）、QC 检查（RMSD 稳定性、参数一致性）、跨复制聚合 5. ComparisonSet ：两组模拟（如 WT vs 突变体）的差异分析，生成共有/特有氢键列表、残基级差异打分 6. 图论分析 ：以残基为节点、氢键为边构建网络，识别局部子网络与重组织模式 7. 可视化与导出 ：网络图、B-factor 映射、QC 报告 流程 ：轨迹 → 预处理 → Rust 引擎逐帧氢键检测 → Polars 聚合 → 占用率/持久性统计 → （可选）HDX-MS 对比 → HDX-MS 对接的残基级代理分数 ：将 MD 氢键占用率/持久性转化为残基级保护代理分数，并导出为 PDB B-factor 字段，实现计算与实验数据的直接可视化对比。这一"代理分数 + 结构注释"模式可迁移到其他实验-计算对接场景（如交联质谱、突变扫描）。 图论网络分析揭示协同重组织 ：将氢键数据构建为残基级网络，识别局部子网络，可捕捉单个键分析遗漏的协同变化。可迁移到蛋白质构象变化、变构通路分析。 15 与已有知识连接 Baker–Hubbard 几何判据 ：本文使用的氢键判定标准（H–A 距离 < 2.5 Å，D–H–A 角 > 120°）源自 Baker & Hubbard 1984 年的经典工作（Prog Biophys Mol Biol），是 MD 氢键分析的事实标准之一。PHENOMS 与 MDTraj 使用相同判据，与 MDAnalysis 默认判据（D–A 距离 < 3.0 Å，角 > 150°）不同——这解释了部分氢键数量差异。 HDX-MS 与 MD 整合 ：本文引用的前期工作（文献 5–12）建立了 HDX 保护与 MD 氢键占用率相关的框架。PHENOMS 是对这一框架的工程化实现。类似思路可见于 HDXer、DynamXL 等工具，但 PHENOMS 的差异化在于全量保留 + 图论分析 + Rust 加速。 EGFR 突变研究 ：Δ747–749 是 EGFR 外显子 19 缺失突变，L858R 是外显子 21 点突变，均为 NSCLC 常见驱动突变。van Alderwerelt van Rosenburgh 等人的 HDX-MS 研究（文献 20）提供了本文的验证参照。 与 AlphaFold 等 AI Who would be interested in the results, and why Computational structural biologists, HDX-MS practitioners seeking atomistic interpretation of protection data, and researchers developing or using MD analysis tools. Major Strengths The software addresses a real methodological gap by linking HDX-MS protection patterns to atomistic hydrogen-bond dynamics. The Rust-accelerated design is a sensible approach to a known performance bottleneck. The emphasis on reproducibility, including unit tests, Docker workflows, and Zenodo deposition, is exemplary. The focus on per-frame hydrogen-bond resolution rather than filtered or averaged results is scientifically defensible. Major Concerns The benchmark claims are not verifiable from the provided text. The biological validation is qualitative and does not demonstrate statistical significance or quantitative agreement with experimental data. The quality control criteria are described but their sensitivity and specificity are not evaluated. The comparison with MDAnalysis uses different hydrogen-bond definitions, confounding the performance comparison. The manuscript does not describe how the residue-level protection scores are calibrated or validated against experimental HDX-MS data. Minor Comments The abstract claims an average 16-fold speedup and up to 100-fold, while the introduction claims 7- to 22-fold over MDAnalysis and up to ~115-fold over MDTraj, and the results section reports 11-fold and 115-fold for the full system. 生物膜相关酶（GelE）而触发噬菌体释放的水凝胶递送系统，从而在导管表面原位抑制生物膜形成？ 为什么重要 : CAUTIs 占医院获得性感染约 12.9%（美国 CDC 数据），80% 的医院获得性 UTI 与导管相关；生物膜对抗生素和免疫系统高度耐受，现有涂层策略多为被动释放，缺乏响应性。 现有方法不足 : 传统抗菌涂层（如银合金、抗生素浸渍）依赖连续或被动释放，无法根据感染状态按需释放，且可能促进抗生素耐药。 精确研究问题 : Can a GelE-responsive GelMA hydrogel achieve enzyme-triggered, localized phage release sufficient to suppress biofilm formation under dynamic (flow) conditions? 04 背景与发展脉络 阶段一：被动抗菌涂层 （银合金、抗生素浸渍导管）——减少黏附但效果不稳定，存在耐药风险。 阶段二：噬菌体疗法 （游离噬菌体或简单包埋）——特异性强但易失活、释放不可控。 阶段三：刺激响应性水凝胶 （pH、温度、酶响应）——智能释放但多用于药物小分子，噬菌体（大颗粒）递送研究较少。 阶段四（本文位置） : 验证方式 : 选择结构差异大的序列实验验证降解速率 - 创新状态 : unverified Review setup Input scope Full manuscript text Assessment boundary Scientific content, technical soundness, and claims as presented in the provided manuscript Shared manuscript claim summary The authors propose HydroGuard, a Gel-MA hydrogel system loaded with bacteriophages, designed to release phages in response to GelE-mediated degradation to combat E. faecalis biofilms associated with catheter-associated urinary tract infections (CAUTIs). The work combines preliminary wet-lab experiments using an E. coli surrogate system with a multiscale computational framework covering biofilm formation, hydrogel degradation, phage-bacteria dynamics, and protein design. Visible evidence base Abstract, Introduction, Materials and Methods, Results, Discussion, Conclusion, Data availability statement Missing materials affecting confidence Figures 1-15 are referenced but not provided. Experimental protocols for cloning, transformation, and protein expression are described only in summary form. Quantitative data, statistical analyses, and raw numerical outputs from computational models are not included. No information on phage-bacteria specificity assays, cytotoxicity, or material characterization beyond qualitative observations. Reviewer Overall assessment This manuscript presents an early-stage proof-of-concept for a phage-loaded, enzyme-responsive hydrogel intended to prevent CAUTIs. The conceptual integration of a biofilm-associated protease trigger with phage delivery is interesting and potentially relevant to the growing field of non-antibiotic antimicrobial strategies. However, the experimental evidence is almost entirely qualitative, the computational models are described without sufficient detail for reproducibility, and the link between the surrogate E. coli system and the target pathogen E. faecalis is not experimentally established. The manuscript reads as a project report rather than a complete scientific study, and the core claims of the system's feasibility are not supported by the evidence provided. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers working on bacteriophage therapy, antimicrobial hydrogels, biofilm prevention, and medical device-associated infections may find the conceptual framework of interest. The multiscale modelling approach could appeal to computational biologists studying host-pathogen-material interactions. However, the lack of quantitative experimental validation limits the utility for clinicians or biomaterials scientists seeking actionable data. Major strengths The concept of enzyme-triggered phage release is a thoughtful response to the limitations of passive antimicrobial coatings. The multiscale computational framework is ambitious and attempts to connect molecular, material, and population-level dynamics. The authors are transparent about the preliminary nature of the work and the surrogate system limitations. The use of a BSL-1 system for initial feasibility testing is a pragmatic safety choice. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Experimental evidence Claim pointer The abstract and discussion state that the system shows "preliminary inhibition" against biofilms and that the hydrogel supports "enzyme-triggered release of bacteriophages." Evidence pointer Results section, "Testing of HydroGuard against biofilm"; Figure 4 Concern The only experimental evidence for antimicrobial activity is described as "qualitative observations" of reduced visible bacterial growth. No quantitative data, such as colony-forming unit counts, biofilm biomass measurements, or statistical comparisons, are provided. The claim of enzyme-triggered release is inferred from "small pinprick holes" in the hydrogel, which is not a validated measure of degradation or phage release. Why it matters Without quantitative experimental validation, the central mechanism of the proposed system (GelE-triggered phage release leading to bacterial suppression) remains unsupported. The manuscript cannot establish feasibility on the basis of qualitative observations alone. Resolution test Provide quantitative data from at least three independent replicates, including bacterial counts, biofilm mass, and phage titers, with appropriate statistical tests. Demonstrate GelE-specific degradation of the hydrogel using controlled experiments with and without GelE or GelE-expressing cells. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Relevance to target pathogen Claim pointer The manuscript claims the system targets E. faecalis biofilms, but all experiments use E. coli DH5α/BL21 as a surrogate. Evidence pointer Materials and Methods, "Cloning" and "Biofilm growth"; Discussion Concern The use of E. coli as a host for GelE expression and as the biofilm organism does not replicate E. faecalis physiology, biofilm structure, or phage susceptibility. The phages used (T2, T4, T7, λ) are E. coli-specific and would not infect E. faecalis. The manuscript does not present any data on E. faecalis growth, GelE production, or phage activity against the target organism. Why it matters The clinical rationale for the system depends on activity against E. faecalis. The surrogate system can only demonstrate proof of concept for GelE-mediated degradation, not for the proposed therapeutic effect against the target pathogen. Resolution test Include experiments with E. faecalis, including GelE production assays, phage susceptibility testing, and biofilm inhibition studies. If E. faecalis-specific phages are not available, state this limitation explicitly and provide a clear pathway for how the system would be adapted. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Computational model validation Claim pointer The multiscale computational framework is described as providing "predictive insight" and "linking biofilm development and environmental conditions to enzyme-mediated hydrogel degradation, phage release, and bacterial suppression." Evidence pointer Materials and Methods, "Computational modelling"; Results, "Model of E. faecalis biofilm formation", "Hydrogel diffusion modelling", "Modelling the phage-bacteria interaction", "Protein design modelling" Concern The computational models are described at a high level, but no equations, parameter values, or validation against experimental data are provided. The models are not compared to the qualitative experimental observations, and no metrics of model fit or predictive accuracy are given. The protein design section reports outputs from AlphaFold3 and ProteinMMP but does not include any experimental validation of the designed peptides. Why it matters Computational models are only useful if they can be evaluated for accuracy and reproducibility. Without equations, parameters, or validation, the models cannot be assessed, and the claim of "predictive insight" is not substantiated. Resolution test Provide full model equations, parameter tables, and code availability. Validate model outputs against the experimental data presented, or clearly state which predictions remain untested. For the protein design, include experimental data on peptide synthesis, folding, and GelE cleavage. Concern ID R1-M4 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Material characterization Claim pointer The manuscript describes Gel-MA hydrogel fabrication and phage encapsulation but does not characterize the material properties relevant to catheter application. Evidence pointer Materials and Methods, "Hydrogel fabrication and characterization" Concern No data are provided on hydrogel mechanical properties, swelling, degradation kinetics, phage loading efficiency, or release profiles under physiological conditions. The manuscript states that "comprehensive material characterization... was beyond the scope" but does not provide any alternative quantitative characterization. Why it matters For a catheter coating, mechanical integrity, stability, and controlled release are critical. Without these data, the practical feasibility of the system cannot be evaluated. Resolution test Include measurements of hydrogel stiffness, degradation rate in urine or PBS, phage encapsulation efficiency, and release kinetics over time, with at least three replicates per condition. Minor Comments Concern ID R1-m1 Severity Minor Axis Clarity Affected element Results section, "Phage propagation and validation" Evidence pointer Figure 2 Issue The text states that restriction digestion produced patterns matching in silico predictions for T2, T4, and T7, but λvir produced "weak but interpretable fragments." The criteria for "interpretable" are not defined. Required correction Define the criteria for successful restriction digestion and provide the in silico predictions alongside the experimental data. Concern ID R1-m2 Severity Minor Axis Reproducibility Affected element Materials and Methods, "Testing of HydroGuard against biofilm" Evidence pointer Location not provided Issue The method for placing biofilms on hydrogels and collecting samples is described only briefly. The volume of phage injected, the number of replicates, and the incubation conditions are not specified. Required correction Provide a detailed protocol, including sample sizes, volumes, concentrations, and incubation times. Concern ID R1-m3 Severity Minor Axis Terminology Affected element Abstract and Discussion Evidence pointer Location not provided Issue The term "cocktail" is used to describe the phage mixture, but the manuscript does not specify the composition, ratios, or rationale for the combination. Required correction Specify the phage cocktail composition and the rationale for selecting these phages. Concern ID R1-m4 Severity Minor Axis Data presentation Affected element Results, "Protein design modelling" Evidence pointer Figure 15 Issue The "Composite Score" is defined as (DOM + CLS - DP), but the definitions of DOM, CLS, and DP are not provided in the text. Required correction Define all acronyms and explain how the composite score relates to rigidity and degradability. Technical failings that need to be addressed before the case is established R1-M1: Lack of quantitative experimental data for antimicrobial efficacy. R1-M2: No experiments with the target pathogen E. faecalis. R1-M3: Computational models not described in sufficient detail for evaluation or reproduction. R1-M4: No material characterization data for the hydrogel system. Risk / unsupported claims The claim that the system provides "enzyme-triggered release of bacteriophages" is unsupported by direct experimental evidence; the observation of "pinprick holes" is not a validated measure. The claim that the multiscale framework provides "predictive insight" is unsupported because model equations, parameters, and validation are not provided. The claim that the phage cocktail "produced the greatest apparent reduction in visible bacterial growth" is based on qualitative observation without statistical support. The claim that the system "could potentially be adapted" to other pathogens is speculative and not supported by data. The claim that the work has "clinical and societal relevance" is overstated given the absence of any in vivo or clinically relevant experimental model.

01 基本信息 标题 ：Replicate-resolved pressure-cooling responses of tobacco mosaic virus coat protein reveal robust volumetric changes and non-dominant conformational redistribution 作者与单位 ：Bonafe, Carlos Francisco Sampaio; Teixeira, Juan Philippe; Cesar de Melo Freire, Caio; Bajay, Miklos Maximiliano; de Lima Neto, Daniel Ferreira（单位未提供） 期刊/平台 ：Journal of Biomolecular Structure & Dynamics 年份 ：2026（在线日期 2026-11-06） 论文类型 ：计算分子动力学（MD）研究 领域 ：蛋白质构象响应、高压/低温处理、MD 模拟 关键词 ：high hydrostatic pressure; molecular dynamics; tobacco mosaic virus coat protein; conformational sampling; hydration; volumetric changes DOI/arXiv 号 ：10.1080/07391102.2026.2758346 代码 ：未提供 数据 ：未提供（89,109 帧分析数据描述于文中） 阅读日期 ：2026-05-12（按当前日期推算） 在课题方向中的位置 ：本文属于「蛋白质结构相关计算研究 × 物理模拟（MD）」方向，聚焦压力-温度耦合条件下蛋白质的体积、水合与构象重分布，不涉及 AI/深度学习，但提供了可迁移的 replicate-resolved 分析框架与压力-冷却 MD 路径设计，对构象采样与 ensemble 分析有参考价值。 02 一句话总结 本文通过三组独立速度初始化的 20 ns MD 模拟（Native、HHP 2500 bar、HHP+LT 2500 bar/255 K），发现烟草花叶病毒外壳蛋白（TMVcp）在高压下表现出稳健的体积收缩（-9.15%）与密度增加（+10.07%），冷却进一步加剧这些变化（-11.49% 体积，+12.98% 密度），但构象重分布在 PC3-PC4 中仅呈非主导性且未完全收敛，且未证明表位重塑的因果性。 03 研究问题 具体问题 ：高静水压（HHP）及 HHP 与低温（LT）联合作用如何影响 TMVcp 的体积、水合层和构象系综？这些响应是否在独立重复模拟中可复现？ 为什么重要 ：高压处理是蛋白质稳定性、病毒灭活和疫苗开发中的关键物理扰动，理解其分子机制有助于设计压力-based 生物物理实验和解释功能变化。 现有方法不足 ：多数 MD 研究仅用单一轨迹或短时间尺度，未区分系统体积效应与局部水合效应，也未评估 replicate 间变异性，导致结论可能受初始条件影响。 精确研究问题 ：Can replicate-resolved MD simulations distinguish pressure-driven densification from cooling-associated local hydration effects in TMVcp, and is the conformational redistribution statistically robust yet non-dominant? 04 背景与发展脉络 阶段一 ：早期高压 MD 研究（2000s-2010s）—— 关注压力对蛋白质二级结构和体积的直接影响，常用单轨迹，方法为 NPT 系综，优点为揭示压力诱导去折叠趋势，局限为忽略系综变异性。 阶段二 ：压力-温度耦合模拟（2010s-2020s）—— 引入低温联合处理以模拟冷冻-高压工艺，方法为多条件对比，优点为更贴近实际应用，局限为缺乏 replicate 统计。 阶段三 ：replicate-resolved 与系综分析（2020s 至今）—— 强调多重复轨迹和统计检验（如置换检验、Jensen-Shannon divergence），本文属于此阶段，主张通过 replicate 分离条件信号与随机波动。 本文位置 ：在压力-冷却 MD 路径基础上，首次对 TMVcp 进行 replicate-resolved 分析，区分体积/密度响应（稳健）与构象重分布（非主导），并强调不收敛与因果性限制。 脉络核验 ：此脉络为「仅本文框架」—— 作者未在摘要中引用具体文献，阶段划分基于领域常识，需外部文献进一步核验。 05 核心痛点 痛点 表现 成因或作者解释 文中证据 构象信号弱且分散 PC1-PC2 无法区分条件（JSD 0.771 vs 0.768, p=0.476），信号集中在 PC3-PC4 条件相关变异占总方差比例低，主导变异来自 replicate 内波动 摘要：PC1-PC2 未分离，PC3-PC4 有显著差异 模拟未完全收敛 前半与后半轨迹的 divergence 不一致 20 ns 时间尺度不足以达到平衡，尤其 HHP+LT 条件 摘要：first-half vs second-half divergences 指示不完整收敛 水合效应与体积效应混淆 原始水合增加（+10.73% HHP, +18.45% HHP+LT）但归一化后 HHP 近零（+0.6%） 体积收缩导致 bulk 密度增加，需归一化才能分离局部水合 摘要：normalization 后 HHP 残余 +0.6%，HHP+LT +4.9% 表位变化因果性不明 端点表位比较显示 Native 和 HHP+LT 有富集，HHP 无 构象重分布非主导，不足以支持抗体重塑的因果推断 摘要：endpoint epitope comparisons 未显示 HHP 富集 06 核心思想 表面方法 ：对 TMVcp 进行三条件（Native、HHP、HHP+LT）各 3 个独立速度初始化的 20 ns MD 模拟，丢弃前 200 ps，分析 89,109 帧；使用体积/密度、水合数、Cartesian PCA、C-alpha RMSD、二面角 PCA 和表位比较。 核心洞察 ：压力驱动的体积/密度响应是稳健且可复现的（replicate 间一致），但构象重分布是「非主导」的——即条件信号存在于低方差主成分（PC3-PC4）中，且不收敛，说明压力-冷却主要改变系综的局部偏好而非全局折叠态。 可能的普适教训 [Analysis] ：在 MD 研究中，replicate 设计是区分真实物理响应与初始条件伪影的必要条件；体积/密度等全局量比构象坐标更易收敛，因此应优先报告稳健的全局响应，并对构象结论附加收敛性警告。 07 方法总览 输入 ：TMVcp 初始结构（来源未提供，推测为 PDB 结构），三组独立速度初始化。 输出 ：体积/密度变化、水合数、PCA 投影、RMSD、表位富集分析。 模块 ： 1. 模拟设置：NPT 系综，压力 1 bar/2500 bar，温度 300 K/255 K，时间 20 ns，丢弃前 200 ps。 2. 体积/密度计算：基于 box 尺寸。 3. 水合分析：0.35 nm 内水分子计数，归一化处理。 4.
