Scientific content, methodological rigor, dataset construction, benchmarking approach, and interpretation of results Shared manuscript claim summary The authors present MODNAP, a curated dataset of 1039 experimentally determined structures containing ribose-based modified nucleotides, and benchmark AlphaFold 3 on this dataset, reporting high global accuracy but variable local accuracy for modified residue placement, frequent intramolecular validity failures, and reduced performance on post-training-cutoff structures Visible evidence base Full text, methods descriptions, results narrative, figure legends (Figs 1-10), supplementary figure legends (S1-S17), tables referenced (Table 1) Missing materials affecting confidence Actual figures and supplementary figures not provided; Table 1 not provided; raw data files not inspected; PoseBusters and RNAspider output files not provided; AlphaFold 3 configuration files not provided Reviewer Overall assessment This manuscript addresses a timely and important gap in the structural biology community: the systematic evaluation of AI-based structure prediction methods on modified nucleic acids. The construction of MODNAP represents a valuable community resource. The benchmarking results are informative and the observation that global accuracy metrics mask local errors in modified residue placement is an important cautionary finding. However, several methodological details require clarification, the statistical treatment of results needs strengthening, and the interpretation of the training-cutoff analysis warrants more careful framing. The manuscript is potentially suitable for publication after substantial revision. Who would be interested in the results, and why Structural biologists using AlphaFold 3 for nucleic acid modeling, developers of structure prediction methods, researchers studying modified nucleic acids in epigenetics and RNA biology, computational chemists developing force fields for non-canonical residues, and the broader AI-for-science community interested in benchmarking methodology. Major strengths The dataset fills a clear gap in the field, as no curated benchmark set for modified nucleic acid modeling previously existed. The systematic analysis of the chemical landscape of modified nucleotides in the PDB is comprehensive and well-executed. The use of multiple evaluation metrics (RMSD, TM-score, lDDT, INF, I-INF) provides a multi-faceted assessment. The inclusion of a post-training-cutoff test set is a thoughtful design choice for assessing generalization. The PoseBusters analysis adds an important dimension beyond simple geometric superposition. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Statistical rigor Claim pointer The manuscript reports success rates exceeding 80% at an RMSD threshold of 2.5 Å across the full MODNAP benchmark set, and stratifies results by molecule type and modification type Evidence pointer Results section "Performance of AlphaFold 3 on the MODNAP benchmark set", Fig 4, Table 1 Concern The manuscript reports success rates and percentages across categories but provides no confidence intervals, statistical comparisons between categories, or measures of variability. The dataset is heavily skewed toward a small number of modifications (e.g., 5CM with n=172, 8OG with n=90, BRU with n=64), while 63 of 129 CCD IDs are represented by a single structure. Aggregate success rates will be dominated by the well-represented modifications, and the reported percentages for rare modifications are based on extremely small sample sizes. No statistical framework is presented for determining whether differences between categories (e.g., RNA vs DNA, or base vs sugar modifications) are meaningful. Why it matters Without appropriate statistical treatment, readers cannot assess whether reported differences between categories reflect genuine performance variations or sampling noise. The skewed distribution means that the overall success rate may not be representative of performance on rare or chemically unusual modifications, which are precisely the cases of most interest to the community. Resolution test Provide confidence intervals for all reported success rates, perform statistical comparisons between categories (e.g., Fisher's exact test or chi-square test for proportions), and clearly report sample sizes for each category. For categories with very small sample sizes, either aggregate them into broader groups or explicitly flag them as preliminary. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Methodological transparency Claim pointer The manuscript states that AlphaFold 3 models were generated using default parameters with a single random seed (modelSeeds = [10]) and five diffusion samples, with the top-scoring model selected by pTM or ipTM Evidence pointer Methods section "AlphaFold 3 modeling" Concern The use of a single random seed is a significant methodological limitation. AlphaFold 3's diffusion-based generative module is stochastic, and different seeds can produce substantially different predictions, particularly for challenging targets. The selection of the top model by pTM or ipTM from only five samples may not be representative of the model's typical performance. The manuscript does not report any measure of run-to-run variability, nor does it explain why a single seed was chosen. Additionally, the criteria for selecting pTM versus ipTM for ranking are not specified; it is unclear whether this choice was made per-target or uniformly. Why it matters The stochastic nature of AlphaFold 3 means that results from a single seed may not be reproducible or representative. If the benchmark is intended as a community resource for evaluating and improving structure prediction methods, the results must be robust to the choice of random seed. The lack of variability reporting undermines confidence in the reported success rates. Resolution test Run a subset of targets (e.g., 50-100 structures spanning different categories) with multiple seeds (at least 3-5) and report the variability in success rates and RMSD values. If computational cost is prohibitive, justify the single-seed approach with evidence that AlphaFold 3 is deterministic or that variability is negligible for the targets studied. Clearly specify the model selection criteria. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Interpretation of training-cutoff analysis Claim pointer The manuscript states that performance was consistently lower for post-cutoff structures than pre-cutoff structures across nearly every category, and interprets this as evidence that a portion of AlphaFold 3's accuracy is attributable to structures available during training Evidence pointer Results section "Performance of AlphaFold 3 on the MODNAP test set", Fig 10C and 10D Concern The interpretation of the post-cutoff performance decline as evidence of training-set memorization is confounded by several factors. First, the post-cutoff set (n=103) is small and may not be representative of the broader distribution of modified nucleic acid structures. Second, structures deposited after September 30, 2021 may systematically differ from earlier structures in terms of resolution, complexity, or novelty of modifications, independent of whether AlphaFold 3 saw them during training. Third, the manuscript does not report whether the post-cutoff structures contain modifications that are chemically distinct from those in the training set, which would be an alternative explanation for reduced performance. The claim that reduced performance "reinforces the interpretation that fine-grained placement of nucleotide modifications is a comparatively weaker aspect of AlphaFold 3's predictive capability" conflates memorization with generalization failure. Why it matters The training-cutoff analysis is a key contribution of the manuscript, as it addresses the important question of whether AlphaFold 3 generalizes to novel structures. If the interpretation is confounded, the conclusions may be misleading. The distinction between memorization and generalization failure has different implications for how the community should use and improve these methods. Resolution test Provide a more detailed characterization of the post-cutoff set, including the distribution of modification types, structural complexity, and resolution compared to the pre-cutoff set. If possible, identify whether the post-cutoff structures contain modifications or folds that are chemically or structurally novel relative to the training set. Consider alternative explanations for the performance decline and discuss them explicitly. Concern ID R1-M4 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Benchmark design Claim pointer The manuscript describes MODNAP as "the first curated dataset of experimentally determined structures containing modified nucleotides" and states it is designed for "benchmarking and/or training structure prediction methods" Evidence pointer Abstract, Introduction, Results section "Features and composition of MODNAP" Concern The dataset construction criteria are not fully described. The manuscript states that structures with resolution 3.5 Å or better and sequence lengths within certain limits were included, but does not describe how redundancy was handled (e.g., sequence similarity clustering, structural similarity filtering). It is unclear whether the 1039 structures represent independent folds or whether many are near-duplicates of well-studied systems. The manuscript also does not describe how the "test set" was selected from the full benchmark set beyond the training cutoff date, and whether this introduces selection bias. Finally, the claim of being "first" requires more careful verification, as other benchmark sets for nucleic acid structure prediction may exist. Why it matters For a benchmark resource, the construction criteria directly affect its utility and the interpretability of results obtained with it. If the dataset contains many near-duplicate structures, the effective sample size is much smaller than 1039, and reported success rates may be inflated. The community needs to understand the dataset's limitations to use it appropriately. Resolution test Describe the redundancy filtering approach in detail, including any sequence or structural similarity thresholds used. Provide a clear description of how the test set was selected and whether it is representative of the full benchmark set. Verify the claim of being "first" by searching for existing benchmark sets for modified nucleic acid structure prediction. Concern ID R1-M5 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Technical validation Claim pointer The manuscript reports that PoseBusters analysis reveals frequent intramolecular validity failures, primarily due to non-ideal ribose ring geometries, and that only 30.4% of models passed the non-aromatic ring non-flat test Evidence pointer Results section "Structure validity checks with PoseBusters test suite", Fig 3 Concern The manuscript does not provide a detailed breakdown of which specific PoseBusters tests were failed, the distribution of failure severity, or whether failures correlate with specific modification types or structural contexts. The statement that "models that failed chemical validity checks did not appear to cluster around specific CCD IDs" is based on visual inspection of supplementary figures, not statistical analysis. The manuscript also does not discuss whether the ribose ring geometry failures are specific to modified nucleotides or whether they also occur for canonical nucleotides in the same predictions, which would help distinguish between a general limitation of AlphaFold 3 and a modification-specific problem. Why it matters The PoseBusters analysis is a key finding of the manuscript, as it reveals that high global accuracy can coexist with local chemical invalidity. Understanding the specific nature and distribution of these failures is essential for the community to know which types of predictions can be trusted and which require additional validation or refinement. Resolution test Provide a detailed breakdown of PoseBusters test failures by category and modification type, with statistical analysis of correlations. Compare ribose ring geometry failures between modified and canonical nucleotides within the same predictions. Discuss the practical implications of these failures for downstream applications. Minor Comments Concern ID R1-m1 Severity Minor Axis Clarity Affected element Methods section "Evaluation of AlphaFold 3 models against experimental structures" Evidence pointer Methods section, location not provided Issue The description of RMSD calculation states that it was performed "following least-squares global alignment of the entire complex," but it is unclear which atoms were included in the RMSD calculation (all atoms, backbone only, heavy atoms only). The manuscript also does not specify whether the RMSD was calculated over the full structure or over specific regions when comparing "full structure" versus "modified nucleotide only" RMSD values. Required correction Specify the atom selection for RMSD calculations and clarify the alignment procedure. State whether the same alignment was used for both full-structure and modification-specific RMSD calculations. Concern ID R1-m2 Severity Minor Axis Completeness Affected element Results section "Performance of AlphaFold 3 on the MODNAP benchmark set" Evidence pointer Fig 4, Table 1 Issue The manuscript reports success rates at a 2.5-Å RMSD threshold but does not report results at other thresholds. The choice of 2.5 Å is not justified, and it is unclear whether conclusions would change at stricter (e.g., 1.5 Å) or looser (e.g., 4 Å) thresholds. Required correction Report success rates at multiple RMSD thresholds (e.g., 1.5, 2.0, 2.5, 3.0, 4.0 Å) or justify the choice of 2.5 Å as the primary threshold. Concern ID R1-m3 Severity Minor Axis Interpretation Affected element Results section "Entanglements in AlphaFold 3 models of modified RNA structures" Evidence pointer Supplementary Fig S12-S14 Issue The manuscript reports that entanglements were detected in models across several CCD IDs but does not provide a quantitative comparison of entanglement rates between modified and canonical RNA structures, nor does it discuss whether the observed entanglement rates are higher or lower than expected based on previous studies of AlphaFold 3 on unmodified RNA. Required correction Provide quantitative entanglement rates and compare with published results for unmodified RNA, if available. Discuss whether the presence of modified nucleotides influences entanglement propensity. Concern ID R1-m4 Severity Minor Axis Presentation Affected element Discussion section Evidence pointer Discussion, location not provided Issue The discussion of limitations focuses on the choice of AlphaFold 3 and the composition of the dataset, but does not discuss the potential impact of the single-seed approach or the lack of statistical power for rare modifications on the conclusions. Required correction Add a discussion of how the single-seed approach and the skewed distribution of modifications might affect the generalizability of the findings. Concern ID R1-m5 Severity Minor Axis Reproducibility Affected element Data availability statement Evidence pointer Data availability section Issue The data availability statement provides links to Zenodo and GitHub, but does not specify the exact contents of these repositories, the software versions used, or the computational environment required to reproduce the analysis. Required correction Provide a detailed description of the repository contents, including file formats, software dependencies, and version numbers. Concern ID R1-m6 Severity Minor Axis Literature context Affected element Introduction Evidence pointer Introduction, location not provided Issue The introduction cites several databases for modified nucleotides but does not discuss existing efforts to benchmark structure prediction methods on modified nucleic acids, if any exist. The claim that this is the first such evaluation should be supported by a more thorough literature search. Required correction Expand the literature review to include any prior evaluations of structure prediction methods on modified nucleic acids, and clarify the novelty of the current work in this context. Risk / unsupported claims The claim that MODNAP is "the first curated dataset of experimentally determined structures containing modified nucleotides" is not fully verified against existing resources. The interpretation that reduced performance on post-cutoff structures reflects training-set memorization is confounded by potential differences in structure characteristics between pre- and post-cutoff sets. The statement that "AlphaFold 3 achieves success rates exceeding 80% at an RMSD threshold of 2.5 Å" is presented without confidence intervals or consideration of the skewed distribution of modifications. The claim that "co-folding in the presence of protein partners may improve overall intramolecular geometric consistency" is based on aggregate comparisons without statistical testing. The assertion that entanglements are "not necessarily due to the presence of a specific modified nucleotide but is instead dependent on the RNA tertiary fold itself" is based on a limited number of examples and lacks systematic comparison with unmodified RNA structures.

They report a three-role classification of conformational states, with large aggregate formation associated with a "promiscuous" set of states. They further report differences in role occupancies between wild-type and the cataract-associated W42R variant, consistent with the hypothesis that W42R monomers more readily occupy conformations conducive to larger aggregate formation. Major strengths The abstract frames a clear conceptual advance by proposing a role-based classification of conformational states within aggregation networks, rather than treating aggregation as a simple binary property. The explicit consideration of two-way coupling between intermolecular interactions and monomeric conformations is thoughtful. The inclusion of a disease-associated variant provides a clinically relevant test of the framework. Without statistical rigor, the claim that W42R shifts conformational state occupancy toward aggregation-prone roles is not established. Resolution test Provide quantitative role occupancy distributions for both variants, with error bars or confidence intervals, and appropriate statistical tests (e.g., permutation tests or bootstrapping) demonstrating significant differences. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Biological relevance Claim pointer The authors discuss the relationship between conformational states and aggregation, considering the two-way influence between intermolecular interactions and monomeric conformational states. Evidence pointer Abstract only; no experimental validation or connection to known biophysical data Concern The abstract does not indicate whether the simulation predictions are compared with any experimental data on gammaD-crystallin aggregation, such as light scattering, microscopy, or in vitro aggregation assays. The biological relevance of the three-role system remains speculative without such validation. Why it matters The lens environment is highly crowded and complex, and simulation predictions may not translate to in vivo behavior. Experimental correlation would strengthen the claim that the identified roles are biologically meaningful. Resolution test Include comparisons with available experimental data on gammaD-crystallin aggregation kinetics or equilibrium behavior, or clearly state the predictions that could be tested experimentally. Minor Comments Concern ID R1-m1 Severity Minor Axis Clarity Affected element Definition of "promiscuous" states Evidence pointer Abstract, first paragraph Issue The term "promiscuous" is used without a precise definition. It is unclear whether this refers to a high number of interaction partners, a high binding affinity, or a lack of specificity in interactions. Required correction Define "promiscuous" operationally in terms of network metrics, such as degree centrality or interaction partner diversity. Concern ID R1-m2 Severity Minor Axis Readability Affected element Description of the three-role system Evidence pointer Abstract, second paragraph Issue The abstract mentions a "three-role system" but does not describe the nature of the three roles or how they differ. This limits the reader's ability to interpret the findings. Required correction Briefly describe the three roles and their distinguishing features in the abstract. Concern ID R1-m3 Severity Minor Axis Scope Affected element Generalizability of findings Evidence pointer Abstract, final sentence Issue The abstract focuses on gammaD-crystallin and the W42R variant, but it is unclear whether the three-role framework is expected to generalize to other crystallins or cataract-associated mutations. Required correction Add a sentence addressing the potential generalizability or limitations of the framework to other crystallin proteins. Technical failings that need to be addressed before the case is established R1-M1 and R1-M2 are blocking. The absence of methodological detail and statistical support means the central claims cannot be evaluated. R1-M3, while not blocking, is important for establishing biological relevance. Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality: The conceptual framing of conformational states as network roles is a novel perspective, but the abstract does not demonstrate how this advances beyond existing descriptions of crystallin aggregation. Scientific importance: The topic is important for understanding cataract formation and protein behavior in crowded environments, but the significance of the specific findings cannot be assessed without quantitative results. Interdisciplinary readership: The work bridges biophysics, computational biology, and ophthalmology, which could appeal to a broad audience, but the abstract is too technical in places and lacks context for nonspecialists. Technical soundness: Not assessable from the abstract; the absence of methods and statistical detail is a major limitation. Readability for nonspecialists: The abstract is generally clear but uses terms like "multi-scale simulation" and "aggregate topology" without sufficient explanation for a general scientific audience. Recommendation posture Currently not established from the provided evidence. The conceptual framework is promising, but the abstract alone does not provide sufficient methodological or statistical support to evaluate the claims. I would be supportive if the full manuscript addresses the technical and statistical concerns outlined above. Risk / unsupported claims The existence of a three-role system of conformational states is unsupported without methodological detail on how roles were defined and validated. The association between "promiscuous" states and large aggregate formation is unsupported without quantitative network analysis. The claim that W42R monomers more readily occupy aggregation-conducive conformations is unsupported without statistical comparison. The two-way influence between intermolecular interactions and monomeric conformational states is asserted but not demonstrated with data. Any implication that the simulation results reflect in vivo lens behavior is unsupported without experimental validation.

Reviewer Overall assessment This manuscript presents a computationally driven candidate prioritization study with a commendable degree of methodological transparency and a careful, appropriately hedged interpretation of results. The authors consistently distinguish between computational prediction and experimental validation, and they explicitly acknowledge the exploratory nature of their findings. However, the scientific impact is limited by the absence of experimental confirmation, the reliance on a single MD trajectory per complex, and the modest concordance between the two docking programs. The manuscript is technically sound in its execution but does not establish a novel biological or therapeutic claim beyond what computational screening can offer. The relevance to placenta previa is contextual rather than mechanistic, and the authors correctly avoid overstating this connection. The work may be of interest to a specialized audience in computational drug discovery, but its broader significance is constrained by the lack of functional validation. Who would be interested in the results, and why Computational chemists and structural biologists working on kinase-targeted drug discovery may find the integrated workflow and the comparative analysis of docking and MD methods useful. Researchers investigating natural products as lead scaffolds, particularly anthraquinone glycosides, may also be interested. However, clinicians and translational researchers in obstetrics are unlikely to find actionable insights, as the study does not provide evidence of biological activity, selectivity, or safety in pregnancy-relevant models. Major strengths 1. The authors demonstrate a rigorous and transparent computational workflow, including explicit validation of the docking protocol via redocking with RMSD assessment. 2. The interpretation of results is consistently cautious and appropriately hedged, with clear statements about what the computational data can and cannot establish. 3. The use of two independent docking programs and the reporting of their concordance adds methodological credibility. 4. The authors explicitly address the distinction between placenta previa and related conditions, avoiding inappropriate extrapolation from other obstetric syndromes. 5. The limitations section is thorough and candid, particularly regarding the single MD trajectory and the small number of snapshots used for end-point energy estimates. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Evidence sufficiency Claim pointer The manuscript claims that Emodin-8-glucoside is "consistently prioritized among the highest-ranked compounds" and that MD simulations showed "persistent binding-site association." Evidence pointer Results section, Tables 2, 5-9, Figures 7-12 (location not provided) Concern The central claim of persistent binding is based on a single 500 ns MD trajectory per complex, as explicitly acknowledged by the authors. Without replicate simulations with different initial velocity seeds, the observed stability metrics (RMSD, RMSF, hydrogen bonds, interaction energies) cannot be distinguished from trajectory-specific artifacts. The authors acknowledge this limitation but do not address it methodologically. Additionally, the MM-PBSA result for Emodin-8-glucoside is near-zero with substantial variability, which undermines the claim of favorable binding energetics under that model. The manuscript does not provide a criterion for what constitutes "persistent" association beyond qualitative inspection of distance plots. Why it matters The central conclusion that Emodin-8-glucoside is a viable candidate for experimental testing rests on the assumption that the computationally predicted binding mode is stable and energetically plausible. A single trajectory and method-dependent energy estimates do not provide sufficient evidence to prioritize this compound over the many other phytochemicals that were not subjected to MD. Without replicate simulations and convergence analysis, the claim of persistent binding is not robustly supported. Resolution test The authors should perform at least three independent MD simulations with different initial velocity seeds for each complex and report the mean and standard deviation of key metrics across replicates. They should also assess convergence using block averaging or similar methods. If the MM-PBSA estimate remains near-zero across replicates, the claim of favorable binding should be revised to reflect the method-dependence of the result. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Relevance of context Claim pointer The manuscript frames the study in the context of placenta previa and suggests that VEGFR1 kinase domain is a candidate molecular target for this condition. Evidence pointer Introduction, Discussion (location not provided) Concern The connection between VEGFR1 kinase activity and placenta previa is not established by any data presented in this study. The authors correctly state that placenta previa tissue studies have reported altered VEGF expression and vascular morphology, but they do not demonstrate increased VEGFR1 kinase activity in this condition. The manuscript does not provide any placenta previa-specific molecular data, patient samples, or disease models. The contextual framing is therefore speculative, and the relevance of the computational findings to placenta previa is not supported by evidence. Why it matters The title and framing imply a disease-relevant investigation, but the study is purely a computational screening exercise. If the connection to placenta previa is not evidence-based, the significance of the work is substantially reduced, and the framing may mislead readers about the translational relevance of the findings. Resolution test The authors should either (a) provide evidence from the literature or preliminary data that VEGFR1 kinase activity is relevant to placenta previa pathogenesis, or (b) reframe the manuscript as a general computational exploration of VEGFR1-binding phytochemicals, with placenta previa mentioned only as a hypothetical future application. The current framing overstates the disease relevance. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Methodological validation Claim pointer The authors state that the redocking of 8ST reproduced its experimental pose with a heavy-atom RMSD of 1.465 Å, which is used to validate the docking protocol. Evidence pointer Results section, Figure 6 (location not provided) Concern While the RMSD of 1.465 Å is below the 2.0 Å threshold, this validation is limited to a single ligand. The manuscript does not report whether the docking protocol was validated against a set of known VEGFR1 inhibitors or whether the scoring functions were benchmarked for this specific target. The moderate Spearman correlation (rho = 0.553) between VINA and MOE rankings suggests that the two methods do not strongly agree, which raises questions about the reliability of the prioritization. Why it matters The prioritization of Emodin-8-glucoside depends on the reliability of the docking scores. A single-ligand redocking validation is insufficient to establish that the protocol is robust for the diverse set of 21 phytochemicals tested. The moderate inter-method concordance further weakens confidence in the ranking. Resolution test The authors should validate the docking protocol using a set of known VEGFR1 kinase inhibitors with experimentally determined binding affinities, reporting enrichment factors or similar metrics. They should also discuss the implications of the moderate VINA-MOE correlation for the robustness of the prioritization. Minor Comments Concern ID R1-m1 Severity Minor Axis Clarity Affected element Abstract Evidence pointer Abstract (location not provided) Issue The abstract states that Emodin-8-glucoside "represents an in-silico-prioritized exploratory candidate requiring biochemical, selectivity, placental-cell, and pregnancy-safety validation." This is appropriately cautious, but the abstract does not mention the method-dependent nature of the end-point energy estimates or the lack of replicate MD simulations. A reader relying solely on the abstract may overestimate the strength of the computational evidence. Required correction Add a brief statement in the abstract acknowledging that the computational predictions require experimental confirmation and that the binding energetics were method-dependent. Concern ID R1-m2 Severity Minor Axis Reproducibility Affected element Methods, MD simulation section Evidence pointer Methods, "Molecular dynamics simulation studies" (location not provided) Issue The manuscript does not report the software version for the AMBER force field parameterization beyond "AmberTools25," nor does it specify the exact commands or parameter files used for the MM-GBSA and MM-PBSA calculations. This limits reproducibility. Required correction Provide a detailed description of the parameterization workflow, including specific AmberTools module versions, and consider depositing input files and parameter files in a public repository. Concern ID R1-m3 Severity Minor Axis Data presentation Affected element Results, ADMET section Evidence pointer Results, "ADMET analysis of Emodin-8-glucoside" (location not provided) Issue The ADMET predictions are presented as a list of individual properties, but the implications of these predictions for the compound's drug-likeness are not discussed in a integrated manner. For example, the low gastrointestinal absorption and P-glycoprotein substrate status are noted, but the authors do not discuss how these properties would affect the feasibility of oral administration or the need for alternative delivery routes. Required correction Add a brief discussion of the integrated ADMET profile and its implications for the compound's developability, including potential formulation strategies or route-of-administration considerations. Technical failings that need to be addressed before the case is established 1. Single MD trajectory per complex without replicate simulations (R1-M1). 2. Lack of evidence linking VEGFR1 kinase activity to placenta previa pathogenesis (R1-M2). 3. Insufficient validation of the docking protocol beyond a single redocking test (R1-M3). Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality : Moderate. The application of a combined docking-MD-ADMET workflow to a specific compound is not methodologically novel, but the specific target-compound combination has not been previously reported. Scientific importance : Low to moderate. The study does not establish a new biological mechanism, therapeutic target, or clinical insight. Its value is primarily as a hypothesis-generating exercise. Interdisciplinary readership : Limited. The work is likely to appeal mainly to computational chemists and structural biologists. The clinical relevance to obstetrics is not established. Technical soundness : Adequate with reservations. The methods are generally appropriate, but the lack of replicate simulations and limited validation reduce confidence in the conclusions. Readability for nonspecialists : Good. The manuscript is clearly written, and the authors make a commendable effort to explain the limitations of computational approaches for a broader audience. Recommendation posture Currently not established from the provided evidence. The manuscript is technically competent but does not provide sufficient evidence to support the central claim that Emodin-8-glucoside is a prioritized candidate for VEGFR1 targeting in placenta previa. The lack of replicate simulations, the method-dependent energetics, and the unestablished disease relevance are significant gaps. The authors should address these concerns and consider reframing the manuscript to more accurately reflect the exploratory and hypothesis-generating nature of the work. Risk / unsupported claims The claim that Emodin-8-glucoside shows "persistent binding-site association" is not robustly supported due to the single MD trajectory and method-dependent energy estimates. The relevance of VEGFR1 kinase inhibition to placenta previa is asserted as a context but is not supported by any data presented in this study. The ADMET predictions, while appropriately labeled as computational, include several active toxicity endpoints that are not discussed in terms of their potential impact on the compound's viability as a therapeutic candidate. The statement that Emodin-8-glucoside was "consistently prioritized" across methods is weakened by the moderate Spearman correlation (rho = 0.553) between the two docking programs.

04 背景与发展脉络 （标注：以下脉络基于本文框架，未经外部核验） - 阶段一：TRPV1 门控的单态模型 。早期研究认为 TRPV1 激活后进入单一开放态，不同刺激只是激活概率不同。代表方法：全细胞和单通道电生理。优点：简单可量化。局限：无法解释刺激特异性的药理学差异。 - 阶段二：多态门控的初步证据 。部分研究提示 TRPV1 存在多个电导水平或亚状态，但缺乏系统性结构-功能关联。代表方法：单通道记录、突变分析。优点：揭示状态异质性。局限：难以将功能状态映射到具体构象。 - 阶段三：结构生物学与计算建模结合 。冷冻电镜解析了 TRPV1 的多种构象（闭合、开放、脱敏），但静态结构难以直接对应功能状态。Rosetta 等计算工具可用于构建刺激特异性的构象模型。优点：提供原子级结构假设。局限：计算模型需要实验验证。 - 本文位置 ：本文主张 TRPV1 门控是「刺激分区、多态」过程，即不同刺激稳定不同的开放态（不同电导水平），且这些状态对应不同的开放孔构象。本文创新在于将单通道电导、异常摩尔分数效应、位点定向荧光和 Rosetta 模型四者结合，形成功能-结构互证的证据链。 05 核心痛点 痛点 表现 成因或作者解释 文中证据 开放态异质性被忽视 以往研究默认 TRPV1 激活后进入单一开放态 缺乏能区分功能状态的高分辨率方法；单通道电导差异可能被归因于噪声或实验误差 本文观察到不同激活剂产生离散电导水平（Results 节） 功能状态与构象的对应关系不明 电导差异无法直接解释为结构差异 电生理测量是间接的，缺乏结构层面的直接证据 异常摩尔分数效应提示不同开放态离子通路不同（Results 节） 共激活效应未系统研究 多刺激同时存在时的门控行为未知 以往研究多关注单一刺激的剂量-效应关系 共激活减慢通道开放，而非协同加速（Results 节） 计算模型缺乏功能验证 Rosetta 等预测的构象难以直接与功能状态关联 计算模型通常只预测静态结构，不包含功能读数 位点定向荧光与 Rosetta 模型一致（Results 节） 06 核心思想 表面方法 ：结合单通道电生理（测量电导水平）、异常摩尔分数效应（检测离子通路中的多位点结合）、位点定向荧光（监测孔道构象变化）和 Rosetta 结构建模（生成刺激特异性的开放态模型），系统比较不同 TRPV1 激活剂（如辣椒素、质子、热）的门控效应。 核心洞察 ：TRPV1 的不同激活剂并非驱动同一开放态，而是稳定功能上不同的开放态，表现为离散的单通道电导水平。这些功能差异对应不同的开放孔构象。共激活的负协同效应（减慢开放）提示不同刺激的构象变化可能在亚基间不兼容，即门控是「刺激分区」的。 可能的普适教训 [Analysis] ：对于多峰受体或通道，功能状态异质性可能被单一态假设掩盖。将功能读数（电导、荧光）与计算结构模型结合，可以揭示刺激特异性的构象状态，这对蛋白质构象采样和结构预测课题的启示是：预测的构象集合应尽可能覆盖功能上不同的状态，而非仅预测能量最低的单一结构。 07 方法总览 输入 ：TRPV1 通道蛋白（表达于异源系统）、不同激活剂（辣椒素、质子、热）、离子（Na⁺、K⁺ 等） 输出 ：单通道电导水平、异常摩尔分数效应曲线、位点定向荧光信号、Rosetta 结构模型 模块 ： 1. 单通道电生理记录（膜片钳） 2. 异常摩尔分数效应测量（改变离子组成，观察电导变化） 3. 位点定向荧光标记与记录（监测孔道构象变化） 4. no methods, figures, or statistical details were available for evaluation Shared manuscript claim summary The authors report that TRPV1 activators stabilize functionally distinct open states with discrete single-channel conductance levels, that these states arise from distinct open-pore conformations supported by anomalous mole fraction effect measurements and site-directed fluorescence recordings, that Rosetta-guided structural models are consistent with these observations, and that coactivation by two stimuli slows channel opening, suggesting conformational incompatibility across subunits. The authors conclude that TRPV1 gating is a stimulus-partitioned, multistate process with implications for selective modulation in pain management. Visible evidence base Abstract text only; no figures, tables, methods, or supplementary materials were provided Missing materials affecting confidence Full manuscript, methods, statistical analyses, raw electrophysiology and fluorescence data, structural model details, and any control experiments Reviewer Overall assessment The abstract presents a potentially significant revision of the prevailing model of TRPV1 activation, moving from a single activated state toward stimulus-specific open states. The combination of single-channel conductance measurements, anomalous mole fraction effects, site-directed fluorescence, and Rosetta-guided modeling is intellectually compelling and would be of broad interest to the ion channel and pain research communities. However, the abstract alone does not provide sufficient methodological detail, quantitative support, or control information to assess the robustness of the claims. The central conclusions rest on several inferences that require careful experimental validation, particularly the link between conductance levels and discrete pore conformations, and the interpretation of slowed coactivation kinetics. The work is promising but not fully established from the provided material. Who would be interested in the results, and why Ion channel biophysicists studying gating mechanisms, structural biologists interested in conformational dynamics of TRP channels, pharmacologists and drug developers targeting TRPV1 for pain management, and neuroscientists studying nociceptor signaling. The claim of stimulus-partitioned open states would challenge current assumptions about TRPV1 activation and could inform selective modulation strategies. Major strengths The study addresses a fundamental and unresolved question in TRPV1 biology. The use of multiple orthogonal approaches, including electrophysiology, fluorescence, and computational modeling, is a notable strength. The observation of discrete conductance levels and the anomalous mole fraction effect provides functional evidence for distinct open states. The coactivation experiment is a clever design that may reveal subunit-level conformational interactions. The potential therapeutic implication for selective TRPV1 modulation is clinically relevant. Major Concerns R1-M1 (Major, Blocking: Yes, Axis: Technical soundness, Claim pointer: "TRPV1 activators stabilize functionally distinct open states that yield discrete single-channel conductance levels", Evidence pointer: "location not provided"): The abstract does not specify which activators were tested, how many conductance levels were observed, or whether these levels were statistically distinguishable across experiments. Discrete conductance levels could arise from subconductance states that are not necessarily linked to distinct open-pore conformations. Without details on the number of independent recordings, the amplitude resolution, and the criteria used to classify conductance levels, the claim of functionally distinct open states is not fully supported. R1-M2 (Major, Blocking: Yes, Axis: Technical soundness, Claim pointer: "These functional states appear to arise from distinct open-pore conformations, as evidenced by anomalous mole fraction effect measurements", Evidence pointer: "location not provided"): The anomalous mole fraction effect is a valuable tool, but its interpretation requires careful control of ion species and concentrations. The abstract does not describe the ion conditions, the magnitude of the effect, or whether the effect was observed for all activators or only a subset. Without these details, the link between the mole fraction effect and distinct pore conformations is suggestive but not conclusive. R1-M3 (Major, Blocking: Yes, Axis: Technical soundness, Claim pointer: "Structurally, stimulus-specific changes in pore conformation were directly observed using site-directed fluorescence recordings, consistent with Rosetta-guided structural models", Evidence pointer: "location not provided"): The abstract claims "direct observation" of conformational changes, but site-directed fluorescence reports on local environmental changes, not direct structural coordinates. The consistency with Rosetta-guided models is mentioned without any description of the model quality, the number of models generated, or the criteria for consistency. The abstract does not indicate whether the fluorescence changes were calibrated against known structural states or whether the models were validated by independent methods. R1-M4 (Major, Blocking: Yes, Axis: Technical soundness, Claim pointer: "coactivation by two stimuli markedly slows channel opening rather than producing synergistic acceleration, suggesting potential conformational incompatibility across subunits", Evidence pointer: "location not provided"): The interpretation of slowed opening kinetics as evidence for conformational incompatibility is one possible explanation, but alternative mechanisms, such as altered ligand binding kinetics, desensitization, or channel block, are not addressed. The abstract does not specify which two stimuli were used, the concentration ranges, or whether the slowing was observed across multiple coactivation pairs. Without these details, the conclusion is speculative. Minor Comments R1-m1 (Severity: Minor, Axis: Readability for nonspecialists, Affected element: Abstract text, Evidence pointer: "location not provided", Issue: The term "polymodal nociceptor" and "anomalous mole fraction effect" are used without brief explanation, which may limit accessibility for readers outside the ion channel field. Required correction: Provide a brief parenthetical definition or context for these terms. R1-m2 (Severity: Minor, Axis: Scientific importance, Affected element: Abstract text, Evidence pointer: "location not provided", Issue: The abstract states "highlight opportunities for selective modulation of TRPV1 in pain management" but does not specify how the findings translate to selective modulation. Required correction: Clarify the proposed mechanism for selective modulation or temper the claim to match the evidence presented. R1-m3 (Severity: Minor, Axis: Technical soundness, Affected element: Abstract text, Evidence pointer: "location not provided", Issue: The abstract does not mention the number of independent experiments or replicates for any of the key measurements. Required correction: Include a statement of sample sizes and statistical significance in the abstract or indicate that these details are in the full manuscript. Technical failings that need to be addressed before the case is established R1-M1, R1-M2, R1-M3, R1-M4 Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality: High. The proposal of stimulus-partitioned open states for TRPV1 is a novel conceptual framework that challenges the prevailing single-state activation model. Scientific importance: High. If substantiated, the findings would reshape understanding of TRPV1 gating and could inform new approaches to pain therapy. Interdisciplinary readership: Moderate to high. The topic bridges biophysics, structural biology, and pharmacology, but the abstract's technical density may limit appeal to a broader readership. Technical soundness: Not assessable from the abstract alone. The claims require detailed methodological and statistical validation that is not provided in the visible material. Readability for nonspecialists: Moderate. The abstract is concise but uses specialized terminology without sufficient context. Recommendation posture Supportive if technical concerns are resolved. The conceptual advance is significant and the experimental strategy is appropriate, but the current abstract does not provide enough evidence to establish the central claims. A revised version with detailed methods, quantitative results, and explicit controls would be needed to assess the case fully. Risk / unsupported claims The claim that TRPV1 activators stabilize functionally distinct open states is not fully supported without details on the number and statistical separation of conductance levels. The claim that distinct open states arise from distinct open-pore conformations is inferred from the anomalous mole fraction effect but lacks the necessary experimental context. The claim of "direct observation" of conformational changes via site-directed fluorescence is overstated, as this method reports on local environmental changes rather than direct structural coordinates. The interpretation of slowed coactivation kinetics as evidence for conformational incompatibility is speculative without ruling out alternative mechanisms. The therapeutic implication for selective modulation of TRPV1 is not substantiated by the evidence described in the abstract.

RNA）？这里的「复杂」指需要多个原子在三维空间中精确协同定位才能实现功能，例如金属离子配位、催化残基网络、底物特异性识别等。 为什么重要 ：酶催化和 RNA 功能依赖于原子级精确的空间排列。现有设计方法（如基于残基的扩散模型）在残基层面操作，难以满足多原子协同约束；而手工搭建活性位点再寻找支架的方法效率低、成功率低。 现有方法为何不足 ：RFdiffusion 前代版本（RFD1/RFD2）以残基为基本单元（Cα 或全原子残基框架），无法直接对原子坐标进行精细调控；基于 Rosetta 的经典设计方法需要大量人工迭代和能量优化，难以处理金属离子配位等复杂约束。 精确研究问题 ：Can a generative model that diffuses free atoms directly satisfy complex multi-atomic functional site constraints and produce functional enzymes in zero-shot design campaigns? 04 背景与发展脉络 注：以下脉络基于本文框架及作者在文中引用的背景，部分经外部核验（标注）。 阶段 代表性方法 优点 局限 本文位置 1. 经典物理设计 Rosetta (能量函数 + 序列设计) 可解释、物理约束明确 功能位点的本质是原子间的空间关系，而非残基间的拓扑关系 。将扩散单元从残基降为原子，使得模型可以直接编码和满足「原子 A 与原子 B 距离为 X、角度为 Y」这类约束，而无需通过残基框架间接表达。这类似于从「句子级生成」降为「字符级生成」，虽然搜索空间增大，但约束表达能力显著增强。 3) 可能的普适教训 [Analysis] 一个可迁移的教训是： 当目标功能依赖于比当前生成单元更细粒度的空间关系时，降低生成单元粒度（从残基到原子）可能比增加约束编码更有效 。这提示在蛋白质设计、RNA 设计、配体设计等领域，生成模型的「基本单元」选择应与功能位点的「最小功能单元」对齐。 07 方法总览 输入 ：功能位点的原子级约束描述（如金属离子配位几何、催化残基位置、底物结合口袋形状）、目标链长、序列长度、可能的二级结构约束。 输出 预测中性能随相互作用类别差异显著，尤其在动力学重要、缺乏强共进化历史的相互作用中表现下降，并将这些局限组织为四类挑战区域，主张未来需减少对 MSA 的依赖、区分相互作用强度与特异性、超越静态结构预测。 03 研究问题 具体问题 ：为什么 AlphaFold2 等 AI 驱动的结构预测方法在蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用预测中性能不稳定？哪些类别的相互作用是当前方法难以处理的？ 为什么重要 ：PPI 预测是理解细胞功能、疾病机制和药物设计的基础；AlphaFold2 的成功使人们对其在复合物预测上的能力产生过高期望，但实际应用中失败模式多样且未被系统化。 现有方法为何不足 ：现有方法（尤其 AlphaFold2 类）依赖 MSA 中的共进化信号，对缺乏共进化历史的相互作用（如弱/瞬时相互作用）无能为力；同时静态结构预测无法捕捉动力学、无序和细胞环境依赖的相互作用。 精确研究问题 ：Can current AI-driven structure prediction methods reliably predict protein-protein interactions across all interaction classes, or are their limitations systematically tied to co-evolutionary signal, structural ambiguity, and dynamic/context-dependent interactions? 04 背景与发展脉络 阶段一 ：AlphaFold2 之前——传统对接方法（如 ClusPro、HADDOCK）依赖几何互补和物理能量函数，计算成本高、精度有限，尤其对构象变化大的复合物。 阶段二 ：AlphaFold2 引入——利用 MSA 共进化信息和端到端深度学习，在单体结构预测上达到实验级精度，并推广至复合物预测（AlphaFold-Multimer），在强共进化信号的复合物上表现优异。 阶段三 ：当前——性能饱和与失败暴露。方法在部分相互作用类别上仍不可靠，包括动力学主导的相互作用、缺乏共进化信号的相互作用、竞争/旁系同源/化学计量导致的歧义、以及依赖细胞环境或无序区域的相互作用。 本文主张的位置 Visible evidence base Abstract text only; no figures, tables, methods, or results sections provided Missing materials affecting confidence Full manuscript, all figures and tables, methods description, quantitative performance data, and any validation of the proposed categorization framework Reviewer Overall assessment This is a perspective-style manuscript that identifies a genuine and timely problem in the field of protein-protein interaction prediction. The proposed categorization of interaction prediction challenges into four regions is conceptually reasonable and may be useful for organizing future research efforts. However, the abstract alone provides no empirical evidence to support the claimed performance variations, and the categorization framework is presented without any systematic justification or validation. The manuscript's contribution is therefore primarily organizational and speculative at this stage, and its impact will depend on the depth of analysis and evidence provided in the full text. Who would be interested in the results, and why Computational biologists and bioinformaticians working on protein structure prediction, protein-protein interaction prediction, and AI-driven methods for molecular biology. Experimental biologists studying protein interactions, particularly those involving dynamic complexes, disordered regions, or context-dependent assembly, may also find the categorization useful for selecting appropriate computational tools. The manuscript could serve as a roadmap for method developers and a cautionary guide for users of existing prediction tools. Major strengths The manuscript addresses a well-recognized and important limitation of current AI-based prediction methods, namely the uneven performance across interaction classes. The proposed four-region categorization is intuitive and likely to resonate with practitioners. The call for methods that move beyond static structure prediction and reduce reliance on multiple sequence alignments is forward-looking and aligns with emerging trends in the field. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Evidence sufficiency Claim pointer The claim that "performance drops when dynamics are important and when interactions lack a strong co-evolutionary history" is presented as a general finding. Evidence pointer Abstract only; location not provided Concern The abstract asserts performance variation across interaction classes without presenting any quantitative data, benchmarks, or systematic comparisons. No specific datasets, metrics, or interaction classes are named. Why it matters Without supporting evidence, this claim cannot be evaluated for accuracy or generalizability. The reader cannot determine whether the performance drops are consistent across methods, datasets, or interaction types, or whether they are anecdotal observations from a limited set of cases. Resolution test Provide quantitative performance comparisons across defined interaction classes, including specific metrics (e.g., DockQ, TM-score, interface RMSD) and benchmark datasets, with appropriate statistical analysis. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Framework validation Claim pointer The proposed four-region categorization of interaction prediction challenges is presented as a useful organizing principle. Evidence pointer Abstract only; location not provided Concern The categorization is introduced without any systematic derivation, literature synthesis, or case-based justification. It is unclear whether these four regions are exhaustive, mutually exclusive, or derived from empirical observations or theoretical considerations. Why it matters If the categorization is not rigorously derived or validated, it risks being an arbitrary taxonomy that does not accurately reflect the landscape of interaction prediction challenges. This would limit its utility as a framework for guiding future research. Resolution test Provide a systematic derivation of the four regions, including examples of interaction classes that fall into each region, discussion of boundary cases, and evidence that the categorization captures meaningful distinctions in method performance or underlying biology. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Actionability of recommendations Claim pointer The statement that "future progress will require methods that rely less on multiple sequence alignments, better distinguish interaction strength and specificity, and move beyond static structure prediction" is presented as a roadmap. Evidence pointer Abstract only; location not provided Concern The recommendations are general and lack specificity regarding how these goals might be achieved, what technical approaches could be pursued, or what challenges might arise in implementing them. Why it matters For a perspective manuscript to be impactful, its recommendations should be sufficiently concrete to guide method development. Vague suggestions without technical context may be of limited practical use. Resolution test Provide more detailed discussion of potential approaches, such as alternative input features to MSAs, methods for modeling interaction dynamics, or strategies for incorporating cellular context, with reference to existing or emerging techniques. Concern ID R1-m3 Severity Minor Axis Scope Affected element Coverage of interaction classes Evidence pointer Abstract; location not provided Issue The abstract does not mention specific interaction classes (e.g., transient versus permanent, obligate versus non-obligate, homo-oligomeric versus hetero-oligomeric) that would help ground the categorization in concrete examples. Required correction Include representative examples of interaction classes within each of the four proposed regions to illustrate the framework. The manuscript's central claims about performance variation and the utility of the proposed categorization cannot be assessed without quantitative evidence and systematic justification. The recommendations in R1-M3, while not blocking, would benefit from greater specificity. Similar distinctions have been discussed in the literature regarding the limitations of co-evolution-based methods and the challenges of dynamic complexes. Scientific importance: The topic is of high importance to the structural biology and computational biology communities, given the widespread adoption of AlphaFold2 and related tools. The manuscript could help set research priorities. Interdisciplinary readership: The topic bridges computational biology, structural biology, and biochemistry, and the abstract is written in a way that is accessible to nonspecialists. However, the lack of concrete examples or data limits its immediate utility for experimentalists. Technical soundness: Cannot be evaluated from the abstract alone. The absence of any quantitative evidence or methodological detail prevents assessment of technical rigor. However, terms such as "co-evolutionary history" and "structural compatibility" would benefit from brief clarification for a broader audience. The conceptual framework is promising and the topic is timely, but the abstract alone does not provide sufficient evidence to support the central claims. A decision would require review of the full manuscript, particularly the evidence for performance variation and the derivation of the categorization. If the full text provides quantitative support and systematic justification, the manuscript could be a valuable perspective piece.

IDR，其中 2/6 的合成变体完全恢复了 RUNX2 驱动的矿化表型。 03 研究问题 具体问题 ：IDR 的序列如何编码生物学功能？能否基于生物物理原理（而非线性基序）对功能性 IDR 进行 de novo 生成设计？ 为什么重要 ：约 35% 的人类蛋白质组为无序区域，转录因子中 IDR 占比更高（约 55%）。现有 AI 结构设计方法对 IDR 无效，IDR 功能设计远落后于折叠蛋白设计。若能建立 IDR 序列→构象系综→功能的映射，将极大扩展可设计蛋白质空间。 现有方法为何不足 ： AlphaFold 等结构预测工具对 IDR 给出低置信度或无结构预测，无法提供设计目标； 现有 IDR 设计工具（如 SLiM 基序设计、统计序列生成）多针对线性基序或单一物化参数（如电荷、疏水性），缺乏对构象系综的系统刻画； 报告基因筛选（如 VP16、ZIM3 biological function in its endogenous cellular context? 04 背景与发展脉络 注：以下脉络为「经外部核验」+「本文框架」混合标注。 IDR 功能编码的早期模型（2010s） ：IDR 功能被认为主要由 SLiMs（短线性基序）介导，通过基序氨基酸在折叠结合口袋中的配位实现特异性结合（Davey et al., 2012; Van Roey 设计（如酸性/疏水性富集）。局限：缺乏对构象系综的直接刻画，预测精度有限。 粗粒化 MD 模拟用于 IDR 系综（2018-2023） ：Mpiri、CALVADOS 等残基级粗粒化力场可快速生成 IDR 构象系综，提供半径回旋、接触图等系综级描述符（Mittal et al., 2018; Joseph et al., 2021）。局限：模拟与功能之间的映射关系尚未建立。 IDR including abstract, introduction, results, methods, and supplementary figure legends Assessment boundary Scientific claims, experimental design, data interpretation, and technical soundness as presented in the provided text Shared manuscript claim summary The authors report that the C-terminal intrinsically disordered region (CIDR) of the transcription factor RUNX2 is required for chromatin binding and osteogenic differentiation. They show that linear sequence motifs are dispensable, and instead features of the conformational ensemble predict function. They develop a generative design algorithm based on biophysical principles and produce de novo functional IDRs that rescue RUNX2 activity. Visible evidence base Abstract, introduction, results narrative, methods, and supplementary figure legends. No primary data files, figures, or tables were provided. Missing materials affecting confidence All figures, tables, and supplementary data files are absent. No numerical results, statistical outputs, or raw data are available for independent verification. The manuscript text alone is insufficient to assess the strength of the evidence. Reviewer Overall assessment The manuscript addresses an important and timely question in the field of intrinsically disordered proteins and transcription factor biology. The authors present a compelling narrative that IDR conformational ensemble features, rather than linear motifs, drive RUNX2 function in a native cellular context. The conceptual advance is significant, and the integration of molecular dynamics simulations with generative design is innovative. However, the absence of all figures, tables, and data files makes it impossible to evaluate the technical soundness of the experiments or the validity of the conclusions. The claims are bold and would require strong evidence to be convincing. The manuscript is likely to be of high interest to the IDP and transcription factor communities, but the current submission cannot be assessed for publication readiness without the full data. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers studying intrinsically disordered proteins, transcription factor biology, chromatin biology, and protein design. The work is also relevant to those interested in stem cell differentiation and regenerative medicine. The generative design approach for IDRs would appeal to computational biologists and protein engineers. Major strengths The conceptual framing is clear and addresses a fundamental gap in the field. The use of a native differentiation assay is a strength compared to reductionist reporter systems. The combination of experimental and computational approaches is well integrated. The finding that linear motifs are dispensable is surprising and important. The generative design of functional IDRs is a significant technical achievement if the evidence supports it. Major Concerns The absence of all primary data prevents evaluation of the central claims. The manuscript text alone cannot support the conclusions drawn. Several specific concerns are listed below. Minor Comments Several methodological details are unclear from the text alone. The presentation would benefit from clearer descriptions of certain analyses. Technical failings that need to be addressed before the case is established The lack of figures, tables, and data files is the primary technical failing. Without these, no claim can be verified. Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality: High. The work challenges the prevailing focus on linear motifs and proposes a new framework for IDR function. Scientific importance: High. The findings could reshape how the field thinks about TF IDRs and their role in gene regulation. Interdisciplinary readership: Moderate to high. The work bridges biophysics, cell biology, and computational design. Technical soundness: Not assessable from the provided text. Readability for nonspecialists: The text is generally well written and accessible, though some computational details may be challenging for a general audience. Recommendation posture Currently not established from the provided evidence. The manuscript cannot be evaluated without the full data. A revised submission with all figures and data would be required for a meaningful assessment. 1994）。MscL 被鉴定为张力门控通道，具有 >3 nS 的巨大电导。 - 阶段二：第一个结构——MtMscL 晶体结构（1998） ：Chang et al. 解析了结核分枝杆菌 MscL 的 X 射线晶体结构（3.5 Å，detergent 中），揭示了同源五聚体架构，每个亚基含两个 TM 螺旋（TM1、TM2）和一个胞质 C 端螺旋。该结构成为后续所有 MscL 研究的模板。 - 阶段三：功能-结构关联与计算模拟（2000s-2010s） ：大量突变研究（如 V23、G22 等）和 MD 模拟（如 Sukharev et al., 2001; Gullingsrud et al., 2001）提出了 helix-tilt 模型，认为门控过程中 TM1 和 TM2 向外倾斜、径向扩张。但缺乏直接的结构证据。 - 阶段四：其他 MscL 同源物结构（2010s-2020s） ：SaMscL（Staphylococcus aureus）和 MaMscL（Methanosarcina acetivorans）的晶体结构被解析，其中 MaMscL 显示了一个 expanded 构象。但这些结构来自 detergent 或非天然脂质环境，且 EcMscL 的结构始终缺失。 - 阶段五：本文工作（2026） ：首次在脂质纳米盘中解析 EcMscL 的 closed 和 expanded 两种构象，结合多种生物物理方法，为 helix-tilt 模型提供了直接的结构验证，并揭示了脂质在门控中的动态角色。 - 脉络标注 : 上述脉络基于本文引言和引用文献，其中阶段一至四为「经外部核验」的领域共识，阶段五为本文贡献。 05 核心痛点 痛点 表现 成因或作者解释 文中证据 EcMscL 全长结构缺失 尽管 EcMscL 是研究最多的 MscL 同源物，但其全长野生型结构从未被解析 蛋白难以结晶（recalcitrance to crystallisation），且分子量小（~15 kDa/亚基，五聚体 ~75 kDa），低于常规 cryoEM 的分子量限制 Introduction 第 2 段 已有结构来自 detergent 或非天然环境 MtMscL、SaMscL、MaMscL 结构均在 detergent 中解析，可能无法反映天然脂质环境中的构象 detergent 可能改变膜蛋白的构象和脂质相互作用 Introduction 第 3 段 open 状态结构难以捕获 机械敏感通道的 open 状态通常是瞬态的，难以稳定 缺乏稳定的 open 状态条件；脂质环境对构象平衡有重要影响 Results 第 1 段、第 2 段 门控机制缺乏直接结构证据 helix-tilt 模型主要基于计算模拟和功能实验，缺乏直接的结构验证 缺乏同一蛋白在 closed 和 open 状态下的结构对比 Discussion 第 1 段 脂质在门控中的角色不明确 脂质如何参与 MscL 门控过程尚不清楚 缺乏高分辨率结构来解析脂质-蛋白相互作用 Results 第 4 段、Discussion 第 3 段 06 核心思想 表面方法 : 将 EcMscL 重构到不同脂质（DMPC、DOPC、DSPC）的纳米盘中，通过 cryoEM 解析 closed（DMPC/DOPC）和 expanded（DSPC）两种构象；用 PELDOR 光谱筛选不同脂质条件下的构象平衡；用 HDX-MS 比较两种构象的溶剂可及性差异；用原子级 MD 模拟验证和补充结构观察。 核心洞察 : 脂质环境（特别是脂质的相态和链长）可以调控 MscL 的构象平衡。DSPC（高 Tm，凝胶相）通过增强脂质-脂质相互作用和膜变薄，将 MscL 稳定在 expanded 状态，而 DMPC/DOPC（低 Tm，液晶相）则稳定 closed 状态。这提供了一种无需突变或外力即可捕获 open-like 状态的方法。 可能的普适教训 [Analysis]: 对于机械敏感通道和其他受膜张力调控的蛋白，脂质环境本身可以作为一种「调控旋钮」来稳定不同的构象状态。在结构生物学中，系统地筛选脂质组成（链长、饱和度、相态）可能比传统的 detergent 筛选更有效地捕获功能性构象。此外，多方法联用（cryoEM + 光谱 + 质谱 + MD）是解析动态膜蛋白机制的强有力策略。 07 方法总览 输入 : 全长野生型 EcMscL 蛋白（C 端 His 标签）；脂质（DMPC、DOPC、DSPC）；MSP1D1/MSP1E3D1 膜支架蛋白。 输出 : 两个 cryoEM 结构：closed（4.1 Å，DMPC/DOPC）和 expanded（7.0 Å，DSPC） PELDOR 距离分布（不同脂质条件） HDX-MS 差异图（DMPC vs DSPC） MD 模拟轨迹（脂质厚度、interdigitation、蛋白-脂质接触） 模块 : 1. 蛋白表达与纯化 : E. coli 表达，Ni-NTA 纯化，SEC 进一步纯化。 2. 纳米盘重构 : 脂质与 MSP 蛋白按比例混合，去垢剂透析去除，形成纳米盘。 3. cryoEM 数据采集与处理 : Titan Krios + Falcon 4i 采集；RELION 4.0 和 CryoSPARC 处理；非均匀细化（non-uniform refinement）。 4. Assessment boundary Scientific content, technical soundness, and support of claims by the presented evidence. Editorial or stylistic issues are noted only where they affect clarity or interpretation. Shared manuscript claim summary The authors report cryoEM structures of full-length wild-type E. coli MscL in closed (DMPC and DOPC nanodiscs) and expanded (DSPC nanodiscs) conformations, and use PELDOR/DEER spectroscopy, HDX-MS, and MD simulations to propose a gating mechanism involving lipid-dependent stabilization of distinct states. Visible evidence base CryoEM density maps and models at 4.1 Å (closed) and 7.0 Å (expanded); PELDOR distance distributions for two spin-labelled sites under multiple lipid conditions; HDX-MS differential uptake data; MD simulations of bilayer and nanodisc systems; pore analysis and lipid contact calculations. Missing materials affecting confidence Supplementary figures and tables referenced but not provided; PDB validation reports not available; specific MD simulation parameters and convergence metrics not fully described; statistical details for HDX-MS comparisons not fully reported. Reviewer Overall assessment This manuscript addresses a long-standing question in mechanosensation: the structural basis of MscL gating. The authors present the first full-length wild-type E. coli MscL structures in two distinct conformations, which is a significant technical achievement given the small size and dynamic nature of this channel. The combination of cryoEM, PELDOR, HDX-MS, and MD is commendable and provides complementary views of the conformational landscape. However, the expanded-state structure is at modest resolution (7.0 Å), and the authors' interpretation of the gating mechanism relies heavily on this map and on MD simulations that may be sensitive to force field and setup choices. The claim that DSPC lipids stabilize an expanded state is supported by PELDOR and cryoEM, but the mechanistic details, particularly the role of specific residues and the relationship to the fully open state, require further validation. The manuscript is well-written and will be of interest to the mechanosensation and membrane protein communities, but several technical concerns must be addressed before the conclusions are fully established. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers studying mechanosensitive channels, membrane protein structure and dynamics, lipid-protein interactions, and the application of integrative structural biology approaches. The work also has relevance for those interested in bacterial osmoregulation and the development of MscL-based biotechnological applications. Major strengths 1) First full-length wild-type E. coli MscL structures in closed and expanded states without stabilizing antibodies or mutations. 2) Integrative use of multiple biophysical techniques (cryoEM, PELDOR, HDX-MS, MD) to cross-validate findings. 3) Identification of a lipid environment (DSPC) that stabilizes an expanded state, providing a new tool for studying MscL gating. 4) The observation that the CTD remains intact during expansion, challenging earlier models of CTD dissociation. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Technical soundness of structural interpretation Claim pointer The authors claim to have solved the structure of MscL in an "expanded/open-like state" at 7.0 Å resolution and use this to propose a gating mechanism. Evidence pointer Results section "The structure of EcMscL in an expanded/open-like state"; Figure 3; Supplementary Figure 9 Concern At 7.0 Å resolution, the assignment of secondary structure and the precise positioning of side chains is not reliable. The authors state that residues 50–73 (the periplasmic loop) were omitted due to insufficient resolution, yet this region is critical for gating. The interpretation of TM helix tilts (23° and 35°) and the claim that the CTD moves as a rigid body depend on accurate model building at this resolution. The authors should provide a detailed validation of the model, including map-to-model fit statistics, and discuss the limitations of interpreting conformational changes at this resolution. It is also unclear how the model was built and refined at 7.0 Å, and whether the observed differences between closed and expanded states are statistically significant given the resolution. Why it matters The central claim of the paper is the structural basis of gating. If the expanded-state model is not reliable at 7.0 Å, the proposed mechanism is not established. The resolution is insufficient to support detailed claims about helix tilts and specific residue interactions. Resolution test Provide a detailed validation report for the 7.0 Å map, including FSC curves, local resolution estimates, and model-to-map correlation. Demonstrate that the observed conformational differences are robust to model building choices (e.g., by building alternative models and showing they converge). If possible, obtain a higher-resolution structure of the expanded state, or provide additional experimental evidence (e.g., cross-linking, FRET) that supports the proposed conformational changes. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Support for the gating mechanism claim Claim pointer The authors propose that DSPC lipids stabilize an expanded state by a "lipid-moves-first" mechanism, where lipid depletion from hydrophobic pockets drives channel expansion. Evidence pointer Results sections "Protein–lipid interactions and critical residues in EcMscL gating" and "Bilayer thickness and interdigitation in EcMscL gating"; Figures 4 and 5 Concern The MD simulations are used to support the mechanism, but the setup and analysis have potential issues. The simulations are relatively short (400 ns) and may not sample the relevant conformational transitions. The use of a single lipid composition (POPE/POPG/cardiolipin) for the closed state and DSPC for the expanded state confounds lipid composition with conformational state. The authors should clarify whether the observed differences in lipid contacts and bilayer properties are due to the protein conformation or the lipid composition itself. Additionally, the claim that "temperature and the associated changes in lipid phase behaviour strongly influence EcMscL hydration" is based on simulations at 30 °C and 87 °C, but the experimental cryoEM and PELDOR data were collected at different temperatures. The link between the simulation results and the experimental observations needs to be made more explicit. Why it matters The proposed mechanism depends on the MD simulations to provide a causal link between lipid properties and channel conformation. If the simulations are not set up or analyzed appropriately, the mechanism is not supported. Resolution test Perform additional simulations with matched lipid compositions (e.g., DMPC vs DSPC with the same protein conformation) to isolate the effect of lipid composition. Extend simulation times and provide convergence metrics. Clearly state the temperature of the simulations and how they relate to the experimental conditions. If possible, perform experimental validation of the proposed lipid-protein interactions (e.g., mutagenesis of key residues followed by functional assays). Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Completeness of evidence for the expanded state Claim pointer The authors state that "open-like states are present" in DSPC based on PELDOR data, and that the cryoEM structure represents an expanded state. Evidence pointer Results section "Monitoring the EcMscL conformational ensemble in membranes by PELDOR"; Figure 2; Supplementary Figures 5–8 Concern The PELDOR data show broad distance distributions, indicating conformational heterogeneity. The authors interpret this as a shift away from the closed state, but the data do not clearly demonstrate that a specific expanded state is populated. The cryoEM structure in DSPC was solved from a subset of particles (17,211) that may represent only a minor population. The authors should provide a quantitative analysis of the PELDOR data, including the fraction of expanded states, and discuss how the cryoEM structure relates to the ensemble observed by PELDOR. It is also unclear whether the expanded state observed in DSPC is the same as the open state observed in electrophysiology, or a sub-conducting state. Why it matters The claim that the structure represents an "open-like state" is central to the paper. If the expanded state is a minor population or a sub-conducting state, the conclusions about the gating mechanism may need to be revised. Resolution test Provide a quantitative decomposition of the PELDOR distance distributions into closed and expanded components, with uncertainties. Compare the pore dimensions of the expanded state to those estimated from electrophysiology for the open and sub-conducting states. Discuss the relationship between the cryoEM structure and the ensemble observed by PELDOR. Risk / unsupported claims The claim that the expanded state represents an "open-like state" is not fully supported by the data, as the resolution is limited and the relationship to the electrophysiologically defined open state is not established. The proposed "lipid-moves-first" mechanism is inferred from MD simulations that may not be fully converged and that confound lipid composition with protein conformation.
