no external data or unpublished materials consulted Shared manuscript claim summary The authors report an integrated computation-guided workflow for thermostabilizing the fungal sweet protein Honey Truffle Sweetener (HTS). They determined the HTS crystal structure, used Rosetta and ThermoMPNN for candidate mutation screening, developed a machine learning model (SMRC-Net) for Tm prediction, and assembled stabilizing mutations stepwise. The final variant FM achieved a melting temperature of 82.1 °C (27.5 °C above wild-type), retained sweetness in untreated samples, and showed improved heat and pH tolerance in terms of solubility and secondary structure. Visible evidence base Crystal structure (Table 1, Fig. 1), computational screening results (Fig. 2), SMRC-Net cross-validation metrics (Fig. 3, Table S4), prospective variant testing (Fig. 4, Table S16), modular assembly Tm data (Fig. 5, Table S9), CD spectra (Fig. 6), MD analyses (Fig. 7, Fig. 8, Tables S11–S13), sensory evaluation (Table S3), disulfide variant data (Table S1), H16A/F99A mutant data (Table S15) Missing materials affecting confidence Supplementary figures and tables referenced but not provided in full (Figs. S1–S7, Tables S1–S18); detailed SMRC-Net architecture and hyperparameters only in Supplementary Methods; sensory evaluation raw data not shown; statistical details for some comparisons not fully specified Reviewer Overall assessment This manuscript presents a well-structured and potentially valuable workflow for protein thermostabilization, with a clear demonstration of success in a challenging target protein. The integration of structure determination, complementary computational screening, machine learning, and stepwise experimental assembly is logical and the reported Tm improvement is substantial. However, several technical aspects require clarification and additional evidence before the case is fully established, particularly regarding the generalizability of SMRC-Net, the statistical robustness of the sensory data, and the mechanistic interpretation of the MD analyses. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers in protein engineering, food science, and structural biology would be interested. The work addresses a practical bottleneck in using sweet proteins as sugar substitutes, and the computation-guided workflow could be applicable to other compact proteins with limited stability. The combination of physics-based and deep learning methods, plus the residual learning framework, may interest computational biologists developing protein stability prediction tools. Major strengths 1) The crystal structure provides a solid foundation for rational design. 2) The complementary use of Rosetta and ThermoMPNN is sensible and well-justified. 3) The stepwise modular assembly strategy is methodologically sound and reduces risk of incompatible mutations. 4) The final Tm improvement of 27.5 °C is substantial and practically meaningful. 5) The inclusion of heat and pH tolerance assays adds practical relevance beyond simple Tm measurements. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Technical soundness of SMRC-Net validation Claim pointer "Repeated nested cross-validation supported quantitative Tm prediction within the HTS scaffold, while prospective testing showed 9/10 directional agreement in a small, computationally selected variant set." Evidence pointer Section 3.3, Fig. 3, Table S4; Section 3.4, Fig. 4, Table S16 Concern The nested cross-validation is performed on 65 variants, all derived from the same protein scaffold and selected through the same computational pipeline. This creates a potential selection bias: the model is trained and tested on variants that were pre-filtered by Rosetta and ThermoMPNN, which may not represent the full mutation space. The prospective set of 10 variants is very small, and the reported 9/10 directional agreement, while encouraging, has wide confidence intervals. More critically, the manuscript does not report whether the SMRC-Net predictions were compared against simpler baselines (e.g., using only ESM2 features, or only MD features) in the nested cross-validation, which would be necessary to demonstrate the added value of the residual correction module. Why it matters The central methodological contribution of this work is the SMRC-Net framework. If its performance is not rigorously benchmarked against appropriate baselines and its generalizability is not demonstrated beyond a narrow, pipeline-selected variant set, the claim that it provides a useful "mutation-centered" prediction tool is not fully supported. Resolution test Provide ablation studies in the nested cross-validation (ESM2-only, MD-only, and combined models). Report confidence intervals for the 9/10 directional agreement. Ideally, test the frozen model on a set of variants that were not selected by the same Rosetta/ThermoMPNN pipeline, even if small. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Evidence for retained sweetness Claim pointer "Untreated FM retained sweetness, while separate heat- and pH-treatment assays showed retained solubility and largely preserved secondary-structure profiles. Sweetness after these treatments was not evaluated." Evidence pointer Section 3.5, Table S3 Concern The sensory evaluation is described only in terms of threshold values in Table S3, which is not provided in the main text. The manuscript states that "sweetness thresholds of Mut10-1 and FM remained within a range similar to that of WT," but no statistical analysis of these thresholds is presented. With only eight panelists, the power to detect meaningful differences is limited. Furthermore, the critical claim for practical application would be sweetness retention after heat or pH treatment, which the authors explicitly state was not evaluated. This is a significant gap given that the stated motivation is use in thermally processed foods. Why it matters The practical value of the engineered variant depends on retaining sweetness under processing-relevant conditions. Without data on sweetness after heat or pH treatment, the claim that FM is suitable for thermally processed foods is not established. Resolution test Provide the full sensory data with statistical analysis (e.g., confidence intervals for thresholds). At minimum, evaluate sweetness of FM after a relevant heat treatment (e.g., 80 °C for 1 h) to demonstrate functional retention under the conditions where solubility and structure are maintained. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Mechanistic interpretation of MD analyses Claim pointer "Molecular dynamics analyses indicated that FM was not uniformly rigidified but instead exhibited localized flexibility redistribution and a more consolidated conformational ensemble." Evidence pointer Section 3.6, Fig. 7, Fig. 8, Tables S11–S13 Concern The MD analyses are descriptive and correlative. The manuscript reports differences in RMSF, SASA, contact persistence, and free-energy landscapes between WT and FM, but does not establish a causal link between specific mutations and the observed stability increase. For example, the H16-F99 contact is identified as contributing to stability based on a double mutant, but it is unclear how this contact relates to the other 11 mutations in FM. The free-energy landscape analysis (Fig. 8d) is qualitative; no quantitative metrics (e.g., free-energy differences between basins) are provided. Why it matters Without a clearer mechanistic link between the introduced mutations and the observed stability changes, the generalizability of the design principles to other proteins is uncertain. The manuscript would be strengthened by identifying which mutations contribute most to stability and why. Resolution test Perform additional MD analyses to quantify free-energy differences between conformational states. Consider alanine scanning or reversion mutants to identify key stabilizing mutations and test their individual contributions. Relate specific mutations to the observed flexibility redistribution. Minor Comments Concern ID R1-m1 Severity Minor Axis Clarity of methods Affected element SMRC-Net architecture description Evidence pointer Section 2.5 (implied), Supplementary Methods Issue The main text provides only a high-level description of SMRC-Net. Key details such as the number of MD features, the specific feature selection method, and the model architecture (e.g., number of layers, regularization) are relegated to the Supplementary Methods. Required correction Provide a concise summary of the SMRC-Net architecture and key hyperparameters in the main text or a table, so that readers can assess the model without consulting the supplement. Concern ID R1-m2 Severity Minor Axis Statistical reporting Affected element Tm measurements and comparisons Evidence pointer Fig. 2c, Fig. 5c, Table S9 Issue The manuscript reports Tm values as mean ± SD from triplicate measurements but does not state the number of independent protein preparations or whether the triplicates are technical or biological replicates. The statistical significance of differences between variants is not consistently reported. Required correction Clarify the nature of replicates and report the number of independent experiments. Where comparisons are made, provide appropriate statistical tests and effect sizes. Concern ID R1-m3 Severity Minor Axis Completeness of data presentation Affected element Sensory evaluation Evidence pointer Table S3 Issue The sensory evaluation is summarized only as threshold values. The manuscript does not describe the training of panelists, the number of sessions, or the variability across panelists. Required correction Provide a brief description of the sensory protocol in the main text and include individual panelist data or a measure of inter-panelist variability in the supplement. Concern ID R1-m4 Severity Minor Axis Interpretation of CD data Affected element Fig. 6c, Fig. 6f, Table S10 Issue The CD spectra are described as showing "largely preserved secondary-structure profiles," but the quantitative secondary-structure content estimates (presumably from BeStSel) are only in Table S10. It is unclear whether the differences between WT and FM under stress conditions are statistically significant. Required correction Report the secondary-structure content estimates in the main text or a main-text figure, with appropriate statistical comparisons. Concern ID R1-m5 Severity Minor Axis Disulfide bond validation Claim pointer "The final variant, FM, had a melting temperature of 82.1 °C, 27.5 °C higher than that of wild-type HTS." Evidence pointer Section 3.5, Fig. 5b, Table S1 Issue The manuscript states that an engineered disulfide bond was introduced (Cys37-Cys46), but it is not explicitly stated whether formation of the disulfide bond was experimentally confirmed (e.g., by mass spectrometry or non-reducing SDS-PAGE). The Tm increase attributed to the disulfide bond could be confounded by the accompanying mutations. Required correction Provide evidence for disulfide bond formation in the purified FM protein, or acknowledge that the contribution of the disulfide bond to stability is inferred from the Tm of the disulfide-only variant. Technical failings that need to be addressed before the case is established 1) Lack of ablation studies for SMRC-Net to demonstrate the added value of the MD residual correction over the ESM2 baseline alone. 2) Absence of sweetness evaluation after heat or pH treatment, which is central to the practical application claim. 3) Insufficient statistical detail for sensory data and some Tm comparisons. 4) No experimental confirmation of disulfide bond formation in FM. Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality: The integration of complementary computational methods with a residual learning framework is a novel contribution, though individual components are established. Scientific importance: The work addresses a real bottleneck in sweet protein application and provides a potentially transferable workflow. Interdisciplinary readership: The work bridges structural biology, computational biology, and food science, and should appeal to readers across these fields. Technical soundness: The experimental design is generally sound, but the validation of SMRC-Net and the sensory data require strengthening. Readability for nonspecialists: The manuscript is clearly written and accessible, though the SMRC-Net section may be challenging for readers without machine learning background. Recommendation posture Supportive if technical concerns are resolved. The core experimental achievement (a 27.5 °C Tm increase with retained sweetness) is significant and likely reproducible. However, the validation of the computational framework and the missing post-treatment sweetness data must be addressed before the broader claims of the workflow's utility are fully established. Risk / unsupported claims The claim that SMRC-Net provides "quantitative Tm prediction" is only supported within a narrow, pipeline-selected variant set; generalizability to other proteins or even other regions of the HTS sequence space is not demonstrated. The claim that FM "retained sweetness" is based on threshold data in the supplement without statistical analysis; the claim that it is suitable for thermally processed foods is unsupported because sweetness after heat or pH treatment was not evaluated. The mechanistic interpretation that FM stabilization arises from "localized flexibility redistribution and a more consolidated conformational ensemble" is correlative; no causal link between specific mutations and these changes is established. The statement that the engineered disulfide bond contributes to stability is inferred from Tm data but not directly confirmed by structural or biochemical evidence of disulfide formation.

Claims and evidence presented in the abstract; no access to full methods, figures, tables, or supplementary material Shared manuscript claim summary The authors report a computational analysis of non-synonymous SNPs in the human TNF gene, identifying I118F and I118N as high-risk variants with predicted destabilizing effects at a conserved residue. Molecular dynamics simulations (200 ns) are claimed to show increased structural fluctuations, reduced compactness, altered principal component and free energy landscapes, and weaker dynamic coupling for these mutants relative to wild-type TNF. The authors state that relevance to ALD-associated neuroinflammation remains hypothetical. Visible evidence base Abstract text only; no quantitative data, simulation parameters, validation metrics, or statistical analyses are provided Missing materials affecting confidence Full methods, simulation setup and force field parameters, convergence criteria, replicate details, pathogenicity prediction scores, conservation analysis details, all figures and tables, and any supplementary data Reviewer Overall assessment The abstract presents a plausible computational workflow for prioritizing nsSNPs in TNF and characterizing two candidate variants via MD simulations. However, the evidence base is limited to qualitative statements without quantitative support, and the link to ALD is explicitly acknowledged as hypothetical. The technical soundness cannot be fully assessed from the abstract alone, and the scientific advance over existing computational SNP prioritization studies is not clearly articulated. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers in computational genomics and protein biophysics interested in TNF variant effects; investigators studying ALD pathophysiology who may use these predictions to guide experimental validation. The work may also interest methodologists applying MD simulations to disease-associated SNPs. Major strengths The study integrates multiple established pathogenicity prediction tools, which is a standard and defensible approach. The use of 200 ns MD simulations with multiple analyses (RMSD, Rg, PCA, FEL, DCCM) is comprehensive for a computational study. The authors appropriately acknowledge the hypothetical nature of the ALD connection, avoiding overclaiming. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Technical soundness Claim pointer "MD simulations demonstrated that these mutations result in heightened structural fluctuations, as indicated by elevated RMSD and Radius of Gyration (Rg) values, signifying a reduction in structural compactness." Evidence pointer Abstract; location not provided Concern The abstract reports qualitative outcomes (elevated RMSD and Rg) without any numerical values, error estimates, or statistical comparisons between wild-type and mutants. It is unclear whether the observed differences exceed simulation noise or replicate variability. Why it matters Without quantitative data and appropriate statistical treatment, the claim of "heightened structural fluctuations" cannot be evaluated for significance. This is central to the paper's main conclusion about variant-induced destabilization. Resolution test Provide mean and standard deviation (or confidence intervals) for RMSD and Rg across replicates, with statistical tests (e.g., per-residue or per-time-point comparisons) demonstrating significant differences between wild-type and each mutant. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Technical soundness Claim pointer "The PCA and FEL analyses showed that the wild-type protein keeps a stable energy minimum, whereas DCCM analysis indicated that the I118F and I118N mutations exhibit weaker dynamic coupling with more than one metastable state, leading to lesser stable structure." Evidence pointer Abstract; location not provided Concern The interpretation of PCA, FEL, and DCCM results is presented without methodological details or quantitative descriptors. No free energy values, projection plots, or correlation coefficients are given. The claim of "more than one metastable state" is not supported by any visible metric. Why it matters These analyses are used to support the conclusion of compromised trimer stability and dynamics. Without quantitative evidence, the conclusions are not reproducible or verifiable from the abstract. Resolution test Include free energy differences between basins, PCA eigenvalue spectra, and DCCM correlation matrices with significance thresholds. Provide representative plots in the main text or supplementary material. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Scientific importance Claim pointer "These findings suggest that the identified TNF variants may influence TNF protein stability and conformational dynamics; however, their relevance to ALD-associated neuroinflammation remains hypothetical and requires experimental and clinical validation." Evidence pointer Abstract; location not provided Concern The abstract does not establish a mechanistic or epidemiological link between TNF nsSNPs and ALD. The selection of TNF as a target is motivated by its role in neuroinflammation, but no evidence is presented that I118F or I118N occur in ALD patients or are associated with disease severity. Why it matters The title and framing imply a role in ALD, but the abstract explicitly concedes the connection is hypothetical. This limits the translational significance and may overstate the relevance to the disease context. Resolution test Clarify whether these variants have been observed in ALD cohorts or general populations, and discuss their allele frequencies. If not, reframe the study as a general TNF variant analysis with potential relevance to neuroinflammatory conditions. Minor Comments Concern ID R1-m1 Severity Minor Axis Readability for nonspecialists Affected element Methods description Evidence pointer Abstract; location not provided Issue The list of prediction tools is dense and may overwhelm nonspecialist readers without context on how they complement each other. Required correction Briefly explain the rationale for using multiple tools (e.g., consensus scoring) and define key terms like "nsSNP" and "conserved residue" for a broader audience. Concern ID R1-m2 Severity Minor Axis Technical soundness Affected element Simulation length justification Evidence pointer Abstract; location not provided Issue The choice of 200 ns simulation time is stated but not justified. For a trimeric protein, this may be insufficient to sample large conformational changes. Required correction Provide a justification for the simulation length, referencing convergence tests or prior studies on similar systems. Concern ID R1-m3 Severity Minor Axis Scientific importance Affected element Variant selection Evidence pointer Abstract; location not provided Issue Only two variants (I118F and I118N) are selected for MD simulations, but the criteria for this selection beyond "strong computational evidence" are not specified. Required correction State the exact thresholds or ranking criteria used to select these variants from the initial SNP pool. Technical failings that need to be addressed before the case is established R1-M1 and R1-M2 are blocking because the central claims of structural destabilization and altered dynamics are not quantitatively supported. The lack of statistical analysis and methodological detail prevents verification of the conclusions. Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality: Moderate. The application of standard computational tools to TNF is not novel, though the specific focus on position 118 may be new. Scientific importance: Limited. The ALD connection is hypothetical, and the abstract does not demonstrate clinical or functional relevance. Interdisciplinary readership: Narrow. The work is primarily of interest to computational biologists and ALD researchers; the abstract does not frame findings for a broader audience. Technical soundness: Not fully assessable from the abstract. The workflow is standard, but quantitative evidence is missing. Readability for nonspecialists: Acceptable but could be improved with clearer definitions and less jargon. Recommendation posture Currently not established from the provided evidence. The abstract presents a reasonable computational study, but the lack of quantitative data and the explicitly hypothetical ALD link mean the core claims cannot be evaluated. Supportive if technical concerns are resolved and the ALD relevance is either substantiated or appropriately de-emphasized. Risk / unsupported claims The claim that I118F and I118N are "high-risk" variants is unsupported without population frequency data or experimental validation. The claim of "reduction in structural compactness" is unsupported without quantitative Rg values and statistical comparison. The claim of "more than one metastable state" is unsupported without free energy landscape data. The relevance of TNF variants to ALD-associated neuroinflammation is explicitly acknowledged as hypothetical and is therefore not an established claim.

01 基本信息 标题 ：Large-scale prospective evaluation of co-folding across hundreds of Mac1-ligand complexes and three virtual screens 作者与单位 ：Kim, Jongbin; Correy, Galen J; Hall, Brendan W; Rachman, Moira M; Mailhot, Olivier; Togo, Takaya; Gonciarz, Ryan L; Jaishankar, Priyadarshini; Neitz, R Jeffrey; Hantz, Eric R; Doruk, Yagmur U; Diolaiti, Morgan E; Reid, Rashad; Gopalkrishnan, Saumya; Krogan, Nevan J; Renslo, Adam R; Ashworth, Alan; Shoichet, Brian K; Fraser, James S（加州大学旧金山分校等，具体单位未提供） 期刊/预印本平台 ：eLife 年份 ：2026 论文类型 ：前瞻性基准评估（prospective evaluation） 领域 ：蛋白质-配体共折叠预测、虚拟筛选、结构生物学、AI 药物发现 关键词 ：co-folding, AlphaFold3, Boltz-2, Chai-1, Mac1, virtual screening, docking, structure-based drug design DOI/arXiv 号 ：10.7554/eLife.110475 代码 ：https://github.com/jongbin99/cofold-em 数据 ：468 个新 Mac1-配体复合物结构（PDB 收录），另有 22 个来自早期研究；三个虚拟筛选数据集来自 LSD（https://lsd.docking.org/） 阅读日期 ：2026-10-12 在课题方向中的位置 ：本文是共折叠（co-folding）深度学习方法（AF3、Boltz-2、Chai-1）在蛋白质-配体复合物结构预测与虚拟筛选重排序中的大规模前瞻性评估，直接面向「结构预测 × 分子对接 × AI 方法」交叉领域，提供了关于泛化性、记忆效应、置信度-亲和力相关性的关键证据。 02 一句话总结 本文通过 551 个训练截止日期后测定的 Mac1-配体共晶结构及三个大型虚拟筛选数据集，前瞻性评估了 AF3、Boltz-2、Chai-1 三种共折叠方法，发现它们能高保真重现多数配体构象（>50% 优于 2 Å RMSD），但无法捕捉蛋白构象变化，且其置信度/亲和力分数在区分真实配体与对接假阳性方面弱于传统对接打分。 03 研究问题 具体问题 ：共折叠深度学习方法（AF3、Boltz-2、Chai-1）在训练截止日期后的全新蛋白质-配体复合物上，能否准确预测配体结合构象？其内部置信度/亲和力分数能否用于虚拟筛选命中重排序？ 为什么重要 ：共折叠方法被广泛用于结构预测和药物发现，但其评估多基于训练集内或回顾性数据，存在记忆效应风险；前瞻性、大规模、独立于训练数据的评估是判断其真实泛化能力的关键。 现有方法不足 ：已有评估样本量小、缺乏训练独立性控制，且多聚焦于蛋白结构预测而非配体构象与亲和力排序；DOCK 等物理方法虽快但精度有限，缺乏与深度学习方法在大规模前瞻性数据上的系统对比。 精确研究问题 ：Can co-folding methods (AF3, Boltz-2, Chai-1) prospectively predict ligand binding poses and rank ligands by affinity on complexes determined after their training cutoff dates, and do their confidence/affinity scores outperform docking in distinguishing true ligands from false positives in virtual screening hit lists? 04 背景与发展脉络 （标注：以下脉络为「经外部核验」的领域共识，结合本文引言整理） 1. AlphaFold2/RosettaFold 时代（2021-） ：革命性提升蛋白结构预测精度，但主要针对 apo 蛋白，无法直接处理配体。 2. 共折叠方法兴起（2024-） ：AF3、Chai-1、Boltz-2 等通过扩散模型或流匹配直接预测蛋白-配体复合物结构，并输出置信度分数（ipTM、pLTP）和亲和力预测（Boltz-2 pIC50）。 3. 回顾性评估的局限 ：早期评估多使用训练集内或已知结构，存在记忆效应；少量前瞻性研究样本量小，结论不一致。 4. 本文位置 ：首次在数百个训练截止后测定的复合物和三个大型虚拟筛选数据集上，系统评估共折叠方法的结构预测与亲和力排序能力，并与传统对接（DOCK3.7）对比，填补了前瞻性大规模评估的空白。 05 核心痛点 痛点 表现 成因或作者解释 文中证据 训练数据记忆效应 模型可能在训练集内结构上表现好，但泛化未知 共折叠方法训练数据包含大量 PDB 结构，测试集若与训练集重叠会高估性能 作者特意选择训练截止日期后测定的 551 个复合物，并量化了与训练集的相似性（图 1d） 蛋白构象变化无法预测 配体结合诱导的肽段翻转、loop 开放等构象变化未被共折叠方法重现 共折叠方法倾向于预测 apo 或常见构象，缺乏对诱导-fit 的显式建模 19 个 twisted 态仅 4 个被 AF3 正确预测，20 个 open 态全部失败（图 2b） 置信度分数与亲和力相关性弱 AF3 L-pLDDT 与实验 IC50 相关性弱（r=0.314），DOCK 能量更弱（r=-0.225） 置信度分数主要反映结构确定性而非结合自由能；亲和力预测模块与结构模块解耦 图 4a，Results 节 虚拟筛选中假阳性区分度不足 AF3 L-pLDDT 在三个虚拟筛选数据集中 AUC 仅 46.4-60.5，部分低于随机 共折叠方法对高打分但非真实配体的分子缺乏物理化学区分能力 图 5a-c，Results 节 亲和力绝对误差大 Boltz-2 pIC50 在 Mac1 上 MAE 约 1.6 kcal/mol，校正后约 0.7 kcal/mol 亲和力预测模块训练数据有限，且对弱结合剂预测偏差大 图 4a，Results 节 06 核心思想 表面方法 ：对 551 个 Mac1-配体复合物和三个虚拟筛选数据集（AmpC、σ2、D4），分别运行 AF3、Boltz-2、Chai-1 共折叠预测，计算配体 RMSD、置信度分数（L-pLDDT、ipTM、pIC50），并与 DOCK3.7 对接打分对比，评估结构预测准确性和亲和力排序能力。 核心洞察 ： - 共折叠方法在配体构象预测上显著优于传统对接（>50% 优于 2 Å RMSD），且对训练集外分子泛化良好，说明其学到了可迁移的分子识别模式。 - 但共折叠方法无法预测蛋白构象变化（诱导-fit），且其置信度/亲和力分数在虚拟筛选假阳性区分上弱于对接打分，说明结构预测能力 ≠ 亲和力排序能力。 - 物理方法（DOCK）与深度学习方法（共折叠）的错误相关性低，提示两者在命中发现中可能互补。 可能的普适教训 [Analysis]：共折叠方法擅长「几何匹配」但缺乏「物理化学判别力」；在药物发现中，结构预测精度与亲和力排序是两种不同任务，应分别评估和优化；将物理打分与深度学习置信度结合可能是更优策略。 07 方法总览 输入 ：蛋白序列（Mac1、AmpC、σ2、D4）、配体 SMILES、蛋白结构（对接用，PDB 5SQW 等） 输出 ：预测的蛋白-配体复合物结构（mmCIF）、配体 RMSD、置信度分数（AF3 L-pLDDT、Chai-1 ipTM、Boltz-2 pIC50）、DOCK3.7 能量打分 模块 ： 1. They report that co-folding methods reproduce ligand poses with >50% accuracy at 2 Å RMSD, that confidence scores weakly track affinity, and that co-folding does not outperform docking in distinguishing true ligands from false positives in virtual screening hit lists. Visible evidence base Full text including results narrative, figure references, supplementary file references, methods section, and data availability statement Missing materials affecting confidence Figures, tables, and supplementary files referenced but not provided; specific numerical values for many reported statistics; details of statistical test implementations; complete crystallographic data Reviewer Overall assessment This manuscript addresses an important and timely question: whether deep-learning co-folding methods can be applied prospectively to ligand pose prediction and virtual screening hit prioritization. The Mac1 dataset of 551 previously unpublished complexes is a substantial and valuable resource, and the prospective nature of the evaluation is a genuine strength. However, the manuscript's central claims are only partially supported by the evidence presented. The pose prediction results are convincing, but the affinity correlation analyses are weakened by the limited dynamic range of the dataset and the absence of key statistical details. The virtual screening results, while interesting, are presented in a way that makes it difficult to assess whether the conclusions are robust. The manuscript would benefit from clearer presentation of the statistical methods, additional analyses to support the claim of complementarity between docking and co-folding, and a more nuanced discussion of the limitations of the affinity predictions. Who would be interested in the results, and why Computational chemists and structural biologists working on ligand-protein complex prediction and virtual screening will find this study directly relevant. Drug discovery scientists using structure-based methods will be interested in the practical implications for hit prioritization workflows. Developers of deep-learning methods for molecular modeling will find the prospective evaluation valuable for understanding the strengths and limitations of current approaches. The Mac1 dataset itself will be a useful benchmark for future method development. Major strengths The prospective design of the study is a significant strength, as it avoids the circularity that plagues many retrospective evaluations. The Mac1 dataset is large and previously unpublished, providing a genuinely independent test set. The comparison across three co-folding methods and three different targets in the virtual screening component adds breadth. The authors are appropriately cautious in their interpretation of the affinity correlations, acknowledging the limited dynamic range. The discussion of complementarity between physics-based and deep-learning approaches is thoughtful and well-framed. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Statistical rigor Claim pointer The authors report that Boltz-2 affinity predictions showed the strongest correlation with measured potency and achieved lower mean absolute error than a baseline predictor after calibration. Evidence pointer Results section, Figure 4a; Methods, Statistical analysis Concern The claim that Boltz-2 affinity predictions outperform a baseline predictor is based on a comparison to the mean pIC50 of the dataset. However, the dataset has a limited dynamic range (sub-micromolar to >500 µM), and the baseline predictor is not clearly defined. The manuscript does not report confidence intervals for the MAE values, nor does it specify how many compounds were used in the calibration. The statistical comparison between Boltz-2 and the baseline is not described with sufficient detail to assess its validity. Why it matters The claim that Boltz-2 provides meaningful affinity predictions is a key finding of the study. If the comparison to baseline is not statistically robust, the conclusion that co-folding methods can predict affinity is weakened. The limited dynamic range of the dataset may also inflate the apparent performance of the baseline predictor, making the comparison less meaningful. Resolution test The authors should provide a clear definition of the baseline predictor, report confidence intervals for all MAE values, and describe the statistical test used to compare Boltz-2 to the baseline. They should also report the distribution of pIC50 values in the dataset and discuss how the limited dynamic range affects the interpretation of the results. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Evidence sufficiency Claim pointer The authors state that co-folding methods did not meaningfully outperform docking in distinguishing true ligands from false positives in the three virtual screening hit lists. Evidence pointer Results section, Figure 5; Methods, Benchmarking co-folding on experimentally validated compounds Concern The virtual screening analysis is presented with limited methodological detail. The manuscript does not specify how the hit lists were constructed, how many compounds were in each list, or how the thresholds for true hits and non-binders were defined for each target. The AUC values are reported, but the authors do not provide confidence intervals or statistical tests to determine whether the differences between methods are significant. The claim that co-folding methods "struggle" to re-rank hit lists is based on a comparison that may not be statistically powered. Why it matters The virtual screening results are a central component of the manuscript's conclusions about the limitations of co-folding methods. Without clear methodological details and statistical analysis, it is not possible to determine whether the findings are robust or whether they reflect the specific choices made in this study. Resolution test The authors should provide a detailed description of the hit list construction, including the number of compounds and the criteria for selecting them. They should report confidence intervals for all AUC values and perform statistical tests to compare the performance of different methods. They should also describe the thresholds used to define true hits and non-binders for each target. Evidence pointer Results section, Figure 3—figure supplement 3; Discussion Concern The claim of complementarity is based on the observation that errors between methods are not highly correlated. However, the manuscript does not provide a quantitative analysis of this complementarity, nor does it demonstrate that combining the methods would improve performance. The suggestion that integrating the methods "may help" is speculative and not supported by direct evidence. Why it matters The claim of complementarity is a key takeaway of the manuscript and has practical implications for how these methods might be used in drug discovery. Without a direct demonstration that combining methods improves performance, the claim remains an interesting hypothesis rather than a supported conclusion. Resolution test The authors should perform an analysis that directly tests whether combining docking and co-folding scores improves hit prioritization compared to either method alone. 18/24），层深选择本身就是一个可优化的超参数维度。 集成多样性来自三个正交维度 ：pLM 家族（预训练范式差异）、层深（信息抽象层次差异）、预测头（归纳偏置差异：卷积捕捉局部模式、Transformer 捕捉长程依赖、门控循环捕捉序列方向性）。三者交叉产生的多样性无法通过单一模型的参数扩展复制。 膜蛋白界面具有可学习的序列信号 ：尽管跨膜区 MSA 退化，但 pLM 嵌入中编码的疏水打包模式、螺旋-螺旋接触基序和拓扑约束足以支持高精度界面预测，无需显式结构输入。 3) 可能的普适教训 [Analysis] 集成设计应追求「表征空间的正交性」而非「模型数量的堆叠」 ：本文的对照实验显示，同一 pLM 不同层的集成增益远小于跨 pLM 家族的集成增益，说明真正带来性能提升的是信息源的多样性而非参数量的增加。这一原则可迁移到其他蛋白质预测任务（如稳定性预测、功能位点注释）。 「最优层」是任务相关的 ：本文的层深分析提示，不同下游任务可能需要不同抽象层次的特征。这为迁移学习实践提供了一个通用建议：在冻结 pLM 时，应系统搜索层深而非默认使用最后一层。 生物物理先验可作为验证而非输入 ：CHORUS 不使用任何结构/拓扑先验，但通过跨膜定位、螺旋连接度等探针验证了预测结果与已知生物物理规律的一致性。这种「先预测、后验证」的策略适合数据稀缺领域。 07 方法总览 输入 ：膜蛋白氨基酸序列（仅序列，无结构、无 MSA、无伙伴信息） 输出 ：每个残基的 PPI 界面概率 p_i ∈ [0,1]，以及经阈值 τ_val = 0.554 二值化的界面/非界面分类 模块 ： 1. pLM 嵌入提取 ：本文解决的是 膜蛋白残基级 PPI 界面预测 任务，即给定单条膜蛋白序列，预测哪些残基参与与其他蛋白的物理接触（≤5Å）。这不是复合物结构预测，不预测结合伙伴身份、结合亲和力或构象变化。 有边界的结论 ： 1. 在膜蛋白范围内 ，CHORUS 的 chain-macro-AP 为 0.643，优于 18 种既有方法（最佳基线 0.613），但绝对性能仍有提升空间——约 36% 的界面残基无法被正确识别。 2. 跨膜核心区优势最显著 （AP = 0.746），但 可溶性蛋白迁移性能不稳定 （AUROC 0.469-0.960），且固定阈值在可溶性蛋白上失效——模型学到的可能是膜环境特异的接触规则。 3. 集成增益来自跨 pLM 家族互补性 ，而非参数规模或简单模型平均。对照实验显示，同 pLM 不同层/不同种子的集成增益远小于跨家族集成。 4. 预测界面与配体结合位点正交 （O/E ≈ 0.979），说明模型捕捉的是 PPI 特异信号而非通用口袋特征——但这也意味着 PPI 界面与配体位点的协同/变构关系未被建模。 5. 蛋白质组规模图谱是预测而非实验验证 ：80,619 条序列的界面注释全部来自模型推断，未经湿实验验证。图谱的价值在于假设生成和优先级排序，而非确定性注释。 不可支持的更强结论 ： - 不能声称 CHORUS 可替代结构生物学实验或 AlphaFold 类方法进行复合物结构解析。 - 不能声称序列嵌入「理解」了膜蛋白折叠物理——AP 提升可能来自统计关联而非因果机制。 - 不能将 5Å 接触阈值等同于功能相关界面——几何接触 ≠ 功能必需。 12 作者自认局限 局限 具体表现 作者提出的未来方向 来源 5Å 阈值为几何代理 接触距离不能直接反映结合亲和力或热力学贡献 引入结合自由能或突变实验数据作为监督信号 学到什么 标题写「Agent 提炼的知识候选」 可迁移的概念 「表征正交性」优于「参数规模」 ：CHORUS 最核心的可迁移洞见是——集成学习的收益来自信息源的多样性（不同 pLM 家族、不同层深、不同归纳偏置），而非模型数量或参数量的堆叠。对照实验显示，跨 pLM 家族集成增益（0.643 vs 单模型最优 0.614）远大于同 pLM 内层深或种子的变化。 迁移建议 ：在设计蛋白质预测模型时，与其扩大单一模型，不如系统探索多个预训练模型的表征互补性。 层深是未被充分利用的超参数 ：CHORUS 证明最优层因 pLM 家族和任务而异（ESM-2 在 layer 30，ProtT5 在 layer 18/24），且最优层通常不是最后一层。 迁移建议 ：在冻结 pLM 做下游任务时，应系统搜索层深而非默认使用最后一层或平均池化。 「先预测、后验证」的生物物理一致性检查 ：CHORUS 不使用任何结构先验，但通过跨膜定位、螺旋连接度、配体位点正交性等探针验证预测结果与已知生物物理规律的一致性。 迁移建议 ：在数据稀缺的蛋白质预测任务中，可用已知生物物理规律作为预测结果的验证锚点，而非仅依赖监督标签。 严格同源性隔离的评测协议 ：CHORUS 的 419 拓扑簇划分确保测试集与训练集无 ≥30% 序列同一性，且外部验证集经同样过滤。 迁移建议 ：在蛋白质预测任务中，序列相似性聚类应作为数据划分的默认协议，否则性能估计会因泄漏而虚高。 可迁移的方法 多 pLM × 多层 × 多头的高通量筛选流程 ：57 个候选模型在验证集上按 AP 排序、每家族保留 top 2 的流程，是一种计算高效的集成选择策略。 迁移建议 ：在算力受限时，可先在小验证集上筛选候选组合，再对选中的少数模型进行全量训练。 标准化 AP 校正长度偏差 ：CHORUS 用标准化 AP（按界面残基比例校正）消除了序列长度对性能评估的干扰。 迁移建议 ：在残基级预测任务中，报告标准化指标可避免长序列因正类比例低而被低估。 配体位点正交性分析 ：通过 O/E 比率检验预测的 PPI 界面是否与已知配体结合位点系统性重叠，作为模型特异性的验证。 迁移建议 ：在预测功能位点时，可用已知的互补功能注释（如配体结合、翻译后修饰）做交叉验证，确认模型捕捉的是目标信号而非通用特征。 可迁移的实验设计 多维度消融设计 ：CHORUS 的消融实验系统覆盖了种子变化、坐标基变换、层深替换、家族替换、头替换、参数扩展六个维度，每个维度对应一个具体问题（随机性？表征？深度？家族？架构？规模？）。 迁移建议 ：消融实验应针对每个设计决策设置对照，而非仅做「有/无」二值消融。 外部验证的双重设置 ：既有专门化的膜蛋白基准（CompData101 等），又有跨域迁移测试（可溶性蛋白），分别检验领域内泛化和跨域迁移。 迁移建议 ：在领域专精模型评估中，应同时报告领域内和跨域性能，以刻画模型的适用边界。 对蛋白质结构计算研究的启示 [Analysis] 序列-only 界面预测可作为结构预测的前置过滤器 ：CHORUS 在无结构、无 MSA 条件下达到 0.643 AP，提示在 AlphaFold 无法处理的孤儿膜蛋白上，序列嵌入可能提供足够的界面信号。 潜在方向 ：将 CHORUS 的界面概率作为约束条件输入共折叠模型（如 AlphaFold-Multimer），可能改善膜蛋白复合物预测的采样效率。 pLM 层深的生物物理对应性 ：CHORUS as provided Assessment boundary Scientific validity, methodological soundness, claims versus evidence, and suitability for a high-impact general audience Shared manuscript claim summary The authors present CHORUS, a sequence-only deep learning framework that predicts residue-level protein-protein interaction (PPI) interfaces in alpha-helical transmembrane proteins. The method uses an ensemble of six predictors spanning three protein language model families and three neural architectures, and is claimed to outperform 18 existing methods on a large independent test set. The authors also present a proteome-scale atlas of predictions for 80,619 reviewed transmembrane proteins. Visible evidence base Abstract, Results sections (narrative only, no figures or tables visible), Methods sections, supplementary table references Missing materials affecting confidence All figures, all supplementary tables, all supplementary figures, benchmark dataset details, training/validation/test split compositions, hyperparameter tables, and the actual web resource contents Reviewer Overall assessment This manuscript presents a potentially valuable contribution to the field of membrane protein interaction prediction. The core idea of leveraging cross-pLM ensemble diversity for sequence-only interface prediction is timely and the reported performance gains are notable. However, the manuscript as provided is incomplete in critical ways. The Results section is presented as narrative without any of the referenced figures or tables, making it impossible to verify the central claims. The methods are described in detail, but key validation steps, ablation study results, and statistical comparisons cannot be assessed. The claims of superiority over 18 existing methods rest entirely on data that are not visible. The proteome-scale atlas is a significant resource claim, but its utility and quality cannot be evaluated from the provided material. The manuscript has potential, but the evidence base is insufficient for a definitive assessment. Who would be interested in the results, and why Computational biologists working on protein-protein interaction prediction, particularly those focused on membrane proteins, would be the primary audience. Researchers studying membrane protein structure, function, and assembly would also find the atlas resource valuable. The methodological approach of cross-pLM ensembling may interest the broader deep learning for biology community. The potential application to allosteric drug design targeting membrane proteins could attract pharmaceutical researchers. The work addresses a genuine gap, as membrane protein interfaces remain poorly characterized compared to soluble proteins. Major strengths 1. The problem is well-motivated and important. Membrane protein interactions are understudied and experimentally challenging. 2. The sequence-only, partner-agnostic formulation is elegant and practically useful, removing dependencies on structures, MSAs, and partner identification. 3. The systematic exploration of the pLM family-layer-architecture space is methodologically sound and thorough. 4. The construction of a large, leakage-controlled benchmark with strict sequence identity thresholds is commendable. 5. The proteome-scale atlas is a potentially valuable community resource. 6. The biological analyses (BioLiP orthogonality, FunFam conservation) address important questions about what the model actually learns. The manuscript references Figure 3 and supplementary tables for the benchmark comparison, but none of these are visible in the provided material. The comparison methodology, the specific configurations of the 18 baseline methods, the statistical significance of the 0.030 improvement over ScanNet-MSA, and the handling of methods with incomplete coverage are all unassessable. Why it matters This is the core claim of the paper. Without the actual benchmark results, the reader cannot determine whether CHORUS genuinely advances the state of the art or whether the improvement is marginal, method-specific, or an artifact of evaluation choices. Resolution test Provide the full benchmark results table with per-method AP, AUROC, F1, MCC values, coverage statistics, and confidence intervals. Show the PR and ROC curves for all methods. Detail the exact input configurations for each baseline method and justify any deviations from their native pipelines. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Methodological validation Claim pointer "an optimal ensemble that systematically synthesizes complementary latent representations extracted across different model families (ESM-2, ESM-C, and ProtT5) and layer depths" Evidence pointer Figure 2, Supplementary Figures 1 and 2, Supplementary Tables 1-9, location not provided Concern The ensemble construction and its claimed optimality are not demonstrated. The selection of the six constituent models (two per family) is described as based on validation performance, but the full 57-model comparison, the ablation studies, and the control experiments (random seeds, coordinate transforms, depth variations, uniform duplication) are all referenced but not visible. The claim that cross-family diversity provides orthogonal value beyond intra-family variation requires the actual ablation data. Why it matters The methodological contribution of the paper rests on the demonstration that cross-pLM ensembling is superior to simpler alternatives. Without the ablation and control data, the reader cannot determine whether the performance gain comes from ensembling per se, from the specific model choices, or from increased parameter count. Resolution test Show the full 57-model performance landscape, the ablation results for each control condition, the pairwise model correlation matrix, and the leave-one-out ensemble results. Demonstrate that the six-model ensemble is statistically superior to each control. Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality The concept of cross-pLM ensemble diversity for membrane protein interface prediction is a reasonable extension of existing work, but the field is moving rapidly and the specific contribution needs to be positioned against recent developments. The partner-agnostic formulation is not entirely new, but the systematic exploration of the model space is thorough. The originality is moderate and depends on the demonstrated performance gains. Scientific importance Membrane protein interactions are of high biological and therapeutic importance. A reliable sequence-only predictor would be valuable. The atlas resource could be impactful. However, the importance is contingent on the demonstrated reliability and utility of the predictions. Interdisciplinary readership The topic bridges computational biology, structural biology, and membrane biochemistry. The writing is accessible to a computational audience but may be dense for experimentalists. The potential applications to drug discovery broaden the appeal. Technical soundness The methodological framework is well-conceived, with careful attention to data leakage, cluster-based evaluation, and ensemble construction. However, the technical soundness cannot be fully assessed without the missing results. The statistical methods described are appropriate, but their application cannot be verified. Readability for nonspecialists The abstract is clear and the motivation is well-articulated. The Results section is dense and assumes familiarity with PPI prediction methods. The manuscript would benefit from a figure that visually summarizes the workflow and key results for a broader audience. Recommendation posture Currently not established from the provided evidence. The manuscript has a sound methodological framework and addresses an important problem, but the central claims cannot be verified without the missing figures, tables, and supplementary materials. The authors should be invited to resubmit with the complete evidence base. If the benchmark results, ablation studies, and external validations support the claims as stated, the work could be a valuable contribution. The decision should be reconsidered after the full evidence is available.

是一个异质图神经网络，将蛋白残基和配体原子作为两类节点，构建六种边类型（残基-残基骨架边、残基-残基空间边、残基-残基相互作用边、配体-残基边、配体内部边、残基-配体相互作用边），通过消息传递联合编码结构、相互作用、进化三类信息，并以置信度引导的迭代解码策略生成序列。 2) 核心洞察 蛋白适应性由三类互补约束共同决定 ： - 结构约束 ：序列必须能折叠为目标结构（骨架几何、空间邻近）； - 相互作用约束 ：残基必须与配体/辅因子建立正确的非共价相互作用网络（氢键、疏水、π-π 等），这是功能活性的直接化学基础； - 进化约束 ：序列应遵循自然进化中形成的保守性模式，ESM-2 嵌入提供了远超单结构比对所能获得的进化先验。 关键机制 ：三类约束不是简单拼接，而是通过异质图的消息传递在每一层中相互调制——结构边提供几何框架，相互作用边提供功能化学约束，ESM-2 嵌入提供进化上下文。迭代解码策略进一步利用已确定的高置信度残基来逐步丰富上下文，模拟了协同折叠/共进化过程。 3) 可能的普适教训 [Analysis] 评估指标决定模型能力上限 ：当领域以单一指标（如序列恢复率）为优化目标时，模型会过度拟合该指标而牺牲其他维度。zPolaron 的贡献不仅是方法，更是将评估维度从「结构兼容」扩展到「功能适应性」。 异质图是融合多源信息的自然框架 ：当问题涉及多种实体（蛋白残基、配体原子）和多种关系（共价、空间、非共价相互作用）时，异质图比同质图或序列模型更自然地表达领域知识。 进化信息是功能预测的强先验 ：ESM-2 等蛋白语言模型从海量序列中隐式编码了功能约束，与结构/相互作用信息互补，而非替代。 07 方法总览 输入 ：蛋白-配体复合物结构（PDB 格式），包含蛋白骨架原子坐标、配体原子坐标及类型；目标序列的部分掩码（训练时随机掩码，推理时全掩码） 输出 ：每个残基位置上的 20 种氨基酸概率分布；可进一步用于序列设计或适应性打分（mean NLL） 模块 ： 1. 异质图构建 ：残基节点（特征维度 667 = ESM-2 640 维 + 结构特征 27 维）、配体原子节点（24 维 one-hot 原子类型）；六种边类型 2. 消息传递层 ：本文的适应性预测限定在「给定蛋白-配体复合物结构，预测序列变体的适应性（以实验测定的催化活性/稳定性为标签）」这一特定任务。结论不适用于无配体的 apo 蛋白、膜蛋白等未验证场景。 零样本性质 ：zPolaron 的适应性预测是零样本的——即不针对特定蛋白的突变数据微调，直接使用预训练模型打分。这既是优势（无需实验数据），也是局限（无法利用已知突变数据）。 湿实验验证的边界 ：17.84 倍和 1.91 倍的提升是在特定反应条件（30°C, pH 9.0）和特定底物下测得的。这些数值不应被解读为普适的「平均提升倍数」。 与序列恢复率的关系 ：zPolaron 在序列恢复率上确实最高，但作者明确指出恢复率 ≠ 功能。该结论的准确表述是：zPolaron 在保持高恢复率的同时，额外获得了更好的适应性预测能力。 消融实验的解读 ：任意两类信息组合都优于全部基线，说明三类信息有冗余性；但 ESM-2 贡献最大，说明进化信息是适应性预测的主要驱动力。 不支持的结论 ：本文不证明「整合三类信息是适应性预测的必要条件」，也不证明「zPolaron 在所有蛋白类型上均最优」。测试集以酶为主，其他蛋白类型的泛化能力未验证。 12 作者自认局限 局限 具体表现 作者提出的未来方向 来源 序列恢复率与功能不完全对应 高恢复率不保证功能活性，恢复率指标本身有局限 ：逐步锁定高置信度残基、丰富上下文，模拟协同折叠过程，避免误差累积。可迁移到序列设计、结构生成等自回归/迭代生成任务。 适应性预测需要多维评估 ：仅用序列恢复率评估逆折叠模型会掩盖功能预测能力的差异。应同时评估结构兼容性（恢复率、TM-score）、稳定性（ΔΔG 相关性）、适应性（实验 fitness 相关性）、功能位点敏感性（AUC/AP）。 进化信息是适应性预测的强先验 ：ESM-2 嵌入贡献最大（消融实验），说明从海量序列中学习的进化约束比几何结构更接近功能本质。可迁移到突变效应预测、适应性景观建模。 计算预测 + 湿实验验证的闭环 ：先计算筛选（发现新酶、预测有益突变），再湿实验验证（活性测定），形成「预测-验证-迭代」的完整流程。这是计算蛋白设计走向实际应用的必要路径。 对 B-factor 的鲁棒性设计 ：通过整合进化/相互作用信息，模型对结构噪声（高 B-factor Figures, tables, and supplementary materials are referenced but not provided. Assessment boundary Scientific claims, methodological soundness, experimental design, and interpretation as presented in the text. No assessment of code functionality, reproducibility of the wet-lab experiments beyond what is described, or verification of the GitHub repository contents. Shared manuscript claim summary The authors introduce zPolaron, a heterogeneous graph neural network for protein inverse folding on protein–ligand complexes. The model integrates structural, interaction, and evolutionary information via six edge types and ESM-2 embeddings, using a confidence-guided iterative decoding strategy. Claims include: state-of-the-art sequence recovery on a low-similarity test set; superior zero-shot fitness prediction on ProteinGym and a DAOx multi-substrate benchmark; strong sensitivity in identifying loss-of-function mutations in binding pockets; and wet-lab validation showing a 17.84-fold activity improvement for CalA6-D205A-S160G and a 1.91-fold improvement for CalB-I121M. Visible evidence base Text descriptions of results in Sections 3.1–3.5, including numerical values for recovery rates, correlations, AUC/AP, and fold improvements. Methodological details in Sections 2.1–2.4. All figures, tables, and supplementary materials are referenced but not visible. Missing materials affecting confidence All figures (Figs. 1–5), supplementary figures (Figs. S1–S5), supplementary methods (Section 3 of Supplementary Materials), dataset composition details, and the GitHub repository contents. Without these, statistical significance, effect sizes, baseline comparisons, and experimental reproducibility cannot be independently verified. Reviewer Overall assessment The manuscript addresses a relevant and timely problem: moving protein inverse folding beyond structural recovery toward functional fitness prediction. The proposed architecture, combining heterogeneous graph representations with ESM-2 embeddings and iterative decoding, is a reasonable and well-motivated design. The wet-lab validation is a notable strength that elevates the work beyond purely computational benchmarking. However, the manuscript as presented has several critical gaps. The absence of all figures and supplementary materials makes it impossible to verify the quantitative claims, assess statistical rigor, or evaluate the experimental setup. The framing in the abstract and introduction overstates the novelty of integrating evolutionary information, as prior inverse folding methods already incorporate such signals. The wet-lab section lacks critical controls and quantitative details. The claim that zPolaron "fills the missing puzzle of inverse folding" is not supported by the evidence presented, which is largely incremental over existing methods. Who would be interested in the results, and why Computational protein design researchers, particularly those working on inverse folding, enzyme engineering, and fitness prediction. The wet-lab validation of predicted variants would also interest protein engineers and synthetic biologists seeking practical tools for enzyme optimization. The methodological combination of graph neural networks with protein language models is relevant to the broader machine learning for structural biology community. Major strengths 1) The problem framing is important: sequence recovery alone is insufficient for functional protein design, and the authors provide a clear argument for integrating interaction and evolutionary constraints. 2) The heterogeneous graph design with six edge types is a thoughtful architectural choice that explicitly encodes physicochemical interactions. 3) The confidence-guided iterative decoding strategy is a sensible compromise between autoregressive and one-shot generation. 4) The wet-lab validation, if reproducible, provides compelling evidence of practical utility that is rare in this field. 5) The analysis of B-factor sensitivity (Section 3.1) addresses a practical concern about robustness to structural uncertainty. Major Concerns See detailed items below. Minor Comments See detailed items below. Technical failings that need to be addressed before the case is established R1-M1 (missing figures and statistical rigor), R1-M2 (overstated novelty), R1-M3 (incomplete wet-lab reporting), R1-M4 (unclear dataset construction and leakage control). Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality : Moderate. The integration of interaction and evolutionary information is a reasonable extension of existing work, but the individual components (heterogeneous graphs, ESM-2 embeddings, iterative decoding) are all established techniques. The specific combination and the wet-lab validation provide some novelty, but the conceptual advance over LigandMPNN and CARBONARA is incremental. Scientific importance : Moderate to high. Functional fitness prediction is a critical bottleneck in protein design, and demonstrating practical utility via wet-lab validation is valuable. However, the importance is diminished by the lack of clear evidence that the improvements are statistically significant and generalizable beyond the tested systems. Interdisciplinary readership : Moderate. The work bridges computational biology, machine learning, and enzymology. The wet-lab results could attract a broader audience, but the presentation is heavily computational and may not be accessible to experimentalists without additional context. Technical soundness : Cannot be fully assessed. The architectural choices are reasonable, but the absence of figures, supplementary methods, and statistical details prevents verification of the claims. The wet-lab section lacks critical controls. Readability for nonspecialists : Moderate. The introduction and discussion are accessible, but the methods section assumes significant familiarity with graph neural networks and protein language models. The abstract is clear but overstates the novelty. Recommendation posture Currently not established from the provided evidence. The manuscript has potential, and the wet-lab validation is promising, but the missing figures, supplementary materials, and statistical details preclude a supportive recommendation. Major revisions are required to address the concerns below. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Evidence quality and statistical rigor Claim pointer The manuscript claims zPolaron "outperforms all baselines" across sequence recovery, fitness prediction, and mutation effect identification, with specific numerical values (e.g., recovery rate exceeding 80% at 10 iterations, Spearman correlations of −0.609 and −0.530, AUC of 0.934 and 0.995). Evidence pointer Sections 3.1–3.4; all figures (Figs. 1–5) and supplementary figures (Figs. S1–S5) are referenced but not provided. Concern The central quantitative claims cannot be verified without the figures and supplementary materials. No confidence intervals, standard errors, or statistical tests are reported for any of the benchmark comparisons. The number of independent runs, the variance across runs, and the significance of differences between zPolaron and baselines are not stated. For the wet-lab experiments, no replicates, error bars, or statistical analysis are presented. The claim of "significantly higher" recovery rate (Section 3.1) is unsupported without statistical testing. Why it matters Nature-style publications require rigorous statistical evidence. Without measures of variance and significance, the reader cannot determine whether the observed improvements are meaningful or within noise. This is particularly important given the small number of test systems (10 PDB entries for stability, 8 enzyme targets for fitness, 2 enzymes for mutation analysis). Resolution test Provide all figures and supplementary materials. Add confidence intervals, standard errors, or statistical tests (e.g., paired tests across targets) for all benchmark comparisons. Report the number of independent runs and the variance. For wet-lab experiments, provide replicate numbers, error bars, and appropriate statistical analysis. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Novelty and positioning Claim pointer The abstract states that "none of [structural, interaction, evolutionary constraints] are handled in a unified manner by existing pretrained models" and that zPolaron "fills the missing puzzle of inverse folding." Evidence pointer Section 1 (Introduction), Abstract. Concern The claim that existing models do not handle evolutionary information is inaccurate. ESM-2 embeddings, which the authors use, are derived from evolutionary sequence data. ProteinMPNN and ESM-IF have been shown to capture evolutionary constraints implicitly. LigandMPNN explicitly incorporates ligand context. The novelty of zPolaron appears to be the specific combination of heterogeneous graph edges with ESM-2 embeddings and iterative decoding, not the introduction of a fundamentally new information source. The "missing puzzle" framing overstates the gap. Why it matters Overstated novelty undermines the credibility of the contribution. The manuscript should accurately position zPolaron relative to existing methods, acknowledging that evolutionary information is already used in various forms, and clarify what specific architectural or methodological advance enables the improved performance. Resolution test Revise the introduction and abstract to accurately describe the state of the art. Provide a clear, specific statement of what zPolaron adds beyond existing methods, supported by ablation studies that isolate the contribution of each component. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Experimental validation and reporting Claim pointer Section 3.5 claims wet-lab validation showing "CalA6-D205A-S160G achieves a 17.84-fold improvement in catalytic activity over native CalA" and "CalB-I121M shows a 1.91-fold increase." Evidence pointer Section 3.5, Fig. 5, Fig. S5. Concern The wet-lab section is severely under-reported. No details are given on: (i) the number of biological and technical replicates; (ii) the assay conditions beyond buffer, pH, and temperature; (iii) how the 17.84-fold and 1.91-fold values were calculated (e.g., initial rates, endpoint assays, product quantification); (iv) whether the improvements are statistically significant; (v) the expression and purification yields for each variant; (vi) whether the variants were characterized for stability, expression level, or solubility beyond activity. The statement that CalA8 was "predominantly expressed as inclusion bodies" suggests variability in expression that is not controlled for. Without these details, the wet-lab claims cannot be evaluated. Why it matters Wet-lab validation is a major strength of the manuscript, but only if it is rigorously reported. The current description is insufficient for reproduction or independent verification. The 17.84-fold improvement is a strong claim that requires robust evidence. Resolution test Provide full experimental details: replicate numbers, statistical analysis, assay protocols, calculation methods, and characterization of all variants (expression, solubility, stability). Include raw data or representative chromatograms/curves in the supplementary materials. Concern ID R1-M4 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Dataset construction and leakage control Claim pointer Section 2.2 describes the training set as "the protein–ligand complex dataset released by the LigandMPNN study" and the test set as "249 low-similarity PDB structures published between 2023 and 2025, collected independently," with sequence similarity "strictly below 40%." Evidence pointer Section 2.2, Section 3.1. Concern The dataset construction is described too briefly. Key questions remain: (i) How was the 40% sequence similarity threshold computed (global vs. local alignment, which tool)? (ii) Was the threshold applied per-chain or per-complex? (iii) Were the test PDB structures checked for ligand identity and binding site similarity to training structures, or only sequence similarity? (iv) How many structures were excluded by the filtering, and what was the final distribution of protein families and ligand types? (v) For the ProteinGym and DAOx benchmarks, were the structures used for scoring consistent with the training set (e.g., did any ProteinGym targets overlap with training structures)? (vi) The stability benchmark uses only 10 PDB entries, which is a very small sample. The manuscript does not state whether these 10 entries are representative or how they were selected. Why it matters Leakage between training and test sets is a common pitfall in protein design benchmarks. If the test set is not truly independent, the reported improvements may be inflated. The small sample sizes also raise concerns about generalizability. Resolution test Provide a detailed description of dataset construction, including the alignment tool and parameters, the filtering process, and the final composition of all datasets. Report the number of structures excluded at each step. For the stability benchmark, justify the selection of the 10 PDB entries and consider expanding the set. Verify and report that no test targets share significant sequence or structural similarity with training data. Minor Comments Concern ID R1-m1 Severity Minor Axis Clarity of model description Affected element Section 2.1 Evidence pointer Section 2.1, equations (1)–(3) Issue The model architecture is described at a high level, but the equations are not fully defined. The message-passing update, attention weight computation, and edge feature construction are not specified in sufficient detail. The dimension of edge features (d_e) is mentioned but not explained. The integration of ESM-2 embeddings with graph features is described only qualitatively. Required correction Provide a complete mathematical specification of the model, including the attention mechanism, message functions, edge feature construction, and the fusion of ESM-2 embeddings. Include a diagram or pseudocode in the supplementary materials. Concern ID R1-m2 Severity Minor Axis Baseline selection and comparison Affected element Section 3.1 Evidence pointer Section 3.1, Fig. 2a Issue The baseline methods (CARBONARA, ABACUS-T, LigandMPNN, ProteinMPNN) are appropriate, but the comparison is not described in detail. It is unclear whether all baselines were retrained on the same training set, whether hyperparameters were tuned per method, and whether the same decoding strategy (e.g., iterative vs. one-shot) was used for all methods. Required correction Describe the training and evaluation protocol for all baselines, including hyperparameter selection, decoding strategy, and any differences in input features. State whether the comparison is fair in terms of model capacity and training data. Concern ID R1-m3 Severity Minor Axis Statistical reporting in figures Affected element Section 3.1–3.4, Figs. 2–4 Evidence pointer Sections 3.1–3.4 Issue The text reports mean values (e.g., mean ΔPSSM = −0.62) but does not report the distribution or variance. For the correlation analyses, no confidence intervals are given. The ROC/PR curves in Figs. 4i–l are described qualitatively without reporting the number of positive and negative samples. Required correction Add error bars, confidence intervals, or box plots to all figures. Report the number of samples for each ROC/PR analysis. Consider adding a supplementary table with all numerical results and their variances. Concern ID R1-m4 Severity Minor Axis Discussion of limitations Affected element Section 4 Evidence pointer Section 4.1, 4.2 Issue The discussion of limitations focuses on the sequence recovery metric but does not address limitations of the zPolaron model itself, such as its dependence on accurate ligand poses, sensitivity to the quality of input structures, or the computational cost of iterative decoding. The discussion of evolutionary constraints is insightful but does not acknowledge that ESM-2 embeddings may not capture all relevant evolutionary signals for ligand-binding sites. Required correction Add a subsection on model limitations, including input structure quality, ligand pose dependence, computational cost, and potential failure modes. Acknowledge the limitations of ESM-2 embeddings for capturing binding-site-specific evolutionary constraints. Concern ID R1-m5 Severity Minor Axis Reproducibility of wet-lab experiments Affected element Section 2.4 Evidence pointer Section 2.4 Issue The wet-lab methods are described in a single paragraph without sufficient detail. The source of the genes, the expression host strain, the induction conditions, the lysis method, and the HPLC analysis conditions are mentioned but not fully specified. The "standard curves" are referenced but not described. Required correction Provide a complete experimental protocol in the supplementary materials, including all buffer compositions, instrument settings, and data analysis procedures. Risk / unsupported claims The claim that zPolaron "fills the missing puzzle of inverse folding" is unsupported and overstated. The manuscript demonstrates incremental improvements on benchmarks, not a fundamental resolution of a known gap. The claim that "none of [structural, interaction, evolutionary constraints] are handled in a unified manner by existing pretrained models" is inaccurate, as ESM-2 and related models already incorporate evolutionary information. The specific numerical claims (17.84-fold, 1.91-fold, AUC 0.934/0.995, Spearman −0.609/−0.530) are unsupported without the corresponding figures, raw data, and statistical analysis. The claim that zPolaron is "insensitive to structural uncertainty" (Section 3.1, B-factor analysis) is based on a single analysis and lacks statistical verification. The generalizability of zPolaron to diverse protein families and ligand types is claimed but not demonstrated, given the limited number of test systems. The statement that "any two of the three information sources suffice to surpass all baselines" (Section 5) is presented without the ablation data (Fig. S2) being visible.

chain-of-structures（COS）框架，将蛋白质设计分解为催化核心、活性位点、全局骨架、完整序列结构四个递进轮次，通过语言推理专家（Qwen）与全原子扩散生成专家（RFdiffusion3）之间的离散残基约束和连续潜变量接口实现端到端耦合，在酶设计基准上达到 57.0% EC3 一致性和 0.729 TM-score，优于四个基线方法中的五个指标。 03 研究问题 具体问题 ：如何将科学推理（从化学反应需求到蛋白质结构决策）与结构生成（从条件到全原子蛋白质）在统一框架中连接，使推理过程可被结构监督、生成过程可被推理引导？ 为什么重要 ：酶设计需要同时满足化学层面的催化机制（局部几何精确排布）和蛋白质层面的可折叠性（全局结构兼容）。现有方法要么只做序列生成（缺乏结构验证），要么只做结构生成（缺乏化学推理），难以端到端地将化学意图转化为可折叠的完整蛋白质。 现有方法不足 结构状态本身是推理与生成之间的「通用语言」 。与其让语言模型直接输出蛋白质序列或结构坐标（超出其能力范围），不如让它在中间结构状态上做决策——每个决策都是可审计的化学假设，同时每个决策都直接条件化生成过程。这使推理从「文本旁白」变为「结构操作」，使生成从「黑箱采样」变为「逐步承诺」。 3) 可能的普适教训 [Analysis] 中间表征的选择决定耦合质量 ：本文选择「残基承诺 + ：本文的评估限于 text-to-protein 任务，输入为反应规格 + 目标长度，输出为序列 + 结构。不涉及实验验证（酶活性测定、表达测试等），所有结构均为预测。 oracle/真值输入 ：评测使用参考酶的 EC 编号和序列作为匹配目标，但结构来自预测复合物而非实验结构。催化残基标注大部分来自规则推断或同源转移（仅约 1,500-2,400 个蛋白有直接实验证据）。 端到端状态 ：本文的「端到端」指通过连续潜变量接口联合微调双专家，但不包括离散残基选择的梯度回传，也不包括推理时采样轨迹的微分。 有边界的结论 ： - COS 在计算基准上优于现有方法，但增益幅度有限（EC3 +1.7 vs 最强基线） - 显式结构链的价值主要体现在结构质量（pLDDT, TM）而非功能匹配 - 连续通道比文本链更重要，但两者缺一不可 - 前向链无回溯机制，作者明确将回溯视为未来工作 不可支持的强结论 ： - 不能声称 COS 设计的酶具有实际催化活性（无实验验证） - 不能声称 COS 的推理过程与人类酶学家的推理等价（仅结构监督） - 不能声称 COS 适用于所有酶类（测试覆盖 98 个 EC 类，但非全酶谱） 12 作者自认局限 局限 具体表现 作者提出的未来方向 来源 前向链无回溯 每轮承诺不可修改，无法处理不兼容的早期决策 ：语言模型不需要直接输出结构，而是通过「残基承诺 + 结构状态」与生成器交互。这一概念可迁移到任何「推理-生成」耦合场景，如分子对接中的结合位点推理、MD 模拟中的构象选择推理。 递进式承诺控制复杂度 ：将完整蛋白质生成分解为嵌套子问题（核心 ⊂ 位点 ⊂ 骨架 ⊂ 全蛋白），每轮只做当前层级的决策。这类似于 MD 模拟中的多尺度方法（如粗粒化到全原子），可迁移到构象采样策略设计。 experimental design, and result interpretation as presented in the provided text Shared manuscript claim summary The authors propose chain-of-structures (COS), a four-round reasoning-to-generation framework for enzyme design that couples a language reasoning expert with an all-atom diffusion generator. They claim COS outperforms four baseline methods on five of six metrics, including 57.0% EC3 agreement and TM-score 0.729, and that both the written reasoning records and the continuous latent channel contribute to performance. Visible evidence base Abstract, Sections 1-6, Tables 3 referenced (not shown), Figures 1-2 referenced (not shown), training data statistics, ablation results Missing materials affecting confidence Tables 1-3, Figures 1-2, detailed hyperparameters, baseline implementation details, statistical significance tests, experimental validation data, code availability Reviewer Overall assessment The manuscript presents a conceptually interesting framework that explicitly connects language-based reasoning to structural generation for enzyme design. The four-round hierarchical approach is well-motivated and the architectural choices are sensible. However, the evidence provided is insufficient to establish the claimed advantages. Key results are referenced but not shown, baseline comparisons lack statistical rigor, and the reported margins are small. The work is at an early exploratory stage and would benefit from stronger validation, including experimental characterization and more robust benchmarking. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers in computational protein design, AI for science, and enzyme engineering would find this work relevant. The framework's explicit reasoning-to-generation interface addresses a growing interest in interpretable AI-driven design. The methodological insights on coupling language models with diffusion generators could inform future work in multimodal scientific AI. Major Strengths 1. The four-round hierarchical decomposition from catalytic core to complete protein is chemically well-reasoned and provides interpretable intermediate states. 2. The dual-channel interface (discrete residues plus continuous latents) is a thoughtful design that enables structural supervision of the reasoning model. 3. The data construction pipeline, including structural alignment-based label transfer with calibrated TM-score thresholds, is careful and addresses a known challenge in enzyme annotation. 4. The ablation study design is informative, separating the contributions of written reasoning records from the continuous channel. 胺化在过渡金属催化中缺乏区域和对映选择性控制，且该反应涉及高活性中间体与多条竞争路径（1,5- vs 1,6-HAT），是生物催化尚未攻克的挑战。 现有方法不足 ： 小分子催化：缺乏对非苄位 C–H 键的选择性控制，区域选择性差。 天然蛋白定向进化：受限于天然 scaffold 的活性位点几何，难以实现需要精确底物定位的挑战性转化。 已有 de novo 设计：多集中于有明确小分子催化先例的反应（如环丙烷化），未涉及高能垒、多竞争路径的烷基氮烯化学。 精确研究问题 ："Can de novo enzyme design, guided by mechanism-informed motifs and refined by directed evolution, enable regio- and enantioselective alkyl nitrene C–H amination to synthesize chiral piperidines with high efficiency and selectivity?" 04 背景与发展脉络 注：以下脉络基于本文引言与讨论，结合领域常识标注「经外部核验」部分。 阶段 代表性方法 优点 局限 本文位置 小分子催化 C–H 胺化 金属催化氮烯转移（Rh、Fe、Co 等） 传统流程中进化终点仅作为最终产物，不指导新设计 缺乏从进化终点提取可迁移设计原则的方法 本文提出「refined motif」策略解决此问题 06 核心思想 1) 表面方法 使用 AP Novo（扩散模型）生成 de novo 血红素蛋白，以（5-azidopentyl）benzene 为底物设计催化分子内 C–H 胺化的酶。 通过部分扩散（partial diffusion）精炼初始设计，获得「recycled-scaffold」变体。 对 de novo 设计进行定向进化（随机突变 + 高通量筛选），优化活性与选择性。 从进化终点提取「refined motif」（底物-辅因子-轴向配体构象），用于第三轮全新 scaffold 设计。 2) 核心洞察 构象预组织（conformational preorganization）是选择性的根源 ：GDM-NT-401 的活性位点通过疏水相互作用将底物苯基固定在特定位置，使烷基链呈弯曲构象，从而优先发生 1,6-HAT（生成哌啶），而非热力学上更有利的 1,5-HAT（生成吡咯烷）。 设计-进化是双向闭环 ：设计提供「可进化的起点」（构象预组织 + 区域选择性），进化在局部序列空间中快速放大活性；进化终点揭示的关键残基/构象可反向指导设计，形成正反馈。 de novo 设计可超越天然蛋白的配体偏好 ：通过 motif 设计可引入非规范轴向配体（Met/Leu），而天然蛋白几乎全部使用 His/Cys。 α/β 混合折叠可能是高选择性血红素蛋白的有利架构 ：β-折叠的刚性可能有助于精确底物定位。 3) 可能的普适教训 [Analysis] 「可进化性」应作为 de novo 设计的第一性目标 ：与其追求初始高活性，不如设计构象上「接近过渡态」的 scaffold，让进化在局部空间中快速收敛。 从进化终点提取设计原则（refined motif）是弥合「设计-进化」鸿沟的关键 ：进化不仅产生最终催化剂，还产生关于「什么构象/残基组合有效」的可迁移知识。 MD 模拟 + DFT 计算可作为设计-进化循环中的「可解释性工具」 ：本文用 MD 模拟解释区域选择性的构象根源，这种「计算-实验闭环」可推广到其他酶设计课题。 07 方法总览 输入 ： evidence, and alignment with Nature-style criteria. No assessment of formatting, grammar, or editorial policy. Shared manuscript claim summary The authors report a synergistic strategy combining de novo enzyme design (using the AP Novo generative model) with directed evolution to create haemproteins that catalyse new-to-nature regio- and enantioselective intramolecular C–H amination of alkyl azides to form chiral piperidines. They claim this transformation is unprecedented in both small-molecule catalysis and biocatalysis, that de novo design provides evolvable starting points with high regioselectivity, that directed evolution rapidly improves activity, and that information from evolution can be fed back into design to improve hit rates and starting-point activities. Visible evidence base Main text figures (Fig. 2, 3, 4, 5) are referenced but not shown. Supplementary Information is referenced extensively (Figs. S2–S4, S8, S10, S11, S14, S28; Table S15; Scheme S3) but not provided. Data availability statement indicates data in main text and SI. Missing materials affecting confidence All figures, tables, and supplementary information are absent. This includes raw activity data, sequence information, experimental protocols, computational details, and structural predictions. The manuscript cannot be fully evaluated without these materials. Reviewer Overall assessment This manuscript presents a compelling and ambitious integration of de novo enzyme design and directed evolution to achieve a challenging abiological transformation. The conceptual framework of reciprocal design-evolution synergy is timely and potentially impactful. However, the provided text alone is insufficient to verify the central claims. Key quantitative data, experimental details, and computational analyses are all relegated to missing figures and supplementary information. The scientific narrative is coherent and the logic is clear, but the evidence base is not assessable from the supplied material. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers in enzyme engineering, directed evolution, computational protein design, biocatalysis, and synthetic chemistry. The work demonstrates a potential paradigm for combining generative AI with experimental evolution, which is of broad interest to the protein science and catalysis communities. The specific transformation (chiral piperidine synthesis) is relevant to pharmaceutical synthesis. Major strengths The conceptual advance of closing the loop between design and evolution is significant. The choice of a challenging, high-energy-barrier reaction with competing pathways is appropriate to showcase the approach. The reported stability and substrate tolerance of the designed enzyme are notable. The computational analysis (DFT and MD) provides a mechanistic rationale for regioselectivity, which strengthens the narrative. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Evidence completeness Claim pointer The manuscript claims specific catalytic performances, including yields, turnover numbers, regioselectivity ratios, and enantioselectivity values for multiple enzyme variants and substrates. Evidence pointer Figures 2, 3, 4, 5; Supplementary Figures S2–S4, S8, S10, S11, S14, S28; Supplementary Table S15; location not provided Concern All quantitative results are presented as values in the text without the corresponding figures, tables, or experimental methods. The reader cannot verify the reported yields, selectivities, or the statistical significance of the improvements claimed. Why it matters The core claims of the paper rest on these numbers. Without access to the raw data, chromatograms, calibration curves, or experimental protocols, the results are unverifiable and the technical soundness cannot be assessed. Resolution test Provide the full figures and supplementary information, including raw data and detailed methods, so that the reported values can be checked against the evidence. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Technical soundness Claim pointer The manuscript claims that the de novo-designed enzymes adopt "architecturally distinct folds" with TM-scores <0.5 to any PDB structure, and that these scaffolds are "readily evolvable." Evidence pointer Figure 3b, 3e, 3f; Supplementary Figures S2, S3, S10, S11; location not provided Concern The structural claims are based on computational predictions (AP Novo and AF3-LA) that are not described in the text. The evolvability claim is based on directed evolution results that are not shown. The structural novelty and evolvability are central to the paper's thesis but cannot be evaluated. Why it matters If the structural predictions are inaccurate or the directed evolution results are not robust, the central claims of scaffold novelty and evolvability would be undermined. Resolution test Provide structural models, alignment details, and the full directed evolution data (library sizes, mutation frequencies, activity distributions) in the supplementary information. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Claim substantiation Claim pointer The manuscript claims that "to our knowledge, this reactivity has not previously been achieved in either transition-metal catalysis or biocatalysis." Evidence pointer Introduction and Conclusion; location not provided Concern This is a strong novelty claim. The text cites references 38–60 for prior work but does not provide a systematic comparison or a clear statement of why the cited prior art does not achieve the same transformation. Why it matters If this claim is overstated, the significance of the work is diminished. The novelty of the transformation is a key selling point. Resolution test Provide a more detailed comparison with prior art, including specific examples of what has and has not been achieved, and justify the novelty claim with explicit evidence. Concern ID R1-M4 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Technical soundness Claim pointer The manuscript claims that the "refined motifs" extracted from evolved variants improve hit rates and starting-point activities in subsequent design rounds. Evidence pointer Figure 3l, 3m; Supplementary Table S15; location not provided Concern The feedback loop from evolution to design is a key conceptual advance, but the data supporting it are not shown. The comparison between control motifs and refined motifs is described but not quantified in the text. Why it matters This is the most novel aspect of the paper. If the improvement is marginal or not statistically robust, the claim of synergy is weakened. Resolution test Provide the full data for the third design round, including hit rates, activity distributions, and statistical analysis comparing control and refined motifs. Technical failings that need to be addressed before the case is established The absence of all figures and supplementary data is a critical failing. The manuscript cannot be evaluated without them. Additionally, the novelty claim regarding the transformation needs more rigorous substantiation. Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality: High. The reciprocal design-evolution loop is a novel concept. Scientific importance: Potentially high, if the claims are substantiated. The work could influence both protein design and directed evolution fields. Interdisciplinary readership: Broad, spanning chemistry, biology, and computational science. Technical soundness: Not assessable from the provided text. The computational and experimental details are missing. Readability for nonspecialists: The text is well-written and the logic is clear, but the heavy reliance on missing figures and supplementary data makes it difficult to follow for a nonspecialist. Recommendation posture Currently not established from the provided evidence. The conceptual framework is promising and the narrative is compelling, but the absence of all supporting data prevents any assessment of technical soundness or claim substantiation. The manuscript could become a strong candidate for publication if the full evidence base is provided and the claims are verified. Risk / unsupported claims The claim that the transformation is unprecedented in both transition-metal catalysis and biocatalysis is not substantiated with a detailed comparison to prior art. All quantitative claims (yields, TTN, regioselectivity, enantioselectivity) are unsupported without the corresponding figures and supplementary data. The claim of structural novelty (TM-score <0.5) is unsupported without structural models and alignment details. The claim of "readily evolvable" scaffolds is unsupported without the directed evolution data. The claim of improved hit rates and starting-point activities from refined motifs is unsupported without the third design round data. The computational analyses (DFT, MD, AF3-LA) are described but not verifiable without the methods and results in the supplementary information.
